神经科学在探索创造力的道路上迈出了重要一步，它绘制了大脑半球的分布图，并确定了它们各自的功能：左脑负责演绎和归纳逻辑、线性思维、数学、模式识别和语言；右脑则负责因果逻辑和类比、视觉化、听觉想象、非语言表达、直觉、节奏感、情感和情绪。

Consider, for example, Carl Sandburg’s poem “Fog”:

例如，请看卡尔·桑德堡的诗作《雾》：

The fog comes
雾气弥漫
on little cat feet.
像猫一样轻盈。
It sits looking
它静静地伫立着，望着前方。
over harbor and city
俯瞰港口和城市
on silent haunches
静静地蹲着
and then moves on.
然后继续前进。

When imagining this poem, images of “cat” and “fog” floated through Sandberg’s mind. While his left brain saw two unrelated examples of biology and weather, his right brain noted a connection only a creative mind would spot and suddenly merged the two into an utterly new third thing, linked by a sense of stillness. As we read the poem, the poignant beauty of his metaphor enriches our inner life with a never-felt-before sensation. The unearthing of an unseen likeness is the most beautiful gift one mind can give another.

在构思这首诗时，“猫”和“雾”的意象在桑德伯格的脑海中浮现。他的左脑看到的是生物学和天气这两个毫不相干的例子，而他的右脑则捕捉到了只有富有创造力的人才能发现的联系，并突然将二者融合为一个全新的事物，而连接二者的是一种静谧之感。当我们阅读这首诗时，他那意味深长的比喻之美，以一种前所未有的方式丰富了我们的内心世界。发掘出不为人知的相似之处，是心灵之间最美好的馈赠。

Creativity is, in essence, the discovery of the third thing. Talent is a duality-seeking sensor that spots hidden analogies between things that already exist. Then, in a creative flash, artists change the known into the new, melding two things into a never-seen-before fusion.

创造力本质上是对第三种事物的发现。天赋是一种寻求二元性的传感器，它能发现已存在事物之间隐藏的相似之处。然后，在灵光乍现的瞬间，艺术家们将已知转化为新事物，将两种事物融合为前所未有的新组合。

In which direction does creativity flow to discover the third thing? Right brain to left or left brain to right? Particular to universal or universal to particular? Answer: Genius flows in both directions—at times alternating slowly, at others instantaneously—as reason and imagination inspire each other. 2

创造力究竟朝哪个方向流动，才能发现第三件事？是右脑流向左脑，还是左脑流向右脑？是特殊到普遍，还是普遍到特殊？答案是：天才的灵感是双向流动的——有时缓慢交替，有时瞬间迸发——因为理性和想象力相互激发。

For example, consider Fantasy. When creating magical characters, writers often begin with archetypes (Wise Man, Warrior, Earth Mother), then bring them down to earth to walk and talk among the common folk (a movement from conceptual to actual). Or when writing a Social Drama, a writer might start with an actual case taken from the news, then design a cast to express the battle between Justice and Injustice on a grand, symbolic scale (a progression from actual to conceptual). Compare, for example, two films from 2017: Wonder Woman , in which a goddess descends from heaven to fight in a human war, and Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri , in which a gift shop owner’s revenge for her daughter’s murder becomes a symbolic act.

例如，以奇幻作品为例。在创作奇幻角色时，作家通常先从原型人物（智者、战士、大地之母）入手，然后将他们带到人间，与普通民众互动交流（这是从概念到现实的转变）。又如，在创作社会剧时，作家可能取材于新闻事件，然后设计一系列角色，以宏大的象征手法展现正义与非正义之间的斗争（这是从现实到概念的演进）。例如，比较一下2017年的两部电影：《神奇女侠》，讲述一位女神从天而降，参与人类战争；以及《三块广告牌》，讲述一位礼品店老板为女儿复仇，最终演变成一场象征性的行动。

Like the god Hermes, creativity is a wing-footed messenger that flies back and forth between two worlds—rational/irrational, left brain / right brain—taming real-life chaos with aesthetic order.

就像赫尔墨斯神一样，创造力是一位长着翅膀的信使，在理性/非理性、左脑/右脑这两个世界之间来回穿梭，用审美秩序驯服现实生活的混乱。

Like a child going out to play, creativity leaves reason at home and saddles up free association for long galloping rides. When two random thoughts suddenly collide and merge into a third idea, the right brain seizes this gem and hands it over to the left, so the writer can use her conscious skills to fit this shiny piece of originality inside a sketch-in-progress, reshaping it into a memorable character.

就像孩子外出玩耍一样，创造力抛开理性，骑上自由联想的战马，驰骋天马行空。当两个随机的想法突然碰撞融合，形成第三个想法时，右脑会抓住这颗宝石，将其交给左脑，让作家运用意识技巧，将这闪耀的原创灵感融入正在创作中的草稿，最终塑造出一个令人难忘的角色。

#↩

TWO THEORIES OF CHARACTER CREATION

两种角色塑造理论

How this process unfolds is subject for debate. Do writers invent characters or give them birth? Are characters conscious creations or subconscious manifestations?

这个过程究竟如何展开，尚存争议。作家是创造人物还是赋予人物生命？人物是有意识的创作还是潜意识的体现？

#↩

Invention

发明

Some writers start with an inspiration for a story, then brainstorm and improvise characters with traits and dimensions that fulfill the promise of their original vision.

有些作家先从故事灵感入手，然后集思广益，即兴创作出具有各种特征和维度的人物，以实现他们最初的构想。

Here’s Suzanne Collins, author of The Hunger Games : “One night I was lying in bed, very tired, channel surfing. I flipped through images of reality shows where young people competed for a million dollars or a bachelor or whatever. Then I saw footage from the Iraq War. These two things fused together in an unsettling way, and that was the moment I got the idea for Katniss’s story.”

以下是《饥饿游戏》作者苏珊·柯林斯的自述：“一天晚上，我躺在床上，非常疲惫，漫无目的地换着电视频道。我看到一些真人秀节目，年轻人为了赢得一百万美元、单身汉或其他什么而竞争。然后我看到了伊拉克战争的画面。这两件事以一种令人不安的方式交织在一起，就在那一刻，我萌生了创作凯特尼斯故事的想法。”

Novelist Patrick McGrath often finds his story spark in intriguing real-life behaviors, perhaps something as simple as an odd tone of voice or a hat worn at an eye-catching angle. He then asks the question: “What kind of person would talk in that voice and wear their hat that way?” Fingers on his keyboard, he merges his creative talents with a lifetime of observations and personal knowledge of human impulses, transforming the intrigue of a trait into a psychologically compelling character and story.

小说家帕特里克·麦格拉斯常常从引人入胜的现实生活中的行为中汲取故事灵感，比如一个古怪的语调，或者一顶戴得格外引人注目的帽子。他会问自己：“什么样的人会用那种语调说话，那样戴帽子？” 他将自己的创作天赋与毕生对人性的观察和深刻理解融为一体，把一个看似微不足道的特征，转化成一个个心理刻画入微、引人入胜的角色和故事。

#↩

Giving Birth

分娩

Other writers see themselves as a kind of bystander, a conduit for personalities finding their way into a yet-to-be-written story. Their characters seem to live an independent existence in another realm, then pass through a mental birth canal into the author’s awareness.

另一些作家则将自己视为一种旁观者，一种将人物引入尚未写成的故事的媒介。他们笔下的人物似乎在另一个世界独立存在，然后通过某种精神上的“产道”进入作者的意识之中。

Elizabeth Bowen, in her book Notes on Writing a Novel , says that notion of character creation is misleading. Characters, she feels, preexist. They reveal themselves slowly to the novelist’s perception—as might a fellow traveler chatting in a dimly lit railway carriage.

伊丽莎白·鲍恩在她的著作《小说写作笔记》中指出，人物塑造的概念具有误导性。她认为，人物是预先存在的。他们会像在昏暗的火车车厢里与人闲聊的旅伴一样，慢慢地向小说家的感知显现出来。

Elizabeth Strout, author of the Pulitzer Prize–winning novel Olive Kitteridge , said that her characters never echo her personal experiences, as readers often assume. Rather, they come to life mysteriously, organically, in stray scenes or bits of dialogue and then, through a process she finds difficult to explain, eventually coalesce. She scribbles snippets on scraps of paper and lets the scraps accrue. Discarding some, keeping others, she waits until “characters do their little things and I keep what’s truthful.”

伊丽莎白·斯特劳特是普利策奖获奖小说《奥利弗·基特里奇》的作者。她说，她笔下的人物并非如读者通常认为的那样，反映了她个人的经历。相反，他们是以一种神秘而自然的方式在零星的场景或对话片段中鲜活起来的，然后通过一个她自己也难以解释的过程，最终凝聚成形。她把一些片段潦草地记在纸片上，任其堆积。她丢弃一些，保留一些，等待着“人物做出他们自己的小举动，而我则保留那些真实的部分”。

Novelist Anne Lamott noted, “I’ve always believed that these people inside me—the characters—know who they are and what they’re about and what happens, but they need me to help get it down on paper because they don’t type.”

小说家安妮·拉莫特指出：“我一直相信，我内心的这些人——我笔下的人物——知道自己是谁，知道自己的本质，知道会发生什么，但他们需要我帮助他们把这些写在纸上，因为他们不会打字。”

For most writers, the day-in-day-out work of role creation calls on both modes—surprises from the subconscious (giving birth) and improvisation while pacing a room (invention). With each new character, the writer juggles all sources of inspiration, trying to get the balance just right.

对大多数作家而言，日复一日的角色创作需要两种模式的配合——潜意识的灵感迸发（角色诞生）和在房间里踱步时的即兴发挥（构思）。每创作一个新角色，作家都要权衡所有灵感来源，力求找到最佳平衡点。

There’s mystery in creativity, no doubt, but the claim that a character refuses to do what her writer wants her to do strikes me as literary narcissism. Would a composer claim that a chord she wants to play refuses to sound itself? Would a painter claim that the color red has a mind of its own? Certain writers, hoping to make themselves mysterious, want us to believe that writing is dreamlike, that authors simply surrender to native impulses, that they are conduits for instinctive forces beyond their control. This romance has always sounded a bit phony, a bit pretentious.

创造力中的确蕴含着神秘感，这一点毋庸置疑，但声称笔下人物拒绝按照作者的意愿行事，在我看来不过是文学界的自恋罢了。作曲家会声称自己想弹奏的和弦拒绝发出声音吗？画家会声称红色有自己的意识吗？某些作家为了营造神秘感，试图让我们相信写作如梦似幻，作者只是顺应本能冲动，成为某种不受自身控制的本能力量的管道。这种浪漫的说法总显得有些虚假，有些矫揉造作。

Suppose, like a character created by Woody Allen or Luigi Pirandello, one of your roles stepped out of your telling and into reality. I don’t mean into the fantastic realities of The Purple Rose of Cairo or Six Characters in Search of an Author ; I mean into actuality. Suppose this character wanted to write her story. Suppose she took over your keyboard. Then suppose this gal discovers that she has no talent. Where would you go from there?

假设，就像伍迪·艾伦或路易吉·皮兰德娄笔下的人物一样，你笔下的某个角色突然从你的叙述中走出来，进入了现实。我指的不是《开罗紫玫瑰》或《六个寻找作者的剧中人》那种奇幻的现实，而是真正的现实。假设这个角色想要写下她的故事。假设她霸占了你的键盘。然后假设她发现自己根本没有写作天赋。接下来你会怎么做？

Characters are works of art, not artists. They manifest in an author’s mind and will do exactly what she imagines them doing, although in often surprising ways. Being surprised by your own ideas is a daily experience for the talented writer. The subconscious mind absorbs an artist’s direct experience of life and factual researches, as well as the artist’s dreams and imaginings, then stirs all this material into new forms to be sent back to the conscious mind. This work goes on out of sight until suddenly, unexpectedly, insights into behavior and radical fusions of character traits take the writer by surprise. These flashes of genius result from subconscious churnings that go on behind the artist’s awareness while she strains against the harness of craft.

人物是艺术品，而非艺术家。他们诞生于作者的脑海中，会按照作者的想象行事，尽管方式往往出人意料。对于才华横溢的作家来说，每天都会经历被自己的想法所震撼的体验。潜意识会吸收艺术家对生活的直接体验和事实研究，以及艺术家的梦境和想象，然后将所有这些素材融合成新的形式，再传递给意识。这项工作在作者的潜意识中默默进行，直到突然间，对人物行为的深刻洞察和性格特征的巧妙融合令作者猝不及防。这些灵光乍现的瞬间源于潜意识的翻腾，在艺术家努力挣脱技艺束缚的同时，这些翻腾在她意识之外持续进行。

Like the Lamaze method, creativity gives birth in a wide-awake world. No mystical spirit, no daughter of Zeus will descend from Olympus to inspire you. Writing will be what it always has been: giving breath to what you already know.

就像拉玛泽分娩法一样，创造力诞生于一个清醒的世界。不会有神秘的精灵，也不会有宙斯的女儿从奥林匹斯山降临来启发你。写作依然是它本来的样子：赋予你已知的知识以生命。

#↩

CREATIVE HUNGER

创作欲望

An artist amasses scraps and smidgeons of knowledge over a lifetime of learning, experiencing, and imagining, all swirling in the subconscious mind. A talented right brain gathers random bits, spots links between them, unites two into one, and then passes these creations to the left brain for use. With that, however, arises the artist’s persistent problem: Because you can create only from what’s already in your mind, your work is strictly limited by the contents of your unthought thoughts.

艺术家一生都在学习、体验和想象中积累零碎的知识，这些知识如同漩涡般在潜意识中翻腾。才华横溢的右脑收集各种零散的信息，发现它们之间的联系，将两者融合为一体，然后将这些成果传递给左脑进行运用。然而，这也带来了艺术家们始终面临的难题：由于创作只能基于已有的思维内容，因此作品的创作也严格受限于那些尚未被思考过的想法。

The less you know and experience, the less likely your talent will generate originalities; contrariwise, the greater your understanding and insight, the more likely your talent will discover new ideas. An ignorant but talented writer may manage pieces of brief beauty, but authorship of complex full-length works demands a breadth and depth of knowing.

知识和经验越少，你的才华就越难产生原创性；反之，理解力和洞察力越强，你的才华就越有可能发掘新思想。一个无知但才华横溢的作家或许能写出优美的短篇作品，但要创作复杂完整的作品，则需要广博而精深的知识。

The moment your inspiration provides an intriguing but unfamiliar character, you suddenly realize that what you know is not enough. It never is. For your talent to fight above its weight, it needs to bulk up on knowledge. An author is not a pretender, not a literary fake, but someone with wide, deep awareness, someone with the cerebral power to punch home the truth. For that reason, writers of one-of-a-kind characters underpin their creativity with research.

当你的灵感迸发，创造出一个引人入胜却又陌生的角色时，你突然意识到，你所掌握的知识远远不够。事实上，永远都不够。要想让你的才华超越自身局限，就必须不断充实于知识。作家不是伪装者，也不是文学的赝品，而是拥有广博而深刻的认知，拥有足以直击真相的智慧。正因如此，那些塑造独一无二角色的作家，都会以严谨的研究为创作的基石。

Suppose one night you had this dream: A family dressed in white lab coats feverishly frets over tables filled with a dazzling array of test tubes. Something about this scene wakes you in a sweat. The next morning you start making notes in pursuit of this mysterious family. And what’s in your notes? Questions demanding answers:

假设你某天晚上做了这样一个梦：一家人穿着白大褂，焦急地围着摆满琳琅满目试管的桌子。这场景让你惊醒，冷汗涔涔。第二天早上，你开始做笔记，试图了解这个神秘的家庭。而你的笔记里都写了些什么呢？一些亟待解答的问题：

Who are these characters? Mother? Father? Son? Daughter? Are they scientists or saboteurs? What is their specific task? To create or destroy? Or do figures in lab coats symbolize something so personal it has nothing to do with science? Whichever way you answer, new questions will rise up to demand answers you may or may not have. Without a reservoir of unique knowledge, you can only imitate other writers. So how can you create a fascinating cast of original characters?

这些人物是谁？母亲？父亲？儿子？女儿？他们是科学家还是破坏分子？他们的具体任务是什么？创造还是毁灭？或者，这些身穿白大褂的人物象征着某种与科学无关的私人意义？无论你的答案是什么，新的问题都会不断涌现，而你可能知道答案，也可能不知道。如果没有独特的知识储备，你只能模仿其他作家。那么，如何才能创造出一群引人入胜、独具特色的角色呢？

Start by filling files with everything you know about the characters and their world. You may think you know, but you don’t know you know until you can write it down. Words spelled out on a page pull you out of self-deception and into reality, pointing the way to creative investigation. For if you find you cannot put your knowledge on paper, it means only one thing: It’s time to learn.

首先，把你了解的所有关于角色及其世界的信息都记录下来。你或许自以为了解，但只有写下来才能真正确定。纸上的文字能让你摆脱自欺欺人的幻想，回归现实，并指引你进行创造性的探索。如果你发现自己无法将所学知识诉诸笔端，那就意味着一件事：是时候学习了。

#↩

THE FOUR RESEARCHES THAT FEED CREATIVITY

激发创造力的四大研究

Research travels down four roads: personal, imagined, factual, and actual.

研究沿着四条道路展开：个人道路、想象道路、事实道路和实际道路。

#↩

1. Personal Research

1. 个人研究

Your memory collects all the meaningful emotional experiences you have undergone in both reality and fiction. Over time, the origins of these two sources begin to blur because memory stores them in the same mental vault. That’s why we often act as if what actually happened to us were a story and as if stories actually happened to us. The result? We know far more than we think we know… if we take pains to explore our past.

你的记忆会收集你在现实和虚构世界中经历的所有有意义的情感体验。随着时间的推移，这两种来源的界限开始模糊，因为记忆将它们存储在同一个心理库中。这就是为什么我们常常会把真实发生的事情当作故事，把故事当作真实发生的事情。结果呢？如果我们用心探索过去，就会发现我们了解的远比我们自认为的要多得多。

Inventorying memory is the first and most fundamental form of research. When you struggle to bring truth to light, simply ask, “What do I know directly from life that would help me create these characters?”

梳理记忆是研究的首要且最基本的形式。当你难以揭示真相时，只需问问自己：“我从生活中直接了解到的哪些信息可以帮助我塑造这些角色？”

Let’s say that you’re a female writer composing a story that revolves around a patriarchal family, and you envision the son rebelling against his punishing father. How could memory help you create these characters and make this rebellion scene surprising, revealing, and cliché free?

假设你是一位女性作家，正在创作一个以父权家庭为背景的故事，你设想儿子反抗严苛的父亲。记忆如何帮助你塑造这些人物，并使这场反抗戏份出人意料、发人深省且不落俗套？

Think back to your childhood. You were no doubt disciplined but perhaps never severely. Nonetheless, you reacted against your parent’s rules. The dynamic of punishment and rebellion, with its core emotions of pain and anger, is universal. Ask yourself: What’s the worst emotional pain I’ve ever suffered? What’s the angriest I’ve ever been? What did I do in pain? In anger?

回想一下你的童年。你无疑会受到管教，但或许从未受到严厉的惩罚。尽管如此，你还是会反抗父母的规矩。惩罚与反叛的动态关系，以及其中蕴含的痛苦和愤怒，是普遍存在的。问问自己：我经历过的最痛苦的情感折磨是什么？我最愤怒的时刻是什么？在痛苦中，我做了什么？在愤怒中，我又做了什么？

Re-create these scenes from your past and write them down in a vivid, diary-like way. Focus on the inner sensations of your emotions and their manifestations in physical behavior—what you saw, what you heard, what you felt, and, most important, what you said and did. Express these images and actions in language that makes your palms sweat and your heart pound as if it were happening again.

重现你过去的这些场景，并以生动的日记形式记录下来。专注于你内心的情绪感受及其在身体行为上的体现——你所看到的、听到的、感受到的，以及最重要的，你所说和所做的事情。用能让你手心冒汗、心跳加速的语言来描述这些画面和行为，仿佛一切又重现眼前。

Now go back to your characters. Using your remembrances as a guide, imagine how your past experience might transfer, transform, or even reverse into theirs.

现在回到你的角色身上。以你的记忆为指导，想象一下你过去的经历会如何转移、转化，甚至逆转到他们的经历中。

#↩

2. Imaginative Research

2. 想象力研究

Memory takes whole events from the past and re-creates them in the present. Imagination, on the other hand, takes something that happened to you when you were five and couples it with something that happened to you when you were twenty-five. It takes an item you read in the news and pairs it with a dream you had one night, blends both of them with words you heard on a street corner, and finally ribbons all three inside an image you saw in a film. Your imagination uses the power of analogy to invent today’s wholes out of bits of the past.

记忆将过去的完整事件重现于当下。而想象力则不同，它将你五岁时的经历与你二十五岁时的经历结合起来。它将你在新闻中读到的一条信息与你某夜做的一个梦联系起来，再将两者与你在街角听到的话语融合在一起，最终将这三者编织成你在电影中看到的画面。你的想象力运用类比的力量，将过去的碎片拼凑成今天的完整图景。

So, before your father and son begin to defy and dominate each other, simply bring them to mind. See them, hear them. Walk around them 360 degrees. Don’t make lists of their traits, analyze their motives, or put words in their mouths. Not yet. Instead, take them for a long walk through your imagination.

所以，在你父亲和儿子开始互相对抗、互相压制之前，只需在脑海中浮现他们的身影。看着他们，听着他们。360度环视他们。不要列出他们的性格特征，分析他们的动机，也不要替他们设定说话方式。现在还不是时候。相反，先带着他们，在你的想象中漫步一番。

In this early stage you’re trying to gain an overall impression, the kind you might take away after chatting with someone at a party. But once you decide that a character deserves creation, you will have to submerge your imagination in much deeper waters.

在初期阶段，你试图获得一个整体印象，就像你在聚会上与人聊天后产生的那种感觉。但一旦你决定要创造一个角色，你就必须让你的想象力深入到更深的领域。

#↩

3. Book-Bound Research

3. 装订成册的研究

If you were to write about a conflicted father and son, you could draw on families you’ve lived in, families you’ve observed, and all those you might imagine. But no matter how familiar the subject, you will soon find that memory and imagination take you only so far. The knowledge you have at the beginning of a project is rarely enough to finish it. To that you must add book-bound learning.

如果你要写一个关于父子冲突的故事，你可以借鉴自己生活过的家庭、观察过的家庭，以及你能想象到的所有家庭。但无论主题多么熟悉，你很快就会发现，记忆和想象的作用终究有限。你在项目开始时所掌握的知识往往不足以完成它。除此之外，你还需要书本知识的积累。

If you read penetrating works on the psychology and sociology of the parent-child relationship, taking notes as if you were doing a thesis, two powerful things would happen:

如果你阅读有关亲子关系心理学和社会学的深刻著作，并像写论文一样做好笔记，那么将会发生两件意义重大的事情：

1. You would discover your family in all the families under study, confirming the truth or untruth of everything you know. You would see that parents and children in differing cultures undergo common pressures and move through similar stages. Each family reacts and adapts in its own special way, but human beings are far more alike than different. Therefore, if your writing rings true, your particular will become universal as people recognize their personal household in your fictional clan. In other words, your writing will find its readers or audiences.

1. 你会发现，在所有研究的家庭中，都能找到自己家庭的影子，从而验证你所知道的一切的真伪。你会发现，不同文化背景下的父母和孩子面临着共同的压力，经历着相似的成长阶段。每个家庭都有其独特的应对和适应方式，但人类的相似之处远大于差异。因此，如果你的文字真实可信，你的个人经历就会具有普遍意义，因为人们会在你的虚构家庭中找到自己家庭的影子。换句话说，你的文字终会找到它的读者或受众。

2. Insights you could never discover on your own will leap off those pages. As what you learn melds with what you know, creative choices flood the mind, one-of-a-kind choices that help you win the war on clichés.

2. 你永远无法独自发现的洞见将跃然纸上。随着你所学知识与已有知识的融合，创造性的选择将涌入你的脑海，这些独一无二的选择将帮助你战胜陈规陋习。

#↩

4. Grounded Research

4. 扎根研究

Your father-son showdown needs a setting. You may imagine them as equestrians, bickering as they practice for a dressage competition; or under their horse trailer, arguing as they fix a broken hitch; or on the highway home, yelling about who’s to blame when the trailer comes loose. Three promising scenes, but you’ve never witnessed any of them.

父子俩的冲突需要一个场景。你可以想象他们是马术运动员，在练习盛装舞步比赛时争吵不休；或者在马车拖车底下，一边修理坏掉的挂钩一边争论不休；又或者在回家的高速公路上，拖车松动时，两人大声争论到底是谁的责任。这三个场景都很有意思，但你却从未亲眼见过。

Now, like a documentary filmmaker, locate these scenes in the real world so you can watch what happens, talk to people who live these events, and take notes until you master your subject. Never finish writing anything until you feel that you have gone deeper into your subject than anyone who has written about such things before, that you have become an absolute authority on your characters and their settings.

现在，就像纪录片导演一样，把这些场景放到现实世界中，观察事件的发生，与亲历者交谈，并做好笔记，直到你完全掌握你的主题。在你感觉自己对主题的理解比以往任何写过类似题材的人都更深入，在你感觉自己对笔下的人物及其所处环境了如指掌之前，永远不要结束你的写作。

#↩

AN AUTHOR’S VISION OF HUMAN NATURE

作者对人性的看法

Original characters grow out of an original perception of humanity, and so every fine writer develops her personal theory of what makes people do the things they do in the ways they do them. There is no recipe for this; artists are not necessarily orderly or disciplined. So every writer must piece her concepts into a singular vision her own way.

独特的人物形象源于对人性的独特洞察，因此，每一位优秀的作家都会发展出自己关于人们行为方式及其行为动机的理论。这没有固定的模式；艺术家未必都是循规蹈矩或严谨自律的。所以，每位作家都必须以自己的方式，将各种概念拼凑成独一无二的艺术视野。

Your personal theory will then flow into your characters, influencing their sense of meaning and purpose, what they ought to do, what they must never do, what they ought to strive for or against, what they may hope to build or destroy, what vision of love and the relationships they work toward, what social changes they want to make, what choices and actions they want to take.

然后，你的个人理论将融入你的角色之中，影响他们的意义感和目标感，他们应该做什么，他们绝对不能做什么，他们应该追求什么或反对什么，他们可能希望建立什么或摧毁什么，他们对爱情和关系的愿景是什么，他们想要做出哪些社会变革，以及他们想要采取哪些选择和行动。

How your theory takes shape will depend on how you see mankind. Do you believe in a primal human nature shared by all or a plasticity that’s molded by parental, economic, and cultural forces? Does human nature stay the same from person to person, or differ from men to women? Culture to culture? Class to class? Self to others?

你的理论如何形成取决于你如何看待人性。你相信所有人都拥有共同的原始人性，还是相信人性具有可塑性，并受到父母、经济和文化力量的影响？人性是始终如一的，还是因人而异？因文化而异？因阶级而异？因自我而异？

To help you test your personal theories against some of history’s more prominent beliefs, the following section is divided into two opposite points of view on one grand question, “Why do human beings do the things they do?”

为了帮助你将你的个人理论与历史上一些更著名的观点进行比较，以下部分将围绕一个重大问题“为什么人类会做他们所做的事情”展开，分为两个对立的观点。

This duality argues the nature-versus-nurture debate: What matters most? The genes and capacities a person was born with—her intrinsic nature? Or the way she was raised and acculturated—her extrinsic nurturing? In other words, who gets credit for humanity’s successes? And who takes the blame for its relentless failures?

这种二元性引发了先天与后天之争：什么最重要？是与生俱来的基因和能力——她的内在天性？还是她后天的养育和文化熏陶——她的外在培养？换句话说，人类的成功应该归功于谁？而人类屡屡失败的责任又应该由谁承担？

#↩

THE TWO GRAND THEORIES

两大理论

When humankind began to think in depth about itself, it developed beliefs to make sense of chaos. These master creeds tend to split into two contradictory points of view on why human beings do the things they do. They take either the inside-out subjective, intrinsic view of the self, or the outside-in objective, extrinsic angle of society. In other words, nature versus nurture.

当人类开始深入思考自身时，便发展出各种信仰来理解纷繁复杂的世界。这些核心信条往往演变为两种截然相反的观点，分别解释人类行为的成因。一种观点从内在出发，强调主观和内在的自我认知；另一种观点则从外在出发，强调客观和外在的社会因素。换句话说，就是先天与后天之争。

#↩

Indian

印度

Let’s start with two beliefs from India:

让我们先从印度的两种信仰说起：

Intrinsic

固有的

Buddhism teaches that no unchanging soul or permanent identity exists within a human being. Rather, when we hear our thoughts, what we mistake for the “me” who thinks them, for a conscious self, is in fact a mirage, a nonself. In short, reality exists but the self is an illusion.

佛教教导我们，人体内并不存在一成不变的灵魂或永恒的身份。相反，当我们听到自己的想法时，我们误以为是思考这些想法的“我”，误以为是意识自我，而实际上那只是海市蜃楼，是无我。简而言之，现实存在，但自我只是一种幻觉。

Extrinsic

外在

Hinduism proposes the opposite belief: The self exists but reality is an illusion. The ground for what is is unknown and unknowable. Maya, the power of illusion, gives form to formlessness but conceals and distorts the source. The world we experience with our senses exists but as a pale imitation of the ultimate reality that hides behind Maya’s illusions. This realm is unexplainable because language itself is a by-product of Maya.

印度教则持相反的观点：自我存在，但现实是一种幻象。万物存在的根源未知且不可知。幻象之力“摩耶”（Maya）赋予无形以形，却掩盖并扭曲了其源头。我们感官所体验的世界确实存在，但它只是隐藏在“摩耶”幻象背后的终极现实的苍白模仿。这个领域无法解释，因为语言本身就是“摩耶”的产物。

#↩

Greek

希腊语

Greek philosophy, developing at about the same time, contradicted both of these beliefs:

与此大致同时期发展的希腊哲学，与这两种观点都相悖：

Intrinsic

固有的

Socrates, in contradiction to Buddhism, argued that the self, far from being an illusion, sits at the center of existence. “The unexamined life is not worth living,” he taught, therefore, “know thyself.” How can we hope for wisdom of the world that surrounds us until we come to terms with the world inside us? How can we understand other human beings until we perceive the humanity within ourselves?

与佛教相反，苏格拉底认为自我远非幻象，而是存在的中心。他教导说：“未经审视的人生不值得过，所以要认识你自己。”如果我们不先了解自己的内心世界，又怎能指望从周遭世界获得智慧？如果我们不先觉察到自身的人性，又怎能理解他人？

Extrinsic

外在

Aristotle, in contradiction to Hinduism, believed that the world is both real and knowable. At heart, we are political animals and our natural home is society. Fulfillment consists in the active, public exercise of our finest faculties aimed at the betterment of others. The well-lived life displays virtue, excellence, and distinctively rational thought in a like-minded community, extended over a lifetime.

与印度教相反，亚里士多德认为世界既是真实的，又是可知的。从本质上讲，我们是政治动物，我们天然的家园是社会。人生的意义在于积极地、公开地运用我们最优秀的才能，以造福他人。美好的人生体现在与志同道合的社群中，展现美德、卓越和独特的理性思维，并持续一生。

#↩

Chinese

中国人

Chinese philosophy parallels both the Greek and the Indian:

中国哲学与希腊和印度哲学都有相似之处：

Intrinsic

固有的

Taoism, like Socrates and Buddha, looked out on reality from within the self. This philosophy emphasizes living in harmony with the substance and patterns of the natural, rather than social, world. Taoism does not call for elaborate public rituals, but rather simplicity, spontaneity, compassion, and humility—behavior in accordance with the inner spirit of nature. Taoism teaches that mastering others requires force, while mastering the self requires strength; knowing others is wisdom, while knowing yourself is enlightenment.

道家如同苏格拉底和佛陀一样，从内在的自我视角审视现实。这种哲学强调与自然而非社会世界的本质和规律和谐共处。道家不提倡繁复的公共仪式，而是崇尚简朴、自发、慈悲和谦逊——一种符合自然内在精神的行为。道家认为，征服他人需要力量，而征服自我需要力量；了解他人是智慧，而了解自己是觉悟。

Extrinsic

外在

Confucius, like Aristotle and Hinduism, believed that well-being depends on a well-ordered society. Confucianism takes society’s point of view to emphasize public morality, family loyalty, ancestor veneration, and a strict hierarchy in which elders are respected by their children, husbands by their wives, and in all cases, justice prevails.

孔子与亚里士多德和印度教一样，认为幸福取决于秩序井然的社会。儒家思想从社会角度出发，强调公共道德、家庭忠诚、祭祀祖先以及严格的等级制度，在这种制度下，长辈受子女尊敬，丈夫受妻子尊敬，并且在所有情况下，正义都能得到伸张。

#↩

Nineteenth Century

十九世纪

Two thousand, five hundred years later, philosophy remained split along the same divide:

两千五百年后，哲学界的分歧依然存在：

Extrinsic

外在

Karl Marx, like Aristotle, believed that social forces determine consciousness. Like Buddha, Marx felt that a fixed self does not exist: “All of history is a continuous transformation of human nature.”

卡尔·马克思和亚里士多德一样，认为社会力量决定了意识。马克思也像佛陀一样，认为不存在一个固定不变的自我：“整个历史就是人性的不断变化。”

Intrinsic

固有的

Sigmund Freud reversed Marx. In his theory, the subconscious mind commanded the center of the universe; social structures beyond the family are irrelevant. His model of inner life comprised three components: id (the source of life’s energy or libido), ego (the self or sense of identity), and superego (the conscience). Psychoanalysts since Freud have argued about which, if any, of these three components is the true self.

西格蒙德·弗洛伊德颠覆了马克思的观点。在他的理论中，潜意识是宇宙的中心；家庭之外的社会结构无关紧要。他构建的内心世界模型包含三个组成部分：本我（生命能量或力比多的来源）、自我（自我意识或身份认同感）和超我（良知）。自弗洛伊德以来，精神分析学家们一直在争论，这三个组成部分中究竟哪一个（如果有的话）才是真正的自我。

#↩

Twentieth Century

二十世纪

Extrinsic

外在

In the mid-twentieth century, anthropologist Joseph Campbell invented his radical theory of myth. He took Carl Jung’s belief in subconscious primordial archetypes and cast them as roles in an all-purpose story. Campbell claimed that his monomyth had been passed through the ages from culture to culture, when in fact it was more invention than legend. 3 Belief in this monomyth led many writers to reduce action characters to dimensionless clichés.

二十世纪中期，人类学家约瑟夫·坎贝尔提出了他激进的神话理论。他借鉴了卡尔·荣格关于潜意识原始原型的信念，并将它们塑造成一个万能故事中的角色。坎贝尔声称他的单一神话体系已在各个文化中代代相传，但事实上，它与其说是传说，不如说是虚构的。对这种单一神话的信仰导致许多作家将动作人物简化为缺乏立体感的陈词滥调。

Intrinsic

固有的

Psychologist William James viewed inner life as an ongoing contradiction: At times the private self seems like a solid inner awareness, but then daydreams and confusions liquefy consciousness into ever-changing streams of images and impressions. James wondered, “How can it be that each of us has both a sense of an ongoing singular identity, plus a sense of the very different selves we used to be?” How can we be the one person we know and all the former selves that litter our memories? These Jamesian paradoxes help inspire the authorship of complex characters.

心理学家威廉·詹姆斯认为内心世界是一个持续不断的矛盾体：有时，私人的自我似乎是一种坚实的内在意识，但随后白日梦和迷茫又会将意识液化成不断变化的图像和印象之流。詹姆斯不禁思考：“我们每个人怎么可能既拥有持续存在的独特身份感，又拥有曾经截然不同的自我意识呢？”我们怎么可能既是我们所认识的那个人，又是散落在记忆中的那些曾经的自我呢？这些詹姆斯式的悖论激发了作家们创作复杂人物的灵感。

#↩

Twenty-First Century

二十一世纪

In the most recent decades, the polarized dialogue on human nature took this form:

近几十年来，关于人性的两极分化对话呈现出以下形式：

Extrinsic

外在

Critical Theory, aka postmodernism, is a nurture-based system that sees the mind as a socially conditioned organ. Therefore, the use of one culture’s subjective beliefs to judge another culture’s behaviors and values is bigoted. This conviction went so far as to reject the scientific method itself—evidence gathering, experimentation, rational deduction—as biased and culturally skewed.

批判理论，又称后现代主义，是一种基于后天教养的体系，它将人的心智视为受社会制约的器官。因此，用一种文化的主观信念去评判另一种文化的行为和价值观是带有偏见的。这种信念甚至到了否定科学方法本身——包括证据收集、实验和理性演绎——认为它们都带有偏见和文化扭曲的地步。

Intrinsic

固有的

Cognitive Science, the counterpoint to Critical Theory, grew out of linguistics, IT, and computer research. In this nature-based theory, the mind is a biological computer designed by evolution. CS believes that once we decipher the brain’s codes and networks, the ultimate causes of human behavior will, thanks to science, be completely understood.

认知科学与批判理论相对立，它起源于语言学、信息技术和计算机研究。这种基于自然的理论认为，心智是一台由进化设计的生物计算机。认知科学相信，一旦我们破译了大脑的编码和网络，人类行为的根本原因，借助科学的力量，终将得到彻底的理解。

My sense of this intrinsic/extrinsic debate is that life always stirs some of both, but the quality and quantity of influence between genes and culture varies widely. More importantly, however, none of history’s belief systems contemplates the impact of coincidence.

我对这种内在/外在之争的理解是，生活总是会受到两者的影响，但基因和文化之间影响的质量和程度差异很大。然而，更重要的是，历史上没有任何一种信仰体系考虑到了巧合的影响。

Consider the research done on identical twins: Two people born genetically the same will in time take on distinctively different personalities. Whether they are raised together in the same family or apart in different families, they keep certain similarities but do not remain identical. From twin to twin, therefore, neither nature nor nurture makes the key difference. What does? Randomness.

以同卵双胞胎为例：两个基因相同的人，随着时间的推移，会发展出截然不同的性格。无论他们是在同一个家庭一起长大，还是在不同的家庭中分开长大，他们都会保留某些相似之处，但不会完全相同。因此，对于双胞胎而言，先天因素和后天因素都不是决定性因素。那么，究竟是什么因素在起作用呢？是随机性。

Beginning with the accident of birth, haphazard collisions of worldly forces become a way of life for every human being: A child’s genes interplay with the often impulsive behaviors of parents and siblings; a culture not of her choosing bends and shapes her; she is at the mercy of her teacher-by-teacher education; the same is true of her religious life service by service; games won and lost; her personal one-of-a-kind encounters with corporate politics, sending her career up and down the pyramid of power; and finally the physical environment up to and including the weather. Sun-browned kids left to run wild under blue skies are not the same as sun-starved kids raised in a rainy clime, watching nature programs on TV.

从出生的偶然开始，世俗力量的偶然碰撞便成为每个人生活的一部分：孩子的基因与父母和兄弟姐妹常常冲动的行为相互作用；她所处的文化环境并非她所选择，却影响着她；她受制于一位又一位老师的教育；她的宗教生活也同样如此，一次又一次的宗教服务；她经历的每一次比赛的胜负；她与职场政治的独特交锋，让她在权力金字塔中起起落落；最后，还有包括天气在内的自然环境。在蓝天下自由奔跑、晒得黝黑的孩子，与在阴雨气候中长大、只能观看电视自然节目、缺乏阳光的孩子，截然不同。

Which direction her life takes—up, down, or neither—turns on luck as much as any other factor. Once chance has done its thing, the character reacts. In reaction to coincidence, the forces of nature and nurture finally come into play.

她的人生走向何方——上升、下降还是平淡无奇——很大程度上取决于运气，而非其他因素。一旦命运的安排奏效，人物便会做出反应。面对巧合，先天因素和后天因素最终都会发挥作用。

#↩

THREE KEYS TO AUTHORSHIP

写作的三大关键要素

Take from this survey of beliefs what you will or reject them all. It matters not so long as your insights into humanity go deeper than common experience and routine schooling. To develop your personal theory, focus on a trio of faculties within yourself: Moral Imagination, Logical Implication, and Self-Knowledge. The final, fundamental preparation for writing is to focus your unique talents on these three conundrums. Solving them will give you a broader, more reflective understanding of why your characters do the things they do.

你可以从这份信仰调查中汲取你想要的，也可以全盘否定。这都无关紧要，只要你对人性的洞察能够超越寻常经验和常规教育的局限即可。为了构建你的个人理论，你需要专注于自身三种能力：道德想象力、逻辑推理和自我认知。写作的最终也是最根本的准备，就是将你的独特才能集中于这三个难题。解决它们将使你对笔下人物行为背后的原因有更广阔、更深刻的理解。

#↩

1. Moral Imagination

1. 道德想象力

Moral Imagination means a sensitivity to life’s values, an ability to recognize shifting charges (positive versus negative), shifting levels (conscious versus subconscious), shifting intensities (subtle versus overt)—the changing qualities that compel and propel people as they decide and act (or vacillate and procrastinate) in their efforts to confront (or evade) conflict.

道德想象力意味着对生活价值观的敏感性，能够识别不断变化的情绪（正面与负面）、不断变化的层次（有意识与潜意识）、不断变化的强度（微妙与公开）——这些不断变化的特质促使人们在面对（或逃避）冲突时做出决定和行动（或犹豫和拖延）。

To create a complex character, a writer’s moral imagination peers into a character’s inner realms to identify and measure the values at play in her personal and private lives—Maturity versus Immaturity, Honesty versus Dishonesty, Generosity versus Selfishness, Kindness versus Cruelty—all the dynamic charges of human nature.

为了塑造一个复杂的人物，作家的道德想象力会深入人物的内心世界，去识别和衡量其个人和私人生活中所体现的价值观——成熟与不成熟、诚实与不诚实、慷慨与自私、善良与残忍——所有这些都是人性的动态特征。

To create a complex setting, a writer clashes the positive and negative charges of its social and physical environment—what’s good versus what’s evil, vital versus trivial, just versus unjust, meaningful versus meaningless, and so on down life’s multitudinous values.

为了创造一个复杂的环境，作家会将社会和自然环境中的正面和负面因素进行碰撞——什么是善与恶，什么是重要与琐碎，什么是公正与不公正，什么是有意义与无意义，等等，涵盖了生活中众多的价值观。

Without conflicting values, a story’s social setting amounts to little more than a board game; without an author’s moral imagination to align trait against trait, a role adds less than a Monopoly token. So, whether a writer starts with a setting and draws characters out of it or starts with characters and wraps a setting around them, she must ultimately charge both with her perception of life’s values. 4

如果没有价值观的冲突，故事的社会背景就如同棋盘游戏一般；如果没有作者的道德想象力将人物性格进行对比，角色就如同大富翁游戏中的一个棋子一样毫无意义。因此，无论作者是先设定背景再塑造人物，还是先塑造人物再围绕他们构建背景，最终都必须将她对人生价值观的理解融入到人物和背景之中。

#↩

2. Logical Implication

2. 逻辑蕴含

A storyteller must be blessed with the kind of mind that given a fingertip takes an arm, given an arm takes an army. In the same way that a composer hears a chord and creates a melody, a painter sees a swath and fills a canvas with wonder, a writer takes a hint and imagines a human.

讲故事的人必须拥有那种天赋异禀的头脑，仿佛指尖轻触就能化作手臂，手臂轻触就能化作军队。正如作曲家听到一个和弦就能谱写旋律，画家看到一片景象就能在画布上描绘出奇妙的画面，作家也能从灵感中捕捉到人物形象。

You will never meet everyone you would need to know to fill multiple casts over a lifetime of storytelling. So instead, develop your power of deductive and inductive implication: Learn to work forward from piece into whole—see a child and imagine her tribe; work back from a whole to a piece—dream of a teeming city and find a lost soul.

你一生中永远不可能遇到所有你需要认识的人，从而创作出无数精彩的故事。所以，你应该培养演绎和归纳推理的能力：学会从碎片推导出整体——想象一个孩子，然后想象她的部落；从整体反推碎片——想象一座熙熙攘攘的城市，然后找到一个迷失的灵魂。

#↩

3. Self-Knowledge

3. 自我认知

All writing is autobiographical. Every nugget of improvisation from within yourself and every trigger of inspiration from outside yourself finds its way to the page through you, filtered through your mind, your imagination, your feelings. This does not mean your characters are alter egos, but rather that self-knowledge is the taproot of character creation.

所有的写作都是自传性的。你内心每一个即兴的灵感火花，以及来自外界的每一个启发，最终都会通过你，经由你的思想、想象和情感，最终呈现在纸上。这并不意味着你笔下的人物是你的另一个自我，而是说自我认知是人物塑造的根基。

You are the only human being you will ever know in depth and breadth. Yours is the only subjectivity you will ever view objectively. Yours is the only inner voice you will ever converse with self to self. You live in the prison cell of your own mind, and so no matter how long your intimate, personal relationship with another person may last, you will never really know what goes on in her inner world. You can guess at it but never know it.

你唯一能真正深入了解的人，只有你自己。你唯一能客观审视的，只有你自己的主观感受。你唯一能与自己对话的，只有你自己的内心声音。你生活在自己思想的牢笼里，所以无论你与他人的亲密关系持续多久，你永远无法真正了解她内心的世界。你可以猜测，但永远无法知晓。

The only self you ever know is yours, and even then there are limits. Because self-deception distorts self-awareness, you never know who you are as well as you think you do. Self-knowledge is imperfect and in many ways fallacious. Nonetheless, it’s all you have.

你唯一真正了解的自我只有你自己，即便如此，它也存在局限。因为自欺会扭曲自我认知，你永远无法像你自认为的那样了解自己。自我认知并不完美，在很多方面甚至存在谬误。然而，这却是你所拥有的一切。

So, if you know yourself only in part and other people even less, how can you create original, complex characters? By asking this question, “If I were this character in these circumstances, what would I think, feel, do?” Then listen for the honest answer because it’s always correct. You would do the human thing. The more you penetrate the mysteries of your own humanity, the more you’re able to understand the humanity of others.

所以，如果你对自己的了解仅限于皮毛，对他人更是知之甚少，又该如何塑造出鲜活而复杂的人物形象呢？你可以问问自己：“如果我是这个人物，身处这样的境地，我会怎么想，怎么感受，怎么做？” 然后倾听内心最真实的答案，因为它永远是正确的。你会做出人之常情。你越深入探索自身人性的奥秘，就越能理解他人的人性。

Despite clear differences between people—differences of age, gender, race, language, culture—we are all far more alike than we are different. We are human beings having the same fundamental human experiences. Therefore, if you are thinking and feeling it inside yourself, you can be certain that every person coming down the street toward you, each in her own way, is thinking and feeling it, too.

尽管人与人之间存在着明显的差异——年龄、性别、种族、语言、文化——但我们之间的相似之处远多于差异。我们都是人类，拥有着相同的基本人类体验。因此，如果你内心有这样的想法和感受，那么你可以确信，街上迎面走来的每个人，尽管方式不同，也都在有这样的想法和感受。

When we realize that the key to character creation is self-knowledge, and then watch the parades of characters, numbering into the hundreds, who have marched out of the minds of the world’s greatest writers—William Shakespeare, Leo Tolstoy, Tennessee Williams, Toni Morrison, William Wyler, Vince Gilligan, Ingmar Bergman, and many, many others—characters that are so individual, so fascinating, so memorable, and all the product of one imagination, it dazzles.

当我们意识到塑造人物的关键在于自我认知，然后观看数以百计从世界最伟大作家——威廉·莎士比亚、列夫·托尔斯泰、田纳西·威廉姆斯、托妮·莫里森、威廉·惠勒、文斯·吉利根、英格玛·伯格曼等等——的脑海中走出来的人物队伍时，这些人物如此独特、如此迷人、如此令人难忘，而且都是同一个想象力的产物，这真是令人叹为观止。

#↩

PART 2

第二部分

#↩

BUILDING A CHARACTER

塑造人物性格

My characters are conglomerations of past and present stages of civilization, bits from books and newspapers, scraps of humanity, rags and tatters of fine clothing, patched together as is the human soul.
我笔下的人物是过去和现在文明阶段的集合体，是书籍和报纸上的片段，是人性的碎片，是精美衣物的破烂碎片，就像人类的灵魂一样，被拼凑在一起。
—August Strindberg 1
—奥古斯特·斯特林堡 1

What’s the best angle on character creation? Outside in or inside out? Should a writer first create a setting and then populate it with a cast? Or begin by imagining a cast and then building a world around them?

角色塑造的最佳角度是什么？由外而内还是由内而外？作家应该先创造一个背景，然后再填充角色吗？还是应该先构思角色，然后再围绕他们构建一个世界？

In either case, once a particular character comes into focus, the same questions apply: Should the writer invent surface traits and backtrack to the character’s inner core? Or start at the core and work out to his traits? The next two chapters examine these contrasting techniques.

无论哪种情况，一旦某个角色逐渐清晰，都会面临同样的问题：作者应该先塑造角色的表面特征，然后再回溯到角色的内心世界？还是应该从角色的内心世界入手，逐步展现其性格特征？接下来的两章将探讨这两种截然不同的写作技巧。

#↩

4

CHARACTER INSPIRATION: OUTSIDE IN

角色灵感：由外而内

Inspiration rarely blazes into a finished, fully cast story. An artist’s instincts usually spark just a sliver of intuition or a hint of mystery. These intriguing fragments send chain reactions of free association spiraling through the imagination. At first, what seems like a breakthrough usually dead-ends in a cul-de-sac of clichés, but in time precious insights trace a winding trail to success.

灵感很少会直接迸发出完整的故事。艺术家的直觉通常只会激发一丝灵感或一丝神秘感。这些引人入胜的片段会引发一系列自由联想，在想象中螺旋式上升。起初，看似突破性的发现往往最终会陷入陈词滥调的死胡同，但随着时间的推移，宝贵的洞见会指引一条通往成功的曲折道路。

Inspiration can erupt from any of the many realms that surround an author, so picture the storyteller’s universe as five concentric spheres nested one inside the other:

灵感可以来自作者周围的任何领域，所以不妨把故事讲述者的世界想象成五个同心球，一个套着一个：

1. The outermost shell comprises actuality—time and place, people and things, past and present.
1. 最外层的外壳包含现实——时间和地点、人和事物、过去和现在。
2. Inside the actual world rotates the fictional media of page, stage, and screen.
2. 在现实世界中，虚构的媒体——书页、舞台和银幕——轮转不息。
3. Within that sphere orbit the storytelling genres with their various conventions.
3. 在这个领域内，围绕着各种故事类型及其不同的惯例展开。
4. Each story houses a backstory reaching back to the characters’ births, turning points that happen during the telling, and themes that unite all these events.
4. 每个故事都包含一个追溯到角色出生的背景故事、讲述过程中发生的转折点，以及将所有这些事件联系起来的主题。
5. At the epicenter stands the author’s creative self, looking out, in search of inspiration.
5. 在中心，站着作者的创作自我，向外眺望，寻找灵感。

Let’s begin on the outside and work our way in to the writer.

让我们从外在开始，逐步深入了解作者。

#↩

REALITY AS INSPIRATION

现实即灵感

An impulse for character creation often sparks when the density of reality (objects, images, words, sounds, odors, flavors, textures) collides with a boundless imagination. Any random sensation or experience could trigger a cascade of freewheeling impressions that ultimately matures into a complex character. For the storyteller, however, the most frequent inspiration comes from other people.

当现实的丰富内涵（物体、图像、文字、声音、气味、味道、质感）与无限的想象力碰撞时，往往会迸发出创作的灵感。任何随机的感觉或经历都可能引发一系列自由奔放的印象，最终孕育出一个复杂的人物形象。然而，对于讲故事的人来说，最常见的灵感来源往往是他人。

People are to writers what sounds are to musicians. When an author improvises a character, human nature supplies the notes that the writer composes into a symphony of behaviors. As a result, fictional characters and real people divide into two very different genera of humanity.

人之于作家，犹如声音之于音乐家。当作者即兴创作一个人物时，人性便如同音符，为作者谱写出一曲行为交响曲。因此，虚构人物与真实人物被划分为截然不同的两类人。

A real person is enigmatic and incomplete—a life yet to be lived; a character is an artwork—a complete and expressive version of its original inspiration. People exist, yet characters often seem more intensely real. When people sail directly at us, we alter course to avoid collisions. Characters just glide on by, busily unaware that we watch their every turn. People confront us; we affect them. Characters intrigue us; we absorb them.

真实的人是神秘而不完整的——他们的人生尚未展开；而角色则是一件艺术品——是其最初灵感的完整而富有表现力的体现。人是存在的，但角色往往显得更加真实。当人们迎面而来时，我们会改变航向以避免碰撞。而角色则轻松自如地从我们身边掠过，浑然不觉我们正注视着他们的一举一动。人会与我们正面交锋，我们会影响他们。角色则吸引着我们，我们沉浸其中。

Early-twentieth-century authors such as Henry James and Luigi Pirandello felt that although characters could be known in godlike ways (as their novels and plays demonstrated), they had little confidence in objective observations of real people. Since they could witness only gestures and traits, they doubted they could ever know people in depth. They felt that the diagnosis of hidden motives is, at best, a guess—an educated guess, perhaps, but subject to error and prejudice.

二十世纪初的作家，如亨利·詹姆斯和路易吉·皮兰德娄，认为尽管人物形象可以被像神明般了解（正如他们的小说和戏剧所展现的那样），但他们对客观观察真实人物的能力却缺乏信心。由于他们只能观察到人物的姿态和特征，因此他们怀疑自己是否能够真正深入了解一个人。他们认为，对隐藏动机的诊断充其量只是一种猜测——或许是一种有根据的猜测，但难免会受到错误和偏见的影响。

And they were right. If you’re writing a memoir, for example, your cast will naturally include people you know, but an acquaintance turned into a character can be as superficial as a snapshot. When you draw directly from life, look beneath the surface, uncover silent truths, surprise us with your insights. Do not copy. Rather, reimagine real people into intriguing characters we can believe in.

他们说得没错。比如，如果你在写回忆录，你的角色自然会包括你认识的人，但把一个熟人变成一个角色，可能就像一张快照一样肤浅。当你直接从生活中汲取灵感，深入挖掘，揭示那些不为人知的真相，用你的洞察力给我们带来惊喜时，不要照搬。相反，要将真实的人物重新塑造成引人入胜、令人信服的角色。

In other words, finding inspiration in a real person does not guarantee credibility. If a writer doesn’t trust or believe in someone, he doesn’t feel compelled to write him. But if, trait after trait, credibility grows in his mind, deepening his belief, then the work begins. Often, one unique facet suddenly implies an entire humanity, and this “telling detail” lifts an interesting inspiration out of the what is and into the what could be.

换句话说，从真人身上汲取灵感并不能保证作品的可信度。如果一位作家不信任或不相信某人，他就不会觉得有必要去写他。但如果随着他发现对方的种种特质，这种可信度在他心中逐渐增强，他的信念也日益坚定，那么创作便由此开始。通常，一个独特的侧面会突然展现出完整的人性，而这个“关键细节”能将有趣的灵感从“现实”提升到“未来”。

Writers with limited knowledge of their character’s setting, society, and traits generalize and thus shrivel their belief and with that, their power to invent. Writers with a global purchase on reality generate unique characters in one-of-a-kind settings that instantly involve readers and audiences.

对笔下人物所处环境、社会背景和性格特征了解有限的作家，往往会进行概括，从而削弱其创作的可信度，进而扼杀其想象力。而对现实世界有着深刻理解的作家，则能创造出独具特色的人物和独一无二的背景，瞬间吸引读者和观众。

#↩

MEDIUM AS INSPIRATION

媒介即灵感

Choice of medium, the second source of inspiration, not only influences the shape of an author’s stories but the traits and behaviors of the characters who live in them. To please the camera, for example, screen characters tend to act more visually than verbally. Screenwriters, therefore, tend to create characters who can express themselves with looks and gestures. To please theatre audiences, stage characters act more verbally than visually. Playwrights, therefore, tend to endow their characters with expressive dialogue.

媒介的选择是第二个灵感来源，它不仅影响作者故事的形态，也影响故事中人物的性格特征和行为。例如，为了迎合镜头，银幕人物往往更注重视觉表达而非语言表达。因此，编剧倾向于塑造能够通过眼神和肢体语言来表达自我的角色。为了取悦戏剧观众，舞台人物则更注重语言表达而非视觉呈现。因此，剧作家倾向于赋予角色富有表现力的台词。

Stage and screen characters perform in the present tense, aiming verbal and visual actions at their future desires. Prose voices usually narrate in the past tense, recalling events, retrospectively interpreting what happened in detail. Prose writers, therefore, often give their first-person narrators keen memories, discerning eyes, and sensitivity to subtext.

舞台和银幕上的角色以现在时态表演，通过言语和视觉动作来表达他们对未来的渴望。而散文叙述者通常以过去时态回忆事件，回顾性地解读已发生的细节。因此，散文作家往往会赋予第一人称叙述者敏锐的记忆力、洞察力和对言外之意的理解力。

Beyond characterizing roles, choice of medium also impacts a writer’s personal sense of identity. Who am I? A playwright? Showrunner? Screenwriter? Novelist? Each of these titles has a noble tradition, but I urge writers to move freely back and forth from page to stage to screen. Shrinking your writerly identity to a single medium limits your creative range.

除了塑造角色之外，媒介的选择也会影响作家的个人身份认同。我是谁？剧作家？剧集制作人？电影编剧？小说家？这些头衔都拥有崇高的传统，但我鼓励作家们在文字、舞台和银幕之间自由切换。将你的写作身份局限于单一媒介会限制你的创作空间。

If, for example, no one offers to produce your screenplay, why not rework it in another medium? Stage it as a play or publish it as a novel. Put your characters in public and watch how readers and audiences react. The insights you gain can never be glimpsed alone at your desk. Air your stories, field responses, and watch your skills grow. Flex your talents and give yourself an all-media title: writer.

例如，如果你的剧本无人问津，何不尝试用其他媒介进行改编？把它改编成舞台剧或小说出版。让你的角色出现在公众视野中，观察读者和观众的反应。这些感悟是你独自伏案写作时永远无法获得的。让你的故事广为传播，收集反馈，见证你的技能不断提升。充分发挥你的才能，给自己一个全能媒体的头衔：作家。

To take your identity a level deeper, ask: “Am I in love with the art in myself or myself in the art?” 1 Do you write because the life inside you demands expression? Or because you dream of living an artist’s life? Many novices nurture crushes on Hollywood or Broadway or the writer-infested countryside of Connecticut. After a few rejections, their dream implodes and they quit. So make certain that whichever medium inspires you harmonizes with more than a lifestyle.

为了更深入地了解你的身份，不妨问问自己：“我爱的是自己内在的艺术，还是艺术中的自我？”你写作是因为内心深处渴望表达吗？还是因为你梦想成为一名艺术家？许多新手都对好莱坞、百老汇，或是作家云集的康涅狄格乡村充满向往。几次被拒稿后，他们的梦想破灭，最终放弃。所以，务必确保你所选择的媒介，不仅仅与一种生活方式相契合。

#↩

GENRE AS INSPIRATION

类型作为灵感

Most writers, I suspect, find inspiration in reality far less than they think and in fiction far more than they know. A true first spark rarely flashes from something seen on a street corner or glimpsed online. More often than not, it’s a phrase of dialogue or beautifully turned image found in a novel, play, film, or series written in the genre they love.

我怀疑，大多数作家从现实生活中汲取的灵感远比他们想象的要少，而从虚构作品中汲取的灵感则远比他们意识到的要多。真正的灵感火花很少来自街角所见或网络上的匆匆一瞥。更多时候，它来自他们所钟爱的小说、戏剧、电影或剧集中的一句对话或一幅精美的画面。

The major media contain numerous genres (see Chapter 14 ), each with various subgenres, all of which can be combined or merged into an endless variety of story designs. So when in search of a new, original subject, pay attention to your own story-going habits. What screen series do you binge on? What films and plays do you run to see? Which novels do you read? What genre do you love? Let your passions inspire your early inspirations for character.

主流媒体包含众多类型（见第十四章），每种类型又包含各种子类型，所有这些类型都可以组合或融合，创造出无穷无尽的故事情节。因此，在寻找新颖原创题材时，不妨留意一下自己的阅读习惯。你追哪些剧？你经常去看哪些电影和戏剧？你读哪些小说？你最喜欢哪种类型？让你的热情激发你最初的人物灵感。

#↩

EVENTS AS INSPIRATION

以事件为灵感

Konstantin Stanislavsky, the Russian stage director, taught his actors a technique to unlock their talents that he called the “Magic If”—the shift to a hypothetical way of thinking that opens the imagination. To create a true-to-character moment, the actor asks the open-ended question “If XXX happened, what would I do?” then imagines his reaction.

俄罗斯戏剧导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基教给演员们一种名为“神奇的假设”（Magic If）的技巧，以此激发他们的表演天赋——即通过假设性的思维方式来打开想象力。为了塑造一个符合角色性格的瞬间，演员会提出一个开放式的问题：“如果XXX发生了，我会怎么做？”然后想象自己的反应。

So, for example, if the cast were rehearsing a family argument scene, an actor might silently ask himself, “What would happen if at this moment I were to punch my brother? How might he react? How might I react to his reaction?” With these hypothetical questions, these ifs, his imagination leaps to an unexpected yet truthful behavior.

例如，如果剧组正在排练一场家庭争吵的戏，演员可能会默默地问自己：“如果此时我打了我的兄弟，会发生什么？他会作何反应？我又会如何回应他的反应？” 带着这些假设性的问题，这些“如果”，他的想象力会跃然纸上，展现出一种出人意料却又真实的行为。

Character creators do the same. As the Magic If floats through a writer’s imagination, he improvises an inciting incident that in turn triggers the events that follow: If a shark ate a vacationer, what kinds of characters would go after the shark? 2 If a woman discovered that throughout nearly five decades of marriage her husband was secretly in love with his first love, his long-deceased fiancée, what kind of wife would let that revelation destroy her happiness? 3

角色创造者也是如此。当“如果”这个奇妙的想法在作家的想象中浮现时，他会即兴创作一个引发事件，进而触发后续剧情：如果一条鲨鱼吃掉了一个度假者，什么样的角色会去追捕鲨鱼？如果一个女人发现，在近五十年的婚姻生活中，她的丈夫一直暗恋着他的初恋——他早已去世的未婚妻，什么样的妻子会让这个真相摧毁她的幸福？

The question “What would happen if…?” often inspires a story’s inciting incident; that in turn inspires the characters who react to it; that then determines whether the telling is plot-driven or character-driven. Stephen King says his novels always begin plot-driven. To launch a telling, he magic-ifs an inciting incident beyond his protagonist’s control. From that point on, however, he hopes his characters will take over and make decisions he didn’t see coming, so that by the last page, his tales feel character-driven. 4

“如果……会发生什么？”这个问题常常激发故事的开端；而开端又会激发人物的反应；最终决定故事是情节驱动还是人物驱动。斯蒂芬·金说他的小说总是以情节驱动开篇。为了展开叙述，他会“魔法般地”制造一个超出主人公掌控的开端事件。然而，从那时起，他希望笔下的人物能够掌控局面，做出他意想不到的决定，这样，到了最后一页，他的故事就会变成人物驱动的。

#↩

THEME AS INSPIRATION

主题即灵感

Writing is an exploration of life. Like a seafarer, an author sails into his story, never quite sure where he’s headed or what he will find when he gets there. In fact, if nothing on the horizon surprises him, he’s steering a timeworn passage and needs a new compass point.

写作是对人生的探索。如同航海家一般，作者驶入自己的故事，永远无法确定目的地，也无法预知最终会发现什么。事实上，如果前方的一切都毫无惊喜，那说明他正航行在一条陈旧的航道上，需要一个新的方向。

Eventually, as characters and events merge in climactic turning points, the writer discovers his story’s meaning. In other words, the story surprises the writer with this insight; the writer does not dictate meaning to the story. And what is that meaning?

最终，随着人物和事件在关键转折点交织融合，作者发现了故事的意义。换句话说，是故事本身赋予了作者这种洞见；作者并没有为故事设定意义。那么，这意义究竟是什么呢？

All well-told stories, from ancient myths to modern satires, express one essential idea: How and why life changes. This meaning arises out of deep causes that arc a story’s core value from negative to positive or positive to negative—for example, from hate to love or the reverse, or from freedom to slavery or the reverse, or from a meaningless life to a meaningful life or the reverse, and so on through the myriad values at stake in humanity’s countless tales. As a writer works in search of story, hidden causes from beneath the surface of society or within a character’s subconscious mind suddenly reveal themselves, delivering insights into character an author can discover only through improvisation.

所有精彩的故事，从古代神话到现代讽刺作品，都表达着一个核心理念：人生如何以及为何会改变。这种意义源于深层次的原因，这些原因推动着故事的核心价值从消极走向积极，或从积极走向消极——例如，从仇恨到爱，或从爱到自由，或从奴役，或从奴役，或从无意义的人生到有意义的人生，或从无意义的人生到有意义的人生，等等，人类无数故事中都蕴含着各种各样的价值。当作家在创作故事的过程中，隐藏在社会表象之下或人物潜意识深处的原因会突然显现，为作者提供只有通过即兴创作才能获得的深刻洞察。

However, when writers move in the opposite direction, when they start with a belief and then concoct a plot and cast to demonstrate it, spontaneity hardens and the unforeseen is never discovered. Belief-fixated writers, in their burning zeal to prove their point, reduce stories to illustrated lectures and characters to mouthpieces. This practice is as old as medieval morality plays that cast a universal human being or Everyman as protagonist and then surrounded him with players who acted out his encounters with ideas such as Virtue and Vice, Mercy and Mischief, Beauty and Knowledge, Birth and Death—all in an effort to educate the morally illiterate.

然而，当作家反其道而行之，先入为主地抱持某种信念，再精心构思情节、塑造人物来论证时，自发性便会丧失，意想不到的惊喜也将随之消失。这些执迷于信念的作家，为了证明自己的观点，往往将故事简化为图文并茂的说教，将人物沦为传声筒。这种做法可以追溯到中世纪的道德剧，它们塑造了一个普世的普通人或“人人皆可成为”的主角，然后让一群演员围绕着他，演绎他与诸如美德与罪恶、仁慈与邪恶、美与知识、生与死等主题的种种遭遇——所有这些都是为了教化那些道德沦丧的人们。

Today, the practice of working backward from idea to story is the unfortunate tendency of Social Drama. This genre takes its themes from the many maladies that infect society: poverty, sexism, racism, political corruption—injustices and sufferings in all their guises.

如今，从构思到故事的反向创作方式是社会剧的一种不幸倾向。这一剧种的主题取材于社会中存在的诸多弊病：贫困、性别歧视、种族歧视、政治腐败——各种形式的不公正和苦难。

A writer, for example, may come to believe that although drug dependency is a terrible social ill, it can be cured by love. So starting with the theme “Love cures addiction,” he first creates a last-act climax in which an act of love turns an addict from decades of enslavement to a lifetime of sobriety. Knowing his ending, he then strings turning points back to a pill-popping inciting incident, filling events in between with characters who enact his theory. The good people become very very good people; the bad people very very bad people; and all the dialogue argues on-the-nose explanations of the power of love to cure addiction. The plastic results change no one’s mind about love or addiction.

例如，一位作家可能认为，尽管毒瘾是一种可怕的社会弊病，但爱可以治愈它。于是，他以“爱能治愈毒瘾”为主题，首先精心设计了一个高潮，让一个瘾君子从数十年的毒瘾奴役中解脱出来，重获终身清醒。他早已洞悉结局，然后将一系列转折点串联起来，最终指向一个吸毒的诱发事件，并在其间穿插塑造人物，让他们践行自己的理论。好人变成了非常非常好的人；坏人变成了非常非常坏的人；所有的对话都在直白地论证爱能治愈毒瘾的力量。然而，这种矫揉造作的结局并没有改变任何人对爱或毒瘾的看法。

Meaning discovered while exploring character creation is always more insightful than belief used to mechanize a plot.

在探索角色创造的过程中发现的意义，总是比用机械化的信念来构建情节更有洞察力。

#↩

CHARACTER BIOGRAPHY AS INSPIRATION

人物传记作为灵感来源

Every character has a life history trailing back to the family that gave him birth. Does this past matter to the writer? Novelist Philip Roth thought yes. For him, the past was a cache of motivational catalysts and jeweled dimensions. That was why he devised five thousand or more biographical bits and pieces per protagonist.

每个角色都有一段可以追溯到其出生家庭的过往经历。这段过往对作家来说重要吗？小说家菲利普·罗斯认为重要。对他而言，过往经历蕴藏着丰富的创作灵感和珍贵的人生维度。正因如此，他为每个主人公精心构建了五千多个传记片段。

Playwright David Mamet thought not. For him, inventing childhoods, with or without the usual traumas, seemed a waste of time.

剧作家大卫·马梅特却不这么认为。在他看来，虚构童年经历，无论是否包含常见的创伤，都是浪费时间。

These conflicting views have as much to do with the author’s media choices as his work habits. Novels (with exceptions) speak in the past tense and project their characters’ lives over spans of time; the theatre (with exceptions) runs its scenes along the cutting edge of the now. In fact, to get biographical exposition onstage playwrights call on novelistic devices such as reminiscing monologues and flashbacks, as did Edward Albee in Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? and Three Tall Women .

这些相互矛盾的观点与作者的媒介选择及其创作习惯同样密切相关。小说（除少数例外）通常使用过去时，并将人物的生活跨越时间跨度；而戏剧（除少数例外）则将场景置于当下前沿。事实上，为了在舞台上呈现人物传记，剧作家会借鉴小说手法，例如回忆独白和倒叙，正如爱德华·阿尔比在《谁害怕弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫？》和《三个高个女人》中所运用的那样。

I side with Roth. Although few of his five thousand pieces of character biography found their way to the page, they gave him the foundational knowledge that set off fireworks of creative choices.

我赞同罗斯的观点。虽然他笔下五千多个人物的生平事迹最终只有寥寥几篇被搬上纸面，但这些素材为他奠定了坚实的基础，激发了他天马行空的创作灵感。

As you compile a character’s past, look for patterns rather than singularities. Redundant emotional experiences deposit residues. Repeated traumas cause PTSD; daily coddling produces egoists. Imprints left by recurring emotions affect motivations (what to seek/what to avoid), temperaments (calm/nervous), dispositions (optimistic/pessimistic), personalities (charming/irritating), and other such traits.

在构建人物过往经历时，要寻找模式而非个别事件。重复的情感体验会留下痕迹。反复的创伤会导致创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）；日常的溺爱会造就自私自利的人。反复出现的情绪所留下的印记会影响人物的动机（追求什么/避免什么）、气质（冷静/紧张）、性格（乐观/悲观）、人格（迷人/令人厌烦）以及其他类似的特质。

Movements in the subconscious inspire qualities of behavior, and qualities of behavior mirror subconscious movements. Once these patterns take root, they drive lifelong strivings. A character rarely abandons his childhood traits in the face of adult conflicts. Instead, he will often react to a person in the present as if he were someone from his past. Groundwork laid in biography, therefore, will determine the tactics a character uses in later life.

潜意识的活动会激发行为特质，而行为特质又会反映潜意识的活动。一旦这些模式扎根，便会驱动终生的追求。一个人很少会在面对成年冲突时放弃童年时期的特质。相反，他往往会以对待过去某个人的方式来对待现在的人。因此，过往经历奠定的基础将决定一个人在日后生活中所采取的策略。

As you build out a character’s years prior to the story’s inciting incident, focus on early adolescence. It’s in these preteen days that he first dreams about the future, testing and formulating possible meanings and purposes. If he’s lucky, he’ll have a positive experience—an inspirational teacher, a personal epiphany—that commits him to the goal he pursues for a lifetime. Or his first glimpse of a life purpose may turn sharply negative. He suffers confusion, doubt, fear, shame, sadness, anger, depression—any combination or all of these at once. In other words, he becomes a teenager.

在构建故事导火索事件发生前角色的成长经历时，重点关注其青春期早期。正是在这段青春期前的时光里，他开始憧憬未来，探索并构建各种可能的意义和目标。如果他足够幸运，他会经历一次积极的事情——遇到一位鼓舞人心的老师，或者获得一次顿悟——从而坚定地朝着毕生追求的目标前进。然而，他最初对人生目标的领悟也可能急转直下，变得消极。他会经历困惑、怀疑、恐惧、羞愧、悲伤、愤怒、抑郁——这些情绪可能以任何一种组合出现，也可能同时袭来。换句话说，他开始步入青少年时期。

He then spends who knows how many years in an identity crisis of minor or major magnitude, trying to figure out who he is, where he came from, where he’s going, and how he will fit in when he gets there. At some future point, for better or worse, a workable identity solidifies. He matures into a historian of his personal past and a prophet of his personal future, poised to enter your story.

随后，他陷入了一场或大或小的身份认同危机，不知持续了多少年，他试图弄清自己是谁，从何而来，要去往何方，以及到达目的地后该如何融入。在未来的某个时刻，无论好坏，一个可行的身份最终会形成。他成长为自己过往的记录者和未来的预言家，准备成为你故事的一部分。

While doing this research, the writer often comes to value the richness of the past over the void of the future. The remembered comes with textures and tensions, scents and shapes; the imagined offers possibilities without subtleties, blanks to be filled. From a character’s point of view, he can only hope that the future will repeat a pattern he’s coped with in the past.

在进行这项研究的过程中，作者往往会更加珍视过往的丰富内涵，而非未来的空虚。记忆中的事物充满质感和张力，散发着气味，呈现出清晰的轮廓；而想象中的事物则缺乏细腻之处，只留下待填补的空白。从人物的角度来看，他只能寄希望于未来能够重现过去他曾应对过的模式。

#↩

THE SELF-STORY AS INSPIRATION

以自我故事为灵感

As a final tack from the outside in, do this: Sit your character down in a chair across from you, introduce yourself, and ask him to tell you his self-story. Your character is, of course, nonexistent, so when he speaks, it will be in a voice only your imagination can hear. In effect, you and your creative self have a conversation.

最后，从外部视角出发，尝试这样做：让你的角色坐在你对面的椅子上，自我介绍，然后请他讲述他的故事。当然，你的角色并不存在，所以当他说话时，那声音只有你的想象力才能听到。实际上，这是你和你的创造性自我之间的一次对话。

Self-stories express how people think about their life and see the reality around them. Elicit your character’s self-story by asking questions about high points, low points, turning points, successes, failures, and other moments of stress. The story a character tells about himself, although rarely factual, expresses who he thinks he is. You have to decide if his version is true or false or some of both.

自我叙事表达了人们如何看待自己的人生以及对周围现实的感知。通过询问有关人生高光时刻、低谷时刻、转折点、成功、失败以及其他压力时刻的问题，来引导角色讲述他们的自我叙事。角色讲述的关于自己的故事，虽然很少是事实，但却表达了他对自己的认知。你需要判断他的版本是真是假，或者两者兼而有之。

As he tells his tale, bear in mind that all statements of self are self-serving. It’s impossible for human beings to do otherwise. All lines of dialogue, for example, that start with the pronoun I are followed, to some degree, by a deceit or exaggeration, no matter how profound or petty. Even when a character confesses to terrible deeds, a whisper from his subtext implies a bit of self-congratulation to the effect, “Aren’t I sensitive, honest, and clear thinking to see these faults in myself and courageous to admit them in public?” When Hamlet curses himself with “Oh what a rogue and peasant slave am I,” a certain pride in self-awareness rolls through his subtext.

在他讲述故事时，请记住，所有关于自我的陈述都带有自利的意味。这是人类无法避免的。例如，所有以“我”开头的对话，无论多么深刻或微不足道，都或多或少地包含着欺骗或夸张。即使一个角色坦白了可怕的罪行，他话语中也暗含着一丝自我陶醉，仿佛在说：“难道我不够敏感、诚实、头脑清醒，才能看到自己的这些缺点，并有勇气公开承认吗？”当哈姆雷特咒骂自己“我真是个卑鄙无耻的奴隶”时，他话语中也流露出某种自我认知的自豪感。

In any case, self-descriptions do not mean what they seem to mean; they always have a purpose beyond the literal. So it’s up to you to sense the difference between truth and BS, between self-awareness and self-deception. Always compare what a character says with what you feel when he says it.

总之，自我描述并非表面意思，它们总有其更深层的含义。因此，你需要自己去分辨真假、自知与自欺。永远要将角色所说的话与你当时的感受进行比较。

No one is who he seems to be. Everyone wears a persona of characterization, the masks they’ve evolved to get through their day with as little friction as possible. To see behind his mask, question your character about his greatest dilemmas, the crisis choices he’s made, and the actions he’s taken in the face of high risk.

没有人是表面看起来那样。每个人都戴着精心设计的面具，这些面具是他们为了尽可能减少摩擦而逐渐形成的。想要看穿面具，就要向你的角色询问他面临的最大困境、他做出的危机抉择，以及他在高风险面前采取的行动。

A self-story, for example, that matches cause with effect and organizes consistent values around persistent goals suggests a character with a well-organized psychology. Whereas an incoherent, inconsistent self-story that disconnects cause and effect and aims at multiple, contradictory goals suggests the opposite. 5

例如，一个将因果关系联系起来，并围绕持续目标构建一致价值观的自我叙事，暗示着一个心理结构良好的人物。而一个脱节、矛盾、脱离因果关系，并追求多个相互矛盾目标的自我叙事，则暗示着相反的情况。

Contradictions within a character form his dimensions. (See Chapter 9 .) So, as you listen to your character’s self-story, be alert to his inner oppositions. People often seek two things that cannot coexist. While he claws his way up the corporate ladder, for example, he expects pats on the back from coworkers. Doubtful. When he tells you about the various things he wants out of life, do they seem consistent or incongruous?

人物性格中的矛盾构成了他的维度。（参见第九章。）因此，在倾听人物的自我叙述时，要留意他内心的冲突。人们常常追求两种无法共存的东西。例如，他一边努力在职场上往上爬，一边又期待同事的认可和赞扬。这很难说。当他告诉你他想要的人生目标时，这些目标看起来是前后一致还是自相矛盾呢？

Find his whys. Your character’s true motivations will be subconscious to him, but nonetheless, he will offer steadfast rationalizations for wanting what he wants. You, like an annoying five-year-old, must repeatedly ask why. Why does he do what he does? How does he explain his actions? His desires? And what’s his plan to reach these desires? Has he mapped out a life strategy, or does he improvise day by day?

找到他行为背后的原因。你的角色真正的动机对他来说是潜意识的，但他仍然会为自己想要的东西给出坚定不移的理由。你必须像个烦人的五岁小孩一样，反复追问为什么。他为什么要做他所做的事？他如何解释自己的行为？他的欲望？他实现这些欲望的计划是什么？他是否制定了人生策略，还是每天随机应变？

Finally, ask about his beliefs. Beliefs create the context for every action a human being takes. Does he believe God exists or not? That romantic love exists or not? In his mind, what’s good? Evil? What institutions does he trust? Private? Public? None? What would he risk his life for? His soul for? What deep beliefs hold his world together?

最后，问问他的信仰。信仰构成了人类所有行为的背景。他相信上帝存在吗？相信爱情存在吗？在他看来，什么是善？什么是恶？他信任哪些机构？私人机构？公共机构？还是根本不信任？他会为了什么而冒生命危险？为了什么而献出灵魂？是什么根深蒂固的信仰维系着他的世界？

Although beliefs mold behavior, they can change… sometimes on a dime. Fanatics, for example, often reverse ideologies and join the opposition side—communists become fascists, fascists communists. For the true believer, the passion of believing is more important than the meaning of belief. 6

虽然信仰塑造行为，但它们也会改变……有时甚至瞬息万变。例如，狂热分子常常会颠倒意识形态，加入反对派——共产主义者变成法西斯主义者，法西斯主义者变成共产主义者。对于真正的信徒来说，信仰的热情比信仰的意义更重要。

Let the insights you gain from all these levels inspire your development of character dimensionality and inner complexity.

让你从所有这些层面获得的见解激发你性格维度和内在复杂性的发展。

#↩

5

CHARACTER INSPIRATION: INSIDE OUT

角色灵感来源：《头脑特工队》

To project yourself into the consciousness of a person essentially your opposite requires the audacity of great genius.
要设身处地地感受与你截然相反的人的意识，需要非凡的胆识和天才般的智慧。
—Henry James 1
—亨利·詹姆斯 1

The second grand source of inspiration places the writer not at the center of her universe but at the heart of her character’s universe. An adventurous writer brings her creation to life by imagining her way into the character’s inner self, seeing through his eyes, hearing with his ears, sensing everything he senses. She envisions the character’s conflicts, improvises choices and takes moment by moment actions as if the character’s fictional life were happening to her. This leap from one consciousness into another requires, as Henry James noted, a certain genius. I call this technique writing in-character .

第二个重要的灵感来源是将作者置于笔下人物宇宙的中心，而非她自身宇宙的中心。一位富有冒险精神的作家会通过想象进入人物的内心世界，用人物的视角去看，用人物的耳朵去听，去感受人物所感知的一切，从而赋予笔下人物生命。她设想人物的冲突，即兴发挥，并像亲身经历人物的虚构人生一样，一步步地做出选择和行动。正如亨利·詹姆斯所言，这种从一种意识跃入另一种意识需要某种天赋。我称这种技巧为“角色内写作”。

As the in-character writer inhabits a role’s inner self, his emotions become hers, her pulse pounds with him, his anger flares inside her; she celebrates his triumphs, she loves his loves. The most powerful inspirations of all strike when the writer experiences what the character experiences. In other words, the character’s first actor is the writer.

当作家化身角色，深入角色内心时，他的情感便化作了她的情感，她的心跳与他同步，他的愤怒在她心中燃烧；她为他的胜利欢呼，她也为他的爱而动容。当作家亲身经历角色所经历的一切时，最强大的灵感便会迸发。换句话说，角色的第一位演员就是作家本人。

An author is an improvisationist. She first imagines herself at the pinpoint center of her character’s consciousness. Once in-character, her mind, emotions, and energies drive character creation. She paces the floor, arms waving, words flying, acting out her creations—man, woman, child, monster. The writer, like the actor, lives inside her character’s senses, seeing and hearing the story’s events as if she were the living character herself so that what happens in the character happens in her.

作者就像即兴表演者。她首先想象自己置身于笔下人物意识的中心。一旦进入角色，她的思想、情感和能量便会驱动角色的塑造。她踱步，挥舞手臂，妙语连珠，演绎着她笔下的人物——男人、女人、孩子、怪物。作家如同演员，生活在角色的感官世界里，如同身临其境般地观看和聆听故事中的事件，以至于角色身上发生的一切也会在她身上重现。

How does a writer get in-character? How does she improvise the character she’s creating? How does she use her own emotions to give life to a fictional being? Once again, she calls on Stanislavsky’s Magic If.

作家如何进入角色？她如何即兴创作她所创造的角色？她如何运用自己的情感赋予虚构人物生命？她再次运用了斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基的“如果”魔法。

In an effort to give her character life, the writer could ask, “If I were in this situation, what would I do?” That thought could certainly get juices flowing, but the writer is not the character. So what the writer might say and do in that moment may be nothing like the actions the character would take.

为了使笔下的人物栩栩如生，作者可以问自己：“如果我身处这种情况，我会怎么做？” 这个想法固然能激发灵感，但作者毕竟不是人物。因此，作者在那一刻的言行可能与人物的实际行动截然不同。

Or the writer could ask, “If my character were in this situation, what would my character do?” But that thought sits the writer in an audience, as it were, picturing the character onstage. Rather than feeling what the character feels, the writer must now guess at his emotions, and guesses are almost always clichés.

或者，作者可以问自己：“如果我的角色身处这种情况，他会怎么做？”但这种思考方式会让作者仿佛置身于观众席，想象着角色在舞台上表演。作者不再能感同身受，而是只能猜测角色的情绪，而猜测几乎总是落入俗套。

To get in-character, therefore, the writer puts the Magic If to work with this thought: “If I were this character in this situation, what would I do?” In other words, the writer acts the scene—not as herself, but as the character. Now the character’s emotions flow, not the writer’s.

因此，为了更好地融入角色，作者会运用“如果”的魔力，思考这样一个问题：“如果我是这个角色，身处这种情境，我会怎么做？”换句话说，作者要扮演这个角色，而不是以自己的身份去演绎场景。这样一来，流露的就不是作者的情感，而是角色的情感。

Writing in-character means more than thinking about what goes on inside a character’s head. It means living within him, so that your mind occupies his mind, his self-awareness becomes yours, and you two act as one. Mastery of the inside-out technique brings characters to life on page, stage, and screen with a truthfulness and subtlety that cannot be achieved any other way.

角色扮演写作不仅仅是思考角色的内心活动，更意味着融入角色，让你的思维与角色的思维交融，让角色的自我意识成为你的，你们合二为一。掌握这种由内而外的写作技巧，能让角色在纸上、舞台上和银幕上栩栩如生，展现出其他任何方式都无法企及的真实与细腻。

Discovering the inspirations that can be found only inside a fictional being calls for sustained, willful and often courageous imaginings. The prerequisite for this feat is insight into your own inner life. The more you understand your true nature, the better you perceive your character’s complexities. To know yourself, you must recognize your rock-bottom inner self, compare your dreams to reality and your desires to morality, and from that base explore the social, personal, private, and hidden selves that complete your multifaceted humanity. Your truth will become the truth of every character you create.

发掘只有在虚构人物身上才能找到的灵感，需要持续不断的、意志坚定的、往往也需要勇气的想象力。而这一切的前提是对自身内心世界的深刻洞察。你越了解自己的真实本性，就越能更好地把握笔下人物的复杂性。要了解自己，你必须认清自己内心最底层的自我，将梦想与现实、欲望与道德进行比较，并以此为基础，探索构成你多面人性的社会层面、个人层面、私密层面以及隐秘层面。你的真实自我，将成为你所创造的每一个角色的真实自我。

So, before you attempt the in-character technique, let’s look inside the multilayered complexity of a human being.

所以，在你尝试角色扮演技巧之前，让我们先来了解一下人类多层次的复杂性。

#↩

THE OBSERVER AND THE OBSERVED

观察者和被观察者

The brain consists of roughly 100 billion neurons laced into 100 trillion interconnections. This immense-beyond-imagining complexity constantly adapts and changes as it interacts with its body, and then through its body with the surrounding physical and social worlds. With every passing day, the brain evolves new thoughts and new feelings, and then stores them in memory as preparation for the future.

大脑由大约1000亿个神经元组成，这些神经元相互连接，形成100万亿条通路。这种难以想象的庞大复杂性，在与身体互动的过程中不断适应和变化，并通过身体与周围的物理和社会世界互动。每一天，大脑都会产生新的想法和感受，并将它们存储在记忆中，为未来做好准备。

Somehow (and science is yet to discover how) consciousness ascends out of this vast conformance, a mind that is not just aware of the things around it but is self-aware—a mind that can step back from itself and see itself as an object. 2

意识以某种方式（科学尚未发现其机制）从这种庞大的顺从中升华，成为一种不仅能感知周围事物，而且具有自我意识的心灵——一种能够跳出自身，将自身视为客体的心灵。

The nature of the inner self has been debated for centuries. Is it a reality or a fantasy? Does a mind staring at itself see itself or mirror images reflecting into infinity?

几个世纪以来，人们一直在争论内在自我的本质。它是现实还是幻想？当心灵凝视自身时，它看到的是自身，还是映照在无限深处的镜像？

Buddha, as we noted, believed that the self is illusionary because what’s inside our minds began as sensory impressions of sights and sounds from outside our minds. What we call the self is actually a bundle of external imprints that appear one after the other like an actor coming and going on- and offstage. Therefore, a true self does not exist—it’s an anatta (nonself), a sort of mental special effect.

正如我们所提到的，佛陀认为自我是一种幻象，因为我们心中的一切最初都源于外界的感官印象，例如视觉和听觉。我们所谓的自我，实际上是一系列外在印记的集合，它们如同演员在舞台上来来去去一般，一个接一个地出现。因此，真正的自我并不存在——它是一种无我（anatta），一种心理特效。

Socrates reversed this. He believed that not only do human beings have a solid inner realm but two selves living within it: the observer and the observed. The core self (the observer) is the epicenter of consciousness that watches life go by and tries to understand it. The core self sends the agent self (the observed) into the world to take action. The core self then perceives its agent self in action and becomes an audience to its own daily life. This is self-awareness—the performance in your inner theatre that no one attends but you. 3

苏格拉底颠覆了这种观点。他认为，人类不仅拥有坚实的内在世界，而且其中还生活着两个自我：观察者和被观察者。核心自我（观察者）是意识的中心，它观察着生活的流逝并试图理解它。核心自我派遣行动自我（被观察者）进入世界采取行动。然后，核心自我感知行动自我的行动，并成为自身日常生活的观众。这就是自我意识——在你内心的剧场中上演的一场表演，除了你之外无人观看。

Consider this: After doing something foolish, don’t you often think the thought, “You idiot!”? When you do, who, exactly, is shaming who? When you manage a success, you often think, “I got that right.” Who is patting whose back? How do self-criticism and self-congratulation work? Who talks to whom?

想想看：做了蠢事之后，你是不是经常会想“你真是个笨蛋！”？当你这么想的时候，究竟是谁在羞辱谁？当你取得成功的时候，你是不是经常会想“我做对了！”？那又是谁在鼓励谁呢？自我批评和自我赞扬是如何运作的？谁在跟谁说话？

As you read this page, an observing awareness within you follows your every move. You perceive (watch yourself read), and then act (take notes on paper or store them in memory). This pivot from awareness-to-action-to-awareness within the mind separates the core self from the agent self. 4

当你阅读此页面时，你内在的观察意识会跟随你的每一个动作。你感知（观察自己阅读），然后行动（在纸上做笔记或将其存储在记忆中）。这种从觉察到行动再到觉察的思维循环，将核心自我与行动自我区分开来。

Some neuroscientists, however, to this day, still side with Buddhism. They argue that because each region of the brain has a separate function and because no single region, in and of itself, causes self-awareness, a core self does not exist. 5

然而，时至今日，一些神经科学家仍然支持佛教的观点。他们认为，由于大脑的每个区域都有其独立的功能，而且没有任何一个区域本身就能产生自我意识，因此并不存在所谓的“核心自我”。

Others agree with Socrates: Human beings have motor neurons for movement, sensory neurons for the senses, and interneurons—by far the most numerous—for the heavy lifting of thought. The brain, with its residue of past experiences and imaginings of future happenings, coupled with the body’s nervous system and the totality of its moment-by-moment sensory encounters, focuses billions of impulses toward the center of awareness, the core self. Self-awareness, therefore, is the side effect of all the neurons in all these regions working in concert. And that’s why damage to any one region of the brain diminishes or extinguishes the sense of self. Peak self-awareness, watching and doing, radiates through the well-nourished brain of a healthy body. 6

其他人则赞同苏格拉底的观点：人类拥有运动神经元负责运动，感觉神经元负责感知，而数量最多的中间神经元则负责繁重的思考。大脑，连同其过往经验的残留和对未来事件的想象，与身体的神经系统以及每时每刻的感官体验相结合，将数十亿个神经冲动集中到意识中心，即核心自我。因此，自我意识是所有这些区域中所有神经元协同工作的副产品。正因如此，大脑任何一个区域的损伤都会削弱甚至消除自我意识。最佳的自我意识，即观察和行动，会通过健康身体中营养充足的大脑散发出来。

This is nothing new. The Egyptians saw the observing self as a protective spirit and named it the Ba Soul; the Greeks called it the Daemon; 7 the Romans dubbed it the Genius. 8 But if, at the end of the day, science decides that the self is a fiction, as Buddha claimed, fine with me. Then it’s our fiction, our nature, what makes us human. 9

这并非什么新鲜事。埃及人将观察自我视为一种保护神灵，称之为巴神（Ba Soul）；希腊人称之为守护神（Daemon）；罗马人称之为天才（Genius）。但如果最终科学认定自我如佛陀所言，只是一种虚构，我欣然接受。那么，自我就是我们的虚构，我们的本性，正是它使我们成为人。

(Try this: Go to a mirror and glance into your eyes. For an instant you’ll sense someone else, deep within, looking back. With the next blink, however, you’ll realize that what you glimpsed was a split-second image of your core self observing you just before your agent self reacted. These moments happen best when unplanned, but it’s worth a test.)

（不妨试试：走到镜子前，瞥一眼自己的眼睛。那一瞬间，你会感觉到内心深处似乎有另一个人在注视着你。然而，眨一下眼，你就会意识到，你刚才看到的只是你内在核心自我观察你的瞬间影像，就在你的意识自我做出反应之前。这种时刻往往在不经意间发生，但值得一试。）

To deepen our understanding of human nature, we must not only accept the idea of the self, but of a cast of selves: the core self (observer); the agent self (observed) plus all the personal and social personae an agent self assumes; all the past selves the core self remembers; and finally, at the deepest level, the hidden self. 10

为了加深我们对人性的理解，我们不仅要接受“自我”的概念，还要接受一系列“自我”的概念：核心自我（观察者）；行动自我（被观察者）及其所扮演的所有个人和社会角色；核心自我记忆中的所有过去自我；以及最终，在最深层次上的隐藏自我。

#↩

FOUR SELVES IN SEARCH OF A CHARACTER

四个自我寻找一个角色

To imagine how each layer of self creates a fully human character, start at the conscious center, the private realm in which the core self copes with inner dilemmas, makes decisions, then directs the agent self to take action.

要想象自我的每一层面如何塑造出一个完整的人格，就要从意识中心开始，也就是核心自我应对内心困境、做出决定，然后指导行动自我采取行动的私人领域。

Next, surround that center with two outer strata: the personal realm in which the agent self assumes various personae as it deals with intimate relationships, and the social realm in which the agent self takes on its public personae as it copes with institutions and individuals.

接下来，围绕中心构建两个外层：个人领域，在这个领域中，行动者自我会扮演各种角色来处理亲密关系；以及社会领域，在这个领域中，行动者自我会扮演其公共角色来应对机构和个人。

Finally, underpin these three levels with a substrata: the subconscious realm in which the hidden self struggles with contradictory desires.

最后，在这三个层次之上，还有一个底层：潜意识领域，在这个领域中，隐藏的自我与矛盾的欲望作斗争。

From story to story, how many of these levels are at play in your characters is up to you, but let’s work through them one at a time:

故事中，你的角色会运用到多少个这样的层次，取决于你自己，但让我们逐一来看：

#↩

The Private Selves: Variations of Identity

私人自我：身份的变体

William James gave the core self names such as the “self of selves,” the “owner-self,” the “proprietor-self.” In his analogy, the core self is a sanctuary within a citadel, the epicenter inside our personal and public personae. 11 James’s concept of “the stream of thought” inspired fiction writers like Virginia Woolf to create the literary style of “stream of consciousness.”

威廉·詹姆斯为核心自我赋予了诸如“自我之我”、“所有者自我”、“主宰者自我”等名称。在他的比喻中，核心自我如同堡垒中的圣殿，是我们个人和公共人格的核心所在。詹姆斯的“思维流”概念启发了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫等小说家，催生了“意识流”这一文学风格。

In the William James view of the private realm, the core self maintains a single identity over a lifetime while observing and absorbing its many past selves. We know we are not the same person we used to be, and yet we feel that we are and always have been our core self. Our mind has a permanent, unchanging, stable sense of identity, and yet, simultaneously, its continuously evolving consciousness acts and reacts, learns and forgets, evolves and devolves, keeps some attitudes about values and desires but changes to others about what’s worth doing, what’s a waste of time, and the like. Day in, day out, we live in a natural state of paradox: We change while we stay the same. 12

在威廉·詹姆斯对私人领域的理解中，核心自我终其一生保持着单一的身份，同时观察并吸收着过往的诸多自我。我们知道自己已不再是过去的自己，但我们仍然感觉自己是、也一直都是我们的核心自我。我们的心灵拥有一种永恒不变的稳定身份感，然而与此同时，其不断演化的意识也在行动与反应、学习与遗忘、进化与退化，它保留着一些关于价值和欲望的态度，但对于什么值得做、什么浪费时间等等的看法却发生了改变。日复一日，我们生活在一种自然的悖论状态中：我们既在改变，又保持不变。

An aside: William James’s younger brother was the author Henry James. The two delved into the nature of thought in both science and fiction. Their work inspired Henry to explore the point-of-view techniques that revolutionized the modern psychological novel. The nineteenth century gave America two sets of James brothers: Henry and William (writers and psychologists) and Jesse and Frank (bank robbers and committers of atrocities).

顺便一提：威廉·詹姆斯的弟弟是作家亨利·詹姆斯。兄弟二人深入研究了科学和小说中的思维本质。他们的作品启发亨利探索视角技巧，从而革新了现代心理小说。十九世纪的美国出现了两对詹姆斯兄弟：亨利和威廉（作家兼心理学家），以及杰西和弗兰克（银行劫匪和暴行犯）。

Imprisoned inside our skull, the core self lives essentially alone. Our inner voice is the only inner voice we will ever hear. Because our core self cannot contact another person’s private realm telepathically, consciousness becomes a kind of cinema of the mind.
