If you then followed that up with exhaustive research into the state of fashion today, plus firsthand observations of trends you see on the street, plus hours spend faux shopping in the hippest of shops, filling notebooks full of details, taking photos with your phone, then you could come away with a one-of-a-kind characterization, a look no one has ever quite seen before—a credible original.

假设你觉得你笔下的角色总体上会很注重时尚。如果你接着对当今的时尚状况进行详尽的研究，加上亲身观察街头潮流，花几个小时在最潮的商店里假装购物，用笔记本记录下所有细节，用手机拍照，那么你就能塑造出一个独一无二的角色，一个前所未见的形象——一个可信的原创角色。

#↩

Intrigue

阴谋

A unique characterization captures our curiosity, making us want to know the true, inner character who lives behind the mask of outer traits.

独特的人物刻画激发了我们的好奇心，让我们想要了解隐藏在外在特征面具背后的真实内在性格。

Suppose we were shown a drunken, abusive, angry, out-of-work husband, sitting in a darkened living room in his underwear, swilling a can of beer, sweating away, running his grease-stained fingers through his beard, watching an NFL rerun. Would that image make us wonder, “But who is he really?” Doubtful. Clichés destroy intrigue.

假设我们看到一个醉醺醺、脾气暴躁、愤怒的失业丈夫，他只穿着内裤，坐在昏暗的客厅里，大口喝着啤酒，汗流浃背，油腻的手指梳理着胡须，看着NFL的重播。这样的画面会让我们好奇“他到底是谁？”吗？恐怕不会。陈词滥调扼杀了悬念。

A clichéd characterization raises a question that answers itself: Who is this character? Exactly who she seems to be. Like a block of cement, she’s the same on the inside as the outside. To create creditable characters that spike the reader’s/audience’s curiosity and reward their intrigue, build a fascinating world and populate this setting with equally fascinating originals.

陈词滥调式的角色塑造会引出一个不言自明的问题：这个角色究竟是谁？她表面上看起来究竟是什么样？就像一块水泥，她表里如一。要想塑造出令人信服的角色，激发读者/观众的好奇心，并让他们乐于探索，就需要构建一个引人入胜的世界，并在这个世界中塑造同样引人入胜的原创角色。

#↩

SETTING: WORLD BUILDING

背景设定：世界构建

Characterization begins in the genes with traits like gender and hair color, but once a character is born, an array of physical and social settings buffet and mold her outer selves. Time and space frame all such events, greatly influencing outer appearances and behaviors.

性格的形成始于基因，例如性别和发色等特征；但一旦角色诞生，一系列的物理和社会环境便会对其外在人格产生影响和塑造。时间和空间构成了所有这些事件的框架，极大地影响着外貌和行为。

Time comes in two dimensions: location and duration. An author could locate a story in a contemporary setting, historical period, hypothetical future, or timeless fantasy. Within each period, the storyteller also sets the duration of the telling in relationship to the lives of her characters. Storytelling time and lifetime could be equal: My Dinner with Andre is a two-hour film about a two-hour dinner. Or the telling could span days, months, years, even a lifetime: Terrance Winter’s longform series Boardwalk Empire and Jonathan Franzen’s novel The Corrections .

时间有两个维度：地点和持续时间。作者可以将故事设定在当代、历史时期、假想的未来或永恒的奇幻世界中。在每个时代背景下，叙述者还会根据人物的生命历程来设定故事的持续时间。故事的叙述时间和人物的生命历程可以相等：《与安德烈共进晚餐》是一部讲述两小时晚餐的两小时电影。或者，叙述时间可以跨越数天、数月、数年，甚至一生：例如泰伦斯·温特的长篇剧集《大西洋帝国》和乔纳森·弗兰岑的小说《纠正》。

Storied space is also two-dimensional: physical location plus level of conflict. A story could be found anywhere—a mountain peak, a farm, a space station, a certain street in a certain city, a certain building on that street, and a certain room in that building. Once set, the physical location houses a cast of characters, and so the writer must determine its level(s) of conflict: physical (woman against nature), social (woman against the law), personal (woman against her in-laws), inner (self against self), or any combination.

故事空间也是二维的：物理地点加上冲突层次。故事可以发生在任何地方——一座山峰、一个农场、一个空间站、某个城市的某条街道、这条街道上的某栋建筑，以及那栋建筑里的某个房间。一旦设定好物理地点，故事中的人物就随之出现，因此作者必须确定故事的冲突层次：生理冲突（女性对抗自然）、社会冲突（女性对抗法律）、个人冲突（女性对抗婆家）、内在冲突（自我对抗），或任何组合。

Patterns of behavior, usually routine, sometimes ritualized, begin at birth and develop through infancy. Daily needs generate activities such as eating and playing, greetings and goodbyes. Humdrum as these customs may be, they embed themselves in a role’s characterization. 1

行为模式，通常是例行性的，有时甚至是仪式化的，从出生开始，并在婴儿期逐渐发展。日常需求催生了诸如吃饭、玩耍、问候和告别等活动。这些习俗虽然看似平凡，却深深融入到角色塑造之中。

#↩

MORAL IMAGINATION

道德想象

An author with a strong moral imagination sees meaning in every aspect of a story’s setting; nothing and no one is neutral—not cop, prop, or raindrop. This writer marshals a constellation of charged values so that everything in her story rings either positively, negatively, or with an ironic fusion of both. Nothing is without value. All things neutral are kept off-page, offstage, offscreen.

一位拥有强烈道德想象力的作家，能从故事场景的方方面面发现意义；没有谁是中立的——无论是警察、道具还是雨滴。这位作家巧妙地运用一系列充满张力的价值观，使故事中的一切都带有正面、负面或两者兼具的讽刺意味。没有什么是毫无价值的。所有中立的事物都被排除在外，从故事背景中抹去。

In the same sense that the writer is the character’s first actor, she’s also the story’s first production designer, intent on making every element in a setting reveal, reflect, counterpoint, or change at least one character, perhaps the whole cast. When an automobile enters, a writer without moral imagination sees it as no more than a vehicle, but to a production designer it comes charged with a value. As a bright pink Maserati pulls up to an opera house, the writer’s choices not only characterize its absurdly wealthy owner but the parking attendant who takes her key with a sarcastic smile.

正如作家是角色的第一位演员一样，她也是故事的第一位布景设计师，力求让场景中的每一个元素都揭示、映照、对比或改变至少一个角色，甚至可能是整个角色群像。当一辆汽车出现时，缺乏道德想象力的作家只会把它看作一辆车，但对布景设计师而言，它却被赋予了某种价值。当一辆亮粉色的玛莎拉蒂驶入歌剧院时，作家的选择不仅塑造了车主那极度富有的形象，也刻画了那个带着讽刺笑容接过她车钥匙的停车管理员。

A moral imagination also ranks values by importance from most to least. Life/Death is a possibility that shadows all stories, but a psychothriller may foreground it as its core value, while a Romantic Comedy backgrounds it as irrelevant. The core value of a War Story is Victory/Defeat, but Life/Death haunts every action. Without a moral imagination, a setting amounts to little more than furniture. 2

道德想象力也会根据重要性对各种价值进行排序。生死是所有故事中都存在的阴影，但心理惊悚片可能会将其作为核心价值凸显出来，而浪漫喜剧则将其视为无关紧要的背景。战争故事的核心价值是胜利/失败，但生死却萦绕在每一个行动之中。如果没有道德想象力，场景就如同家具一般毫无意义。

#↩

CULTURAL RESTRAINTS

文化限制

Time, place, and people not only restrain what a character can do but stipulate what she must not do. As a character enters a scene, webs of restraint curtail her relationship with every person and object: how to walk safely down a dark alley, how to respond to someone’s touch, what to say in a courtroom. In principle, the more positive the relationships that surround a character’s life, the more restricted, more civilized her behavior. The reverse is also true: When a character has nothing to lose, she’s capable of anything.

时间、地点和人物不仅限制了角色的行动，也规定了她不该做什么。当一个角色进入某个场景时，种种限制便会交织成网，束缚着她与每个人和每件事物的关系：如何安全地走过黑暗的小巷，如何回应他人的触碰，在法庭上该说什么。原则上，角色生活中的人际关系越积极，她的行为就越受约束，也越文明。反之亦然：当一个角色一无所有时，她便会无所不能。

#↩

PHYSICAL SETTINGS

物理环境

Like all things in life, the world’s physical and temporal forces—lethal diseases, the car that won’t start, not enough time to get something done, too far to go to get what you need—cut both ways: Sunshine tans you or burns you. Farms and cities provide food and shelter, then pollute rivers with fertilizers and fill the air with noxious pollutants.

就像生活中所有的事情一样，世界上的自然和时间因素——致命的疾病、无法启动的汽车、时间不够用、去不了那么远的地方买所需之物——都具有双重性：阳光既能晒黑也能晒伤。农场和城市提供食物和住所，却也用化肥污染河流，用有害污染物充斥空气。

Environments shape the people who live in them. Scandinavia and the Mediterranean produce people with distinctively different dispositions. Why? The weather. Objects can prompt the conscious mind in one direction and the subconscious in another: Putting a briefcase on a church pew makes people feel competitive; Japan reduced suicides by installing streetlights that gave off a blue glow; the smell of a cleaning liquid makes coal miners want to tidy up. 3

环境塑造了生活在其中的人们。斯堪的纳维亚半岛和地中海沿岸地区的人们性格迥异。为什么？气候。物品可以引导意识朝一个方向发展，而潜意识则朝另一个方向发展：在教堂长椅上放置公文包会让人产生竞争意识；日本通过安装发出蓝光的路灯降低了自杀率；清洁剂的气味会让煤矿工人想要打扫卫生。

When creating a story’s physical setting, ask questions in two directions: (1) How does my story’s time, space, and objects affect the personalities of my characters? (2) How do the setting’s antagonistic forces thwart my characters’ desires?

在构建故事的物理环境时，要从两个方面思考问题：（1）故事的时间、空间和物品如何影响人物的性格？（2）环境中的对抗力量如何阻碍人物的愿望？

#↩

SOCIAL SETTINGS

社交场合

A character and her society constantly interact. Social settings provide various groups—nationalities, religions, neighborhoods, schools, professions—to which an individual aspires or rebels. Either way, they anchor her identity.

人物与其所处的社会环境不断互动。社会环境构成了各种群体——民族、宗教、社区、学校、职业——个人会渴望加入其中，或与之抗争。无论选择哪种方式，这些群体都构成了其身份认同的基石。

For example, the two cultures known as scientists and artists tend to inspire two very contrasted personalities. The same can be said about the citizens of small southern towns versus big northern cities, or kindergarten teachers versus porn stars. Yet within the shared traits of any community, the variety of personalities seems limitless.

例如，科学家和艺术家这两种群体往往会孕育出截然不同的两种性格。南方小镇居民与北方大城市居民，或者幼儿园教师与色情明星，也同样如此。然而，在任何一个群体所共有的特征之下，性格的多样性似乎无穷无尽。

The most striking feature of massive social systems is the price they extract for membership. After successfully climbing a corporate pyramid, an executive may become a superbly efficient employee but a woefully deficient human being. Make no mistake, however, institutions couldn’t dehumanize without help. Many persons secretly welcome their loss of soul and live comfortably inside a shell of self-deception. Cracking it open would demand blunt force honesty, but they put that away long ago. 4

庞大的社会体系最显著的特征在于其成员资格所要付出的代价。成功攀升至企业金字塔顶端的高管，或许会成为效率极高的员工，但却会沦为一个品格低下的人。然而，毋庸置疑，如果没有某种因素的帮助，制度本身也无法使人丧失人性。许多人暗自欣然接受灵魂的消亡，安然生活在自我欺骗的壳中。要揭开这层伪装，需要直面残酷的真相，但他们早已将这种坦诚抛诸脑后。

As the story-driven documentaries of Frederick Wiseman ( High School , Basic Training , Hospital , Ballet ) make clear, people working inside institutions unknowingly dehumanize one another. For a lucky few, however, they sometimes rehumanize.

正如弗雷德里克·怀斯曼（Frederick Wiseman）的叙事性纪录片（《高中》、《新兵训练》、《医院》、《芭蕾舞》）所揭示的那样，在机构内部工作的人们会在不知不觉中将彼此非人化。然而，对于少数幸运儿来说，他们有时也能重塑人性。

When creating a setting, think deeply about the effects of its total culture on your characters, then map out your cast’s specific interactions (see Chapter Fifteen), and finally, whenever complex characters meet, refine them with subtle but distinctive social personae.

在创造一个场景时，要深入思考其整体文化对你的角色产生的影响，然后规划出你的角色之间的具体互动（参见第十五章），最后，每当复杂的角色相遇时，都要用微妙但独特的社会人格来完善他们。

#↩

PERSONAL SETTINGS

个人设置

The inescapable intimacies of families, friends, and lovers create conflicts like none other in life: Friends embrace in joy until they betray each other; a mother’s love shines like the sun until she’s disrespected; nothing explodes into optimism or crumples into pessimism faster than romance. For reasons no family member can understand, one sibling joins a religious cult while another edits American Atheist magazine. Their quarrels never end.

家人、朋友和爱人之间无法回避的亲密关系，造就了生活中其他任何事物都无法比拟的冲突：朋友之间曾欢聚一堂，直至背叛彼此；母亲的爱如同阳光般灿烂，直至遭受不敬；没有什么比爱情更能迅速地将乐观情绪推向高潮，或将悲观情绪彻底击垮。出于任何家庭成员都无法理解的原因，一个兄弟姐妹加入了宗教邪教，而另一个则成为了《美国无神论者》杂志的编辑。他们的争吵永无止境。

When setting up your story, give extended thought to the relationships of intimacy within your cast. This level of conflict offers the greatest opportunity for originality and nuance of characterization.

在构思故事时，要深入思考角色之间的亲密关系。这种程度的冲突能为角色塑造的原创性和细腻程度提供最大的发挥空间。

#↩

SETTING VERSUS CHARACTERIZATION

背景设定与人物刻画

A character’s collisions with her physical, social, and personal worlds etch her characterization, trait by trait. To trace the influence of these settings on your cast, consider these eight possible relationships:

角色与她所处的物质世界、社会环境和个人世界的碰撞，一点一滴地塑造了她的性格特征。为了探究这些环境对角色的影响，请考虑以下八种可能的关系：

1. The setting submerges a character in things such as home, car, job, and poker club, until her belongings become extensions of her core self. In Henry James’s The Portrait of a Lady , Madame Merle explains the principle of character extension to her young admirer, Isabel Archer:

1. 场景的设置使人物沉浸于诸如家、车、工作和扑克俱乐部等事物之中，直到她的所有物都成为她核心自我的延伸。在亨利·詹姆斯的《一位女士的画像》中，梅尔夫人向她的年轻仰慕者伊莎贝尔·阿切尔解释了人物延伸的原则：

“When you’ve lived as long as I you’ll see that every human being has his shell and that you must take the shell into account. By the shell I mean the whole envelope of circumstances. There’s no such thing as an isolated man or woman; we’re each of us made up of some cluster of appurtenances. What shall we call our ‘self’? Where does it begin? Where does it end? It overflows into everything that belongs to us—and then it flows back again. I know a large part of myself is in the clothes I choose to wear. I’ve a great respect for things! One’s self—for other people—is one’s expression of one’s self; and one’s house, one’s furniture, one’s garments, the books one reads, the company one keeps—these things are all expressive.”
“当你活到我这样的年纪，你就会明白，每个人都有自己的外壳，你必须把这个外壳考虑在内。我说的外壳指的是我们所处环境的全部。世上没有孤立的人；我们每个人都是由各种各样的附属物构成的。我们该如何称呼我们的‘自我’？它从哪里开始？到哪里结束？它渗透到我们拥有的一切——然后又反过来流回我们自身。我知道，我选择穿的衣服很大程度上反映了我的自我。我对事物充满敬意！一个人的自我——对他人来说——是他自我的表达；一个人的房子、家具、衣服、读的书、交往的人——所有这些都是表达自我的方式。”

This principle guided writings such as Michael Ondaatje’s The English Patient and Jonathan Franzen’s The Corrections .

这一原则指导了迈克尔·翁达杰的《英国病人》和乔纳森·弗兰岑的《纠正》等作品的创作。

2. The setting releases forces of antagonism that block the characters’ desires.

2. 环境释放出阻碍角色欲望的对抗力量。

In All Is Lost , the Indian Ocean overwhelms a lone sailor; in Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri , injustice drives the mother of a murdered daughter to murder; in Girls Trip , friends, lovers, and ex-lovers sabotage a bachelorette weekend.

在《一切尽失》中，印度洋吞噬了一位孤独的水手；在《三块广告牌》中，不公正驱使一位被谋杀女儿的母亲走上谋杀之路；在《闺蜜之旅》中，朋友、恋人和前任恋人破坏了一场单身女子周末之旅。

When unexpected reactions suddenly open gaps between what a character thinks will happen and what actually does, these fractures on the surface of life send quakes downward to disrupt the subconscious. Then, as if from the floor of a volcano, unwanted desires surge upward into improvised, usually unwanted, and often regretted behavior. This movement radiating down from the setting to the deepest self gives a character depth; the energy rebounding up from the depths of self to the setting gives a story power.

当意料之外的反应突然拉开角色预期与实际发生之间的差距时，这些生活表面的裂痕会引发潜意识的震荡。然后，如同火山爆发一般，不想要的欲望会涌上心头，化作即兴的、通常不情愿的、且往往令人后悔的行为。这种从环境向下辐射至内心深处的动力赋予角色深度；而从内心深处反弹至环境的能量则赋予故事力量。

3. The setting and its cast form one grand metaphor for reality. Like pieces of a puzzle, setting and cast fit together; like mirror opposites, they define each other. The characters give meaning to their setting; the setting reflects back on its characters; and together they stand for life.

3. 场景及其人物构成了一个宏大的现实隐喻。场景和人物如同拼图碎片，完美契合；如同镜像般相互映照，彼此定义。人物赋予场景意义；场景也映照出人物；二者共同象征着人生。

In Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland , Wonderland is ruled by magic, not physics, and its events obey lunacy, not logic. As a result, its cast members, including Alice, reflect their setting by undergoing nonsensical transformations—all working together to create a multidimensional metaphor for the real world, real people, and human absurdity.

在刘易斯·卡罗尔的《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中，仙境由魔法而非物理定律主宰，其事件遵循的是荒诞而非逻辑。因此，包括爱丽丝在内的所有角色都反映了仙境的奇特环境，经历了一系列荒诞不经的变化——所有这些共同构成了一个多维度的隐喻，象征着现实世界、真实的人和人类的荒谬。

This pattern of a setting mirroring its cast and a cast mirroring its society is clearly seen in works such as Succession and Parasite . Each of these tellings merges Domestic Drama with the Thriller Genre so that the characters, their families, and their society mutually infect each other. The stories in turn reflect the politics of the real world in which corruption acts as the secret cement that holds society together. 5

这种场景映照角色、角色映照社会的模式在《继承之战》和《寄生虫》等作品中体现得淋漓尽致。这些作品都将家庭剧与惊悚片融合在一起，使角色、他们的家庭和社会相互影响、相互影响。故事反过来又反映了现实世界的政治，其中腐败如同秘密的粘合剂，维系着社会的运转。

4. The setting floods a character’s mind and sends an onrush of objects, people, and memories streaming through her thoughts: Toni Morrison’s Beloved and David Means’s short story “The Knocking.”

4. 场景充斥着人物的思绪，大量的物品、人物和记忆涌入她的脑海：托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》和大卫·米恩斯的短篇小说《敲门声》。

5. The setting recedes into the background as the foreground overflows with characters. In Larry David’s Curb Your Enthusiasm and Matthew Weiner’s Mad Men , homes, offices, and restaurants serve as picture frames for character portraits.

5. 随着前景人物的涌现，场景退居幕后。在拉里·大卫的《抑制热情》和马修·韦纳的《广告狂人》中，住宅、办公室和餐厅都如同画框一般，衬托着人物肖像。

6. The setting leads an existence so indifferent, so separate from its characters that they seem isolated on an island: Tom Stoppard’s Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead and Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot .

6. 故事的背景与人物之间存在着一种漠不关心、彼此疏离的关系，以至于人物仿佛被孤立在一个孤岛上：汤姆·斯托帕德的《罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿之死》和塞缪尔·贝克特的《等待戈多》。

7. The setting’s objects seem to have a will of their own: Edgar Allan Poe’s “The Fall of the House of Usher” and Brian Evenson’s “A Collapse of Horses.”

7. 场景中的物体似乎有自己的意志：埃德加·爱伦·坡的《厄舍府的倒塌》和布莱恩·埃文森的《马匹的倒塌》。

8. The setting’s objects turn into characters. In Lewis Carroll’s Alice Through the Looking Glass , King, Queen, and Knight, three chess pieces, join Humpty Dumpty, an anthropomorphic egg, to fill out the cast. Guardians of the Galaxy features Groot, a humanoid tree, and Rocket, a genetically engineered raccoon. 6

8. 场景中的物品变成了角色。在刘易斯·卡罗尔的《爱丽丝镜中奇遇记》中，国王、王后和骑士这三个国际象棋棋子，与拟人化的蛋——矮胖子——一起，构成了完整的角色阵容。《银河护卫队》中则有人形树人格鲁特和基因改造的浣熊火箭浣熊。

#↩

CHARACTERIZATION CHANGE

特征变化

When your characters confront physical, social, and personal settings, they put on various outer selves. But none of these encounters are static, and all can dramatically and believably cause changes in a role’s characterization. I can think of four commonplace ways:

当你的角色面对不同的物理、社会和个人环境时，他们会展现出各种各样的外在形象。但这些经历都不是一成不变的，它们都可能对角色的性格塑造产生戏剧性且令人信服的影响。我能想到四种常见的方式：

1. Rebellion: A character may change her setting in hope of sending her personality in the direction she wants it to go. Rural artists head for the big city; scholars drop out of school and enlist in the military.
1. 反叛：角色可能会改变所处的环境，希望以此引导自己的性格朝着自己想要的方向发展。乡村艺术家前往大城市；学者辍学参军。
2. Travel: Adventures abroad encourage a hybrid global identity. Youth culture is one example. Jeans and tennis shoes invented in the USA and made in Asia are the uniform worn by young people everywhere on the seven continents.
2. 旅行：海外探险经历有助于形成融合多元文化的全球认同感。青年文化就是一个例证。牛仔裤和运动鞋，虽然发明于美国，但产自亚洲，如今已成为七大洲年轻人的标配。
3. Time Travel: A character can hide in a pocket of time. Nostalgics live in the past; rat racers live in the future; hedonists live in a perverse present. 7
3. 时间旅行：角色可以藏身于某个时间点。怀旧者活在过去；追逐未来者活在未来；享乐主义者活在扭曲的当下。
4. The internet: Borderless travel to electronic geographies inhabited by citizens with placeless addresses can radically alter an identity. Online culture is instantaneous, anonymous, depthless, and yet real because within it, actual things happen to actual people, changing them for better or worse.
4. 互联网：无国界的旅行，通往由没有固定住址的公民组成的电子地理世界，可以彻底改变一个人的身份认同。网络文化瞬息万变、匿名且缺乏深度，却又无比真实，因为在其中，真实的事情发生在真实的人身上，并对他们产生或好或坏的影响。
#↩

EXPLICIT TRAITS

显性特征

Once you apply your broad strokes, you need to sharpen the explicit traits that express your characters as individuals. No one is simply “born that way.” All complex characterizations display both genetically given and actively acquired traits. Genetic traits (e.g., vocal timbre) tend to last, while acquired traits (e.g., vocabulary) evolve. To create any one trait, hundreds of genes must interact, while at the same time they absorb random impacts from countless external forces. When you work your imagination through both sources, traits coalesce into unique, fascinating characterizations. 8

勾勒出人物的大致轮廓后，你需要进一步提炼那些能展现人物个性的具体特征。没有人是“天生如此”的。所有复杂的人物塑造都体现了遗传和后天习得的特征。遗传特征（例如音色）往往是永久性的，而后天习得的特征（例如词汇量）则会不断发展。任何一个特征的形成，都离不开数百个基因的相互作用，同时它们还要吸收来自无数外部因素的随机影响。当你运用想象力，将这两种因素结合起来时，各种特征就会融合，最终形成独特而引人入胜的人物形象。

Every observable trait sits on a spectrum that ranges from positive to negative. First are those traits acted out in public—such as sophisticated/unsophisticated, social/antisocial, and charismatic/boring—that define a character’s relationships to acquaintances and strangers. Then come behaviors acted out in private—such as generous/selfish, encouraging/fault-finding, and concerned/unconcerned—that mark her personal relationships with family, lovers, and friends.

每一种可观察的特质都存在于一个从正面到负面的连续谱上。首先是那些在公共场合表现出的特质——例如老练/粗俗、善于交际/不善交际、魅力四射/乏味无趣——这些特质定义了人物与熟人和陌生人之间的关系。其次是那些在私下场合表现出的行为——例如慷慨/自私、鼓励/挑剔、关心/漠不关心——这些特质体现了她与家人、爱人和朋友之间的私人关系。

How many traits or how few? In the visual arts, if an empty canvas is 1 and a completely filled canvas is 2, the optimal density that the eye enjoys is 1.3, or three-tenths full. The same, I believe, applies to character. Leave seven-tenths of a protagonist unknown and mysterious. Based on the three-tenths you express, the reader/audience will fill in the rest as needed from their own imagination. For if a writer were to dramatize every possible trait a character might display, the telling would take forever, the role would become incomprehensible, and the reader/audience would be overwhelmed. On the other hand, one lone trait—a foreign accent, for example—shrinks a character to a bit part.

应该展现多少特质？在视觉艺术中，如果空白画布代表1，完全填满的画布代表2，那么人眼最舒适的密度是1.3，也就是十分之三。我认为，这同样适用于人物塑造。让主角的七成特质保持未知和神秘。基于你展现的十分之三，读者/观众会根据自己的想象力填补剩余的部分。因为如果作者要把人物可能展现的所有特质都戏剧化地呈现出来，叙述就会没完没了，人物也会变得难以理解，读者/观众也会感到不知所措。另一方面，仅仅一个特质——比如外国口音——就会把人物贬低成一个配角。

Only the writer can discover the ideal number of traits for any particular character. A trait’s necessity depends on how much is changed by its removal. If you want to cut or add a trait, ask, “What, if anything, is lost or gained?”

只有作者才能发现特定角色最理想的性格特征数量。一个性格特征是否必要，取决于移除它会带来多大的变化。如果你想删减或增加一个性格特征，问问自己：“这样做会失去什么，或者得到什么？”

What follows is a short list of topics that generate traits of characterization. Your particular story will add or subtract from them.

以下列出一些有助于塑造人物特征的主题。你的故事可能会在此基础上进行增减。

#↩

NAMES AND NICKNAMES

姓名和昵称

Like the roles they identify, names express more meaning in fiction than real life. The deliberate plainness of “John” and “Mary,” for instance, gives a character a particular quality of ordinariness that someone actually named “Mary” or “John” would not have.

就像它们所代表的角色一样，名字在虚构作品中比在现实生活中蕴含着更丰富的意义。例如，“约翰”和“玛丽”这样刻意平淡的名字，赋予了角色一种独特的平凡感，而现实中名叫“玛丽”或“约翰”的人则不具备这种特质。

But be careful. Unless you’re hoping for laughs, avoid blatantly symbolic names, such as branding a corporate executive “Mr. Biggman.” On the other hand, in Death of a Salesman , Arthur Miller called his impoverished salesman Willy Loman, a name that, for some reason, never raises an eyebrow.

但要小心。除非你想博君一笑，否则最好避免使用过于明显的象征性名字，比如把一位企业高管称为“大人物先生”。另一方面，在《推销员之死》中，阿瑟·米勒把那个贫穷的推销员叫做威利·洛曼，这个名字不知为何从未引起任何人的注意。

Allegorical genres, such as Fantasy and Horror, create boldly symbolic settings and add fun by giving their characters emblematic names. For example, in C. S. Lewis’s religious allegory The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe , the founder of a new kingdom is named Peter, echoing St. Peter, founder of the Christian church; the betrayer of the story’s Christ figure is a witch named Jadis, as in Judas; an autocratic housekeeper is called Mrs. Macready, as in the imperative “Get ready!”

寓言体裁，例如奇幻和恐怖小说，会创造出大胆的象征性场景，并通过赋予角色象征性的名字来增添趣味。例如，在C·S·刘易斯的宗教寓言小说《狮子、女巫和衣橱》中，新王国的缔造者名叫彼得，这与基督教教会的创始人圣彼得遥相呼应；背叛故事中基督形象的女巫名叫雅迪斯，与犹大同名；专横跋扈的管家名叫麦克雷迪夫人，与命令式的“准备好！”同名。

#↩

NAKED AND CLOTHED

裸体和穿衣

Strip your character naked and run a checklist of biographical items: age and eye appeal, height and weight, texture of muscle and fat, head and body hair, shade and grain of skin, posture and walk. Use your imagination to take her shopping and see what she would like to wear, then look in her closet and find out what she actually owns.

剥去你笔下人物的所有外衣，然后逐一核对以下特征：年龄和外貌吸引力、身高体重、肌肉和脂肪的质地、头发和体毛、肤色和纹理、姿态和步态。发挥你的想象力，带她去购物，看看她想穿什么，然后再打开她的衣橱，看看她到底有哪些衣服。

#↩

GENDER AND SEX LIFE

性别与性生活

What does your character find irresistibly erotic? What is her gender? What, if anything, does she do about it?

你笔下的人物觉得什么最性感？她的性别是什么？她会对此采取什么行动？

#↩

VOCAL TONE AND LANGUAGE

语调和语言

Now close your eyes and listen. Like music, a character’s voice touches unconscious feelings in readers and audiences. Give each of your characters a speech style with a unique vocabulary, sentence structure, pitch, diction, and imagery. 9 The total effect becomes a concert of form and content—not only what she has to say, but how she says it.

现在闭上眼睛，仔细聆听。就像音乐一样，角色的声音能够触动读者和观众潜意识里的情感。赋予每个角色独特的说话风格，包括词汇、句式结构、音调、措辞和意象。最终的效果将是一场形式与内容的完美融合——不仅在于她说了什么，还在于她是如何说的。

#↩

FACIAL EXPRESSIONS AND GESTURES

面部表情和手势

Audiences read the flitting expressions on a character’s face at one-twenty-fifth of a second. So study what’s in your character’s eyes, and then pull back to witness her mannerisms, ticks, and energy.

观众只需1/25秒就能解读角色脸上的细微表情。所以，仔细观察角色的眼神，然后拉远镜头，观察她的举止、小动作和活力。

Gestures create a language of their own in three varieties: (1) hand waves, head tilts, and shoulder shrugs that enrich speech; (2) symbolic gestures like an erect middle finger; (3) imitative gestures like the thumb dance that means “Text me.”

手势创造了一种独特的语言，分为三种类型：（1）挥手、歪头、耸肩，丰富了言语；（2）象征性手势，如竖起中指；（3）模仿性手势，如拇指舞，表示“给我发短信”。

#↩

PROFESSION AND RECREATION

职业与休闲

People often take their identity from what they do for a living. Some take a second identity from what they do for play: golfer, hunter, body builder, and the like. Determine what your character does in both cases and then how much it means to who she is.

人们常常从职业中汲取身份认同。有些人则从业余爱好中获得第二身份认同，例如高尔夫球手、猎人、健美运动员等等。请确定你的角色在这两种情况下分别从事哪些活动，以及这些活动对她的人格塑造有多重要。

#↩

HOME AND TRANSPORTATION

家居与交通

Honore de Balzac said, “Show me what a man owns and I’ll tell you who he is.” The extended self puts its arms around all it owns. For most characters, their two biggest extra-identities are their house and car. Picture them both, then look inside.

奥诺雷·德·巴尔扎克说过：“告诉我一个人拥有什么，我就能告诉你他是什么样的人。” 延伸的自我将他所拥有的一切囊括其中。对大多数人物而言，他们最重要的两个额外身份就是他们的房子和车。想象一下它们，然后仔细观察它们的内部。

#↩

KNOWLEDGE AND IGNORANCE

知识与无知

What does my character know and not know? The amount and quality of her formal education set the ground for this question, but beyond that, life lessons passed and flunked will also matter.

我的角色知道什么，又不知道什么？她接受的正规教育的数量和质量决定了这个问题的基础，但除此之外，她经历过的和没经历过的生活教训也同样重要。

#↩

RELIGION AND BELIEFS

宗教与信仰

A character’s core beliefs, ranging from whether or not God exists to whether or not people can be trusted, determine her choices in the face of conflict. So start a conversation about values. Ask your character if human beings are good or evil, listen to her answer, and keep her talking.

角色的核心信念，从上帝是否存在到人与人之间是否值得信任，决定了她在面对冲突时的选择。所以，不妨和角色展开关于价值观的对话。问问她，人类是善还是恶，认真倾听她的回答，并引导她继续说下去。

#↩

CONVERSATION

对话

If you spend enough time with your character, patterns of talk will recur—money, politics, death, her husband, her children, her health, the latest tech, or ancient history. What she talks about is what she thinks about.

如果你花足够的时间与你的角色相处，你会发现一些反复出现的话题——金钱、政治、死亡、她的丈夫、她的孩子、她的健康、最新的科技，或者古代历史。她谈论什么，就代表她思考什么。

#↩

MANNERS

礼仪

Edmund Burke believed that politeness and manners give birth to all other virtues and are ultimately more important than laws. To put it in twenty-first-century terms, Burke knew that the quality of respect human beings show one another sets the tone for every relationship inside a civilization. How does your character treat people? 10

埃德蒙·伯克认为，礼貌和礼仪孕育了其他一切美德，并且最终比法律更为重要。用二十一世纪的话来说，伯克深知，人与人之间相互尊重的程度，决定了文明中所有关系的基调。你的品格如何待人？

#↩

IMPLICIT TRAITS

隐性特征

All characters begin in mystery. Their outer traits offer clues to possibilities that lie beneath. As scenes unfold, the reader/audience treats the outer traits of each role as clues to their inner traits. So these must be thoroughly explored and mined as well. Here are some ways to think about personalities, intelligence, attitudes, emotions, and more.

所有角色都以神秘的面貌出现。他们的外在特征暗示着隐藏在表面之下的可能性。随着剧情的展开，读者/观众会将每个角色的外在特征视为其内在特质的线索。因此，这些外在特征也必须被深入挖掘和探索。以下是一些思考角色性格、智力、态度、情感等方面的方法。

#↩

VARIETIES OF PERSONALITY

人格的种类

Personalities come in a seemingly infinite array. In 319 BC, Theophrastus, a student of Aristotle, tried to catalogue every ill-behaved character-type he could imagine from “Flatterer” to “Slanderer” but stopped at just thirty. 11 In recent centuries, sharp-eyed humorists, such as Mark Twain, have noted modern versions of the pain in the neck, and some listed noble types as well, but still, no one sees an end.

人格类型似乎无穷无尽。公元前319年，亚里士多德的学生泰奥弗拉斯托斯试图列举他能想象到的所有不良人格类型，从“奉承者”到“诽谤者”，但最终只列出了三十种。近几个世纪以来，像马克·吐温这样眼光敏锐的幽默作家也注意到了现代社会中各种令人讨厌的性格类型，有些人甚至列举了一些高尚的人格类型，但即便如此，似乎也没有人能穷尽所有类型。

To make sense of this anarchy, psychologists have clustered the universe of personalities inside five grand galaxies. As outlined below, each presents a spectrum that runs from positive to negative. The personality of any character you create should fit somewhere inside each of these binaries of behavior.

为了理解这种混乱无序的性格模式，心理学家将人格世界归纳为五大类。如下所述，每类性格都呈现出从积极到消极的连续谱。你所创造的任何角色的性格都应该契合于这些二元行为模式之中。

#↩

1. Openness/Closedness

1. 开放性/封闭性

Openness reflects independence, curiosity, love of the arts, and all things new. A highly open character enjoys euphoric experiences such as skydiving and gambling but may seem unpredictable or unfocused. Conversely, closedness suggests pragmaticism, perseverance, and, occasionally, dogmatic single-mindedness.

开放的性格体现了独立性、好奇心、对艺术的热爱以及对一切新鲜事物的渴求。性格开放的人喜欢跳伞、赌博等刺激的体验，但可能显得难以捉摸或缺乏专注力。相反，封闭的性格则暗示着务实、坚韧，有时甚至会表现出固执己见。

#↩

2. Conscientiousness/Capriciousness

2. 尽责性/任性

Conscientiousness leads to a sense of honor, self-discipline, and planned rather than impulsive behavior. Extreme conscientiousness is often perceived as stubbornness and obsession. Capriciousness may be spontaneous, but it can also seem unreliable and sloppy.

尽责性会带来荣誉感、自律性和计划性而非冲动性的行为。过分尽责往往会被视为固执和执着。任性或许是自发的，但也可能显得不可靠和马虎。

#↩

3. Extraversion/Introversion

3. 外向/内向

The extravert leans toward sociability, talkativeness, and assertiveness, often becoming attention-seeking and overbearing. The introvert may be a shy, reflective personality and yet perceived as aloof or self-absorbed.

外向者倾向于社交、健谈和自信，常常显得爱出风头且咄咄逼人。内向者可能性格害羞、沉思，但却可能被认为冷漠或自我中心。

#↩

4. Agreeableness/Argumentativeness

4. 亲和力/好辩性

Agreeableness tends to reflect compassion and generosity. All-smiles agreeableness is often seen as naïve or foolish. Argumentativeness can make one antagonistic, competitive, suspicious, and untrustworthy.

和蔼可亲往往体现出同情心和慷慨。但总是笑容满面的和蔼可亲常常被视为天真或愚蠢。好辩则可能使人变得敌对、好胜、多疑且不可信赖。

#↩

5. Rationality/Neuroticism

5. 理性/神经质

Rationality encourages a calm, constant personality which, when pushed to its limits, may turn coldhearted and indifferent. Neuroticism, on the other hand, experiences negative emotions such as anger and anxiety, sadness and fear quickly and extremely. Fragile and insecure, a neurotic hungers for stability. 12

理性培养出冷静、沉稳的性格，但当这种性格被推向极限时，可能会变得冷酷无情。而神经质则相反，它会迅速且强烈地体验到愤怒、焦虑、悲伤和恐惧等负面情绪。脆弱且缺乏安全感的神经质者渴望稳定。

These five spectra, mixed and merged, create endless possibilities. But beyond these types, I think the reason personalities are so various is simple. Coincidence. Every human being is a combination of determinism and chance. The trillions of daily collisions between human genomes and countless aspects of their environments are so random, so unpredictable, so riddled with luck, good and bad, that they generate an infinite variety of selves.

这五种光谱混合融合，创造出无限的可能性。但除了这些类型之外，我认为人格如此多样的原因很简单：巧合。每个人都是决定论和偶然性的结合。人类基因组与无数环境因素之间每天发生的数万亿次碰撞，如此随机、如此不可预测，充满了运气（无论好坏），以至于产生了无穷无尽的个体多样性。

What’s more, personalities bend and flex depending on the nature of relationships such as boss-employee, parent-child, lover-friend. This pattern holds, not only for her voice but her gestures, facial expression, posture, word choices, temperament, and the like. In other words, her personality sets certain limits, but as she engages in her social and personal relationships, she shifts expression from one quality to the next.

此外，人的性格会根据人际关系的性质而有所变化，例如老板与员工、父母与子女、恋人与朋友等。这种模式不仅体现在她的声音上，也体现在她的手势、面部表情、姿态、用词、性情等等方面。换句话说，她的性格设定了一定的界限，但随着她参与社交和人际关系，她的表达方式也会从一种特质转变为另一种特质。

#↩

VARIETIES OF INTELLIGENCE

智能的种类

Have you given your character a mind fit to do what you want her to do? If you want her to do dumb things, is she convincingly dumb in all ways? Dumb dialogue? Dumb haircut? Or the reverse—smart to do smart? Above all, is she credible?

你是否赋予了角色一个能够完成你想让她做的事情的思维模式？如果你想让她做蠢事，她是否在各方面都表现得足够愚蠢，令人信服？比如，她说话愚蠢？发型愚蠢？或者反过来——她聪明到能做出聪明的事？最重要的是，她是否可信？

Give thought to more than your character’s IQ, but to her EQ and various CIs as well. IQ measures analytical thinking, spatial recognition, and problem solving. EQ measures emotional intelligence—the ability to perceive a subtle variety of feelings and emotions in yourself and others. CIs measure creative intelligence (the power of imagination), intellectual curiosity (the drive to know), and cultural intelligence (the ability to thrive in foreign settings).

除了智商（IQ）之外，还要考虑角色的情商（EQ）和各种文化智能（CI）。智商衡量分析思维、空间认知和问题解决能力。情商衡量情绪智力——感知自身和他人的细微感受和情绪的能力。文化智能衡量创造性智力（想象力）、求知欲（求知的动力）和文化智能（在异国环境中适应的能力）。

Starting with your character’s particular mix of intelligences, what are her habits of thought? Every human being, for example, develops a personal strategy for relationships. If her method has worked in the past, it doesn’t easily bend when circumstances demand change. How flexible is your character’s mind?

首先，从你笔下人物独特的智能组合入手，想想她的思维习惯是什么？例如，每个人都会发展出一套处理人际关系的策略。如果这种方法过去行之有效，那么当环境需要改变时，它就不会轻易改变。你笔下人物的思维有多灵活？

#↩

ATTITUDES, BELIEFS, VALUES

态度、信念、价值观

What are your character’s attitudes? Her likes and dislikes? Loves and hates? Fears and dreads? Is she optimistic? Pessimistic?

你笔下的人物性格如何？她喜欢什么，讨厌什么？她害怕什么，忧虑什么？她是乐观主义者还是悲观主义者？

To get answers, interrogate your character. What she thinks about herself shapes her beliefs, so ask the key psychological question first: “Who are you?” Does her answer describe her inner nature or name her profession? How much of an identity has she carved out for herself and how much is wrapped up in her career?

要想找到答案，就要深入剖析你的角色。她如何看待自己会塑造她的信念，所以首先要问自己一个关键的心理问题：“你是谁？”她的答案描述的是她的内在本质，还是她的职业？她为自己塑造了多少身份认同，又有多少与她的职业生涯息息相关？

Ask big questions such as “What do you wish to achieve in the future? What must you do for yourself? For others? What must you never do to yourself? To others? How do you judge the essential nature of mankind? Good? Evil? Some of both?”

提出一些意义深远的问题，例如“你希望在未来取得什么成就？你必须为自己做些什么？为他人做些什么？你绝不能对自己做什么？对他人做什么？你如何评判人性的本质？善？恶？还是两者兼有？”

#↩

EMOTION, MOOD, TEMPERAMENT

情绪、心情、气质

Emotion is the side effect of change. As the dominant value in a character’s life changes charge from positive (e.g., wealth) to negative (e.g., poverty), the character suffers a negative emotion; as the value charge moves from negative (e.g., pain) to positive (e.g., pleasure), the character’s mood changes to delight. 13 These experiences, however, are relative to what the character sees as meaningful in her life—what’s negative, what’s positive.

情绪是变化的副产品。当一个角色生活中的主导价值观从正面（例如，财富）转变为负面（例如，贫穷）时，角色会产生负面情绪；当价值观从负面（例如，痛苦）转变为正面（例如，快乐）时，角色的情绪就会转变为愉悦。然而，这些体验都取决于角色对生活中意义的理解——什么是负面的，什么是正面的。

If you were to put your character in a romantic relationship, and then have her lover walk out on her, how would change in the key values of Love/Hate, Happiness/Sadness, and Companionship/Loneliness change her mood? It may not be what you expect.

如果你让你的角色陷入一段恋爱关系，然后她的爱人离开了她，那么爱/恨、快乐/悲伤和陪伴/孤独这几个关键价值观的变化会如何影响她的情绪？这可能与你预想的不同。

Mood is a character trait that tends to draw the same reaction from different experiences. Sober-minded people, for example, often find fun-loving hobbies, such as folk dancing and drone flying, boring and annoying.

情绪是一种性格特征，它往往会对不同的经历产生相同的反应。例如，性格沉稳的人常常觉得像民间舞蹈和无人机飞行这类充满乐趣的爱好枯燥乏味，甚至令人厌烦。

Children have temperaments; adults have personalities. Temperament is the by-product of a character’s brain chemistry, whereas personality is the by-product of socialization. As a child interacts with her world, her temperament evolves from juvenile to adolescent to adult. But no matter how mature she may become, her childhood temperament will follow like her shadow. Is she overall cheery or grouchy? Focused or daydreamy? Thrill-seeking or reclusive? Her fifth-grade teacher could tell you.

孩子有气质，大人有性格。气质是大脑化学反应的产物，而性格则是社会化过程的产物。随着孩子与世界的互动，她的气质会从幼稚期发展到青春期，最终走向成熟。但无论她变得多么成熟，童年的气质都会如影随形。她总体上是开朗活泼还是脾气暴躁？是专注认真还是爱做白日梦？是追求刺激还是孤僻内向？她的五年级老师或许能告诉你答案。

One spectrum of temperament, for example, runs from authoritarianism to antiauthoritarianism. Does your character back in-groups or defend out-groups? Authoritarians favor militarism and religious fundamentalism; antiauthoritarians reject both. Authoritarians look on artists with suspicion; artists, especially comic artists, ridicule authority. Authoritarians champion family unity and the self-discipline of being on time for a job they don’t like very much and then putting in eight productive hours without attitude; antiauthoritarians often flit from job to job, dragging their children with them, forever in search of personal fulfillment.

例如，气质的一个光谱从专制主义延伸到反专制主义。你的性格是支持内部群体还是捍卫外部群体？专制主义者倾向于军国主义和宗教原教旨主义；反专制主义者则反对这两者。专制主义者对艺术家抱有怀疑；艺术家，尤其是漫画家，会嘲讽权威。专制主义者推崇家庭团结和自律，即使自己并不喜欢这份工作，也要准时上班，然后默默地高效工作八小时；反专制主义者则常常频繁更换工作，带着孩子四处奔波，永远在追寻个人成就感。

#↩

MIRROR, WORLD, AUTHOR

镜子，世界，作者

The person a character sees in her makeup mirror today depends in great part on her past. Her memories, however, tend to be interpretations of what happened rather than actual events. The moment an event hits a character’s life, her mind begins to reshape its details, cut much of it, reorder some of it, and often invent things that never happened. From her reconstruction, she construes the meaning of the event and how it affects who she is.

如今，一个角色在化妆镜中看到的自己，很大程度上取决于她的过去。然而，她的记忆往往是对已发生事件的诠释，而非事件本身。当某个事件闯入她的生活时，她的思维便开始重塑事件的细节，删减许多内容，重新排列部分内容，甚至常常虚构一些从未发生过的事情。通过这种重构，她理解了事件的意义以及它如何影响了她自身。

Others who witnessed the event will have a second, rather different, interpretation; you, as author, know the facts and have a third point of view; the reader/audience adds a fourth.

其他目睹事件的人会有第二种截然不同的解读；作为作者，你了解事实，并有第三种观点；读者/观众则提出了第四种观点。

As you write, alternate from all points of view, until every trait, explicit and implicit, serves one purpose: characterization.

写作时，要从各种角度交替叙述，直到每一个特征，无论是显性的还是隐性的，都服务于一个目的：塑造人物形象。

#↩

EXPRESSING CHARACTERIZATION

表达特征

A characterization can be expressed by what it is, what it is not, and what it is like. These three general categories offer the writer at least nine distinctive techniques:

人物刻画可以从“是什么”、“不是什么”和“像什么”三个方面来表达。这三大类概括性的内容至少为作者提供了九种独特的写作技巧：

1. Simile: an analogy that compares a characterization to other people or things. James Thurber, for example, said his boss at the New Yorker “looked like a dishonest Abe Lincoln.”
1. 明喻：一种将人物形象与其他人或事物进行比较的类比手法。例如，詹姆斯·瑟伯说他在《纽约客》的老板“看起来像个不诚实的亚伯拉罕·林肯”。
2. Metaphor: a direct link that connects a characterization to other people or things. Like the above, you may draw on figures from history, mythology, literature, or pop culture: “She’s the Tony Soprano of self-control.”
2. 比喻：将人物描述与其他人或事物直接联系起来。例如，你可以借鉴历史、神话、文学或流行文化中的人物：“她是自制力方面的托尼·索普拉诺。”
3. Correlations: characterization as an extension of personal habits or possessions. “She found her hair color in the same place she found her courage… a bottle.”
3. 关联性：将人物特征视为个人习惯或物品的延伸。“她找到自己喜欢的发色，就像她找到勇气一样……那是一瓶酒。”
4. Contrasts: Differences compare generally: “She’s unlike the typical college grad.”
4. 对比：差异比较一般而言：“她不像典型的大学毕业生。”
5. Oppositions: Contradictions compare more sharply: “She’s an anti-intellectual PhD.”
5. 对立面：矛盾之处更加尖锐：“她是一位反智的博士。”
6. Telling: Sometimes readers may need telling language to picture a characterization: “She stood six feet, two inches tall,” but onstage or on-screen, the audience sees the actor and instinctively judges her height.
6. 叙述：有时读者可能需要叙述性的语言来想象人物形象：“她身高六英尺二英寸”，但在舞台上或银幕上，观众看到的是演员，并本能地判断她的身高。
7. Showing: actions for the eye: “At six-two, she had to duck into my car,” or for the ear: “When she got in my car, I heard Crack! as her skull smacked the door frame, followed by ‘God damn it!’” Both activate the imagination.
7. 展示：视觉动作：“她身高六英尺二英寸，不得不弯腰钻进我的车里。”或者听觉动作：“她钻进我的车里时，我听到‘咔嚓’一声，她的头骨撞到了车门框上，接着是‘该死的！’”两者都能激发想象力。
8. Self-assessments: What the character says about herself may or may not be true, given the gift people have for self-deception, but that she says it and to whom can be a clue to characterization. “I’m a people person.”
8. 自我评价：角色对自己的评价可能属实，也可能不属实，毕竟人们都擅长自欺欺人，但她会这样说，以及对谁说，都可以成为塑造人物性格的线索。“我善于与人交往。”
9. Other-assessments: What one person says about another may or may not be true, given the axes people have to grind, but that it is said and by whom can be an important clue to characterization. “She says she’s a people person, but…”
9. 其他评价：一个人对另一个人的评价可能属实，也可能不属实，毕竟每个人都有自己的私利，但评价本身以及评价者是谁，却能提供重要的线索来了解人物性格。“她说她很会与人交往，但是……”

In “The Short Happy Life of Francis Macomber,” Hemingway introduces Margot Macomber with an inventory of her traits, then seals her true character with a past choice:

在《弗朗西斯·麦康伯短暂而幸福的一生》中，海明威通过列举玛戈·麦康伯的性格特征来介绍她，然后用她过去的一个选择来奠定她真正的性格：

She was an extremely handsome and well-kept woman of the beauty and social position which had, five years before, commanded five thousand dollars as the price of endorsing, with photographs, a beauty product which she had never used.
她是一位容貌极其俊美、衣着考究的女子，拥有如此美貌和社会地位，五年前，她为一款自己从未用过的美容产品拍摄宣传照，就获得了五千美元的报酬。

The phrases “woman of the beauty” and “with photographs” flash the image of a face you might glimpse while paging a fashion magazine (explicit trait), while “well-kept” and “social position” give her an aura of privilege (implicit trait). That she took money to endorse a product she never used suggests an elastic morality (true character) and the dark events to come.

“美貌女子”和“有照片”这两个词组让人联想起翻阅时尚杂志时可能会瞥见的面孔（显性特征），而“保养得当”和“社会地位显赫”则赋予她一种特权的氛围（隐性特征）。她收钱代言自己从未使用过的产品，这暗示了她道德观的摇摆不定（真实性格），也预示着即将发生的悲剧。

#↩

YES, BUT WHO IS SHE, REALLY?

是的，但她究竟是谁？

The ancient adage “Nothing is what it seems” applies directly and deeply to character creation. Explicit and implicit traits form surfaces, and these surfaces hide a truth. Characterization, therefore, expresses only who a character appears to be and not, in fact, who she is.

“眼见未必为实”这句古老的格言，直接而深刻地适用于人物塑造。显性和隐性特征构成了人物的表象，而这些表象掩盖了真相。因此，人物刻画仅仅表达了人物的表象，而非其真实的本质。

When readers or audiences find a characterization credible and intriguing, their thoughts run something like this: “Interesting, but who is she really? Is she honest or dishonest? Loving or cruel? Strong or weak? Generous or selfish? Good or evil? What is her essential, true character?” The next chapter looks at the inner aspects of true character that live out of sight and inside the mind.

当读者或观众觉得某个人物形象塑造得可信且引人入胜时，他们的想法大致如下：“很有意思，但她究竟是怎样一个人？她诚实还是虚伪？慈爱还是残忍？坚强还是软弱？慷慨还是自私？善良还是邪恶？她真正的本质是什么？”下一章将探讨那些隐藏在人心深处、不为人知的性格特质。

#↩

8

THE INNER CHARACTER

内在性格

A character’s public and personal personae combine to form his characterization, the outer facade of who he seems to be. His private and hidden selves generate his true character, the inner person he is in fact. When we first encounter a character, we instinctively peer past the surface of characterization into his depths, seeking an answer to the question we always ask whenever we meet someone new: Who this person… really? As the character takes action in the face of conflict, answers arrive.

人物的公众形象和私人形象共同构成了他的性格刻画，也就是他外在的表象。而他私密而隐秘的自我则塑造了他的真实性格，也就是他内在的真实自我。当我们初次接触一个人物时，我们会本能地透过性格刻画的表象，探寻他的内心深处，试图解答我们每次遇到新朋友时都会问自己的那个问题：这个人……究竟是怎样一个人？随着人物在冲突中采取行动，答案也随之揭晓。

What a character chooses to do in his lightest moments expresses little because they cost him little, but at his darkest, when he’s up against powerful, negative forces, when risks are greatest, his actions reveal the truth. Who is he? Honest or a liar? Loving or cruel? Generous or selfish? Strong or weak? Compulsive or cool? Good or evil? Will he help or hinder? Will he comfort or punish? Will he give his life or take a life? What is his true character?

角色在最轻松的时刻所做的选择，往往无关紧要，因为代价微乎其微；但在最黑暗的时刻，当他面对强大的负面力量，面临最大的风险时，他的行动才会揭示真相。他究竟是谁？诚实还是虚伪？慈爱还是残忍？慷慨还是自私？坚强还是软弱？冲动还是冷静？善良还是邪恶？他会助人还是阻挠？他会安慰还是惩罚？他会献出生命还是夺走生命？他真正的品格是什么？

The character, of course, never asks these questions of himself. He may speculate about what other people think of him; he may wonder about what goes on in his subconscious; but only his author knows all. He created him. He knows his social and personal personae, plus every tactic of self-deception the character uses to hide from what he can’t face in himself.

当然，角色本人永远不会问自己这些问题。他或许会揣测别人对他的看法；或许会思考自己的潜意识里在想些什么；但只有他的作者才知道一切。作者创造了他。作者了解角色的社交和个人形象，以及角色用来掩盖自己无法面对的真相的每一种自欺欺人的手段。

To answer the question “Who is he?” the writer merges his character’s inner world of conscious thought with his hidden subconscious drives. Eventually, after much trial, error and improvisation, the two selves fuse into an irreducible true character.

为了回答“他是谁？”这个问题，作者将人物意识层面的内心世界与潜意识深处的驱动力融合在一起。最终，经过无数次的尝试、错误和即兴发挥，这两个自我融合为一个不可分割的真实人物。

Let’s look at the motivational forces that drive these complex characters:

让我们来看看驱动这些复杂人物的动机：

#↩

MOTIVATION: PUTTING CHARACTER INTO ACTION

动机：将品格付诸行动

Why do people do the things they do?
人们为什么会做他们所做的事？
—Every psychologist’s dying thought
——每位心理学家临终前的想法

Motivation is the least understood term in the writer’s vocabulary and a conundrum for psychologists as well. When researchers ask their subjects why they do what they do, back come rationalizations, not insights. The whys of character action run much deeper than alibis, so let’s first trace their sources.

“动机”是作家词汇中最难理解的术语，也是心理学家们面临的一个难题。当研究人员询问受试者为何做出某种行为时，得到的往往是各种理由，而非深刻的见解。人物行为背后的原因远比借口复杂得多，因此，我们首先需要追溯其根源。

Do the forces that drive human beings press from behind in the past or pull from ahead in the future? 1 In my view, motives and desires form two very different energies. Motivations plant their footings in a character’s past and push from behind, while desires anchor the future and entice a character toward what’s yet to come. 2

驱动人类的力量是来自过去的背后推动，还是来自未来的引领？在我看来，动机和欲望构成了两种截然不同的能量。动机植根于人物的过去，从背后推动；而欲望则锚定未来，引诱人物走向未知。

Scientific theories about what pushes from the past divide into two groups: drives rooted in genes versus pressures wrought by social forces.

关于过去驱动力的科学理论分为两类：基因驱动力与社会力量带来的压力。

#↩

INSIDE-OUT MOTIVATIONS

由内而外的动机

Every human being is born with a collection of drives for survival, love, meaning, and more. These hungers are subconscious and unfocused. Like winds billowing a ship’s sails, they push from behind and urge a character forward. A motivation, therefore, is an unsated appetite.

每个人生来就拥有一系列对生存、爱、意义等等的渴望。这些渴望是潜意识的，也是无目的的。它们如同风吹动船帆一般，从背后推动着人前进。因此，动机就是一种永不满足的欲望。

When there’s nothing to eat, man does indeed live by bread alone. But once fed, his higher internal motivations emerge, and when these are satisfied, newer, still higher drives arise, and so on in a never-ending hunger for something greater. A human being is a perpetually wanting animal.

当食物匮乏时，人的确只靠面包生存。但一旦饱腹，更高层次的内在动力便会涌现；当这些动力得到满足后，更新、更高层次的欲望又会涌现，如此循环往复，永无止境地追求更伟大的事物。人是一种永不满足的动物。

Below are a dozen inner motivations in human nature, ranked from primal to elevated. Review this checklist to see if, when, and how they drive your character.

以下列出了人类本性中的十二种内在动机，按从原始到高尚的顺序排列。请参考这份清单，看看它们是否、何时以及如何影响你的性格。

#↩

1. Immortality

1. 永生

Death, according to Ernest Becker, is life’s most powerful motivator. 3 Knowing we must die inspires the wish to leave behind something of value to symbolize, like a gravestone, that we were here. Indeed, the dread of death motivates humanity to build monuments to itself: cities and their skyscrapers, religions and their sanctuaries, universities and their libraries, and, most immortally, works of art. The most lasting expression of our Ice Age ancestors is the paintings they left on the walls of the caves. Ever since the first burial rites over one hundred thousand years ago, everything human beings have put on this earth is simply one vast immortality project.

根据欧内斯特·贝克尔的说法，死亡是生命中最强大的动力。 3 意识到我们终将一死，便会激发我们留下一些有价值的东西来象征，就像墓碑一样，证明我们曾存在过。的确，对死亡的恐惧驱使人类建造各种纪念碑：城市及其摩天大楼、宗教及其圣地、大学及其图书馆，以及最不朽的艺术作品。我们冰河时代祖先留下的最持久的印记，便是他们在洞穴墙壁上绘制的壁画。自从十多万年前出现最早的葬礼仪式以来，人类在这片土地上创造的一切都不过是一项庞大的永生工程。

#↩

2. Survival

2. 生存

The imperative to survive compels all living things toward what they perceive as positive. This is why mousetraps work. The human sense of what’s positive, however, hinges on complex subjectivities. If a human being views an action as necessary for survival but at the same time immoral, he will, after some hesitation, ultimately act to survive. Moral/Immoral, Good/Evil, Right/Wrong, and Survival/Extinction are four very different sets of values. The first three pairs express the ideal; the last reflects the real. From a character’s point of view, any action that preserves his genes—in himself, his family, his tribe—is positive. This is why wars work.

生存的本能驱使所有生物朝着它们认为积极的方向前进。这就是捕鼠器有效的原因。然而，人类对“积极”的感知却取决于复杂的主观性。如果一个人认为某种行为对于生存是必要的，但同时又不道德，那么在犹豫之后，他最终会为了生存而采取行动。道德/不道德、善/恶、对/错以及生存/灭绝是四组截然不同的价值体系。前三组代表理想状态；最后一组则反映了现实。从角色的角度来看，任何能够保存其基因——无论是自身、家庭还是部落的基因——的行为都是积极的。这就是战争有效的原因。

#↩

3. Balance

3. 平衡

A tiny scale in the brain weighs the positive versus negative charges around it, seeking balance. Radical imbalance threatens survival and takes sanity for a ride, so the mind naturally craves a sovereignty over its existence. When, for example, a crime tilts Justice/Injustice to the negative, society demands revenge as a positive charge that restores balance. When the three brothers in Ray Donovan murder the priest who molested them, all breathe a sigh of relief. Justice done, their lives finally rest in balance.

大脑中有一个微小的天平，它衡量着周围的正负电荷，力求达到平衡。极度失衡会威胁生存，甚至使人丧失理智，因此，人的思维自然渴望掌控自身的存在。例如，当犯罪使正义/不义的天平向负面倾斜时，社会就会要求复仇，将其作为一种正电荷来恢复平衡。在电影《雷·多诺万》中，当三兄弟杀死了性侵他们的神父后，他们都松了一口气。正义得到了伸张，他们的生活终于恢复了平衡。

#↩

4. Pleasure

4. 快乐

The craving for pleasure can be irresistible, even if it causes pain in the future. Victims of abuse, haunted by cruel memories, drown their nightmares in fathoms of opiate-induced amnesia, knowing full well that pleasure is temporary and even greater pain lies ahead.

对快乐的渴望往往难以抗拒，即使它会带来未来的痛苦。遭受虐待的受害者，被残酷的回忆所困扰，沉溺于鸦片类药物带来的失忆之中，试图以此麻痹自己，逃避噩梦，因为他们深知快乐只是暂时的，更大的痛苦还在前方等待着他们。

#↩

5. Sex

5. 性

At the turn of the twentieth century, many psychologists based their theories of human behavior on a single cause. The most famous was Sigmund Freud’s contention that sexual instincts drive all of life’s objectives.

二十世纪初，许多心理学家将人类行为理论建立在单一原因之上。其中最著名的是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的论断，即性本能驱动着人生的所有目标。

#↩

6. Power

6. 权力

Alfred Adler, originator of the “inferiority complex,” said that desire for power focuses all strivings. No matter where people perch on the social pyramid, they constantly survey those above and below, trying to measure their relative power.

“自卑情结”的提出者阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒认为，对权力的渴望驱动着人们的一切努力。无论人们在社会金字塔中处于什么位置，他们都会不断地审视自己上下的人，试图衡量自身的相对权力。

#↩

7. Empathy

7. 同理心

The hunger to belong creates tribes. With belonging comes the feeling that if one member suffers, all others ache in empathetic harmony, and somehow that makes people feel better. 4

归属感催生了群体。归属感带来一种感觉：如果一个成员遭受痛苦，其他成员都会感同身受，这种共鸣会让人感到慰藉。

#↩

8. More

8. 更多

Enough is never enough. Avarice progresses in three steps:

永远都不够。贪婪的滋生分为三个阶段：

A. Greed: the craving for more. Human beings are insatiable and eternally disappointed. When a character wants more than he can reasonably expect, he lives in a state of emptiness. “I pay more and more for greater and greater dissatisfactions,” complained Antonia Wolff to Carl Jung in Morris West’s novel The World Is Made of Glass .

A. 贪婪：对更多事物的渴望。人类永不满足，永远失望。当一个人想要的东西超过他合理所能期望的时，他便生活在一种空虚之中。“我付出越来越多的代价，却得到越来越大的不满，”安东尼娅·沃尔夫在莫里斯·韦斯特的小说《世界是玻璃做的》中向卡尔·荣格抱怨道。

B. Envy: the tortured feeling that someone has something you don’t. When a desired thing seems forever out of reach, the urge to gain the thing reverses into an urge to destroy it. If destructiveness fails, the envious character wallows in self-pity.

B. 嫉妒：一种痛苦的感觉，因为别人拥有你没有的东西。当渴望之物似乎永远遥不可及时，想要得到它的冲动就会转化为想要摧毁它的冲动。如果破坏行为失败，嫉妒者就会沉溺于自怜之中。

In Shakespeare’s The Tragedy of Othello , Iago envies Othello’s prowess and prestige, so he destroys him; in Herman Melville’s Billy Budd , Claggart envies Billy’s beauty and goodness, so he destroys him.

在莎士比亚的《奥赛罗》中，伊阿古嫉妒奥赛罗的英勇和威望，于是毁灭了他；在赫尔曼·梅尔维尔的《比利·巴德》中，克拉加特嫉妒比利的俊美和善良，于是毁灭了他。

C. Jealousy: Envy escalates into jealousy when a rival enters. Jealousy reaches fever pitch when it fears that a beloved prefers a rival.

C. 嫉妒：当竞争对手出现时，羡慕会升级为嫉妒。当担心心爱之人更喜欢竞争对手时，嫉妒会达到极致。

In Amadeus , Salieri seethes with envy of Mozart’s talent. He pleads with God, “Why Mozart? Why not me?” In a rage, he rips a crucifix off the wall and burns it in the fireplace. Risking damnation, greedy for esteem, riven by jealousy, and desperate for the adoration of Vienna’s music patrons, Salieri destroys his young rival, Mozart.

在《莫扎特传》中，萨列里对莫扎特的才华充满了嫉妒。他向上帝祈祷：“为什么是莫扎特？为什么不是我？”盛怒之下，他扯下墙上的十字架，扔进壁炉烧掉。萨列里不顾下地狱的风险，贪图名誉，被嫉妒折磨，一心想要赢得维也纳音乐赞助人的崇拜，最终摧毁了他年轻的竞争对手莫扎特。

#↩

9. Interest

9. 利息

The difference between “want to” and “have to” is all the difference in the world. That’s why a repetitious job is a shit job, no matter the paycheck, and its only cure is curiosity. The mind prefers doing things for their own sake. It likes tasks that demand skill, jobs done right, problems that need solutions simply because they’re problems. This is why the creative process satisfies more than the finished work. Means is its end.

“想做”和“不得不做”之间的差别，简直天壤之别。这就是为什么重复性的工作无论薪水多高都是糟糕的工作，而唯一的解药就是好奇心。人的大脑更喜欢为了做事本身而做事。它喜欢需要技巧的任务，喜欢把工作做好，喜欢那些仅仅因为是问题就需要解决的问题。这就是为什么创造的过程比最终的作品更能带来满足感。过程即是目的。

#↩

10. Meaning

10. 含义

Victor Frankl believed that a meaningless life is a life of vertigo, dizzily out of control. 5 When people get what they thought they wanted—money, fame, a C-suite job—they often fall into depression. Achievement ends the struggle that gave their lives purpose. The obvious solution would be to search for a new, even deeper purpose, but for many people, one life purpose per lifetime is all they’ll ever know.

维克多·弗兰克尔认为，毫无意义的人生如同眩晕，令人头晕目眩，失去控制。当人们得到他们以为自己想要的东西——金钱、名誉、高管职位——时，他们往往会陷入抑郁。成就终结了赋予他们人生意义的奋斗。显而易见的解决办法是寻找新的、更深刻的人生意义，但对许多人来说，一生中只有一个人生意义，这就是他们所能了解的全部。

#↩

11. Fulfillment

11. 实现

A self-knowing mind senses its untapped humanity, its mental and emotional potential. The thoughtful character longs to plumb those depths and fulfill his inner promise.

一个有自知之明的人能够感知到自身尚未开发的精神潜能，以及心理和情感上的无限可能。深思熟虑的人渴望探索这些潜能的深处，并实现其内在的承诺。

#↩

12. Transcendence

12. 超越

Carl Jung believed that the ultimate motivation is a subconscious longing for Faustian supremacy, for godlike knowledge beyond the mind’s reach—a metaphysical perfection.

卡尔·荣格认为，最终的动机是潜意识里对浮士德式至高无上的渴望，对超越心灵极限的神一般的知识的渴望——一种形而上学的完美。

These internal drives, in various combinations, often unawares and beyond control, push us toward the future. Like prehistoric man, we are still kind to friends and fierce to enemies. Progress gives us hospitals instead of magicians, nuclear missiles instead of bows and arrows. Science has made us more efficient at either helping people or killing them, but motivation never changes. 6

这些内在驱动力，以各种组合形式，往往在我们不知不觉中、不受控制地推动着我们走向未来。如同史前人类一样，我们依然善待朋友，对待敌人凶狠。进步带给我们的是医院而非魔法师，是核导弹而非弓箭。科学让我们在帮助他人或杀戮他人方面更加高效，但动机却从未改变。

#↩

OUTSIDE-IN MOTIVATIONS

由外而内的动机

Now let’s take the reverse point of view and look at motivation from the outside in.

现在让我们换个角度，从外部视角来看待动机。

A storyteller studies his setting’s social institutions—economic, political, religious—to measure their impact on his cast. Although cultural systems influence trends (consider the vast effect of social media), if a writer imposes a theory of mass motivation on a specific character, he risks mistaking conditions for causes. Poverty and wealth, for example, are conditions, not causes. The physical and psychological pains caused by poverty may influence a character to become a spiritual leader to relieve suffering, or they may influence a violent criminal to add to it. Or he may simply grit his teeth and persevere. Neither poverty nor wealth cause crime directly. Felons inhabit both extremes in more or less equal percentages.

故事讲述者会研究其故事背景中的社会制度——经济、政治、宗教——以衡量它们对笔下人物的影响。尽管文化体系会影响潮流（想想社交媒体的巨大影响），但如果作家将某种大众动机理论强加于某个特定人物，他就有可能把条件误认为原因。例如，贫穷和财富只是条件，而非原因。贫穷带来的身心痛苦可能促使一个人物成为精神领袖以减轻苦难，也可能促使一个暴力罪犯加剧苦难。或者，他可能只是咬紧牙关，默默忍受。贫穷和财富都不会直接导致犯罪。罪犯在贫富两端所占的比例大致相等。

So for an external social force (e.g., a TV commercial) to motivate a character to act, it must first strike the character’s senses (he sees an ad), and then work its way through his subconscious motivators (arousing an appetite) before he finally chooses an action (buying something). Massive social forces certainly influence a cast, but they must work their way through each unique personality, and who knows what will come out the other side?

因此，外部社会力量（例如电视广告）要想促使角色采取行动，首先必须触动角色的感官（他看到了广告），然后才能影响他的潜意识动机（唤起食欲），最终促使他做出选择（购买商品）。巨大的社会力量固然会影响演员阵容，但它们必须逐个作用于每个角色的独特个性，最终会产生怎样的结果，谁也无法预料。

Because a character is educated doesn’t mean he’s sophisticated; because he’s ignorant doesn’t mean he’s crude; because he’s a servant doesn’t mean he’s servile. The same painful events that destroy one character may inspire another, while a third sleeps it off. 7 When a specific character acts in a specific scene, the effects of the surrounding culture become one of a kind and unpredictable.

受过教育并不意味着他老练世故；无知并不意味着他粗俗不堪；仆人的身份并不意味着他卑躬屈膝。同样的痛苦经历，或许会摧毁一个角色，却可能激励另一个角色，而第三个角色则会选择沉睡忘却。当特定角色在特定场景中采取行动时，周围文化的影响会变得独一无二且难以预料。

#↩

THE OBJECT OF DESIRE

欲望的对象

A classically told story opens with its protagonist’s life in overall balance, his ups and downs more or less routine. But then something happens: An inciting incident caused either by random chance or someone’s decision throws the protagonist’s life radically out of balance.

一个经典的故事开篇，主人公的生活总体上处于平衡状态，起起伏伏也基本按部就班。但随后，一些事情发生了：一个由偶然事件或某人的决定引发的突发事件，彻底打破了主人公生活的平衡。

An inciting incident could pivot a protagonist’s life sharply to the positive (Romeo falls for Juliet) or darkly to the negative (Hamlet discovers his father’s murder). In either case, when life goes out of kilter, a subconscious desire for a stable life stirs into consciousness. This drive for equilibrium becomes a character’s super-objective.

一个引发事件可能使主人公的人生急转直下，走向积极的方向（罗密欧爱上朱丽叶），也可能走向消极的方向（哈姆雷特发现父亲被谋杀）。无论哪种情况，当生活失去平衡时，潜意识中对稳定生活的渴望就会被唤醒。这种对平衡的追求成为角色最重要的目标。

Sensing that life has swung out of control, the protagonist imagines a solution in the form of a life change that’s expressed either situationally (committed love) or physically (dead villain). That which would bring about a positive change we call the object of desire. The protagonist feels that if he could secure this, his life would swing back on an even keel. Now that he knows what he wants, he’s able to act. His super-objective to restore life’s balance and his pursuit of his object of desire points him toward his story’s final crisis and climax.

主人公意识到生活已经失控，于是设想了一种解决方案：改变生活，这种改变可以是情境上的（忠贞的爱情），也可以是物质上的（杀死反派）。这种能带来积极改变的事物，我们称之为欲望对象。主人公觉得，如果能得到它，生活就能重回正轨。如今他明白了自己想要什么，便可以采取行动。他恢复生活平衡的终极目标，以及对欲望对象的追求，将他引向故事的最终危机和高潮。

In every story, the protagonist’s super-objective directs his action toward a unique object of desire. The Action Genre, for example, often aims at something you could hold in your hands. In Jaws , a dead shark. The Education Plot’s object of desire is usually something you could hold in your mind. In Ralph Ellison’s novel Invisible Man , the protagonist searches for an identity, an answer to the question “Who am I?”

在每个故事中，主人公的终极目标都指引着他的行动，指向一个独特的渴望对象。例如，动作片通常追求的是可以握在手中的东西，比如《大白鲨》中的死鲨鱼。而教育题材作品的渴望对象通常是可以存在于脑海中的东西。在拉尔夫·埃里森的小说《看不见的人》中，主人公寻找的是身份认同，是“我是谁？”这个问题的答案。

Therefore, a motivation (e.g., the lust for power) is an unfocused subconscious latency until an inciting incident spurs it to life and focuses it on a desire. By causing the need for a balanced future, the inciting incident puts motivation into action and forms the object of desire that pulls the protagonist through his story-long trek.

因此，某种动机（例如，对权力的渴望）原本处于潜意识中，尚未聚焦，直到某个诱发事件将其激活，并使其聚焦于某种欲望。诱发事件通过引发对平衡未来的渴望，将动机付诸行动，并形成推动主人公完成漫长旅程的欲望对象。

Examples:

例如：

In tragic plots, such as The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet , Romeo’s aroused libido (motivation #5) fixates on a stimulus (the exquisite Juliet) that inspires action (climbing a balcony) in pursuit of the protagonist’s ultimate object of desire (Juliet-as-wife).

在《罗密欧与朱丽叶》这样的悲剧情节中，罗密欧被唤起的性欲（动机#5）专注于某种刺激（美丽的朱丽叶），这种刺激激发了他采取行动（爬上阳台），以追求主人公最终的欲望对象（作为妻子的朱丽叶）。

In Action Plots, such as Vikings , a young warrior tastes victory for the first time and this inciting incident unites motivations #7 and #8, arousing his appetite to rule. The throne, his glittering object of desire, draws him toward the future.

在《维京传奇》这类动作题材作品中，一位年轻的战士初尝胜利的滋味，这一事件将第七和第八个动机融合在一起，激发了他统治的欲望。王位，他梦寐以求的荣耀，引领他走向未来。

In Degeneration Plots, such as A Confederacy of Dunces by John Kennedy Toole, The Tin Drum by Gunter Grass, Perfume by Patrick Suskind, and The Beauty Queen of Leenane by Martin McDonagh, protagonists suffer psychic traumas that ignite subconscious motivations #1, #2, and #3. Their objects of desire call for bizarre, even murderous, deeds until they end either suicidal or insane, or both.

在约翰·肯尼迪·图尔的《傻瓜联盟》、君特·格拉斯的《铁皮鼓》、帕特里克·聚斯金德的《香水》以及马丁·麦克唐纳的《利纳恩的选美皇后》等“堕落情节”中，主人公遭受精神创伤，从而激发了潜意识中的动机#1、#2和#3。他们渴望的对象驱使他们做出怪异的、甚至是谋杀的行为，直到他们最终走向自杀或精神错乱，或者两者兼而有之。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER THROUGH CHOICES

真我品格源于选择

How does a writer express a character’s inner nature?

作者如何表达人物的内心世界？

Not by characterization. In fact, the more fascinating a character’s outer behavior, the more the reader/audience wants to discover his true inner counterpoints: Jack seems tough, but where’s his soft spot?

并非通过人物刻画。事实上，一个角色的外在行为越引人入胜，读者/观众就越想发现他真正的内在反面：杰克看起来很坚强，但他的软肋在哪里？

Not by what others say about him. What one character believes about another may or may not be true, but what’s said and by whom may set up future revelations.

并非取决于他人对他的评价。一个人对另一个人的看法或许属实，或许不属实，但评价的内容以及评价者的身份，都可能为未来的揭示埋下伏笔。

Not by what a character says about himself. Audiences and readers listen to a character’s confessions or braggings with high skepticism. They know that people are as self-deceived as self-aware.

并非通过角色对自己的描述。观众和读者对角色的坦白或吹嘘都抱有高度怀疑。他们知道，人既有自知之明，也有自欺欺人的时候。

Instead, they look for events to build pressure and expose true character in the only way they trust: choices. A human being is the choices he makes over a lifetime.

相反，他们会寻找能够制造压力并揭露人真实性格的事件，而他们唯一信任的方式就是：选择。一个人的一生，就是他一生中所做的选择。

From amoebas to apes, all earthly critters obey nature’s First Law: Choose Life. Nature compels every living thing to preserve its genes by acting toward the positive as it sees the positive. What is a violent death to a gazelle is lunch to a lion.

从变形虫到猿猴，地球上所有生物都遵循着自然的第一法则：选择生命。自然驱使所有生物通过选择积极的方面来保存自身的基因。对瞪羚来说是惨烈的死亡，对狮子来说却是美味的午餐。

Nature’s bias of life over death channels all human choice toward the positive (anything that enhances life) and away from the negative (anything that hints of death). As Socrates taught, no one willingly does what he believes to be wrong; instead, everyone acts toward a perceived positive. In such matters, subjectivity is all. When survival demands it, the mind simply redefines immorality into virtue. 8

自然界对生命而非死亡的偏爱，引导着人类的所有选择趋向积极的（任何有益于生命的事物），远离消极的（任何与死亡相关的事物）。正如苏格拉底所教导的，没有人会心甘情愿地去做自己认为错误的事情；相反，每个人都会朝着自己认为积极的方向行动。在这样的事情上，主观性至关重要。当生存需要时，人的思维会将不道德的行为重新定义为美德。

If the reader/audience understands a character’s point of view and sees him confront a simple positive/negative choice (happiness/misery, right/wrong), they know in advance (probably before the character himself knows) how he will choose. He will reject the negative and choose what he perceives is the positive. The core self always does. It’s the First Law. Therefore, clear choices between negative and positive charges of the same thing (poverty versus wealth, ignorance versus wisdom, ugliness versus beauty) are trivial.

如果读者/观众理解了角色的视角，并看到他面临一个简单的正/负选择（幸福/痛苦，正确/错误），他们就能预先知道（可能比角色自己更早知道）他会如何选择。他会拒绝负面选项，选择他认为的正面选项。人的本性总是如此。这是第一定律。因此，对于同一事物的正反两面（贫穷与富有，无知与智慧，丑陋与美丽），简单的选择其实并不重要。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER THROUGH DILEMMA

困境中的真实品格

The only dramatically compelling and character-revealing decision is a choice between two things of more or less equal value. These dilemmas come in two varieties: positive and negative.

唯一能真正引人入胜、揭示人物性格的抉择，就是在两个价值大致相等的事物之间做出选择。这类两难困境分为两种：积极的和消极的。

A positive dilemma confronts a character with two equally desirable but irreconcilable possibilities. He wants both but circumstances force him to choose only one. For example, in the classic dilemma of Romantic Comedy, a woman finds herself caught between a man who is loving, devoted, and generous but boring versus another who is passionate, brilliant, and fascinating but certain to break her heart.

正向困境是指角色面临两个同样令人向往却又无法调和的选择。他两者都想要，但环境迫使他只能做出选择。例如，在经典的浪漫喜剧困境中，一位女性发现自己陷入两难：一个男人温柔体贴、忠诚慷慨，但却乏味无趣；另一个男人热情奔放、才华横溢、魅力四射，但却注定会让她心碎。

A negative dilemma confronts a character with two equally undesirable possibilities. He wants neither, but circumstances force him to choose one of two evils. For example, the classic marriage drama: If a woman doesn’t marry the man her family favors, they will disown her, but if she does marry her family’s pick, she will suffer a lifetime of boredom.

负面困境是指角色面临两种同样糟糕的选择。他两者都不想要，但环境迫使他二选一。例如，经典的婚姻悲剧：如果一个女人不嫁给家人属意的男人，就会被家人断绝关系；但如果她嫁给了家人选定的男人，就会终生孤独寂寞。

Clear choices are easily made and without jeopardy, but dilemma puts a character under pressure and at risk. A clear choice reveals little or nothing the reader/audience doesn’t already know; a decision in dilemma sends alternative choices running through a character’s imagination. As he struggles to make his choice, the push and pull of possibilities propels the reader’s/audience’s curiosity toward the story’s climax: What will he finally do?

明确的选择容易做出，也无需承担任何风险，但两难困境却会让角色承受压力，面临风险。明确的选择几乎不会揭示读者/观众未知的信息；而两难困境中的抉择则会引发角色脑海中各种可能性的碰撞。当他挣扎着做出选择时，各种可能性的拉扯推动着读者/观众的好奇心，最终将故事推向高潮：他最终会怎么做？

Either way he chooses, his action under pressure will reveal his true character.

无论他选择哪种方式，他在压力下的行为都将揭示他的真实性格。

Three examples: In No Country for Old Men , the Coen brothers’ film adaptation of Cormac McCarthy’s novel, Llewelyn Moss risks his life for $2.4 million in stolen drug money. He chooses the money and pays for it with the lives of both himself and his wife. In Sweat , a play by Lynn Nottage, Cynthia must choose between going on strike with her lifelong working-class pals versus her new job in low-level management. She chooses her job and sacrifices her friendships. In Less , a novel by Andrew Sean Greer, Arthur Less faces this dilemma: struggling for full creative achievement and the painful sacrifices that demands versus accepting less and gaining the pleasures of an easier life. He chooses the latter.

三个例子：在科恩兄弟根据科马克·麦卡锡的小说改编的电影《老无所依》中，卢埃林·莫斯为了240万美元的赃款冒着生命危险。他选择了金钱，却为此付出了自己和妻子的生命。在林恩·诺蒂奇的戏剧《汗水》中，辛西娅必须在与她一生的工人阶级朋友一起罢工和接受一份基层管理的新工作之间做出选择。她选择了工作，牺牲了友谊。在安德鲁·肖恩·格里尔的小说《少》中，亚瑟·莱斯面临着同样的困境：是努力追求充分的创作成就，并为此付出痛苦的牺牲，还是接受更少的成就，享受更轻松的生活。他选择了后者。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER THROUGH ANTAGONISM

通过对抗展现真我

When a character takes action in a high-risk dilemma, he inevitably provokes forces of antagonism in his world. To overcome these obstacles, he must continuously improvise anew. His choices are sometimes instinctive, sometimes deliberate, but always under pressure: He stands to lose in order to gain. The greater this risk-filled pressure, the deeper and truer his choice to who, at heart, he is.

当一个角色在高风险困境中采取行动时，他必然会激起周围世界的对抗力量。为了克服这些障碍，他必须不断地随机应变。他的选择有时出于本能，有时出于深思熟虑，但始终都处于压力之下：他必须承受失去才能获得。这种充满风险的压力越大，他的选择就越深刻、越真实地反映了他内心深处的自我。

As further events impact his life, his evolving nature chooses to conform or rebel, accept or reject his previous beliefs and values. No deeply felt experience is neutral; no choice is impartial; no action is impersonal. Thus, by choice and action he either civilizes or decivilizes himself, he either grows as a human being or shrivels.

随着人生经历的不断演变，他不断变化的本性会让他选择顺从或反叛，接受或摒弃以往的信仰和价值观。任何深刻的体验都不是中立的；任何选择都不是公正的；任何行动都不是客观的。因此，通过选择和行动，他要么使自己文明化，要么使自己堕落；要么成长为更成熟的人，要么走向衰败。

Degrees of pressure, therefore, measure the depth and quality of true character. How, for example, do we know for certain whether a character is honest or dishonest? When nothing is at risk, pressure is light and therefore telling the truth painless. But when everything, even life itself, is at stake, when consequences stretch to the limits of human endurance, then excruciating pressure builds around the choice to tell the truth or lie. Whichever way the character acts, his choice delivers a profound insight into his core self.

因此，压力的程度可以衡量人格的深度和品质。例如，我们如何才能确定一个人是诚实还是不诚实呢？当一切都不成问题时，压力很小，说真话也就不费吹灰之力。但当一切都岌岌可危，甚至生命都面临威胁，当后果逼近人类承受的极限时，选择说真话还是说谎就会承受巨大的压力。无论角色如何选择，他的选择都深刻地揭示了他的内心世界。

Once a character chooses a tactic, he hands the doing of the deed to his agent self, who then takes on one of his personal or social personae. When not directing the show, the core self spends the day like a documentary film crew, watching, listening, and recording every interesting thing his outer selves do. Afterward, the core self usually wishes he had done things a bit better.

一旦角色选定了某种策略，他就会将行动交给他的代理人，代理人会扮演他某个个人或社交人格。当不负责指挥时，核心自我就像纪录片摄制组一样，观察、聆听并记录他外在自我所做的每一件有趣的事情。事后，核心自我通常会希望自己当初做得更好一些。

When creating a complex character, imagine his values along spectra that run from extreme positives (e.g., love, courage, hope) to extreme negatives (e.g., hate, cowardice, despair). For example, if his life is in danger, where does he stand on the courage/cowardice spectrum? Complex characters feel some of both. If his life has lost meaning, how does he see his future along the hope/despair spectrum? If he’s in an intimate relationship, is he capable of love? Where along the love/hate spectrum would you place him?

在塑造一个复杂的人物时，可以设想他的价值观沿着一条从极端正面（例如爱、勇气、希望）到极端负面（例如恨、懦弱、绝望）的光谱分布。例如，如果他的生命受到威胁，他在勇气/懦弱光谱上处于什么位置？复杂的人物往往兼具这两种特质。如果他的人生失去了意义，他在希望/绝望光谱上如何看待自己的未来？如果他处于一段亲密关系中，他是否具备爱的能力？你会把他放在爱/恨光谱的哪个位置？

Consider the value of honesty/dishonesty. A character may appear truthful, others may say he is, he may insist he is, but how will a reader/ audience know for certain whether he’s an honest man, a liar, or morally flexible? If he has nothing to lose and chooses to tell the truth, his honesty seems trivial because it’s risk free. But if he’s under grave threat and he chooses to tell the truth when a lie would save his life, his depth of honesty seems profound. If, on the other hand, the character is a priest who, under threat, refuses to deny his faith, his honesty may seem less impressive because his sacred vows make his choice less free.

思考诚实/不诚实的价值。一个角色可能看起来很诚实，别人也可能这么说，他自己也可能坚持说自己诚实，但读者/观众如何才能确定他究竟是诚实的人、说谎的人，还是道德上模棱两可的人呢？如果他没什么可失去的，选择说真话，那么他的诚实似乎微不足道，因为没有风险。但如果他面临严重威胁，明明说谎可以保命却选择说真话，那么他的诚实就显得意义深远。另一方面，如果这个角色是一位牧师，在受到威胁时拒绝背弃信仰，那么他的诚实可能就不那么令人印象深刻了，因为他的神圣誓言使他的选择并非完全自由。

The interplay between choice and self gives the writer three grand principles to guide the work:

选择与自我之间的相互作用为作家提供了指导创作的三大原则：

1. When a character at risk and under pressure pursues desire, his choices of action express his true character.
1. 当一个身处险境、承受压力的人物追求欲望时，他的行动选择会体现他的真实性格。
2. The greater the risk and pressure, the deeper and truer the choice.
2. 风险和压力越大，选择就越深刻、越真实。
3. The freer the choice, the even deeper and truer the choice to a character’s identity.
3. 选择越自由，对角色身份的选择就越深刻、越真实。

Consider four tragic roles: Othello, Lear, Macbeth, and Hamlet. Brilliant characters all, but Hamlet is the most complex. Why? Choices. Othello’s jealousy blinds him, Lear’s daughters make his decisions for him, and the witches’ prophecies funnel Macbeth to his destiny. Hamlet’s choices are freer and more numerous. He might kill himself or not, revenge himself or not, love Ophelia or not, kill Polonius or not, find life meaningless or meaningful, stay sane or go crazy… all because of his unlimited freedom to choose.

想想四个悲剧角色：奥赛罗、李尔王、麦克白和哈姆雷特。他们都是杰出的人物，但哈姆雷特最为复杂。为什么？因为选择。奥赛罗被嫉妒蒙蔽了双眼，李尔王的女儿们替他做了决定，女巫的预言将麦克白引向了他的命运。哈姆雷特的选择则更加自由，也更加丰富。他可以选择自杀，也可以选择不自杀；可以选择复仇，也可以选择不复仇；可以选择爱奥菲莉亚，也可以选择不爱她；可以选择杀死波洛涅斯，也可以选择不杀他；可以选择觉得人生毫无意义，也可以选择觉得人生意义非凡；可以选择保持理智，也可以选择陷入疯狂……这一切都源于他拥有无限的选择自由。

Therefore, choice and character development relate this way: If a character makes only a few risk-free choices around a single value, he stays shallow and monodimensional. But if the character makes numerous risk-taking choices in the face of various values, he becomes complex and thus involves the reader/audience deeply in his inner life.

因此，选择与角色发展之间存在着这样的关系：如果一个角色只围绕单一价值观做出少数几个无风险的选择，那么他就会显得肤浅而单薄。但如果这个角色在面对各种价值观时做出许多冒险的选择，那么他就会变得复杂，从而让读者/观众更深入地了解他的内心世界。

For example: In the opening episodes of Succession , the autocratic Logan Roy (Brian Cox) dominates his coke-abusing son, Kendall (Jeremy Strong), giving him few if any choices. Kendall’s reactions make him seem weak, shallow, petty. But once he breaks free from his father and follows his own dangerous choices, his character gains heft and complexity, and wins our empathy.

例如：在《继承之战》的开篇几集中，专制的洛根·罗伊（布莱恩·考克斯饰）控制着他吸食可卡因的儿子肯德尔（杰瑞米·斯特朗饰），几乎不给他任何选择。肯德尔的反应让他显得软弱、肤浅、斤斤计较。但当他摆脱父亲的控制，开始追求自己危险的选择时，他的角色变得更加丰满复杂，也赢得了观众的同情。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER AND EMOTION

真实性格与情感

When a character takes an action and his world reacts with antagonism, the charge of value at stake in the scene undergoes change. If a value charge moves from negative to positive, the character experiences an overall positive emotion. And the reverse: If a value’s charge swings from positive to negative, his experience turns overall negative. Emotion, as noted in Chapter Seven, is the side effect of change.

当一个角色采取行动，而他所处的环境对此做出敌对反应时，场景中涉及的价值取向就会发生变化。如果价值取向由负面转为正面，角色就会体验到整体积极的情绪。反之亦然：如果价值取向由正面转为负面，角色的体验就会整体变为负面。正如第七章所述，情绪是变化的副产品。

A stimulus, such as good or bad news, causes glands to open and flood the bloodstream with a chemical cocktail that instills a particular emotion. A beautiful sight floods the brain with dopamine and serotonin, triggering a rush of pleasure; a grotesque image sends chemicals that affect the amygdala and insula cortex, causing woozy pangs of disgust. Soon, however, the limbic system produces counter chemicals to quiet and dispel emotions, returning the mind and body to a state of equilibrium. The intense experiences of pleasure and pain peak, then recede.

诸如好消息或坏消息之类的刺激会促使腺体打开，并将一种化学物质混合物释放到血液中，从而引发特定的情绪。美丽的景象会使大脑释放大量多巴胺和血清素，引发愉悦感；丑陋的画面则会释放影响杏仁核和岛叶皮层的化学物质，导致一阵阵令人头晕目眩的厌恶感。然而，很快，边缘系统就会产生相应的化学物质来平息和消除这些情绪，使身心恢复平衡状态。强烈的愉悦和痛苦体验达到顶峰后，便会逐渐消退。

Pleasure and pain can be subdivided into various tones or qualities, although there’s no scientific agreement on how many. Traditional psychology names just six: joy, fear, anger, sadness, disgust, and surprise. (Notice that the only clearly positive emotion here is joy.) To turn these states into tools for the writer, I’ve expanded the list by pairing them into six oppositions that give the writer a pallet of twelve emotions: Love/Hate, Amity/Anger, Joy/Grief, Surprise/Shock, Pleasure/Disgust, Courage/Fear.

愉悦和痛苦可以细分为各种不同的层次或特质，尽管对于究竟有多少种，科学界尚未达成共识。传统心理学只列出了六种：喜悦、恐惧、愤怒、悲伤、厌恶和惊讶。（请注意，这里唯一明确的积极情绪是喜悦。）为了将这些情绪状态转化为写作的工具，我将它们两两配对，扩展了列表，从而为写作者提供了十二种情绪：爱/恨、友善/愤怒、喜悦/悲伤、惊讶/震惊、愉悦/厌恶、勇气/恐惧。

The words emotion and feeling are often used interchangeably, but in my thinking, they differ greatly by the quality of their impact. Emotion hits with an intense suddenness, peaks in power, then in time fades away. A feeling comes over you more slowly, sits in the background of experience and lasts for long periods of time. Joy is an emotion; happiness is a feeling; grief is an emotion; sadness is a feeling.

“情绪”和“感觉”这两个词经常被混用，但在我看来，它们在影响的性质上有着天壤之别。情绪来得猛烈而突然，强度达到顶峰后，便会逐渐消退。而感觉则来得更慢，它潜藏在体验的背景中，并且持续时间更长。喜悦是一种情绪；快乐是一种感觉；悲伤是一种情绪；难过是一种感觉。

You know how it goes. One morning you wake up feeling great and spend the whole day behind a smile. No particular reason for this; you’re just at the optimistic pitch of your inner teeter-totter. Or you spend a day with a cloud over your head, again for no good reason; you’ve just hit your cynical bottom.

你知道那种感觉。某天早上醒来，你感觉棒极了，一整天都笑容满面。没什么特别的原因；你只是心情愉悦，恰好处于乐观的临界点。或者，你又会整天愁眉苦脸，同样也没什么理由；你只是跌到了愤世嫉俗的谷底。

Feelings—pride of achievement versus shame of failure, hope for a bright future versus a premonition of disaster, a light heart versus a grumpy soul, trust of a loved one versus suspicions of infidelity—often color a personality long after the original stimulus is forgotten, shaping a role’s characterization over a lifetime.

情感——成就的自豪感与失败的羞耻感，对美好未来的希望与对灾难的预感，轻松的心情与暴躁的心情，对爱人的信任与对不忠的怀疑——往往会在最初的刺激被遗忘很久之后，仍然影响着一个人的性格，并在人的一生中塑造着角色的性格特征。

From turning point to turning point, change in the dynamic charge of a life value puts a character through one of the twelve emotions listed above. In a Romantic Comedy, for example, falling in love could fill a grieving character with joy, while losing love could inflict a joyful character with grief.

从一个转折点到另一个转折点，人生价值观动态变化会使角色经历上述十二种情感中的一种。例如，在浪漫喜剧中，坠入爱河可能会让悲伤的角色重获喜悦，而失去爱情则可能让快乐的角色陷入悲伤。

But when writing a scene, knowing the underlying emotion is only a starting point. An emotion in its pure state strikes a character like a blunt instrument. In life, the twelve prime passions range across an infinite variety of qualities and subtle intensities. What, therefore, determines which particular shade of emotion a character expresses in any particular scene? Answer: characterization. The mood, feeling, tone, and texture that emanates from a distinctive personality shapes a primal emotion into a genuinely original performance. Joy in one character might be expressed with a high-stepping song and dance routine, while another only smiles around the edges of his eyes.

但创作场景时，了解潜在的情感仅仅是起点。纯粹的情感如同钝器般冲击着角色。在生活中，十二种基本情感涵盖了无穷无尽的特质和微妙的强度。那么，究竟是什么决定了角色在特定场景中展现的情感呢？答案是：角色塑造。鲜明的个性所散发出的情绪、感受、语调和质感，将原始情感塑造成真正独具匠心的表演。有的角色可能用欢快的歌舞来表达喜悦，而有的角色可能只是眼角泛起一丝微笑。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER AND REACTIONS

真实性格与反应

Reality limits the number of basic actions a human being can take. A person could choose to educate himself or live in ignorance, marry or live alone, work or laze, eat smart or pig out, face life or hide from it, and so on down a rather short list. On the other hand, the variety of moment-to-moment reactions a person may have to any action seems infinite.

现实限制了人类可采取的基本行动数量。一个人可以选择接受教育或生活在无知中，结婚或独居，工作或游手好闲，健康饮食或暴饮暴食，直面生活或逃避生活，等等，清单其实相当有限。另一方面，一个人对任何行为的即时反应却似乎无穷无尽。

When a character struggles to educate himself, for instance, his possible reactions to the trials of learning are as different and as many as they are for all students in all schools everywhere. The same is true of romance, work, health, and every other major aspect of life. The choices a character makes when negative forces block his path express his core identity, but the ways he reacts make him one of a kind.

例如，当一个角色努力自学时，他对学习过程中遇到的困难的反应，与世界各地所有学校的所有学生一样，千差万别，五花八门。爱情、工作、健康以及生活中的其他重要方面也是如此。当负面力量阻碍他前进时，他所做的选择体现了他的核心人格，而他应对这些选择的方式则造就了他独一无二的个性。

In Casablanca , Rick Blaine (Humphrey Bogart) asks Victor Lazlo (Paul Henreid) why he keeps risking his life for the anti-Fascist cause:

在《卡萨布兰卡》中，里克·布莱恩（亨弗莱·鲍嘉饰）问维克多·拉兹洛（保罗·亨雷德饰）为何要不断为反法西斯事业冒生命危险：

LAZLO: We might as well question why we breathe. We stop breathing, we’ll die. We stop fighting our enemies, the world will die.
拉兹洛：我们不妨也问问自己为什么呼吸。如果我们停止呼吸，就会死亡。如果我们停止与敌人战斗，世界就会灭亡。
RICK: What of it? Then it’ll be out of its misery.
里克：那又怎样？那样它就摆脱痛苦了。

Lazlo’s elegant declaration is an answer any idealist might give, but Rick’s reaction, his belief that the death of civilization would be an act of mercy, is character-specific. Rick’s choices, unique to him alone, set him apart from every version of the American antihero before and since.

拉兹洛的优雅宣言是任何理想主义者都可能给出的答案，但里克的反应——他认为文明的消亡是一种仁慈之举——却是他独有的。里克的选择，仅属于他一人，使他与之前和之后所有版本的美国反英雄都截然不同。

Let this principle guide your character work: Choices of action under pressure express true character, but detailed, never-seen-before reactions make a characterization distinctive and intriguing.

让这个原则指导你的角色塑造：压力下的行动选择体现了真实的性格，而细致入微、前所未见的反应则使角色塑造独特而引人入胜。

#↩

TRUE CHARACTER AND FREE WILL

真正的品格与自由意志

A writer’s imagination is the sole source for every decision a character makes and every action he takes; a character’s choices are in fact his author’s choices. But from the point of view of audiences and readers, the opposite seems true. In a fictional world, independent characters lead independent lives, acting of their own free will. So in both realms, the as is and the as if , how free is human choice?

作者的想象力是笔下人物所有决定和行动的唯一来源；人物的选择实际上就是作者的选择。但从观众和读者的角度来看，情况似乎恰恰相反。在虚构的世界里，独立的角色过着独立的生活，完全出于自己的自由意志行事。那么，在现实与虚构这两个层面，人类的选择究竟有多自由呢？

The Matrix explores this question as its protagonist, Neo (Keanu Reeves), discovers that what he experiences as reality is in fact an induced delusion known as the Matrix.
