This false world was created by an all-powerful AI to deceive enslaved human beings into thinking they are free while the AI uses their bodies as biological batteries to run its machines. Neo fights to gain the willpower he needs to defeat the AI’s agents and break free from the Matrix.

《黑客帝国》探讨了这个问题。主人公尼奥（基努·里维斯饰）发现，他所体验到的现实实际上是一种人为制造的幻觉，被称为“矩阵”。这个虚假的世界由一个全能的人工智能创造，旨在欺骗被奴役的人类，让他们误以为自己是自由的，而人工智能则利用他们的身体作为生物电池来驱动其机器。尼奥必须努力获得所需的意志力，才能击败人工智能的代理人，并最终挣脱矩阵的束缚。

The free will / determinism debate is eons old, but with the recent rise of neuroscience and quantum theory, ancient arguments have found new intensity. One side insists that free will is a delusion and that all choice is caused by forces outside human control; 9 others believe the will operates free of any cause, external or internal. 10 This dispute has influenced writers of both speculative and realistic fiction. The side you favor shapes the stories you tell and the casts that populate them.

自由意志与决定论之争由来已久，但随着神经科学和量子理论的兴起，这场古老的争论又焕发出新的活力。一方坚持认为自由意志是一种错觉，所有选择都源于人类无法控制的力量；而另一方则认为意志不受任何内外因素的影响。这场争论影响了科幻和现实主义小说的创作。你支持哪一方的观点，将决定你讲述的故事以及故事中的人物角色。

#↩

Against Free Will

违背自由意志

Free will deniers argue that for the will to be free, choice must be uncaused. An uncaused decision has no connection to anything in the past and is, therefore, utterly spontaneous. But, of course, as we know, in the physical universe, all actions, human or cosmic, are caused. Even the Big Bang had its cause (albeit as yet unknown). Denier logic argues that because an uncaused cause is a non sequitur, the human choice cannot be free.

自由意志否定者认为，自由意志的前提是选择必须是无因的。无因的决定与过去没有任何关联，因此是完全自发的。但是，我们都知道，在物质宇宙中，所有行为，无论是人类的还是宇宙的，都有其原因。即使是宇宙大爆炸也有其原因（尽管至今仍未知）。否定者的逻辑认为，由于无因的原因本身就是不合逻辑的，因此人类的选择不可能是自由的。

#↩

For Free Will

自由意志

In Fawlty Towers , Basil’s car breaks down. After making dire threats to it, he counts to three, gives his car one last chance, then shouts:

在《福尔蒂旅馆》中，巴兹尔的车抛锚了。他对着车子发出了一系列可怕的威胁后，数到三，给了车子最后一次机会，然后大喊：

BASIL: I’ve warned you! I’ve laid it on the line to you time and time again! Right! I’m going to give you a damn good thrashing!
巴兹尔：我警告过你了！我一遍又一遍地跟你强调过！好啊！我要好好揍你一顿！

He rips a branch from a nearby tree and beats the paint off the fenders. Basil blames the car; we blame Basil.

他从附近树上折下一根树枝，把挡泥板上的油漆都打掉了。巴兹尔怪罪于车，我们怪罪于巴兹尔。

Suppose, however, that like the car, Basil had no choice. Suppose the fault is a schizophrenic flaw in his brain chemistry? Or a defect in his upbringing? If so, do we blame his parents? But if his parents have no free will, how can we condemn them? We don’t. Fault finding chases blame after blame into an infinite regress, so we choose to believe that Basil abused his car of his own free will.

然而，假设巴兹尔和那辆车一样，别无选择。假设问题出在他大脑化学物质的某种缺陷上，比如精神分裂症？或者他成长环境的某种缺陷？如果是这样，我们该责怪他的父母吗？但如果他的父母没有自由意志，我们又怎能谴责他们呢？我们不能。追究责任只会陷入无限循环，所以我们选择相信巴兹尔是出于自愿才滥用他的车。

Believing we don’t have free will is not the same as believing we don’t make choices. 11 No matter how our genes and personal history combine to influence our mind, our choices seem real. We sense that deep inside us our neural processes select actions based on a sense of probable consequences, what we think will happen when we take an action. We merge our sum total of living experience with an immediate situation, imagine an outcome, then make a choice. Without belief in choice, we could not hold ourselves responsible for anything we did. Law would evaporate, personal binds unravel, and The Purge would become a 24/365 reality.

认为我们没有自由意志，并不等同于认为我们没有选择。无论我们的基因和个人经历如何共同影响我们的思想，我们的选择似乎都是真实的。我们能感觉到，在我们内心深处，神经系统会根据对可能后果的感知来选择行动，也就是我们认为采取行动后会发生什么。我们将所有的生活经验与当下的情境融合，想象结果，然后做出选择。如果没有对选择的信念，我们就无法为自己的任何行为负责。法律将不复存在，人际关系将瓦解，《人类清除计划》将成为一年365天、一天24小时的现实。

If we have no free will, how can we change, cut, add, merge, or rework ourselves into someone we’ve never been before? If the human will is not free, at least to some degree, how are creativity and change possible? If all choice is determined by the past, how does anything new ever find its way into the world? If free will didn’t exist, nothing unnecessary would exist, yet history is littered with things human beings made just for the fun of it. Like a child making up a game out of things he finds around the house, an artist creates by inventing something that never existed out of what already exists. Childhood play is the essence of free choice, and mature art is its fullest expression. 12

如果我们没有自由意志，我们如何改变、删减、增添、融合或重塑自我，成为从未成为过的人？如果人类的意志并非完全自由，至少在某种程度上，创造力和变革又如何可能？如果所有选择都由过去决定，那么任何新事物又如何能够进入这个世界？如果自由意志不存在，就不会有任何不必要的事物存在，然而历史却充斥着人类仅仅为了娱乐而创造的事物。就像孩子用家里找到的东西自创游戏一样，艺术家通过利用已有的事物创造出从未存在过的事物。童年的游戏是自由选择的本质，而成熟的艺术则是其最充分的表达。

As we noted earlier, any story you create argues both for and against free will. When a story begins and we look into its unknown future, virtually everything and anything seems possible. But at climax, now that we know the protagonist’s psychology in depth, and now that we see the full array of social, personal, and physical forces that surrounded him, we realize that the choices he made were the only choices he could and would have made; the reactions he got from his world were the only reactions his world could and would have given him. The path he took was the only path he could have taken. Character choices seem free and unpredictable when seen from the inciting incident and looking toward the story’s climax, but inevitable and fated when looking back from the climax to the inciting incident. Free will in one direction; retroactive determinism in the other.

正如我们之前提到的，任何故事都会同时论证自由意志的正反两面。故事伊始，当我们展望未知的未来时，几乎一切皆有可能。但到了高潮，当我们深入了解主人公的心理，并目睹他所处的社会、个人和物理环境的全部影响时，我们意识到，他所做的选择是他唯一能够也将会做出的选择；他所处世界的反应也是世界唯一能够也将会给予他的反应。他所选择的道路是他唯一能够选择的道路。从事件的起因到故事的高潮，人物的选择似乎自由且不可预测；但从高潮回溯到事件的起因，却又显得不可避免且命中注定。一方面是自由意志，另一方面是追溯决定论。

Our sense of free will may be a delusion that arises out of ignorance of its causes, but if so, then it’s our delusion and we have no choice but to embrace it. When your characters make choices, they face four possible pathways to a decision, two beyond their control and two within their free will choices:

我们对自由意志的认知或许是一种错觉，源于对自由意志成因的无知。但如果真是如此，那它就是我们的错觉，我们别无选择，只能接受。当你的角色做出选择时，他们会面临四条可能的路径，其中两条不受他们控制，另外两条则在他们的自由意志范围内：

1. Circumstances push a character’s life one way or another and determine the choice, for better or worse, whether he likes it or not.
1. 环境会推动一个角色的人生走向某个方向，并决定他的选择，无论好坏，无论他是否喜欢。
2. The subconscious self makes choices the core self never realizes or rationalizes away.
2. 潜意识自我做出核心自我从未意识到或用理性解释而放弃的选择。
3. The character quickly considers what to do. As choices come to mind, one takes hold, and he makes an instinctive decision.
3. 这个角色迅速思考该怎么做。当各种选择浮现在脑海中时，其中一个选择占据了他的脑海，他随即做出了一个本能的决定。
4. The character slowly considers his choices, makes lists of pros and cons, followed by a concatenation of all possible consequences and a judicious weighing of their effects. He finally makes his choice. This rational mode usually precedes a character’s greatest mistakes in life.
4. 角色会慢慢考虑各种选择，列出利弊清单，然后逐一分析所有可能的后果，并仔细权衡其影响。最终，他会做出选择。这种理性思考模式通常是角色一生中犯下最大错误的先兆。

Ultimately, as author, all choices are yours.

最终，作为作者，所有选择权都在你手中。

#↩

9

THE DIMENSIONAL CHARACTER

立体角色

A UNITY OF OPPOSITES

对立统一

To review: A role’s characterization conceals her true character, and together they float atop her subconscious, that ocean of drives and desires, unthinking habits and sea tides of temperament. These three aspects—outer, inner, hidden—gather to complete a character, but what keeps them from flying apart? What pulls surface personae, inner selves, and subconscious drives together into one unified character?

回顾一下：角色的性格塑造掩盖了她真实的性格，而这些性格特征共同漂浮在她的潜意识之上，那片充满驱动力、欲望、无意识习惯和情绪起伏的海洋。这三个方面——外在的、内在的、隐藏的——共同构成了一个完整的角色，但是什么阻止了它们分崩离析？是什么将表面的人格、内心世界和潜意识的驱动力凝聚成一个统一的角色？

Answer: the power of contradiction.

答案：矛盾的力量。

In the fifth century BCE, the philosopher Heraclitus argued that reality holds itself together through a system of contradictions: “Cold things warm up, the hot cool off; wet becomes dry, dry becomes wet.” Hot/cold merge to create temperature, dry/wet unite into humidity, birth/death forge life. Thus runs the dynamic of all physical existence, creating A Unity of Opposites .

公元前五世纪，哲学家赫拉克利特认为，现实是通过矛盾系统维系自身的：“冷的会变暖，热的会变凉；湿的会变干，干的会变湿。”冷热结合形成温度，干湿结合形成湿度，生死交融孕育生命。一切物质存在的动态规律皆由此而来，构成了对立统一的本质。

This principle applies to humankind as well. The moment a person is born, she begins to die. At every point in her life, she is evolved yet evolving, dreaming while awake, awake while dreaming. No matter her age, she’s both young and old—younger than anyone older, older than anyone younger. No matter her sexual orientation, she’s both female and male.

这条原则同样适用于人类。人从出生那一刻起，便开始走向死亡。在她生命的每一个阶段，她都在进化，在清醒时做梦，在梦中保持清醒。无论年龄多大，她既年轻又年老——比任何年长的人都年轻，比任何年幼的人都年长。无论性取向如何，她既是女性又是男性。

Within the harmony of every well-designed role, a set of living contradictions intersect. The unity of opposites, therefore, is the founding principle of character complexity. Stories populated by complex characters preserve, in an aesthetically purified form, the essential contradictions that unite ugliness with beauty, tyranny with freedom, good with evil, truth with lie, and the like.

在每个精心设计的角色中，都蕴含着一系列鲜活的矛盾交织。因此，对立统一是角色复杂性的根本原则。由复杂角色构成的故事，以一种审美上纯粹的形式，保留了丑陋与美丽、暴政与自由、善与恶、真与假等本质矛盾的融合。

#↩

CHARACTER DIMENSION

角色维度

Human nature’s emotional instrument was strung in a violent past, hundreds of thousands of years before Socrates, Buddha, or Jesus could retune it. Virtues such as honesty, generosity, and courage constantly revert to treachery, selfishness, and cowardice in the same society, the same person. As a result, paradox rules humanity: People love their families yet hate their families, save time yet waste time, seek the truth yet deny the obvious, prize nature yet pollute nature, hunger for peace yet rush to war. Complex characters first display a specific self, then change into its opposite and then back again.

人类情感的琴弦在数十万年前的暴力历史中被拉紧，远在苏格拉底、佛陀或耶稣能够重新调校它之前。诚实、慷慨和勇气等美德，在同一个社会、同一个人身上，却不断地被背叛、自私和懦弱所取代。因此，悖论主宰着人类：人们爱自己的家人却又恨自己的家人，节约时间却又浪费时间，追求真理却又否认显而易见的事实，珍视自然却又污染自然，渴望和平却又急于发动战争。复杂的人物最初展现出某种特定的自我，然后转变为其对立面，之后又重新回归。

These dynamics have a pattern. They swing back and forth from pole to pole depending on the relationships a character has with other characters and within herself—some positive, some negative. The in-vogue client of a professional dominant is a high-powered but highly stressed executive who distains those she subordinates and deifies those who subordinate her. To balance the pleasures of power with the pangs of humiliation, she submits to the whip. Psychologists coined sadomasochist as the perfect oxymoron to name this contradiction in a Dior suit.

这些动态关系遵循一定的模式。它们会根据角色与其他角色以及自身之间的关系——有些是积极的，有些是消极的——在两极之间摇摆不定。一位职业支配者的当红客户是一位权力强大但压力巨大的高管，她鄙视下属，却崇拜那些下属。为了平衡权力带来的快感和屈辱带来的痛苦，她甘愿接受鞭笞。心理学家创造了“虐恋者”这个词，完美地诠释了这种矛盾心理。

When a character’s inner and outer natures fuse into a single function, the role congeals into a type: Nurse, Cop, Teacher, Superhero, Villain, Sidekick, and the like. But when contradictions underpin a role, they activate a more complete, complex, and fascinating character. These oppositions form Dimensions .

当一个角色的内在和外在特质融合为单一功能时，这个角色便凝结成一种类型：护士、警察、教师、超级英雄、反派、助手等等。但当矛盾构成一个角色的基础时，它们便会激发出一个更完整、更复杂、更引人入胜的角色。这些对立面便构成了角色的维度。

Dimensional characters arouse our curiosity by making us wonder how two sides of a contradiction can live within one person. That, in turn, makes them unpredictable and all the more fascinating. From moment to moment, who knows which side will show up?

多面性的角色会激起我们的好奇心，让我们不禁思考矛盾的两面如何能共存于一人之身。反过来，这也使得他们难以捉摸，更加引人入胜。谁又能预料到下一刻哪一面会显露出来呢？

#↩

COMPLEXITY IN SIX DIMENSIONS

六维复杂性

Dimensions span between aspects of a role’s outer characterization, between various inner selves and between facets of the hidden self. What’s more, these three levels often contradict one another. As a result, a complex character may contain six distinct kinds of dimensions.

角色维度涵盖了角色外在特征的各个方面、不同的内在自我以及隐藏自我的各个层面。此外，这三个层面往往相互矛盾。因此，一个复杂的角色可能包含六种截然不同的维度。

#↩

1. A Contradiction Between Two Aspects of Characterization

1. 人物刻画两个方面的矛盾

Picture a woman who spends an hour each morning getting her makeup just right but doesn’t bother to brush her teeth. Suppose this woman abuses her partner but coddles her children; kisses up to her boss but tyrannizes her staff. These three dimensions fuse qualities of characterization—her physical, personal, and social selves—into intriguing behaviors, giving the reader/audience insight into what’s important and unimportant to her.

想象一下，一个女人每天早上花一个小时精心化妆，却懒得刷牙。假设这个女人虐待伴侣，却溺爱孩子；对老板阿谀奉承，却对员工颐指气使。这三个维度——她的外在、内在和社会特质——融合在一起，构成了引人入胜的行为，让读者/观众得以窥见对她而言什么重要，什么不重要。

At the level of characterization, characters are often aware of their traits, although they rarely perceive them as contradictory. Instead, they rationalize them as necessary. These behaviors are also visible to the rest of the cast who think whatever they choose to think about them.

在人物塑造层面，角色通常都清楚自身的性格特征，尽管他们很少会意识到这些特征之间的矛盾。相反，他们会将这些特征合理化为必要的行为。其他角色也能观察到这些行为，并根据自己的理解做出判断。

#↩

2. A Contradiction Between Characterization and True Character

2. 人物塑造与真实性格的矛盾

Envision an elderly woman dozing in a wheelchair. As she awakes, she gazes at the men in her retirement home and suddenly a glint flashes in her eye, lit by her ever-young dream of romantic love.

想象一下，一位老妇人在轮椅上打盹。当她醒来时，她凝视着养老院里的男人们，突然，她眼中闪过一丝光芒，那是她永葆青春的浪漫爱情梦想。

#↩

3. A Contradiction Between Characterization and Subconscious Desire

3. 人物塑造与潜意识欲望之间的矛盾

Imagine a hyperactive woman who never stops doing things, and yet her hidden self always stays deeply calm. This serene self comes out only when she faces danger. Under threat, she goes still, strong and focused.

想象一下，一个精力充沛、永不停歇的女人，但她内心深处却始终保持着平静。这种宁静的自我只有在面临危险时才会显露出来。受到威胁时，她会变得沉稳、坚强而专注。

To discover a character’s subconscious, the key, once again, is contradiction. When a character says one thing and does another, what are the possibilities? One, she’s lying. She knows what she really wants but outwardly pretends to want the opposite. Or two, she’s honest. She really believes what she says, really wants what she wants, but when she tries to get it, something undercuts her efforts. She doesn’t know why, but every once in a while, she turns a rather dark face to the world. A contradictory force lives in her subconscious.

要揭示一个角色的潜意识，关键依然在于矛盾。当一个角色言行不一时，可能是什么情况呢？第一，她在撒谎。她明明知道自己真正想要的是什么，却在表面上假装想要相反的东西。第二，她是诚实的。她真心相信自己所说的话，真心想要自己想要的东西，但当她努力争取时，总有什么东西在暗中破坏她的努力。她自己也不知道为什么，但时不时地，她会露出阴郁的表情面对世界。一种矛盾的力量潜藏在她的潜意识里。

#↩

4. A Contradiction Between Two Conscious Desires

4. 两种意识欲望之间的矛盾

The adulterer’s dilemma: a woman caught between devotion to her husband and passion for her lover.

出轨者的困境：一个女人陷入了对丈夫的忠贞和对情人的激情之间。

At the level of true character, a conscious, self-aware mind analyzes her inner contradiction, worries about it, and struggles to make a choice. If she talks about her dilemma with others, it becomes an aspect of characterization. If she keeps a subtextural conflict to herself, the reader/audience can perceive it only by implication. Once she makes a choice of action, however, the reader/audience reads her mind clearly and senses her inner dimension.

在人物性格的层面，一个有意识、有自知之明的人会分析自己内心的矛盾，为此担忧，并努力做出选择。如果她与他人谈论自己的困境，这便成为人物塑造的一部分。如果她将这种潜在的冲突深藏于心，读者/观众只能通过暗示来感知。然而，一旦她做出行动选择，读者/观众就能清晰地了解她的内心世界，感受到她内在的维度。

To symbolize dimensions between two conscious desires, playwrights such as Samuel Beckett ( Waiting for Godot ), Jean Genet ( The Maids ), and Suzan-Lori Parks ( Topdog/Underdog ) resort to splitting the mind in two and symbolizing an inner contradiction as a pair of bickering characters.

为了象征两种意识欲望之间的维度，像塞缪尔·贝克特（《等待戈多》）、让·热内（《女仆》）和苏珊-洛里·帕克斯（《上位狗/下位狗》）这样的剧作家，都采用将思想一分为二，并将内在矛盾象征为一对争吵不休的角色的方法。

#↩

5. A Contradiction Between a Conscious Desire and a Subconscious Desire

5. 有意识的欲望与无意识的欲望之间的矛盾

The lover’s dilemma: fervent passion for a fiancée versus fear of commitment.

恋人的困境：对未婚妻的热烈爱恋与对承诺的恐惧。

To symbolize dimensions of this fifth type, novels such as Robert Louis Stevenson’s The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde and two novels titled The Double , one by Fyodor Dostoevsky and the other by Jose Saramago, cast conscious/subconscious contradiction as a duet of characters with contradictory drives (one toward good, the other toward evil) that mirror each other.

为了象征第五种类型的维度，罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森的《化身博士》以及陀思妥耶夫斯基和若泽·萨拉马戈的两部名为《双重人格》的小说，将意识/潜意识的矛盾描绘成一对具有相反驱动力（一个向善，另一个向恶）的人物，他们彼此映照。

In Breaking Bad , showrunner Vince Gilligan gives his protagonist, Walter White, a secret second self known as Heisenberg. This doppelgänger comes vividly to the surface in Season 5, Episode 14: Jack, leader of a Nazi biker gang, has Walter’s brother-in-law, Hank, at his mercy. As Jack raises his gun, Walt pleads for Hank’s life. While he’s begging, he is Walter, a man capable of conscious caring.

在《绝命毒师》中，剧集主创文斯·吉利根赋予主角沃尔特·怀特一个秘密的第二人格——海森堡。这个分身在第五季第十四集中鲜明地展现出来：纳粹摩托车帮派头目杰克挟持了沃尔特的妹夫汉克。杰克举起枪时，沃尔特苦苦哀求，想要放过汉克。然而，就在他哀求的时候，他却是沃尔特本人，一个拥有良知和同情心的人。

But immediately after Nazi Jack murders Hank, Walt betrays Jesse, his dearest friend and partner. In that act, Heisenberg, the manifestation of Walter’s savage subconscious, takes charge.

但就在纳粹杰克杀害汉克之后，沃尔特背叛了他最亲密的朋友和搭档杰西。在这一举动中，海森堡——沃尔特野蛮潜意识的化身——占据了主导地位。

#↩

6. A Contradiction Between Two Subconscious Motivations

6.两种潜意识动机之间的矛盾

The family dilemma: the need to sacrifice your desires for the people you love versus the need to sacrifice other people to fulfill your personal ambitions.

家庭困境：为了所爱之人需要牺牲自己的愿望，还是为了实现个人抱负需要牺牲他人？

Subconscious dimensions live below the level of awareness, unthought, and unexpressed. Once again, the reader/audience can perceive an inner contradiction only through the character’s choices of action under pressure.

潜意识层面存在于意识层面之下，未经思考，也未曾表达。读者/观众只能通过角色在压力下的行动选择来感知其内在矛盾。

Children, for example, often harbor contradictory subconscious attitudes toward their parents: fear and awe, love and hate. In The Tragedy of Hamlet , Shakespeare projected a son’s contradictory feelings onto two characters: the noble father versus the dastardly uncle. The Lion King ( Hamlet with a happy ending) repeated this duality onstage and on-screen. The fairy godmother versus wicked stepmother in “Cinderella” does the same for daughters.

例如，孩子们常常对父母怀有矛盾的潜意识态度：既恐惧又敬畏，既爱又恨。在莎士比亚的悲剧《哈姆雷特》中，他将儿子的矛盾情感投射到两个角色身上：高尚的父亲和卑鄙的叔叔。《狮子王》（一个以幸福结局收尾的《哈姆雷特》）在舞台和银幕上都重复了这种二元对立。《灰姑娘》中的仙女教母和恶毒继母也同样体现了女儿们的矛盾情感。

In Persona , Ingmar Bergman expressed the split soul by merging a nurse and patient into one woman, then separated them back into two, then one again, two again…

在《假面》中，英格玛·伯格曼通过将护士和病人合二为一来表达分裂的灵魂，然后再将她们分开，如此反复……

In Black Swan , Nina Sayers (Natalie Portman), a ballet dancer rehearsing Tchaikovsky’s Swan Lake , suffers a conflict between split selves. Because the ballet calls for the same dancer to perform two opposed protagonists, White Swan and Black Swan, the film uses this setup to dramatize her dual self.

在《黑天鹅》中，芭蕾舞演员妮娜·塞耶斯（娜塔莉·波特曼饰）正在排练柴可夫斯基的《天鹅湖》，她内心饱受分裂自我的折磨。由于芭蕾舞剧要求同一位舞者扮演两个截然相反的角色——白天鹅和黑天鹅，影片便以此设定来凸显她双重人格的冲突。

The White Swan role calls for symmetry, grace, cool antisexuality, and, above all, precise skills that define Nina’s longing for poised perfection. The Black Swan demands the opposite talents: creativity, spontaneity, sexual abandon—powerful, animalistic energies alive within Nina that she fiercely suppresses. The war between her uptight White Swan and her voluptuous but stifled Black Swan surfaces in paranoid hallucinations. At the climax, Nina’s two selves finally join forces in a glorious, life-fulfilling performance, then consume each other as she dies, whispering, “It was perfect.”

白天鹅的角色需要对称、优雅、冷峻的反性气质，以及最重要的，精准的技巧，这些都体现了妮娜对完美姿态的渴望。黑天鹅则需要截然相反的天赋：创造力、自发性、性欲的放纵——妮娜体内蕴藏着强大而原始的能量，却被她极力压抑。她拘谨的白天鹅与性感却压抑的黑天鹅之间的冲突，在她偏执的幻觉中显露出来。在高潮部分，妮娜的两个自我最终融合，奉献了一场辉煌而充实的演出，然后在她临终之际，彼此吞噬，低语道：“一切都很完美。”

For a real-life example of the unity of opposites, consider the novelist, playwright, screenwriter, and multidimensional celebrity Graham Greene. Greene was self-hating versus self-glorifying, meticulously disciplined versus self-destructive, deliriously romantic versus bitterly cynical, devout Catholic versus lifelong adulterer, Nobel Prize–nominated novelist versus pulp hack, strict theologian versus moral relativist, salon communist versus closet monarchist, anti-imperialist crusader versus postcolonial parasite, civilized to a fault versus drugged to distraction. Greene was an exceptional artist but no exception to human nature. 1

要了解对立统一的真实例子，不妨看看小说家、剧作家、编剧兼多面名人格雷厄姆·格林。格林既自恨又自恋，既严于律己又自我毁灭，既浪漫至极又愤世嫉俗，既虔诚的天主教徒又终生沉溺于婚外情，既是诺贝尔文学奖提名的小说家又沦为通俗小说作家，既是严谨的神学家又信奉道德相对主义，既是沙龙里的共产主义者又暗藏君主主义，既是反帝国主义的斗士又沦为后殖民时代的寄生虫，既文明过度又沉迷于毒品。格林是一位杰出的艺术家，但他也无法摆脱人性的局限。

To unify characters over time, dimensions must be consistent. If a man rescues a kitten up a tree once, that’s not a dimension; it’s a gratuitous kindness to gain cheap sympathy from the reader/audience. If a woman rescues cats throughout a story but then suddenly kicks a dog, that’s not a dimension, either; it’s a snit.

为了让角色在故事中保持统一，人物性格必须前后一致。如果一个男人只救过一次树上的小猫，那不算性格塑造；那只是为了博取读者/观众廉价同情而做出的无谓善举。如果一个女人在故事中一直救猫，但突然踢了一只狗，那也不算性格塑造；那只是耍脾气而已。

Dimensions must be variable. A character who loves cats but hates dogs and so rescues kittens but abandons puppies wages war within herself. A reader/audience would be amused and curious to discover the roots of this neurotic contradiction, so long as the pattern doesn’t become repetitious. A dimension needs a certain unpredictability and progression—not the same cat and same dog rescued and abandoned in the same backyard.

维度必须是多变的。一个角色爱猫恨狗，救助小猫却遗弃小狗，这种矛盾的内心冲突便由此展开。只要模式不重复，读者/观众就会感到有趣和好奇，想要探寻这种神经质矛盾的根源。一个维度需要一定的不可预测性和发展性——而不是在同一个后院里救助又遗弃同一只猫和同一只狗。

What’s more, to keep its tension, a dimension must seem unresolvable: an atheist who argues that nothing is permanent but subconsciously yearns for the eternal; a neuroscientist who chooses of her own free will to believe that free will is an illusion; a Las Vegas oddsmaker who secretly delights in unpredictable outcomes.

此外，为了保持这种张力，必须存在一个看似无法解决的维度：一个无神论者认为没有什么是永恒的，但潜意识里却渴望永恒；一个神经科学家出于自己的自由意志选择相信自由意志是一种幻觉；一个拉斯维加斯的博彩公司老板暗地里喜欢不可预测的结果。

#↩

THE DEFINING DIMENSION

决定性维度

A protagonist may house many more than three dimensions, while first circle supporting roles generally feature only one or two, but no matter how many dimensions elaborate a role, they do not have equal weight and focus. One tends to stand in the foreground, defining a character’s essential spirit, while the others complete the portrait.

主角可能拥有远超三个维度的特质，而第一层级的配角通常只有一到两个维度。但无论一个角色拥有多少维度，这些维度的重要性和关注度都不尽相同。其中一个维度往往占据主导地位，定义角色的本质精神，而其他维度则起到完善角色形象的作用。

Of the nine dimensions I ascribed to Graham Greene, which one is so crucial to his identity that if it were removed, he would vanish with it? I would suggest Artist/Hack. The other eight dimensions could inhabit someone else, but the creative battle Greene waged within himself was his alone. It defined him.

在我赋予格雷厄姆·格林的九个维度中，哪一个维度对他而言至关重要，以至于如果失去它，他也会随之消失？我认为是“艺术家/黑客”这个维度。其他八个维度或许可以存在于其他人身上，但格林内心进行的创作斗争却是他独有的。它定义了他。

To repeat for clarity: A dimension is a consistent contradiction within or between the planes of a character’s nature. In a complex, multidimensional character, one of these steps forward to define her unique identity.

为了更清楚地说明：维度是指角色性格中不同层面之间或内部存在的持续性矛盾。在一个复杂、多维的角色中，其中一个维度会凸显出来，从而定义她独特的身份。

#↩

CASE STUDY: ODYSSEUS

案例研究：奥德修斯

In a recent survey of “The 100 Stories that Shaped the World,” international experts ranked the Odyssey , Homer’s three-thousand-year-old epic, number one, with his Iliad close behind. 2 As Homer’s human characters strive against vindictive, hypersexed gods and demonic, nightmarish monsters, many scenes in both stories seem like fever dreams, and yet, for all their lust and gore, the Iliad and Odyssey are the foundational stories of European culture, and their pivotal character, Odysseus, King of Ithaca, is history’s first multidimensional character.

在最近一项名为“塑造世界的100个故事”的调查中，国际专家将荷马的三千年史诗《奥德赛》评为第一名，《伊利亚特》紧随其后。荷马笔下的人物与复仇心切、性欲旺盛的神祇以及恶魔般的噩梦般的怪物展开搏斗，两部史诗中的许多场景都如同梦魇一般。然而，尽管《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》充满了情欲和血腥，它们却是欧洲文化的奠基之作，而其中的关键人物——伊萨卡国王奥德修斯——则是历史上第一个多维度的人物。

The battered hero of these tales spends ten years at war against the city of Troy ( Iliad ), then another decade struggling to sail home ( Odyssey ). Odysseus duels enemy warriors, wrathful gods, covetous goddesses, and bloodthirsty beasts, ultimately prevailing through grit, luck, and ingenious improvisations.

这些故事中饱经战火的英雄先是在与特洛伊城的战争中度过了十年（《伊利亚特》），然后又在返乡的路上挣扎了十年（《奥德赛》）。奥德修斯与敌军战士、愤怒的神祇、贪婪的女神和嗜血的野兽搏斗，最终凭借勇气、运气和巧妙的应变能力取得了胜利。

The Iliad gives Odysseus his first two dimensions—Pragmatic/Idealistic and Obedient/Defiant. But after the Odyssey ’s opening line introduces him as “a complicated man,” he gains six more: Truthful/Deceitful, Brilliant/Blundering, Protecting/Jeopardizing, Honorable/Thieving, Cool/Raging, and Faithful/Unfaithful. 3

《伊利亚特》赋予奥德修斯最初的两个维度——务实/理想主义和顺从/反抗。但在《奥德赛》开篇将他描述为“一个复杂的人”之后，他又获得了六个维度：诚实/欺骗、才华横溢/笨拙、保护/危害、正直/偷窃、冷静/愤怒以及忠诚/背信弃义。

#↩

Pragmatic/Idealistic

务实主义/理想主义

Odysseus is a battlefield pragmatist. To him, idealistic codes of honor end when war begins. In ancient heroic tradition, for example, poison was an ignoble, deceitful weapon no true champion would use. Even so, Odysseus coats his arrowheads with arsenic.

奥德修斯是个战场上的实用主义者。对他而言，战争爆发后，理想主义的荣誉准则便不复存在。例如，在古代英雄传统中，毒药是一种卑鄙狡诈的武器，真正的英雄绝不会使用。即便如此，奥德修斯还是在箭头上涂抹了砒霜。

When a captured Trojan spy begs Odysseus for mercy, he manipulates the man into thinking he’ll spare his life in exchange for a military secret. But the moment the spy reveals what he knows, he’s beheaded. Then using the spy’s information, Odysseus and his comrade slaughter an enemy force in their sleep.

一名被俘的特洛伊间谍向奥德修斯求饶，奥德修斯哄骗他以为自己会用一个军事机密换取他的性命。但间谍刚一吐出自己知道的秘密，就被斩首了。之后，奥德修斯和他的同伴利用间谍提供的情报，趁敌军熟睡之际将其屠戮殆尽。

In the tenth year of the war, the Trojans back the Greek army against the sea. Facing massacre, the Greek foot soldiers rise up against their incompetent leaders. In the face of mutiny and certain defeat, a pragmatist might hoist sail for home, but Odysseus stays true to the ideals of victory. Using his powerfully persuasive voice, he reverses the revolt with a fiery prophecy that turns mutineers into warriors and sends them roaring back into the teeth of battle.

战争进入第十年，特洛伊人背水一战，希腊军队被迫撤退。面对屠杀，希腊步兵奋起反抗他们无能的统帅。面对叛乱和必败的局面，务实之人或许会扬帆返航，但奥德修斯却坚守着胜利的理想。他以极具感染力的嗓音，用一段充满激情的预言，将叛乱者重新凝聚成战士，激励他们重返战场。

#↩

Obedient/Defiant

顺从/反抗

Odysseus dutifully obeys his commanding general, King Agamemnon, but when he feels that the king’s tactics are ruinous, he defies his leader, telling him, “Your words are wind and have no meaning.”

奥德修斯忠实地服从他的统帅阿伽门农国王的命令，但当他觉得国王的策略是灾难性的时，他违抗了他的统帅，告诉他：“你的话如同风，毫无意义。”

#↩

Truthful/Deceitful

诚实/欺骗

As an advisor to Agamemnon’s war council, Odysseus always speaks with truthfulness, insight, and wisdom. No comrade ever doubts his word. But once he sets sail for home, he lies from one end of the Mediterranean to the other.

作为阿伽门农战争委员会的顾问，奥德修斯总是言辞真诚、见解深刻、充满智慧。没有哪个战友会怀疑他的话。但一旦他扬帆返乡，他便谎话连篇，从地中海的一端一直撒到另一端。

Again and again, his gift for storytelling charms his way out of trouble. He tricks people by disguising himself as an old man or a beggar or an immigrant from Crete, an island famous for its liars. Odysseus even tries to con his sacred protectress, the goddess Athena, but she sees through him and scolds him with: “You perverse man, how you love your artful, deceitful words.”

他总能凭借讲故事的天赋化险为夷。他乔装成老人、乞丐，或是来自克里特岛的移民——克里特岛以盛产骗子而闻名——以此欺骗他人。奥德修斯甚至试图欺骗他的守护女神雅典娜，但雅典娜识破了他的诡计，斥责道：“你这狡猾的人，竟如此喜爱你那诡诈的言辞！”

#↩

Brilliant/Blundering

精彩/失误

When the war with Troy seems all but lost, Odysseus wins victory for the Greeks by improvising history’s most brilliant military tactic—the Wooden Horse. On the voyage home, however, Odysseus, greedy for loot, sneaks into the cave of Polyphemus, the cannibalistic cyclops. The giant traps Odysseus inside and devours half of his crew.

当特洛伊战争看似败局已定时，奥德修斯凭借历史上最精妙的军事战术——木马——为希腊人赢得了胜利。然而，在返乡途中，贪婪的奥德修斯偷偷潜入了独眼巨人波吕斐摩斯的洞穴。巨人将奥德修斯困在洞穴中，并吞噬了他一半的船员。

That night Odysseus lulls Polyphemus into a drunken stupor, then drives a stake into his one and only eye. Once safely back on ship, however, Odysseus unleashes yet another arrogant impulse. He taunts the now-blind Polyphemus, enraging not only the giant but the giant’s father, Poseidon, Lord of the Seas. The furious sea god batters Odysseus’s ship with massive storms and blows him wildly off course.

当晚，奥德修斯将波吕斐摩斯灌醉，然后用木桩刺瞎了他唯一的一只眼睛。然而，安全返回船上后，奥德修斯又一次展现出傲慢的本性。他嘲弄失明的波吕斐摩斯，不仅激怒了巨人，也激怒了巨人的父亲——海神波塞冬。愤怒的海神掀起滔天巨浪，猛烈冲击奥德修斯的船只，将他吹离了航线。

#↩

Protecting/Jeopardizing

保护/危害

Odysseus protected his warriors throughout the Trojan War, making certain they were well fed and well doctored. But while sailing home, his men discover a tribe addicted to the lotus plant—a narcotic that erases painful memories. These war-damaged, PTSD-suffering veterans, longing to forget, rush to devour the drug. To save his men from themselves, Odysseus drags them back to the ships.

在特洛伊战争期间，奥德修斯一直保护着他的战士们，确保他们吃饱穿暖，得到妥善的医疗照顾。但在返航途中，他的部下发现一个部落沉迷于莲花——一种能够抹去痛苦记忆的麻醉剂。这些饱受战争创伤、患有创伤后应激障碍的老兵，渴望遗忘一切，纷纷服用这种药物。为了拯救他的部下，奥德修斯将他们带回了船上。

Later, however, as Odysseus’s fleet sails toward a foreign shore, he again senses danger, but this time he jeopardizes his men’s lives by anchoring their ships in the open, while concealing his behind rocks. Suddenly, gargantuan cannibals attack and capsize the ships, spearing and eating his men as if they were fish. Only Odysseus and his crew escape.

然而，后来当奥德修斯的舰队驶向异国海岸时，他再次感到危险，但这一次他却将船停泊在开阔地带，自己却躲在礁石后，从而危及了船员的生命。突然，一群体型庞大的食人族袭击了他们，掀翻了船只，像吃鱼一样用长矛刺杀并吞食他的船员。只有奥德修斯和他的船员侥幸逃脱。

#↩

Honorable/Thieving

光荣/盗窃

Throughout the war, Odysseus fought courageously, dividing spoils honorably and treating his fellow warriors with respect. But on the voyage home, he turns pirate, plundering peaceful towns, killing their defenders, and taking women as slaves.

战争期间，奥德修斯英勇作战，公平分配战利品，并尊重他的战友。但在返乡途中，他却沦为海盗，劫掠和平城镇，杀害守卫者，并将妇女掳为奴隶。

#↩

Cool/Raging

酷/狂暴

In war and at sea, in the face of armies and monsters, Odysseus always keeps his cool, solving problems with calm, clear, balanced decisions.

在战争和海上，面对军队和怪物，奥德修斯总是保持冷静，以冷静、清晰、平衡的决定解决问题。

Meanwhile, back in Ithaca, a group of boisterous young men known as the Suitors invade his palace and revel in his wealth. For ten years, each of them tries repeatedly to seduce Odysseus’s wife, Penelope. Once home, Odysseus, roiled with Achilles-like rage, takes revenge. He slaughters all 108 suitors, then all the servants who served the suitors and the female slaves who slept with them.

与此同时，在伊萨卡岛，一群被称为求婚者的喧闹青年闯入奥德修斯的宫殿，肆意挥霍他的财富。十年间，他们不断试图引诱奥德修斯的妻子佩涅洛佩。回到家后，奥德修斯怒火中烧，如同阿喀琉斯一般，展开了复仇。他屠杀了所有108名求婚者，随后又杀死了所有服侍他们的仆人和与他们同寝的女奴。

#↩

Faithful/Unfaithful

忠诚/不忠诚

Away from home, Odysseus is repeatedly adulterous, bedding nymphs such as Circe. But when Calypso, a goddess of divine beauty, offers Odysseus an eternity of pleasure, he stays faithful to his beloved Penelope.

远离家乡的奥德修斯屡次出轨，与喀耳刻等仙女发生关系。但当美貌女神卡吕普索许诺给予奥德修斯永恒的快乐时，他仍然忠于自己心爱的佩涅洛佩。

Odysseus’s Eight Dimensions
奥德修斯的八个维度

What makes Odysseus an enduring creation is the dark side of his dimensions. Any clichéd hero can act out positive charges such as bravery, intelligence, and calm under pressure, but it’s his impulsive, hard-hearted, raging, thieving, self-serving, and deceitful traits that expand Odysseus’s character, giving him a multidimensional nature, the power of unpredictability, and a depth of character that makes his surprising choices satisfyingly creditable.

奥德修斯之所以能成为经久不衰的经典人物，正是因为他性格中阴暗的一面。任何老套的英雄人物都能展现出勇敢、智慧和临危不乱等积极品质，但正是他冲动、冷酷、暴怒、偷窃、自私和欺骗的特质，丰富了奥德修斯的形象，赋予他多面性、不可预测的力量和深刻的性格内涵，使他那些出人意料的选择也显得合情合理。

Of his eight dynamic contradictions, the one that serves as his defining dimension is his dazzling brilliance versus his erratic impulses. Odysseus, after all, devised the Trojan Horse ploy that ended a decade of war, but then he blundered his way into Polyphemus’s cave. His impulsive adventures risk his life repeatedly, but his hypnotic storytelling saves it just as often. He’s both brilliant and foolish. There’s no one quite like him in the three thousand years of fiction that followed Homer.

在他八大矛盾之中，最能定义他性格的莫过于他惊人的才华与反复无常的冲动。毕竟，奥德修斯设计了特洛伊木马的计策，结束了长达十年的战争，但他随后又误入了独眼巨人波吕斐摩斯的洞穴。他冲动的冒险屡屡将他置于险境，但他引人入胜的叙事能力也同样屡次救他于危难之中。他既才华横溢又愚蠢至极。在荷马之后的三千年文学作品中，再无第二个像他这样的人物。

Odysseus remains perpetually modern—conflicted yet willful, death damaged yet life embracing. He set the stage for psychologically and morally complex characters of future generations: Anonymous’s Beowulf, Shakespeare’s Macbeth, Stendhal’s Julien Sorel, F. Scott Fitzgerald’s Jay Gatsby, Raymond Chandler’s Philip Marlowe, Vladimir Nabokov’s Humbert Humbert, Mario Puzo’s Michael Corleone, Philip Roth’s Alexander Portnoy, Hilary Mantel’s Thomas Cromwell.

奥德修斯始终具有现代性——他内心充满矛盾却又意志坚定，饱经死亡摧残却又拥抱生命。他为后世那些心理和道德都十分复杂的人物奠定了基础：佚名的贝奥武夫、莎士比亚的麦克白、司汤达的于连·索雷尔、菲茨杰拉德的杰伊·盖茨比、雷蒙德·钱德勒的菲利普·马洛、纳博科夫的亨伯特·亨伯特、马里奥·普佐的迈克尔·柯里昂、菲利普·罗斯的亚历山大·波特诺伊、希拉里·曼特尔的托马斯·克伦威尔。

#↩

CASE STUDY: TONY SOPRANO

案例研究：托尼·索普拉诺

How dimensional can a character become? Consider David Chase’s creation, the New Jersey mafia don, Tony Soprano. The Sopranos ran for eighty-six episodes, and Tony was the only character to appear in every episode.

一个角色究竟能塑造到什么程度？以大卫·蔡斯笔下的新泽西黑手党教父托尼·索普拉诺为例。《黑道家族》共播出86集，托尼是唯一一个每集都有出场的角色。

The Twelve Dimensions of Tony Soprano
托尼·索普拉诺的十二个维度

To portray a man’s life enmeshed in this huge number of interconnected relationships, dramatized over eighty-six hours, with dozens of backstory events waiting for revelation, reaching back decades to Tony’s infancy—all this time and content called for one of the most complex characters ever conceived for any storytelling medium.

要描绘一个男人在众多相互关联的关系中挣扎的一生，并在八十六小时内将其戏剧化呈现，还有数十个背景故事事件等待揭晓，甚至可以追溯到几十年前托尼的婴儿时期——所有这些时间和内容都需要塑造一个有史以来在任何叙事媒介中都难以想象的最复杂的角色之一。

Moving counterclockwise:

逆时针方向移动：

#1. Guilt-ridden/Sociopath. A sociopath is someone without a conscience, an antisocial, self-centered personality who’s incapable of feeling shame or remorse. At times, Tony is clearly a sociopath.

#1. 内疚感作祟/反社会人格。反社会人格者缺乏良知，性格反社会、以自我为中心，无法感受到羞耻或悔恨。有时，托尼显然就是一个反社会人格者。

Except at other times, Tony is as guilt-ridden as Macbeth. His remorseful heart pursues him relentlessly, nagging and tormenting him into panic attacks.

除了某些时候，托尼就像麦克白一样充满罪恶感。他那颗悔恨的心如影随形，不断地折磨着他，让他陷入恐慌发作。

This Macbeth-like core contradiction of outer cruelty versus inner conscience makes Tony Soprano one of the most fascinating characters ever written for page, stage, or screen.

托尼·索普拉诺身上这种类似麦克白式的内在矛盾——外在的残忍与内在的良知——使他成为有史以来在书页、舞台或银幕上塑造的最迷人的角色之一。

When it’s time to kill, Tony acts without hesitation. Nothing can restrain his raging impulses. Over the years he commits eight murders on-screen, and who can count how many hits he orders or commits off-screen? He is a sociopath, no doubt, but a genuinely sociopathic personality would never join any collective organization, even the mafia.

托尼一旦到了杀人的时候，便会毫不犹豫地出手。没有什么能抑制他狂暴的冲动。多年来，他在银幕上犯下了八起谋杀案，而谁又能统计出他在银幕之外指使或亲自执行了多少起暗杀？毫无疑问，他是个反社会人格者，但一个真正的反社会人格者绝不会加入任何集体组织，哪怕是黑手党。

Professional assassins, like Javier Bardem’s Anton Chigurh and Woody Harrelson’s Carson Wells from No Country for Old Men , would happily fill contracts to kill for the mafia, but they rarely join it. The mafia is an illegal society within our legal society, but it demands all those qualities of good citizenship conventional society demands: loyalty, honesty, hard work, a stable family life, sobriety, obedience to the tribe’s laws, respectful manners and etiquette, and, most important, submission to the authorities who stand above you in the hierarchy of power.

像哈维尔·巴登饰演的安东·奇古尔和伍迪·哈里森在《老无所依》中饰演的卡森·威尔斯那样的职业杀手，乐于接受黑手党的杀人委托，但他们很少真正加入黑手党。黑手党在我们这个合法社会中是一个非法组织，但它要求成员具备所有普通公民所应具备的品质：忠诚、诚实、勤奋、稳定的家庭生活、节制、遵守帮规、举止得体，以及最重要的——服从权力等级中高于自己的权威。

If you belong to this society, breaking its commandments inflicts the pain of guilt as you accuse and belittle yourself with that nagging voice of self-disgust known as a conscience.

如果你属于这个社会，违反它的戒律会让你感到内疚的痛苦，因为你会用那种被称为良心的、令人厌恶的、喋喋不休的声音来谴责和贬低自己。

If you have a conscience, that is, and Tony certainly does. His conscience works overtime to fill his dreams with horrifying images and drive him to a psychiatrist for help. This profound dimension of sociopathic callousness contradicted by guilty self-punishment is the axle of Tony’s inner nature, and all his other many dimensions extend like spokes off that hub.

如果你还有良知的话——而托尼显然有。他的良知时刻都在作祟，让他的梦境充斥着恐怖的画面，最终驱使他去看精神科医生。这种反社会人格的冷酷无情与内疚的自我惩罚交织在一起，构成了托尼内心世界的核心，而他其他种种性格维度则如同辐条般从这个中心向外延伸。

#2. Proud/Shamed. He’s proud of his son’s loving gentleness yet shamed by the boy’s weak-willed, suicidal nature.

#2. 自豪/羞愧。他为儿子温柔善良的性格感到自豪，但又为儿子意志薄弱、有自杀倾向的性格感到羞愧。

#3. Calculating/Intuitive. For months, Tony plays Sherlock Holmes as he gathers evidence in his search for the informant who’s ratting him out to the FBI. Then in a dream while suffering food poisoning, a fish comes to Tony, speaking in the voice of his longtime friend and family strong arm, Sal “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero. The fish tells him that his suspicions about Big Pussy are correct. Big Pussy is the FBI rat. So based on a dream, Tony murders his friend.

#3. 精于算计/凭直觉。几个月来，托尼像夏洛克·福尔摩斯一样，四处搜集证据，寻找向FBI告密的线人。后来，在一次食物中毒的梦中，一条鱼来到托尼面前，用他多年的好友兼家族打手萨尔·“大猫”·邦彭西罗的声音说话。鱼告诉他，他对“大猫”的怀疑是正确的。“大猫”就是FBI的告密者。于是，托尼根据一个梦，杀死了自己的朋友。

#4. Depressed/Optimistic. Despair versus hope war within him.

第四点：抑郁/乐观。绝望与希望在他内心交战。

#5. Loyal/Treacherous. He’s devoted to his wife yet betrays her with his many mistresses.

第五点：忠诚/背叛。他对妻子忠贞不渝，却背叛她，与众多情妇厮混。

#6. Calm/Panicked. He’s logical and emotional; he’s cool under pressure but a victim of panic attacks.

#6. 冷静/恐慌。他既理性又感性；他能在压力下保持冷静，但却容易恐慌发作。

#7. Fearless/Terrified. When threatened by gangsters, he’s fearless, but the chance of a terrorist attack terrifies him.

#7. 无所畏惧/恐惧万分。当受到歹徒威胁时，他无所畏惧，但恐怖袭击的可能性却让他感到恐惧。

#8. Sneering/Envying. Tony sneers at the lives of normal people, yet he envies the lives of normal people.

第八点：嘲讽/嫉妒。托尼嘲讽普通人的生活，但他又嫉妒普通人的生活。

#9. Kills/Saves. He hates human beings and kills them, but he loves animals and protects them.

#9. 杀戮/拯救。他憎恨人类并杀害他们，但他热爱动物并保护它们。

#10. Loves women / Fears women. Tony is a macho sex addict, yet he is tortured by nightmares of castration.

10. 爱女人/怕女人。托尼是个大男子主义的性瘾者，但他却饱受阉割噩梦的折磨。

#11. Loves family / Hates family. He hates his mother / loves his mother, hates his uncle Junior / loves his uncle Junior, and above all he loves himself / hates himself.

#11. 爱家人/恨家人。他恨他的母亲/爱他的母亲，恨他的叔叔小朱尼尔/爱他的叔叔小朱尼尔，最重要的是，他爱他自己/恨他自己。

#12. Loves life / Loves death. He enjoys life’s beauty but finds death more and more intoxicating with each murder he commits.

#12. 热爱生命/热爱死亡。他享受生命的美好，但随着每次杀戮，他都越来越沉醉于死亡的诱惑之中。

Tony Soprano is far more dimensional than Hamlet. Shakespeare surrounded Hamlet with a cast of just ten over only four hours of dramatization. David Chase set Tony in a cast of many dozens through eighty-six hours of choices, actions, and reactions socially, personally, privately, consciously, and subconsciously. Tony is a modern model of character complexity because his dimensions crisscross all levels of his being.

托尼·索普拉诺比哈姆雷特要复杂得多。莎士比亚创作《哈姆雷特》时，只用了十位演员，演出时长也只有四个小时。而大卫·蔡斯则让托尼置身于数十位演员之中，在长达八十六个小时的演出中，展现了他在社交、个人、私密、意识和潜意识层面上的种种选择、行动和反应。托尼堪称现代人物复杂性的典范，因为他的性格维度贯穿了他存在的各个层面。

Yet try as he may, unlike Hamlet, Tony cannot change. The series’ narrative drive raises the major dramatic question: Will Tony change into a morally better human being? Answer: No. The Tonys of this world cannot and do not change their core selves.

然而，无论他如何努力，与哈姆雷特不同，托尼无法改变。这部剧的叙事主线引出了一个重要的戏剧性问题：托尼会变成一个道德更高的人吗？答案是：不会。这个世界上的托尼们无法也无意改变他们本性中的那些人。

#↩

10

THE COMPLEX CHARACTER

复杂的人物

COMPLEXITY THROUGH ANTAGONISM

通过对抗实现复杂性

Stoic philosophers, beginning around 300 BC, taught that the gods predetermine life. Olympians know all of mankind’s future events but hide them until they happen. Stoics called this force Fate, and this belief lives on today. When, for example, a tragic accident takes a child’s life, his parents often tell the TV cameras that they bow to “God’s will.”

大约从公元前300年开始，斯多葛派哲学家认为神祇预先决定了人生。奥林匹斯诸神知晓人类未来的一切，却将其隐藏起来，直到事件发生。斯多葛派称这种力量为命运，而这种信仰至今仍然存在。例如，当一场悲剧夺走一个孩子的生命时，他的父母常常对着电视镜头说，他们顺从“神的旨意”。

Epicurean philosophers took the opposite view. They held that what we mistake for a power outside of ourselves is the work of a free will hidden within ourselves. Random events beyond human control may disrupt us, but our will-driven reactions determine the path life takes. The choices we make under these pressures shape our future. As Heraclitus put it, “Character is destiny.”

伊壁鸠鲁学派哲学家持相反观点。他们认为，我们误以为是外在力量的东西，实际上是隐藏在我们内心的自由意志的体现。人类无法控制的随机事件或许会扰乱我们的生活，但我们意志驱动的反应决定了人生的走向。在这些压力下做出的选择塑造了我们的未来。正如赫拉克利特所说：“性格决定命运。”

The latter belief seems the more likely. An invisible force, as it were, does shape a character’s life, but it emanates from within himself. As Carl Jung taught, the conscious mind lives on the edge of a volcano, and unless a character becomes aware of his subconscious impulses, life will always seem beyond control, and surprising things will always happen to him as if by fate.

后一种观点似乎更可信。某种无形的力量确实塑造着一个人的生活，但这股力量源于他自身。正如卡尔·荣格所言，意识就像生活在火山边缘，除非一个人意识到自己的潜意识冲动，否则生活将永远显得失控，各种意想不到的事情也会像命中注定般发生在他身上。

Picture two ships in a raging storm: One stays afloat; the other goes under. The same seas batter both; the difference is not luck but who captains. As Cassius puts it in The Tragedy of Julius Caesar : “The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves, that we are underlings.”

想象一下两艘船在狂风暴雨中航行：一艘屹立不倒，另一艘沉没。同样的海浪冲击着它们；区别不在于运气，而在于谁是船长。正如卡西乌斯在《尤利乌斯·凯撒》中所说：“亲爱的布鲁图斯，错不在命运，而在于我们自己，我们甘愿做下属。”

As a young character comes of age, a perfect storm of external forces affects his sense of values: What is worth pursuing? What’s foolish to pursue? When his subconscious reinforces his inclinations, they become beliefs. These convictions, rooted in his true character, guide him through this pattern:

随着一个年轻人逐渐长大成人，各种外部因素交织在一起，影响着他的价值观：什么值得追求？什么追求起来又很愚蠢？当他的潜意识强化了他的倾向时，这些倾向就变成了信念。这些根植于他真实性格的信念，引导着他经历以下模式：

1. Based on his beliefs, his core self determines the choices and actions he makes and takes; conversely, his choices express his true character.
1. 基于他的信念，他的核心自我决定了他所做的选择和采取的行动；反过来，他的选择也表达了他的真实性格。
2. His choices under pressure shape his future, not only revealing who he is but how he changes into who he becomes.
2. 他在压力下做出的选择塑造了他的未来，不仅揭示了他是谁，也揭示了他如何变成他最终成为的人。
3. The more various the antagonisms in his life, the more diverse his choices.
3. 他生活中遇到的对抗越多，他的选择也越多。
4. The more diverse his choices, the more complex his nature, and thus the more dimensional, unpredictable, surprising, and ultimately revealing his reactions and actions.
4. 他的选择越多，他的性格就越复杂，因此他的反应和行动就越具有多面性、不可预测性、令人惊讶性，最终也越能揭示其本质。
5. His character, therefore, becomes only as multidimensional as the story’s complex of antagonistic forces that conflict within him.
5. 因此，他的性格只有随着故事中在他内心冲突的各种对立力量的复杂程度而变得多维。

Levels and qualities of conflict range from the physical (nature’s powers spanning from the massive forces of the universe to microscopic diseases) to the social (demands of employment and citizenship) and personal (demands of intimate relationships) to the internal (the mind’s conflicting desires).

冲突的层次和性质从物质层面（自然界的力量，从宇宙的巨大力量到微观疾病）到社会层面（就业和公民身份的要求）和个人层面（亲密关系的要求）再到内在层面（心灵的冲突欲望）。

Let’s work from outermost to the innermost to see how levels of antagonism multiply dimensionality into a complex character.

让我们从外到内分析，看看不同层次的对抗如何使人物性格更加复杂，更具立体感。

#↩

PHYSICAL CONFLICTS

肢体冲突

A story’s outermost level of conflict embraces the four grand components of the physical world:

故事中最外层的冲突涵盖了物质世界的四大组成部分：

1. Natural environments and the powers they contain. From the human point of view, nature is as random as a tornado, as fierce as a wolf pack, and as morally indifferent as evolution.
1. 自然环境及其蕴含的力量。从人类的角度来看，大自然如同龙卷风般随机，如同狼群般凶猛，如同进化般冷漠无情。
2. Man-made environments and the systems they control. Civilizations were conceived with a moral as well as a practical purpose. We human beings, therefore, share responsibility for both the beauty of our creations and the ill effects of pollution, global warming, war, and all other man-made disasters.
2. 人造环境及其控制系统。文明的诞生既有道德目的，也有实际意义。因此，我们人类既要为我们创造的美丽环境负责，也要为污染、全球变暖、战争以及所有其他人为灾难带来的不良后果负责。
3. Our bodily environment and its many maladies. The brain lives inside a trouble-prone beast. This body inflicts aggravations on the mind that range from illnesses to aging to an unfortunately shaped nose. These conflicts are partly random, partly predictable, partly indifferent, partly self-inflicted.
3. 我们的身体环境及其诸多弊病。大脑寄居于一个问题重重的躯体之中。这个躯体会给大脑带来各种各样的困扰，从疾病到衰老，再到鼻子形状不佳，不一而足。这些冲突有的随机，有的可预测，有的无关紧要，有的则是自找的。
4. Our temporal environment and its brevity. Time contains all that exists, and over time it will erase all.
4. 我们所处的时间环境及其短暂性。时间包含一切存在之物，但随着时间的流逝，它也将抹去一切。

Let’s sketch out a characterization based on behaviors at the physical level only: A young man is a daredevil who ski-jumps from frightening heights. If he buys trendy outfits he really can’t afford, he enjoys provoking envy in the ski-lodge spotlight. If he arrives for jump practice hours before sunup, then nervously glances at his watch until his coach arrives, he suffers from time anxiety. If he constantly calls his mother for advice, he lacks maturity. Put these traits together and he becomes an athletic, hyperimpatient, self-absorbed, immature thrill seeker.

让我们仅从生理层面来勾勒人物性格：一个年轻人是个冒险家，喜欢从令人胆寒的高度进行滑雪跳台。如果他买了自己根本负担不起的时髦服装，他就会享受在滑雪小屋里成为众人瞩目的焦点，引人艳羡。如果他天还没亮就到跳台训练场，然后焦急地看表直到教练到来，他就会患有时间焦虑症。如果他总是打电话给母亲寻求建议，他就会显得不够成熟。把这些特质综合起来，他就成了一个运动能力强、极度缺乏耐心、自我中心、不成熟的冒险家。

At this point, his multifaceted characterization prepares him only for a supporting role. To evolve him into a complex protagonist, we need to transform his traits into dimensions. As noted above, when one trait consistently contradicts another, the tension between them fuses into a dimension. So, let’s take each of his traits, imagine its opposite, and see where that leads.

就目前而言，他多面的性格设定只适合扮演配角。要将他塑造成一个复杂的主角，我们需要将他的特质转化为维度。正如上文所述，当一个特质与另一个特质持续矛盾时，它们之间的张力就会融合为一个维度。因此，让我们逐一审视他的每个特质，想象它们的对立面，看看会得出什么结果。

If his vanity hides self-doubt, if PEDs fuel his athleticism, if the adrenaline rush that propels his death-defying stunts masks a mama’s boy longing for a dead father, if his every leap off a ski jump is a minisuicide, if his anxiousness only calms when he’s in midair, he might earn a story of his own.

如果他的虚荣心掩盖了自我怀疑，如果兴奋剂助长了他的运动天赋，如果肾上腺素飙升驱使他做出惊险特技，掩盖了他内心深处对已故父亲的思念，如果他每一次从滑雪跳台上纵身一跃都是一次小小的自杀，如果他的焦虑只有在空中才能平息，那么他或许会拥有属于自己的故事。

#↩

SOCIAL CONFLICTS

社会冲突

Now let’s look at social structures and a character’s struggles at this level of life.

现在让我们来看看社会结构以及人物在这个生活层面上的奋斗历程。

Massive institutions harden over time into hierarchies on a scale so great that the people in them feel little or no personal responsibility. These hierarchies shape human beings into the roles to be played, then organize them inside a pyramidal system in which the people at the bottom have no power, the people at the top have great power, and the people in the middle grab for power as they jostle up and down the chain of command. Stressful as these massive systems are, they couldn’t exist unless the people in them welcomed their roles. Indeed, institutions raise us, educate us, support us, and mold the roles we play.

庞大的机构随着时间的推移会固化成等级森严的体系，其规模之大，以至于身处其中的人们几乎感受不到任何个人责任感。这些等级制度塑造着人们的角色，并将他们组织成一个金字塔式的系统：底层的人毫无权力，顶层的人权力极大，而中间层的人则在权力链条上上下攀升，争夺权力。尽管这些庞大的系统令人倍感压力，但如果身处其中的人们不甘于扮演自己的角色，它们便无法存在。事实上，正是机构养育我们、教育我们、支持我们，并塑造着我们所扮演的角色。

As the documentarian Frederick Wiseman exposed in more than forty film studies of institutions, those who reach an organization’s pinnacle tend to be efficient but callous. As a result, from governments, corporations, and militaries to hospitals, monasteries, and families, institutions, to some degree, narrow their members into someone less than the ideal human being. The grand irony of civilization is that although social structures protect us from one kind of suffering (death by starvation), they inflict misery of another (begrudging obedience). 1 And humanity has no alternative. We need institutions to progress us on an outer level while we pay a price on an inner level.

正如纪录片导演弗雷德里克·怀斯曼在四十多部关于机构的影片研究中所揭示的那样，那些攀升至组织顶峰的人往往效率极高，却也冷酷无情。因此，从政府、企业、军队到医院、修道院、家庭，各种机构在某种程度上都将成员限制在理想人格的范畴之内。文明的巨大讽刺在于，尽管社会结构保护我们免于一种痛苦（饿死），却也带来了另一种痛苦（勉强服从）。而人类别无选择。我们需要机构在外部层面推动我们进步，却在内心层面付出代价。

The ideologies that govern institutions span a spectrum that runs from “I am my brother’s keeper” to “Every man for himself.” At the “Every man for himself” end of the spectrum sits predatory capitalism. This system exploits our innate drives for self-importance, wealth, and power. Sociopaths thrive in this environment. In the population as a whole, sociopaths constitute 1 percent; on Wall Street, 10 percent. 2 At the “I am my brother’s keeper” pole sit absolute governments and dictators claiming to care for their citizens but giving them no choice in what they get. Sociopaths feel equally at home here.

支配各种机构的意识形态涵盖范围很广，从“人人为己”到“人人自私”。在“人人自私”这一端，是掠夺性的资本主义。这种体系利用了我们与生俱来的对自我重要性、财富和权力的渴望。反社会人格者在这种环境下如鱼得水。在总人口中，反社会人格者占1%；在华尔街，这一比例高达10%。在“人人为己”这一端，是那些声称关心公民却不给予公民任何选择权的专制政府和独裁者。反社会人格者在这里同样如鱼得水。

In between these two extremes are meritocracies that promote people up the ladder of power based on hard work, intelligence, and achievement. Once in power, however, these elites pull the ladder up after them, turning their meritocracy into an oligarchy. In the United States, for example, wealthy white Protestant men wrote the Constitution, then created industries and universities—but at the same time, they built their power on slavery, Jim Crow, anti-Catholicism, anti-Semitism, anti-Hispanicism, and anti-feminism. 3

介于这两种极端之间的是精英统治，这种统治基于勤奋、智慧和成就提拔人们晋升权力阶梯。然而，一旦掌权，这些精英就会撤走晋升阶梯，将精英统治转变为寡头统治。例如，在美国，富有的白人新教徒撰写了宪法，然后创建了工业和大学——但与此同时，他们的权力建立在奴隶制、种族隔离、反天主教、反犹太主义、反西班牙裔主义和反女权主义之上。

Because institutions deindividualize, they cause people to do things they normally wouldn’t. Would a normal person taunt a stranger into killing himself? No, but a study of suicides committed in public found that once onlookers gather, they often become a mob, a momentary institution working in unison to bait the guy on the ledge into jumping. Every year during religious ceremonies and sporting events, panicking out-of-control crowds of passionate, like-minded people trample each other to death. 4

因为制度会使人丧失个性，所以它们会驱使人们做出他们通常不会做的事情。一个正常人会挑衅陌生人自杀吗？不会，但一项关于公共场所自杀的研究发现，一旦围观者聚集起来，他们往往会变成暴民，形成一种暂时的集体行为，共同诱使站在悬崖边的人跳下去。每年在宗教仪式和体育赛事期间，惊慌失措、失去控制的、充满激情且志同道合的人群互相践踏致死。

To cope with institutions, a character, beginning in childhood, straps on various social selves to guide his public interactions. Each social self has a set of traits designed to deal with the various institutions he faces. He does not chat with his professor in the same manner he talks to his rabbi or the clerk at the DMV or his boss at work or his cohorts at QAnon or his commanding officer in the National Guard.

为了应对各种机构，主人公从童年时期就开始塑造不同的社会人格，以此指导自己的公共互动。每个社会人格都具备一系列特质，旨在应对他所面对的各种机构。他与教授的交谈方式，与他和拉比、车管所职员、工作上的老板、QAnon的同伙，或是国民警卫队指挥官的交谈方式截然不同。

So let’s give a character a half-dozen traits based on the roles he plays when coping with stress and conflict within these institutions: (1) humble when meeting with his professor, (2) shamed when confessing to his rabbi, (3) obsequious while taking his DMV license renewal test, (4) generous when helping his boss solve a problem, (5) skeptical while conspiring about politics online, and (6) frightened when yelled at by his commanding officer.

所以，让我们根据一个角色在这些机构中应对压力和冲突时所扮演的角色，赋予他六种性格特征：（1）与教授见面时谦逊，（2）向拉比忏悔时感到羞愧，（3）参加车管所驾照更新考试时卑躬屈膝，（4）帮助老板解决问题时慷慨大方，（5）在网上讨论政治阴谋时持怀疑态度，（6）被指挥官吼叫时感到害怕。

These traits add up to a kind, shy, easily intimidated man—someone in need of the friends he finds in a chat room. This monochrome characterization may create a supporting role on the edge of events, but once again, to take him center stage, contradictions are needed to turn his traits into dimensions.

这些特质造就了一个善良、腼腆、容易受惊的男人——一个需要在聊天室里结交朋友的人。这种单调的人物刻画或许能让他成为事件边缘的配角，但要想让他真正成为故事的核心，就需要一些矛盾之处，才能使他的特质更加立体丰满。

Suppose the humble excuses he uses in his professor’s office become bragging recitations that bore his classmates; suppose his shame in his rabbi’s office feeds a secret, perverse sex life; suppose he fawns at the DMV, then drives off like a maniac; suppose his generosity toward his boss reverses into stinginess with coworkers; suppose his conspiracy theory cynicism stems from the gullible belief that people in power actually know what they’re doing; suppose his fear of military authority unleashes a murderous fury on the battlefield. If we were to wrap a story around him that expresses these dimensions, he might carry a telling to a staggering climax.

假设他在教授办公室里卑躬屈膝的借口，变成了令同学们厌烦的吹嘘；假设他在拉比办公室里的羞愧，催生了他秘密而扭曲的性生活；假设他在车管所里阿谀奉承，然后像疯子一样开车逃走；假设他对老板的慷慨，变成了对同事的吝啬；假设他对阴谋论的愤世嫉俗，源于他轻信掌权者确实知道自己在做什么；假设他对军队权威的恐惧，最终在战场上化作杀戮的狂怒。如果我们围绕他编造一个故事，展现他身上的这些特质，那么这个故事或许会走向一个令人震惊的高潮。

#↩

PERSONAL CONFLICTS

个人冲突

Public relationships value consequences; personal relationships value intentions. When a person with social power chooses a course of action, outcome matters more than sincerity. When someone in a personal relationship takes action, sincerity matters more than outcome. We condemn an investor’s financial mistakes no matter his personal intentions; we forgive a lover’s insult in the hope he didn’t mean it.

公共关系重视结果，私人关系重视意图。当拥有社会影响力的人选择行动时，结果比真诚更重要。而当私人关系中的人采取行动时，真诚比结果更重要。我们谴责投资者的财务失误，无论其个人意图如何；我们原谅爱人的侮辱，希望他并非有意为之。

Human beings suffer in social alienation but thrive in close company. The difference between social and personal relationships is intimacy. What bonds family to family, friend to friend, lover to lover are shared thoughts and feelings normally never revealed in public. The chemistry of intimacy takes two people beyond their social roles (coworkers, for example) to friendship and rapport. Depending on the personalities involved, of course, intimacy can be either joyful or painful.

人类在社交疏离中痛苦，在亲密关系中茁壮成长。社交关系和人际关系的区别在于亲密程度。维系家人、朋友、恋人之间关系的，是那些通常不会公开表达的共同思想和情感。亲密的化学反应使两个人超越了各自的社会角色（例如同事），发展出友谊和默契。当然，根据双方的性格，亲密关系既可以是快乐的，也可以是痛苦的。

As the core self moves from childhood to adulthood, it develops its identity along a spectrum of experiences that runs from approving, intense, and multiple loving intimacies at one end to insulting, cold, and singularly cruel intimacies at the other. It is possible, as we often observe, for two people to go through life in a personal relationship—father and son, for example—and never share intimacy, only shifting balances of power. The same is true for business partners who never become pals and strangers who never become lovers.

随着核心自我从童年走向成年，其身份认同的发展也沿着一条经验谱系展开，这条谱系一端是充满赞许、强烈且多元的亲密关系，另一端则是充满侮辱、冷漠且极其残酷的亲密关系。我们常常观察到，两个人即使建立起亲密关系——例如父子关系——也可能终其一生都无法真正分享亲密，而只是不断变换权力平衡。同样的道理也适用于那些永远无法成为朋友的商业伙伴，以及永远无法发展成恋人的陌生人。

Feelings run deepest at the personal level. This is why dramas of personal catastrophe have greater impact than tales of social conflict: Compare Macbeth to Coriolanus , Othello to The Winter’s Tale , King Lear to Julius Caesar .

情感在个人层面最为深刻。这就是为什么个人灾难的戏剧比社会冲突的故事更具感染力：比较《麦克白》和《科利奥兰纳斯》，《奥赛罗》和《冬天的故事》，《李尔王》和《尤利乌斯·凯撒》。

With each close friend, relative, or lover, a character evolves a version of himself that he could not bring out all on his own. If intimacy ends, he not only loses a loved one, he loses the version of himself that she inspired.

每一个亲密的朋友、亲人或爱人，都会帮助角色发展出自己无法独自展现的一面。如果亲密关系结束，他不仅会失去挚爱之人，也会失去她所激发出的那个自我。

To extend the method of character enrichment I used at the physical and social levels, I’ll add complexity to three characters by contradicting a trait of characterization with a pattern of intimate behavior.

为了扩展我在身体和社会层面上使用的角色丰富化方法，我将通过使角色特征与亲密行为模式相矛盾，为三个角色增加复杂性。

#↩

GENEROUS/SELFISH

慷慨/自私

Imagine a waiter working for tips who sends thoughtfully inscribed cards to everyone in his family on every birthday and holiday; who bakes far more cookies than necessary so he can share them by the dozen with neighborhood friends; who drifts from heart-breaking love affair to heart-breaking love affair in search of his dream lover. To everyone who knows him, he’s an idealistic, people-loving saint. Then he wins the lottery.

想象一下，一个靠小费维持生计的服务员，每个生日和节日都会给家人寄送精心写的贺卡；他烤的饼干远远超过所需，以便能一打一打地分给邻居朋友；他经历了一段又一段令人心碎的恋情，只为寻找梦中情人。在所有认识他的人眼里，他都是一个理想主义的、热爱他人的圣人。然后，他中了彩票。

A saint would donate his megamillions to charity, but this character gives nothing to anyone. He banks it all, moves to a warmer clime, and lives like royalty. When he baked cookies, sent cards, and slept around, he was greedy for love. Now that he is rich, this ex-waiter finally gets what he’s always wanted: people sucking up to him.

圣人会把巨额财富捐给慈善机构，但这人却一分钱也不给。他把钱全部存起来，搬到气候温暖的地方，过着帝王般的生活。以前他烤饼干、寄贺卡、到处留情，只是贪恋爱情罢了。如今他成了富翁，这位前服务员终于如愿以偿：人们都对他阿谀奉承。

#↩

SUPPORTIVE/SUBVERSIVE

支持型/颠覆型

Picture a husband who does everything for his wife—shop and cook, fold the laundry, and record her favorite shows. He listens patiently to her complaints and never complains in return. His characterization convinces his wife that he loves her and so she naturally loves him in return.

想象一下，一位丈夫为妻子包揽一切——购物、做饭、叠衣服，甚至录制她最喜欢的节目。他耐心倾听她的抱怨，自己却从不抱怨。他的这种行为让妻子确信他爱她，因此她自然而然地也爱上了他。

At parties, however, after a couple of drinks, he tells amusing tales about his wife that implicitly belittle her. He then ends each sly insult with a cheery “Isn’t that right, sweetheart?” Everyone who hears his anecdotes knows that he thinks his wife is a fool. She, however, only nods and smiles. He wounds her, and then forces her to show love in return by tagging his attacks with “sweetheart.”

然而，在聚会上，几杯酒下肚后，他便开始讲一些关于妻子的趣事，言下之意是贬低她。每说完一句暗讽的话，他都会兴高采烈地加上一句“是不是，亲爱的？”。所有听过他讲这些故事的人都知道，他认为妻子是个傻瓜。而她却只是点头微笑。他先是伤害了她，然后又用“亲爱的”来强迫她以爱回应。

#↩

GUILT/FORGIVENESS

内疚/宽恕

Imagine a hardworking careerist who takes his frustrations out on his children, abuse after abuse. Then one day he tells them that his doctor diagnosed him at risk for a stress-induced heart attack. Nonetheless, he continues to work day and night, so the kids have to forgive his malice and admire his courage. Better still, if he does not tell anyone about his pending coronary and eventually collapses on the job, his kids are forced to love his stoic sacrifice. Either way, his suffering vindicates his cruelty and his children forgive his past abuse. 5

想象一下，一个勤奋的职业人士，却把所有的挫败感都发泄在孩子身上，一次又一次地虐待他们。然后有一天，他告诉孩子们，医生诊断他有患上压力性心脏病的风险。尽管如此，他仍然日夜不停地工作，孩子们不得不原谅他的恶意，并敬佩他的勇气。更妙的是，如果他没有告诉任何人自己即将心脏病发作，最终在工作中倒下，孩子们就被迫去爱他那坚忍不拔的牺牲。无论如何，他的痛苦都为他的残忍开脱，孩子们也原谅了他过去的虐待行为。

As you labor over a character in the making, any pair of positive/negative adjectives that comes to mind could inspire a dimension. Hard/soft, sweet/sour, calm/hyper are three quick examples.

当你精心塑造一个角色时，任何一对浮现在脑海中的正面/负面形容词都可能激发你对角色的理解。例如，坚硬/柔软、甜美/酸涩、平静/亢奋等等。

#↩

INNER DIMENSIONS

内在维度

The mind is its own place and in itself can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.
心灵本身就是一个独立的世界，它可以把地狱变成天堂，也可以把天堂变成地狱。
—John Milton, Paradise Lost
——约翰·弥尔顿，《失乐园》

All outer dimensions—physical, social, personal—trace their roots back to the mind that gave them birth. As a result, complex characters tend to pull the storytelling inside themselves until their inner conflicts become more important, more fascinating than their outer struggles. This is true even when a character’s inner conflicts finally burst into violence. Two examples: Raskolnikov in Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment and Katherine (Florence Pugh) in Alice Birch’s screenplay for Lady Macbeth .

所有外在维度——物质的、社会的、个人的——都源于孕育它们的心灵。因此，复杂的人物往往会将故事的叙述引向内心，直到他们的内在冲突比外在的挣扎更加重要、更加引人入胜。即使人物的内在冲突最终演变为暴力，这一规律依然成立。例如，陀思妥耶夫斯基《罪与罚》中的拉斯科尔尼科夫，以及爱丽丝·伯奇改编的《麦克白夫人》中的凯瑟琳（弗洛伦斯·皮尤饰）。

As a writer works to fit a complex character to events and events to a complex character, the turning points that matter most take place below the surface. The author peers beneath the character’s words and gestures, searching behind his eyes, drawn to his churning psychology, trying to puzzle out the inner effects of what outwardly happens.

当作家努力将复杂的人物与事件相契合，并将事件融入人物之中时，最重要的转折点往往发生在表面之下。作者深入探究人物的言行举止，探寻其眼神背后的含义，被其翻涌的心理所吸引，试图解开外在事件背后更深层次的影响。

He may discover that his story’s external events cause internal reactions that send his character on an arc of change that alters his nature for better or worse: He becomes stronger or weaker, more childish or mature, more fulfilled or emptied out. Interest in the hows and whys of this inner evolution leads the writer’s imagination to enter the character’s core self, and from this subjective point of view invent new events that will enhance and express the character’s evolving nature. Changes in event design lead to further exploration of inner character; changes in inner character lead to a reinvention of events… and on the process goes.

他或许会发现，故事中的外部事件会引发人物的内在反应，推动人物走上一条变化的弧线，从而改变其本性，或好或坏：他可能变得更强大或更虚弱，更幼稚或更成熟，更充实或更空虚。对这种内在演变的来龙去脉的兴趣，会引导作者的想象力深入人物的内心世界，并从这种主观视角出发，创造出新的事件来丰富和展现人物不断演变的本性。事件设计的改变会促使作者进一步探索人物的内在性格；而内在性格的改变又会促使作者重新构思事件……如此循环往复。

Pensive minds like Shakespeare’s Hamlet and Virginia Woolf’s Clarissa Dalloway suffer what today we term cognitive dissonance . They flail in the chasm between thought and action. Their minds rage with an inner turmoil of memories, longings, night and day fantasies, streaming conscious and semiconscious anxieties over acting or not acting, sorting the real from the unreal, the true from the false, until their final choice is carried out in a single action.

像莎士比亚笔下的哈姆雷特和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫笔下的克拉丽莎·达洛维那样沉思的人物，都饱受我们今天所说的认知失调之苦。他们在思想与行动的鸿沟中挣扎。他们的内心翻涌着记忆、渴望、日夜幻想，以及关于行动与不行动的意识和半意识层面的焦虑，他们不断分辨现实与虚幻、真假，直到最终的抉择以一个行动得以实现。

More often than not the spark of contradiction that ignites a dimension comes from the negative side of human nature, the side people hide but writers excavate. These primal sources of character complexity flow from two inner levels: thought-driven contradictions vying in the conscious mind and wordless conflicts warring in the subconscious.

通常情况下，点燃某种维度的矛盾火花源自人性的阴暗面，是人们刻意隐藏却被作家挖掘出来的部分。这些构成人物复杂性的原始源泉来自两个内在层面：意识层面上相互冲突的思维驱动的矛盾，以及潜意识层面上无言的冲突。

#↩

CONSCIOUS CONFLICTS

意识冲突

Depending on his depth of self-awareness, a complex character thinks about, or to some degree senses, his inner incongruities and the disruptions they cause. In his private realm, he knows that sometimes he sees the truth of things, at other times he’s blind to the obvious; sometimes he’s kind, at other times cruel. In most cases, he tries to resolve these contradictions or at least get them under control.

根据自我认知的深度，复杂的人物会思考或在某种程度上感知到自身内在的矛盾及其造成的困扰。在内心深处，他明白自己有时能看清事物的真相，有时却对显而易见的事实视而不见；有时他心地善良，有时却又冷酷无情。大多数情况下，他会努力化解这些矛盾，或者至少将其控制在可控范围内。

Some private dimensions operate at the thinking level and connect two opposed qualities such as Intelligent/Unintelligent, Curious/Incurious, or Imaginative/Unimaginative. Other paradoxes come from the more sentient dimensions of Impulsive/Reflective, Angry/Calm, and Courageous/Timid that give a role emotional complexity.

有些私人维度在思维层面运作，连接着两种对立的特质，例如聪明/愚钝、好奇/不好奇或富有想象力/缺乏想象力。其他悖论则来自更具感知性的维度，例如冲动/反思、愤怒/冷静和勇敢/胆怯，这些维度赋予了情感复杂性。

Many social institutions were invented specifically to address one of these inner conflicts: Alcoholics Anonymous copes with the Craving/Spurning mind of the addicted. Buddhism calms the chronic worrier’s Past/Future frets, what Buddhists call the Monkey Mind—frantic images and words screeching and swinging from idea to idea, flinging thought feces at mental walls.

许多社会机构的创立正是为了解决这些内在冲突：戒酒互助会帮助成瘾者应对渴求与厌恶的矛盾心理；佛教则平息长期忧虑者对过去与未来的焦虑，佛教称之为“猴子心”——脑海中充斥着疯狂的画面和词语，它们在各种念头间跳跃、摇摆，如同将杂乱的思绪抛向心灵的墙壁。

Let’s sketch a couple examples of inner contradiction in the private realm. We’ll start once again with a trait and contradict it into a dimension.

让我们举几个私人领域内在矛盾的例子。我们再次从一个特质出发，并将其矛盾延伸到一个维度。

#↩

LESS VERSUS MORE

少即是多

Imagine a character who asks for nothing and lives a quiet life of less. Because he wants nothing, he lacks the focused desire of a protagonist. Now suppose an experience were to inspire in him a desire to expand outwardly into the noisy life of more. An inner contradiction could take hold between his wish to be celebrated and his need to stay hidden, between his impulse to express himself and his fear of exposure. With these dimensions, he could now star in his own story, as does Arthur Less in Less , a novel by Andrew Sean Greer.

想象一个无所求、过着平静简朴生活的角色。因为他一无所求，所以他缺乏主人公那种明确的欲望。现在假设某种经历激发了他向外拓展、融入喧嚣繁华生活的渴望。一种内在的矛盾便会在他渴望被赞誉与需要保持隐匿、表达自我与害怕暴露之间产生。有了这些特质，他便能成为自己故事的主角，就像安德鲁·肖恩·格里尔的小说《Less》中的主人公亚瑟·莱斯一样。

This contradiction between the need for less and the need for more, between inner and outer lives anchors Shakespeare’s most complex character: Hamlet. When Hamlet looks outward, trying to change the public world for the better, the corruption he finds disgusts him. When he looks inward, trying to change his inner world for the better, the paralysis he finds also disgusts him. He is withdrawn yet theatrical, consumed with grief yet flamboyant with wit, hyperaware of his inner self yet blind to his effect on others, an intellect without a strategy, an unstable self in search of an identity. Because both his inner and outer worlds seem meaningless, he verges on madness.

这种对“少即是多”的渴望，对“少即是多”的矛盾，构成了莎士比亚笔下最复杂的人物——哈姆雷特的性格核心。当哈姆雷特向外寻求改变，试图改善公共世界时，他所目睹的腐败令他作呕；当他向内审视，试图改善自己的内心世界时，他所发现的麻木不仁同样令他厌恶。他既孤僻又戏剧化，既沉浸在悲痛之中又才思敏捷，既对自己的内心世界了如指掌又对自身对他人的影响视而不见，他拥有智慧却缺乏策略，他的内心世界动荡不安，苦苦追寻着自我认同。由于他的内心世界和外部世界似乎都毫无意义，他最终走向了疯狂的边缘。

#↩

BELIEF VERSUS SKEPTICISM

信仰与怀疑

Beliefs treat illusions as truths. Commonly held ideas such as “Human beings are more good than evil,” “The Constitution embodies the perfect political system,” “God rules the universe,” and “My people are superior to your people” unify a society. When reality finally drags an illusion into the light, public belief withers, unity fractures, and people revolt. In the aftermath of revolution, however, society regroups around a more credible illusion and builds institutions to replace an old belief with a new fallacy.

信仰将幻象视为真理。诸如“人性本善”、“宪法体现了完美的政治制度”、“上帝主宰宇宙”、“我的人民优于你们的人民”等普遍接受的观念维系着社会。当现实最终揭穿幻象时，公众的信仰便会瓦解，社会团结瓦解，民众奋起反抗。然而，在革命之后，社会往往会围绕着一个更可信的幻象重新集结，并建立起新的制度来取代旧的信仰，用新的谬论取而代之。

Understanding this cycle, novelist Joseph Conrad divided his characters into two types: Idiots and Convicts. Idiots believe in illusions and enslave themselves to these ideas. Conradian idiots become heroes and nemeses, superpatriots and supervillains.

理解了这种循环，小说家约瑟夫·康拉德将他笔下的人物分为两类：白痴和罪犯。白痴相信幻想，并被这些幻想所奴役。康拉德笔下的白痴既可以是英雄，也可以是反派；既可以是超级爱国者，也可以是超级恶棍。

Convicts see illusions for what they are—comforting deceptions that protect us from an indifferent, hostile, chaotic universe. To a Conradian convict, action seems pointless. They often become the passive/reactive characters of pensive films, plays, and novels.

囚犯们看透了幻象的本质——那些令人感到慰藉的欺骗，它们保护我们免受冷漠、敌对、混乱宇宙的侵扰。在康拉德式的囚犯眼中，行动似乎毫无意义。他们常常成为沉思电影、戏剧和小说中被动/反应型的角色。

The writer’s problem becomes this: A belief inspires something worth doing; stories put beliefs into action. A character void of belief can only pose like a statue.

作者面临的问题是：信仰能激发有价值的行动；故事则将信仰付诸实践。一个缺乏信仰的角色只能像雕像一样摆姿势。

Imagine, for example, a chronic skeptic who thinks beliefs are for fools. He trusts no one and nothing. He never acts, he only scoffs; sardonic wit is his sole trait. This convict might make an amusing sidekick or subject for a short story, but he hasn’t the heft to carry a full-length telling. A story’s spine of action needs a lightning charge of belief to animate action.

例如，想象一下一个根深蒂固的怀疑论者，他认为信仰是傻瓜的行为。他不相信任何人，也不相信任何事。他从不行动，只会冷嘲热讽；他唯一的特点就是尖刻的讽刺。这样的罪犯或许可以成为一个有趣的配角，或者短篇小说的素材，但他缺乏足够的分量来支撑一个完整的故事。故事的脊梁需要信念的闪电般能量来推动情节发展。

So, to prepare a skeptic for his story, give him a belief; to add complexity, contradict it. You could, for example, test his views about the supernatural. Does he believe in the existence of a supreme being or not? As a cynic, he’s probably an agnostic who believes that the only logical position on the question of God’s existence is to doubt both theism and atheism. On that point he’s unshakable… until he falls in love with a believer and begins to doubt his doubt. What will he finally believe or not believe? Whichever way it turns, he’s now an interesting man with story potential.

所以，为了让一个怀疑论者做好接受你故事的准备，先给他灌输一种信念；为了增加故事的复杂性，再反驳这种信念。例如，你可以试探他对超自然现象的看法。他是否相信至高无上的存在？作为一个愤世嫉俗的人，他很可能是一个不可知论者，认为关于上帝是否存在的唯一合乎逻辑的立场就是同时怀疑有神论和无神论。在这一点上，他坚定不移……直到他爱上了一个信徒，并开始怀疑自己的怀疑。他最终会相信什么，又会不相信什么呢？无论结果如何，他现在都成了一个有趣的人物，拥有了故事的潜力。

Each of these examples explored just one dominant dimension, but multiple inner contradictions can easily coexist in the same character, as they did in Odysseus and Tony Soprano. Indeed, the modern writer’s ambition for the longform hundred-hour screen series demands characters of seemingly inexhaustible dimensionality, so that five years after their debut they still amaze audiences with hitherto unrevealed dynamics.

这些例子都只探讨了角色性格的一个主要维度，但多个内在矛盾很容易同时存在于同一个人物身上，就像奥德修斯和托尼·索普拉诺那样。事实上，现代编剧对百小时长篇剧集的雄心壮志要求角色拥有无穷无尽的维度，以至于在首播五年后，他们仍然能以之前未曾揭示的动态变化令观众惊叹不已。

The list of conflicting contradictions in human consciousness seems endless. Think of any adjective, imagine its opposite, and you have the beginning of a character dimension: Independent/Dependent, Neuroticism/Stability, Extraversion/Introversion, Agreeableness/Disagreeableness, Open-to-experience/Closed-to-experience, Conscientiousness/Carelessness, and on it goes. The only limit is your imagination. 6

人类意识中相互矛盾的事物似乎无穷无尽。随便想想一个形容词，再想象一下它的反义词，你就得到了一个性格维度的雏形：独立/依赖、神经质/稳定、外向/内向、宜人/不宜人、开放/封闭、尽责/粗心等等，不胜枚举。唯一的限制就是你的想象力。

#↩

CONSCIOUS VERSUS SUBCONSCIOUS CONFLICT

意识与潜意识的冲突

When talking about the innermost self, I prefer the term subconscious to unconscious . To me, the un- in unconscious suggests an inert, coma-like state, mindless as a rock. In fact, this deepest realm is an active, cognitive subconscious. Sub- simply means “ below consciousness.” 7

谈到内心深处的自我，我更倾向于使用“潜意识”而非“无意识”。在我看来，“无意识”中的“无”字暗示着一种惰性、昏迷般的状态，如同石头般麻木。事实上，这最深层的领域是一个活跃的、认知性的潜意识。“潜”字的意思仅仅是“意识之下”。

During the night, the subconscious rises into mindfulness, disguised inside the symbolic objects and irrational story lines of dreams. Throughout the day, however, the hidden self stays unknown and unheard, busily driving the desires that consciousness puts into action.

夜幕降临，潜意识升腾而起，隐匿于梦境的象征性事物和非理性故事之中。然而，在白日里，这隐藏的自我却始终不为人知，默默运转，驱使着意识所赋予的种种欲望付诸行动。

Because the core self is unaware of this process, a character believes he guides his own life. In fact, he is not in command. An alien, hidden self also occupies him. As Freud said, “The manifestations I notice in myself but do not know how to link up with the rest of my mental life seem to belong to another person.”

由于核心自我对此过程浑然不觉，角色会认为自己掌控着人生。事实上，他并非如此。一个陌生的、隐藏的自我也占据着他。正如弗洛伊德所说：“我注意到自身存在的某些现象，却不知如何与我精神生活的其他部分联系起来，这些现象似乎属于另一个人。”

The conscious and subconscious aspects of the mind are Janus-faced, inseparable, conflicted, and overlapping. Where does the subconscious end and the conscious begin? When does a character become aware of his subconscious desires? When does a conscious habit sink into the unthinking and instinctive? No clear line separates the two. In the sections that follow, I hold these inner realms apart to illustrate the principles of character design. In your work to create multidimensional roles, however, you will have to draw the line specifically, character by character.

意识和潜意识如同双面神雅努斯，密不可分，相互冲突，彼此重叠。潜意识的终点在哪里？意识的起点又在哪里？角色何时会意识到自己的潜意识欲望？有意识的习惯何时会融入无意识的本能？两者之间并没有清晰的界限。在接下来的章节中，我将这两个内在领域区分开来，以此来阐释角色设计的原则。然而，在创作多维角色时，你需要具体地、逐个角色地划清界限。

Confronting antisocial, often violent subconscious impulses is the primary moral struggle for almost every complex character you create. Embracing the hidden self’s dark heart as well as its halo of light is essential to self-knowledge. Light, of course, is easy to see; making darkness visible takes courage.

对抗潜意识中反社会、甚至暴力的冲动，几乎是所有你塑造的复杂角色面临的首要道德困境。接纳内心深处的黑暗面及其光明面，对于自我认知至关重要。光明当然显而易见，但将黑暗显露出来却需要勇气。

When a story’s inciting incident throws the life of a complex character out of balance, two desires appear simultaneously: (1) a conscious object of desire, a specific thing or situation that he feels would restore balance. (2) a subconscious, nascent desire that has lain undisturbed for years stirs to life.

当故事的导火索打破了复杂人物的生活平衡时，两种欲望会同时出现：（1）一种有意识的欲望对象，即他认为能够恢复平衡的具体事物或情境。（2）一种潜意识中、多年来未曾触动的萌芽欲望被唤醒。

#↩

THE CONSCIOUS OBJECT OF DESIRE

欲望的意识对象

Everyone wants reasonable control over their existence and the events that impact it. When an inciting incident throws life out of kilter, the desire to restore equilibrium naturally arises within a protagonist. What he must do to achieve this rebalance may be unclear at first, but sooner or later he will conceive of his object of desire, something he believes has the power to put his life back on its feet.

每个人都渴望对自己的生活以及影响生活的事件拥有合理的掌控权。当突发事件打破生活的平衡时，主人公自然会渴望恢复平衡。起初，他或许并不清楚自己必须做什么才能重获平衡，但迟早他会构想出自己渴望的对象，一个他相信能够帮助他重回正轨的事物。

Depending on the genre, his object of desire could be a physical thing such as a dead monster in the Horror film like Splinter ; a situation such as a family reunion in a Domestic Drama like The Corrections by Jonathan Franzen; or an experience such as a spiritual transformation in an Evolution Plot like The Razor’s Edge by W. Somerset Maugham.

根据题材的不同，他渴望的对象可以是物质的，例如恐怖电影《分裂》中的死去的怪物；可以是情境的，例如家庭剧《纠正》中的家庭团聚；也可以是体验的，例如进化论题材小说《刀锋》中的精神转变。

In the vast majority of stories, the protagonist’s conscious pursuit of an object of desire is sufficient to carry the telling.

在绝大多数故事中，主人公有意识地追求欲望对象就足以推动故事发展。

#↩

THE SUBCONSCIOUS OBJECT OF DESIRE

潜意识中的欲望对象

When a deeply conflicted, complex protagonist begins pursuit of his object of desire, his subconscious often comes into play as well and adds a counterdesire. The subconscious has its own wants and knows what steps to take.

当一个内心充满矛盾、性格复杂的主人公开始追求心仪之人时，他的潜意识往往也会介入，并产生一种与之相反的欲望。潜意识有它自己的需求，并且知道该采取哪些步骤。

As a result, the inciting incident also provokes a subconscious drive, a hidden hunger that seeks its own object of desire, one that will satisfy a long dormant and unrecognized wish or grievance. This subconscious desire contradicts the protagonist’s conscious desire, making the character, in many ways, his own worst enemy. A nascent counterdesire rarely, if ever, focuses on a physical object alone. Once again, depending on genre, his counterdesire could be either a situation such as the domination of an older sibling in a Domestic Drama, like the Skyler/Marie subplot in Breaking Bad , or an experience such as a transcendent, life-fulfilling romance in a Love Story, like The Bridges of Madison County .

因此，引发事件也激起了潜意识中的一种冲动，一种隐藏的渴望，它寻求着自己的欲望对象，以满足长期以来沉睡且未被察觉的愿望或不满。这种潜意识的欲望与主人公的意识欲望相冲突，使他在很多方面都成为了自己最大的敌人。这种萌芽的反欲望几乎从未仅仅指向某个具体的对象。同样，根据作品类型的不同，他的反欲望可能是一种情境，例如家庭剧中兄姐之间的支配关系，就像《绝命毒师》中斯凯勒和玛丽的支线剧情；也可能是一种体验，例如爱情故事中一段超凡脱俗、圆满人生的浪漫爱情，就像《廊桥遗梦》中那样。

If a character’s conscious and subconscious desires are the same (hungry, he opens his refrigerator; horny, he masturbates; depressed, he calls a friend) they add neither complexity nor depth. Why give a character a subconscious desire if it just happens to be the same thing he wants consciously? Who would notice?

如果一个角色的意识和潜意识欲望完全一致（饿了就打开冰箱；性欲高涨就自慰；情绪低落就给朋友打电话），那么这种设定既不复杂也不深刻。如果角色的潜意识欲望恰好与他意识层面的欲望相同，那又何必赋予它潜意识欲望呢？谁又会注意到呢？

But if these two desires contradict each other, if his subconscious desire blocks and reverses his conscious will, then things get interesting. Psychologists from William James to Jacques Lacan have argued that the subconscious is a contra-mirror of its conscious cousin. For writers, reverse reflection has been common knowledge for centuries.

但如果这两种欲望相互矛盾，如果他的潜意识欲望阻碍并逆转了他的意识意志，那么事情就变得有趣了。从威廉·詹姆斯到雅克·拉康，心理学家们都认为潜意识是意识的镜像。对于作家而言，这种反向镜像早已是几个世纪以来的常识。

For a subconscious desire to draw the interest of a reader/audience, it must directly contradict or sharply contrast with the character’s conscious hopes and longings. Then people notice… with interest.

为了吸引读者/观众的潜意识兴趣，这种潜意识的欲望必须与角色有意识的希望和渴望直接矛盾或形成鲜明对比。这样，人们才会注意到……并产生兴趣。

The exact balance of power between a character’s conscious and subconscious selves is up to the writer to strike: Neither dismiss it cynically as animal instinct, nor smugly treat it with a mechanical calculation.

角色意识和潜意识之间的力量平衡，取决于作者的把握：既不能愤世嫉俗地将其视为动物本能，也不能沾沾自喜地用机械的计算来对待它。

#↩

LOVE VERSUS HATE

爱与恨

Consider the dimension that contradicts love with hate:

想想爱与恨相互矛盾的维度：

Jules Feiffer’s screenplay for Carnal Knowledge spans the life of Jonathan Fuerst (Jack Nicholson) from his college days to middle age. If we were to ask Jonathan what he wants out of life, his conscious answer would be: “I’m a good-looking, fun-loving financial success. My life would be paradise if I could just find the perfect woman to share it.” Over the decades he meets woman after woman, all attractive, all intelligent, all loving, but every affair falls into the same pattern: a beautifully amorous beginning, a bitter, boring middle, an ugly, humiliating break-up. In the wreckage of romance, each woman finds herself abandoned.

朱尔斯·费弗为《性爱知识》创作的剧本讲述了乔纳森·弗斯特（杰克·尼科尔森饰）从大学时代到中年的生活。如果我们问乔纳森他想要什么，他理智上的回答会是：“我英俊潇洒，热爱生活，事业有成。如果能找到一个完美的女人与我共度余生，我的生活就如同天堂。”几十年来，他邂逅了一位又一位女性，她们都魅力四射、聪慧过人、温柔体贴，但每一段恋情都遵循着同样的模式：美好的开始，苦涩乏味的中间阶段，以及丑陋屈辱的分手。在爱情的残骸中，每个女人都发现自己被抛弃了。

Jonathan’s dominant dimension follows the tradition set by Don Juan and Vicomte de Valmont: the woman-hating romantic. Consciously, he tells himself that he gave a lifetime of love to women, and yet they, for various reasons, always broke his heart. Subconsciously, he loathed each and every one. Every year, he seduced a woman into adoration, then once he trapped her in that vulnerable place, he systematically crushed the heart out of her. The conscious desire to love and subconscious urge to hate have coexisted since monogamy.

乔纳森的主导维度遵循了唐璜和瓦尔蒙子爵开创的传统：一个憎恨女性的浪漫主义者。他自认为一生都奉献给了女性，然而她们却总是因为各种原因让他心碎。潜意识里，他憎恨每一个女人。每年，他都诱骗一个女人对他倾慕不已，一旦将她困在那个脆弱的境地，便会系统性地将她的心彻底摧毁。自一夫一妻制出现以来，这种有意识的爱欲与潜意识的恨意便一直并存。

#↩

FEAR VERSUS COURAGE

恐惧与勇气

Action writers work along a spectrum that runs from life-risking action to paralyzed terror. When a dimension connects these two extremes, the result is genuine heroism.

动作小说家的创作范围很广，从生死攸关的动作场面到令人窒息的恐惧，无所不包。当某种元素将这两个极端联系起来时，便成就了真正的英雄主义。

Fear is an instinctive reaction to the threat of death, followed by an impulse to flee; courage is a deliberate choice to risk death, followed by action against the threat. Absolute fear begins in the subconscious and ultimately takes full control of a coward; absolute courage begins in a conscious choice and drives an Action Hero.

恐惧是对死亡威胁的本能反应，随之而来的是逃跑的冲动；勇气则是深思熟虑后选择冒生命危险，并采取行动对抗威胁。绝对的恐惧始于潜意识，最终完全控制懦夫；绝对的勇气源于清醒的选择，并驱动着行动英雄。

Superheroes, such as Spider-Man and Wolverine, build a character around one fantastic dimension, often fusing the human with the mythical, animal, magical, or pseudoscientific. Crime fighters, such as John McClane or Dirty Harry Callahan, cluster a characterization of true-to-life yet cool traits into a romanticized tough guy. Both types exhibit superlative, self-sacrificial, courageous altruism on behalf of the victimized, but nothing from their interior ever contradicts anything on their exterior.

超级英雄，例如蜘蛛侠和金刚狼，围绕一个奇幻维度塑造角色，通常将人类与神话、动物、魔法或伪科学元素融合在一起。而像约翰·麦克莱恩或“肮脏的哈里”卡拉汉这样的打击犯罪者，则将真实而又酷炫的特质融合在一个浪漫化的硬汉形象中。这两种类型的角色都展现出超凡的、自我牺牲的、勇敢的利他主义精神，为了受害者而战，但他们的内心世界与外在形象之间却始终保持一致。

Complex heroes such as Henry Fleming in Stephen Crane’s novel The Red Badge of Courage or Richard Phillips (Tom Hanks) in Captain Phillips pit their conscious moral strength against a fear-soaked subconscious. In other words, unlike the idealized calm of an action hero, the mind of a realistic hero does not disconnect the conscious from the subconscious. Rather, the character makes decisions to take life-risking actions while simultaneously gripped by fear.

像斯蒂芬·克莱恩小说《红色英勇勋章》中的亨利·弗莱明，或是电影《菲利普船长》中的理查德·菲利普斯（汤姆·汉克斯饰）这样的复杂英雄，都将他们清醒的道德力量与充满恐惧的潜意识进行对抗。换句话说，与动作英雄理想化的冷静不同，现实主义英雄的内心并非将清醒与潜意识割裂开来。相反，他们会在恐惧的桎梏下，做出危及生命的决定。

#↩

CONFLICTS WITHIN THE SUBCONSCIOUS

潜意识内部的冲突

Readers and audiences perceive subconscious dimensions by implication. They compare what a character says with what he does; they match the reasons and rationalizations he gives others against the actual choices and actions he takes in the world.
