When they spot an inconsistency, they sense a clash of forces at work behind his eyes, fears skulking in the darkness versus angers aimed at the world. These deepest of all wars pit two irreconcilable hungers against each other. Ineffable subconscious conflicts, invisible to the character but glimpsed by the reader/audience, then push and pull through the story.

读者和观众通过暗示感知潜意识层面。他们将角色的言行进行比较；将角色给出的理由和解释与他在现实世界中的实际选择和行动进行比对。当他们发现矛盾之处时，便能感受到角色眼神背后冲突的力量：潜伏在黑暗中的恐惧与指向世界的愤怒。这些最深层的战争，将两种不可调和的欲望置于对立面。这些难以言喻的潜意识冲突，角色自身无法察觉，却能被读者/观众瞥见，并在故事中不断推动和拉扯着人物。

Portraying these hidden, primal conflicts may be the most difficult work that ever confronts an author. Novelists and short story writers often use an omniscient third-person narrator to describe a character’s psychic tensions directly to the reader. Screenwriters and playwrights also use this device but rarely. Of the two kinds of storytellers—those who explain and those who imply—I prefer the latter.

描绘这些隐秘而原始的冲突或许是作家面临的最艰巨的任务。小说家和短篇小说作家常常使用全知全能的第三人称叙述者，直接向读者展现人物的心理张力。编剧和剧作家也会运用这种手法，但并不常见。在两种叙事方式——解释型和暗示型——中，我更倾向于后者。

#↩

SELF VERSUS OTHER

自我与他人

The lower brain obeys two imperatives: Protect yourself and protect your gene pool. In the balance, the life force feels that the second duty is more important than the first. For this reason, parents sacrifice themselves for their children, soldiers die for their country, and believers strap on dynamite vests to kill nonbelievers. The choice between self and genes may seem irrational at times, but it drove the evolution of life on our planet. Consequently, the most persistent, virtually daily conflict waged within the subconscious mind is self-love versus other-love. 8

低级脑遵循两条准则：保护自身和保护基因库。在平衡中，生命力认为后者比前者更为重要。因此，父母会为子女牺牲，士兵会为国捐躯，信徒会穿上炸药背心去杀死非信徒。自我与基因之间的选择有时看似不理性，但正是这种选择推动了地球上生命的进化。因此，潜意识中最持久、几乎每天都在发生的冲突就是自爱与爱他人之间的冲突。

As a famous example, consider Robert Benton’s screenplay for Kramer vs. Kramer . Ted Kramer (Dustin Hoffman) begins the story as a self-absorbed, immature workaholic whose wife labors as a stay-at-home mom for his son while playing surrogate mother to him. Her sudden abandonment of both throws Kramer’s self-content life radically out of balance. This negative turning point arouses within Kramer a previously suppressed, never-acted-on need: the subconscious longing to be a mensch, a loving human being. His son’s well-being becomes far more important than his own. At the climax, he acts to forfeit his needs for his son’s.

以罗伯特·本顿的剧本《克莱默夫妇》为例。故事伊始，泰德·克莱默（达斯汀·霍夫曼饰）是一个自我中心、不成熟的工作狂，他的妻子在家照顾儿子，同时也扮演着代理母亲的角色。妻子的突然离去彻底打破了克莱默原本安逸的生活平衡。这一负面转折唤醒了克莱默内心深处一个被压抑、从未付诸行动的需求：他潜意识里渴望成为一个正直的人，一个充满爱心的人。儿子的幸福远比他自己的幸福重要。在故事的高潮，他为了儿子放弃了自己的需求。

#↩

ILLUSION VERSUS DELUSION

错觉与错觉

Another conflict that could arise in the subconscious concerns a character’s processing of reality—the difference between illusion and delusion. An illusion is belief in a false perception, such as a mirage, a phantom limb, or faith in the impossible; a delusion is a rigid belief in a false reality, a symptom typical of mental disorder.

潜意识中可能出现的另一个冲突涉及角色对现实的认知——错觉和妄想之间的区别。错觉是对错误感知的信念，例如海市蜃楼、幻肢或对不可能之事的信仰；妄想是对错误现实的坚定信念，这是精神障碍的典型症状。

In the backstory of A Streetcar Named Desire , Tennessee Williams’s protagonist, Blanche DuBois, pursued girlhood illusions of romantic love into a ruinous marriage, loss of her family estate, and secret years as a prostitute. Despite it all, she held on to her princess illusions and fantasized an ideal life to come. Finally, under extremes of alcohol, humiliation, and sexual violence, her self-deceptions collapse into total delusion and an asylum for the insane.

在田纳西·威廉姆斯的《欲望号街车》的背景故事中，主人公布兰奇·杜波依斯少女时期对浪漫爱情的幻想，最终导致她步入一段不幸的婚姻，失去了家族产业，并被迫秘密从事卖淫活动。尽管如此，她仍然执着于公主梦，幻想着未来会过上理想的生活。最终，在酒精、羞辱和性暴力的双重折磨下，她的自欺欺人彻底崩溃，陷入了彻底的妄想，最终被送进了精神病院。

Absurdist farces, such as Edward Albee’s A Delicate Balance , aside, characters beset with dimensions of subconscious contradiction often end in death or madness.

撇开爱德华·阿尔比的《微妙的平衡》等荒诞闹剧不谈，那些被潜意识矛盾所困扰的角色往往以死亡或疯狂告终。

#↩

CASE STUDY: ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA

案例研究：安东尼与克利奥帕特拉

For two examples of how dimensions on multiple levels crisscross in a complex character, consider Shakespeare’s magnificent lovers, Antony and Cleopatra.

要了解复杂人物身上多层次的维度是如何交织在一起的两个例子，请看莎士比亚笔下伟大的恋人安东尼和克莉奥佩特拉。

Antony’s prime dimension pits his social self against his hidden self: his command of the Roman Empire versus his lust for the queen of Egypt. Or put another way, a conflict between conscious reason and subconscious drive. Antony’s political self pushes his reputation to its furthest reaches, while his inner self craves carnality at its most intense.

安东尼的核心特质在于他社会化的自我与隐秘的自我之间的冲突：他对罗马帝国的统治与他对埃及女王的欲望之间的矛盾。或者换句话说，这是意识理性与潜意识冲动之间的冲突。安东尼的政治自我将他的声望推向极致，而他的内心却渴望着最强烈的肉欲。

This clever, articulate, pragmatic, proud general is not confused about the politics of Rome. Antony knows what he ought to do. But he’s also a pleasure-loving, beauty-obsessed, lovesick fool. His hunger for Cleopatra drives what he wants to do. And, as noted, the difference between ought and want is all the difference in the world.

这位聪明、能言善辩、务实而又骄傲的将军对罗马的政治局势了如指掌。安东尼知道自己应该做什么。但他同时也是一个沉迷享乐、痴迷美貌、为爱痴狂的傻瓜。他对克利奥帕特拉的渴望驱使着他的一切行为。而且，正如前文所述，应该做什么和想要做什么之间的差别，往往决定着人的命运。

To further enrich Antony’s nature, Shakespeare added numerous contradictions over a wide range of behaviors. When he is on the world’s stage, he roars in the rugged, heedless voice of a warrior-general. When he lounges with Cleopatra, he speaks with the kiss-soaked, caressing voice of a poet. He commands legions yet enslaves himself to a woman. He’s an adult at the head of his armies, an adolescent at the feet of his beloved. He is willful on the battlefield, will-less in Cleopatra’s bed.

为了进一步丰富安东尼的性格，莎士比亚在他的诸多行为中增添了诸多矛盾之处。当他在世界舞台上叱咤风云时，他以粗犷豪放、不顾一切的将军之声咆哮；当他与克莉奥佩特拉幽会时，他又以充满爱意、温柔细语的诗人之声低语。他统领千军万马，却又甘愿臣服于一个女人。在军队中，他是成熟稳重的成年人；在爱人面前，他却像个懵懂的少年。在战场上，他意志坚定；在克莉奥佩特拉的床上，他却又软弱无力。

If we look into the heart of Antony, we may see that for him war and love are just two versions of passion and pleasure. As people who love war will tell you, killing is a passion and victory a deep pleasure. In the film Patton , for example, when General George Patton surveys the carnage of dead and bleeding soldiers on a smoldering battlefield, he whispers, “God help me, but I love it so.” The same words he might whisper in a midnight passion.

如果我们探究安东尼的内心，或许会发现，对他而言，战争和爱情不过是激情与快乐的两种不同表现形式。正如那些热爱战争的人会告诉你的那样，杀戮是一种激情，胜利是一种极致的快感。例如，在电影《巴顿将军》中，当乔治·巴顿将军巡视着战场上血肉模糊、奄奄一息的士兵时，他低声说道：“上帝保佑，但我就是如此热爱这一切。” 这句话，或许也会在他午夜激情澎湃之时脱口而出。

Cleopatra is one of Shakespeare’s most complex characters. She’s a royal decadent and an innocent enchantress. She’s courageous in the face of her enemies yet panic-driven in war. She is a nonstop actress who fills her performances with such truth of feeling, no one doubts her.

克利奥帕特拉是莎士比亚笔下最复杂的人物之一。她既是奢靡的皇室贵族，又是天真无邪的女神。面对敌人，她英勇无畏；而战乱之中，她又容易惊慌失措。她是一位演技精湛的演员，表演真挚动人，令人信服。

In fact, men find her so alluring, that what in other women would be defects and vices, in her become perfections and virtues: Her vicious anger becomes aristocratic command; her wild wailings become the tears of sorrow; her immature clowning becomes charming humor; her drunkenness becomes queenly celebration; her nagging becomes concern for Antony; her begging and bargaining become humility and reasonableness; her bad jokes become wit; her wanton sexuality becomes charisma; her limitless ego and vanity get reinterpreted into patriotism and love of country.

事实上，男人们觉得她如此迷人，以至于在其他女人身上会被视为缺点和恶习的特质，在她身上却变成了完美和美德：她恶毒的愤怒变成了高贵的威严；她狂野的哭喊变成了悲伤的泪水；她幼稚的滑稽表演变成了迷人的幽默；她的醉酒变成了女王般的庆祝；她的唠叨变成了对安东尼的关心；她的乞求和讨价还价变成了谦逊和通情达理；她蹩脚的笑话变成了机智；她放荡的性欲变成了魅力；她无限的自我和虚荣心被重新诠释为爱国主义和对祖国的热爱。

Cleopatra’s genius is this: When forces of rage, greed, and lust arise from her subconscious, her perceptive mind captures them before they can reach the world and converts them into entrancing, persuasive performances. What her lover, her enemies, and subjects see is not darkness but greatness. As a result, her core dimension mirrors Antony’s: shrewd, willful, calculating ambition versus foolish, weak-willed, surrender to passion.

克利奥帕特拉的过人之处在于：当愤怒、贪婪和欲望的力量从她的潜意识中涌现时，她敏锐的洞察力会在它们蔓延至世间之前将其捕捉，并转化为引人入胜、极具说服力的表演。她的爱人、敌人和臣民看到的不是黑暗，而是伟大。因此，她的核心特质与安东尼的截然相反：精明、意志坚定、精于算计的野心，与愚蠢、意志薄弱、屈服于激情形成鲜明对比。

Some define tragedy as never getting what you want; others suggest that true tragedy gives you exactly what you want at its full price.

有人将悲剧定义为永远无法得到你想要的东西；也有人认为真正的悲剧会让你付出全部代价，得到你想要的东西。

#↩

CHARACTER CONFLICT IN DEPTH

深入剖析人物冲突

We often think of characters as if they were containers. We package their qualities inside spatial modifiers such as “round” and “flat.” We label the incurious as “square,” bores as “shallow,” and bigots as “narrow,” while a mind open to new ideas seems “broad.” And perhaps the most common person-as-a-vessel allusion: “deep.”

我们常常把人物想象成容器。我们用“圆形”和“扁平”之类的空间修饰词来概括他们的特质。我们把缺乏好奇心的人称为“方形”，把无聊的人称为“肤浅的”，把偏执的人称为“狭隘的”，而乐于接受新思想的人则被认为是“宽广的”。或许最常见的将人比作容器的说法是：“深邃的”。

These adjectives serve as conversational shorthand, but to invent an intriguing, multidimensional role, an author takes the measure of a soul. By what gauge does someone seem full or empty? How can a writer sound the depths of character?

这些形容词在口语中可以作为简略表达，但要塑造一个引人入胜、多维度的角色，作者需要衡量人物的灵魂。用什么标准来衡量一个人是充实还是空虚？作家如何才能触及人物性格的深层含义？

Human beings have an inborn echo device that pings into play the moment they meet someone. This instantaneous instinct needs no thought; it knows it when it sees it. Our subconscious sonar quickly tracks signs in the face, hears tremors in the voice, senses tensions in gestures, then looks behind the eyes to plumb the inner energies of a human vessel. This sounding of depth has a name: First Impression.

人类天生就有一种回声装置，一旦与人相遇，便会立即启动。这种瞬间的本能无需思考，它一眼就能识别。我们潜意识的声呐会迅速追踪面部表情，辨别声音中的颤抖，感知手势中的紧张，然后透过眼神探寻，深入挖掘一个人的内在能量。这种深度探测有一个名字：第一印象。

The first-impression instinct evolved to answer the question, “Can I trust this person?” The answer was (and still is) a key to survival. Characters that readers and audiences instinctively trust and admire over time tend to have inner dimensions reaching into their private and hidden selves. This sense of depth encourages empathy and trust.

第一印象的本能进化是为了回答“我能信任这个人吗？”这个问题。答案过去是（现在仍然是）生存的关键。读者和观众随着时间的推移，本能地信任和欣赏的角色往往具有深入其私密内心世界的丰富内涵。这种深度感能够激发同理心和信任。

Below are ten traits associated with depth of character, followed by examples taken from stage, screen, and page. If your storytelling ambitions call for characters of complexity and depth, this list should spur your imagination.

以下列出了与人物深度相关的十个特质，并列举了来自舞台、银幕和文学作品的例子。如果你渴望创作出复杂而深刻的人物形象，这份清单应该能激发你的创作灵感。

#↩

1. Ironic Self-Awareness

1. 反讽式的自我意识

He is always on guard against self-deception and rarely fooled by what goes on inside his own mind. Example: Claire Underwood (Robin Wright) in Beau Willimon’s longform series House of Cards .

他时刻警惕自欺欺人，很少会被自己内心的想法所蒙蔽。例如：博·威利蒙的长篇剧集《纸牌屋》中的克莱尔·安德伍德（罗宾·怀特饰）。

#↩

2. Insight into Others

2. 对他人的洞察力

He is always aware of public pretensions and never fooled by what goes on inside society. Example: Madame Merle in Henry James’s The Portrait of a Lady .

他始终洞悉公众的虚伪，从不被社会内部的种种表象所蒙蔽。例如：亨利·詹姆斯小说《一位女士的画像》中的梅尔夫人。

#↩

3. Intelligence

3. 智力

He can think. He gathers knowledge from all disciplines and commands the logic that puts it to work. Example: Miss Marple in twelve novels and twenty short stories by Agatha Christie.

他思维敏捷，博采众长，并能运用逻辑思维将其融会贯通。例如：阿加莎·克里斯蒂笔下十二部长篇小说和二十篇短篇小说中的马普尔小姐。

#↩

4. A History of Suffering

4. 苦难史

As Aeschylus wrote in The Oresteia :

正如埃斯库罗斯在《奥瑞斯忒亚》中所写：

Even in our sleep, pain which cannot forget falls drop by drop upon the heart until, in our despair, against our will, through the terrible grace of God, comes wisdom.
即使在睡梦中，无法忘怀的痛苦也会一滴一滴地落在心上，直到我们在绝望中，违背我们的意愿，通过上帝可怕的恩典，智慧降临。

Although a character wishes for happiness, he finds depth through suffering. The happy mind thinks about life’s benefits; the suffering mind sinks deeper into itself. Suffering takes a character beneath his routines to discover he is not who he thought he was. Losing a loved one smashes through the floor of the core self, revealing a deeper level. Grief then smashes through that floor, revealing yet greater depth. 9

尽管人物渴望幸福，但他却在苦难中找到了人生的深度。快乐的心灵思考着人生的美好；而痛苦的心灵则沉溺于自我之中。苦难将人物带入日常的表象之下，让他发现自己并非自己以为的那样。失去挚爱如同重锤般击碎了自我核心的表层，揭示出更深层次的自我。随后，悲痛又会击碎这层表层，揭示出更为深邃的自我。

Try as people may, they cannot tell themselves to stop feeling pain. Suffering gives them a more accurate sense of their limitations, what they can and cannot control. Pain propels a callow mind into maturity. The wise response places anguished experiences in a moral context and redeems something bad by turning it into something precious. In short, a deep soul has witnessed pain, caused pain, and lived with the guilt. Example: Mike Ehrmantraut (Jonathan Banks) in Breaking Bad and Better Call Saul risks his life in crime after crime to provide a future for his granddaughter.

人们无论如何努力，都无法让自己停止感受痛苦。苦难让他们更清楚地认识到自身的局限，以及哪些事情可以掌控，哪些事情无法掌控。痛苦促使懵懂的心灵走向成熟。明智的做法是将痛苦的经历置于道德的框架下，并通过将其转化为珍贵之物来救赎罪恶。简而言之，拥有深刻灵魂的人既目睹过痛苦，也造成过痛苦，并承受着随之而来的愧疚。例如，《绝命毒师》和《风骚律师》中的迈克·埃尔曼特劳特（乔纳森·班克斯饰）为了给孙女创造一个美好的未来，一次又一次地冒着生命危险犯罪。

#↩

5. Broad Experience over Time

5. 长期积累的广泛经验

A young character may seem wise beyond his years, but in truth, depth needs wide-ranging experience and, above all, time. Example: Claudia Hampton in Penelope Lively’s novel Moon Tiger .

一个年轻角色可能看起来比实际年龄更成熟，但实际上，深度需要广泛的阅历，更重要的是，需要时间。例如：佩内洛普·莱弗利的小说《月虎》中的克劳迪娅·汉普顿。

#↩

6. Focused Attention

6. 专注力

Face-to-face, he listens intently, makes eye contact and reads subtext. Example: Don Vito Corleone (Marlon Brando / Robert De Niro) in The Godfather and The Godfather Part II .

面对面时，他会认真倾听，与人进行眼神交流，并解读言外之意。例如：《教父》和《教父2》中的唐·维托·柯里昂（马龙·白兰度/罗伯特·德尼罗饰）。

#↩

7. Love of Beauty

7. 热爱美

Depth sharpens his sensitivity until beauty is almost painful. Example: Aaliya Sohbi in An Unnecessary Woman by Rabih Alameddine.

深度使他的感知力更加敏锐，以至于美感近乎痛苦。例如：拉比·阿拉梅丁执导的电影《一个不必要的女人》中的阿莉娅·索比。

#↩

8. Calm

8. 冷静

No matter the threat or stress, he keeps his passions under control. Example: Captain Augustus “Gus” McCrae (Robert Duvall) in Larry McMurtry’s miniseries, Lonesome Dove , which was based on his novel.

无论面临怎样的威胁或压力，他都能控制自己的情绪。例如：拉里·麦克默特里根据其小说改编的迷你剧《寂寞之鸽》中的奥古斯都·“格斯”·麦克雷上尉（罗伯特·杜瓦尔饰）。

#↩

9. Cynic and Skeptic

9. 愤世嫉俗者和怀疑论者

Hope, he believes, is the denial of reality. He doesn’t trust anything anyone says until he tests it against his own mind. Example: Mama Nadi in Ruined by playwright Lynn Nottage.

他认为，希望是对现实的否定。除非经过自己的检验，否则他不会相信任何人说的话。例如：剧作家林恩·诺蒂奇的剧作《毁灭》中的纳迪妈妈。

#↩

10. A Searcher for Meaning

10. 意义的追寻者

He gets God’s joke. He knows life has no intrinsic meaning. So he searches for one somewhere in the gap between living for yourself and living for others. Example: Benna Carpenter in Lorrie Moore’s novel Anagrams .

他领会了上帝的玩笑。他知道生命本身没有意义。所以他试图在为自己而活和为他人而活之间的某种空隙中寻找意义。例如：洛莉·摩尔的小说《字谜》中的本娜·卡彭特。

Roll these traits into one role and they often create an antihero—a loner hardened by bad luck but vulnerable to the suffering of others; a stoic bemused by his own suffering; sharp-witted in public, self-mocking when alone; cynical about society’s rules, committed to a personal code; a romantic wary of romance.

将这些特质融合到一个角色中，往往会造就一个反英雄——一个因厄运而变得坚强的孤独者，却又容易被他人的痛苦所触动；一个对自己的痛苦感到困惑的斯多葛主义者；一个在公众面前机智敏锐，独处时却自嘲自笑的人；一个对社会规则愤世嫉俗，却又恪守个人准则的人；一个对爱情保持警惕的浪漫主义者。

All ten traits embedded themselves in Sam Spade ( The Maltese Falcon ), Rick Blaine ( Casablanca ), and Philip Marlowe ( The Big Sleep ), who were portrayed to perfection three times over by Humphrey Bogart. Few actors since have been tested to that depth; Denzel Washington first among the best.

这十项特质都深深地烙印在了山姆·斯佩德（《马耳他之鹰》）、里克·布莱恩（《卡萨布兰卡》）和菲利普·马洛（《夜长梦多》）这三个角色身上，而亨弗莱·鲍嘉三次将这三个角色演绎得淋漓尽致。此后，很少有演员能经受如此深厚的考验；丹泽尔·华盛顿便是其中翘楚。

#↩

LIFE IN THE SUBTEXT

潜台词中的生活

Text: a character’s outer behavior in word and action. These verbal and physical expressions stimulate images in a reader’s imagination or strike the eye and ear of an audience. Together, they create his characterization.

文本：指人物通过言语和行动展现的外在行为。这些语言和肢体表达能够激发读者的想象，或吸引观众的眼球和耳目。它们共同塑造了人物形象。

Subtext: a character’s thoughts and feelings that are conscious but unexpressed as well as subconscious and thus inexpressible. The core self plies these ideas and attitudes within himself and to no one else; while at a deepest level of subtext, his ineffable moods and desires pulse below his awareness. 10

潜台词：角色意识层面上未表达的思想和情感，以及潜意识层面上无法言说的想法和情感。核心自我只在内心深处思考这些想法和态度，不会与他人分享；而在潜台词的最深层，他难以言喻的情绪和欲望在他意识之外涌动。

Minor characters are text only. These roles serve a story by acting out exactly who they seem to be. The writer deliberately denies them depth and an inner life worth knowing.

次要角色仅以文字形式出现。这些角色通过展现他们表面上的形象来服务于故事。作者刻意剥夺了他们的深度和值得了解的内心世界。

A major character, on the other hand, is not who he seems. His text of characterization masks the mystery of his core self, alive in the subtext. His implicit inner life intrigues readers and audiences, sparking the question, “Who is this character… really?” The scent of subtext invites them to explore and unearth the truth of this unknown self. In short, a beautifully conceived and executed multidimensional character turns readers and audiences into psychics.

另一方面，一个主要角色并非表面看起来那样简单。他性格的刻画掩盖了他内心深处的秘密，而这秘密就隐藏在字里行间。他隐晦的内心世界吸引着读者和观众，引发他们思考：“这个角色究竟是谁？”字里行间流露出的神秘感，引导他们去探索和揭开这个未知自我的真相。简而言之，一个构思精巧、刻画生动的多维角色，能够让读者和观众仿佛拥有了通灵能力。

Think about your own story-going hours. When you follow a character’s life, turning pages of prose or sitting in a dark theatre, don’t you have the distinct impression that you’re reading minds, reading emotions? Your perceptions seem to travel beneath their behaviors, and you think to yourself, “I know what’s going on inside that character better than he knows. I can see from the surface to the substance of what he’s really thinking, really feeling, and really wanting, consciously and subconsciously.”

想想你自己的阅读时光。当你跟随一个角色的人生轨迹，翻阅书页或坐在黑暗的剧院里时，难道你没有一种清晰的感受，仿佛在读懂他们的心思，解读他们的情感吗？你的感知似乎能够穿透他们的行为，你会想：“我比这个角色自己更了解他的内心世界。我能透过表象，看透他真正的想法、感受和渴望，无论是有意识的还是无意识的。”

You gain these insights on your own, as you must, because as in life, depth can only be intuited. This is why two people experiencing the same character often come away with very different interpretations. The subtextural someone living inside a complex role can never be fully explained in words, no matter who writes them. No one can tell you what to think about a character, not even the character himself in his most heartfelt confessions. The godlike omniscient narrators of the greatest of novels imply more than they tell, leave far more unsaid than said. This is why the archives of libraries stack thousands of works of literary criticism, all asking who questions: Who is Hamlet? Who is Anna Karenina? Who is Walter White?

这些洞见必须靠自己去体会，因为正如人生一样，深度只能凭直觉感知。这就是为什么两个人即使面对同一个角色，最终的解读也往往截然不同。无论谁来书写，复杂角色背后人物的内在特质都无法用语言完全诠释。没有人能告诉你该如何看待一个角色，即使是角色本人在最真挚的忏悔中也无法做到。伟大小说中那些如同上帝般全知的叙述者，往往暗示远多于直白，留下的未尽之言远多于直白的表达。正因如此，图书馆的档案库里才会堆满成千上万的文学评论，它们都在追问“谁”的问题：哈姆雷特是谁？安娜·卡列尼娜是谁？沃尔特·怀特又是谁？

The partition of text and subtext—what the world sees in the outer self versus the truth concealed behind the eyes—is essential to sanity. If the invasive world cannot be kept safely outside the mind, the inner life becomes unlivable.

区分文本和潜台词——外在世界所见的表象与隐藏在眼底的真相——对于保持理智至关重要。如果无法将外界的侵扰安全地阻挡在心灵之外，内心世界便无法生存。

Like readers and audiences, characters themselves peer into the subtextural depths of each other, trying to discover a hidden truth: Can I believe him? What does he really mean? Really want? Who does he care about? Himself or others? And on it goes as each character reads the subtext of the others: Othello must discover if his wife is virtuous; Lear must discover which daughter, if any, loves him; Hamlet must discover if his uncle murdered his father and finally does so by reading Claudio’s guilty reaction to a murder scene played out onstage.

如同读者和观众一样，剧中人物也彼此窥探对方言外之意，试图发现隐藏的真相：我能相信他吗？他真正的意思是什么？他真正想要的是什么？他关心谁？是他自己还是别人？就这样，每个角色都在解读其他角色的言外之意：奥赛罗必须弄清楚他的妻子是否贞洁；李尔王必须弄清楚哪个女儿（如果有的话）爱他；哈姆雷特必须弄清楚他的叔叔是否谋杀了他的父亲，最终他通过解读克劳狄奥对舞台上演的谋杀场景的愧疚反应而找到了答案。

Introspective characters rerun personal experiences as if they were TV episodes, searching through their subtexts, analyzing their actions, trying to figure out who they really are and how they got that way. Sometimes the self-reflective mind uncovers hidden insights, learns from mistakes, and increases self-awareness; at other times, it obsesses over its failures, doubts its worth, and blinds itself to the truth.

内省型的人会像观看电视剧一样重温个人经历，挖掘其中的弦外之音，分析自己的行为，试图弄清自己究竟是谁，以及自己为何会变成现在这样。有时，这种自我反思的思维会揭示隐藏的洞见，从错误中吸取教训，提升自我认知；而有时，它又会沉溺于失败，怀疑自身的价值，对真相视而不见。

Three examples: the self-absorbed, self-narrating protagonists of the novels A Fan’s Notes by Frederick Exley; The Sea, The Sea by Iris Murdoch; and The Woman Upstairs by Claire Messud.

三个例子：弗雷德里克·埃克斯利的《粉丝笔记》、艾瑞斯·默多克的《大海，大海》和克莱尔·梅苏德的《楼上的女人》这三部小说中，主人公都以自我为中心，进行自我叙述。

#↩

11

THE COMPLETED CHARACTER

已完成的角色

The golden ideal of character creation:

角色塑造的黄金理想：

First, conceive of a compelling, complex nature, rich in human promise but, like anyone with life left to live, incomplete. Then, as she makes and takes pressure-filled decisions and actions over the course of the story, progressively realize her unfulfilled potential. Finally, at the story’s climax, send her through an experience, both emotionally and mentally, that propels her to the absolute limits of her humanity: nothing left undiscovered, nothing left unexplored, nothing left unused, nothing left unfelt, nothing left unexpressed. Everything latent fulfilled, everything actable performed, everything knowable revealed, everything latent expressed, every emotion lived in full. The character is complete.

首先，构思一个引人入胜、复杂多面的人物，她充满人性的光辉，却如同所有尚有余生的人一样，尚未臻于完美。然后，随着故事的推进，她不断做出充满压力的决定和行动，逐步展现她尚未开发的潜能。最后，在故事的高潮，让她经历一场情感和精神上的双重冲击，将她推向人性的极限：一切未被发现，一切未被探索，一切未被利用，一切未被感受，一切未被表达。所有潜能都得以实现，所有可行动的都得以展现，所有可知的都得以揭示，所有潜能都得以表达，所有情感都得以充分体验。至此，人物臻于完美。

To achieve this ideal, role design takes four major steps: Preparation, Revelation, Change, Completion.

为了实现这一理想，角色设计需要四个主要步骤：准备、揭示、改变、完成。

#↩

FOUR MAJOR STEPS OF CHARACTER DESIGN

角色设计的四大步骤

1. Preparation

1. 准备工作

Principle: At the inciting incident, major characters are incomplete.
原则：在事件发生时，主要人物尚未完全形成。

As a story begins, its major characters, like most people, have never experienced their mental, emotional, and moral possibilities to their absolute limits. Their feelings and thoughts have known a certain depth but never the fullest range of passion and insight because life has never asked it of them. They are incomplete but unaware of it. The story that lies ahead will bring them experiences they’ve never known before and affect them in ways they cannot see coming. Only the author knows what’s nascent within them and what their true range of experience may be.

故事伊始，如同大多数人一样，主人公们从未将自身的精神、情感和道德潜能发挥到极致。他们的情感和思想虽有一定深度，却从未体验过最纯粹的激情与洞察力，因为生活从未要求他们如此。他们并不完整，却浑然不觉。即将展开的故事将带给他们前所未有的经历，并以他们无法预料的方式影响着他们。只有作者才知道他们内心深处潜藏着怎样的潜能，以及他们真正的阅历究竟有多丰富。

In my definition, character need is a void in a role’s humanity: unthought intelligence, underfelt emotion, unused talent, underlived life. Need is something half done that needs to be finished; something missing that yearns to be found.

在我看来，角色需求是指角色人性中的某种缺失：未被充分思考的智慧、未被充分感受的情感、未被发掘的才能、未被充分体验的人生。需求是未完成却亟待完善的事物；是缺失却渴望被寻回的东西。

Therefore, as a complex character enters your story, she is a work in progress. To reach the golden ideal, you must put your character through encounters that will take her mentally and emotionally into the deepest depths and farthest stretches of her humanity.

因此，当一个复杂的人物角色进入你的故事时，她是一个不断成长完善的过程。为了达到理想的完美境界，你必须让她经历种种磨难，使她的精神和情感得以深入探索，触及人性的最深处。

But what is her potential? Before your protagonist enters your story, take her measure. What is her IQ and EQ? Her willpower? Her imagination? The depth of her empathy? The height of her courage? Give thought to how far life has taken her and how much deeper the future might carry her.

但她的潜力究竟如何？在你的主人公进入故事之前，先评估一下她。她的智商和情商是多少？意志力如何？想象力如何？同理心有多深？勇气有多大？想想她的人生历程，以及未来她将走向何方。

Next, ask this key question: What event would send my protagonist along a spine of action that ends in a climax of such emotional power and mind-expanding insight that she experiences her humanity at its supreme limit and thus, for better or worse, completes herself? The answer, once you find it, will become your story’s inciting incident. The choice of an inciting incident perfectly tuned to the protagonist’s need makes fine writing possible.

接下来，问问自己这个关键问题：什么样的事件会推动我的主人公沿着一条充满行动的主线前进，最终达到一个情感冲击力极强、令人醍醐灌顶的高潮，让她体验到人性的极致，从而无论好坏，都得以完善自我？一旦你找到了答案，它就将成为你故事的触发事件。选择一个与主人公需求完美契合的触发事件，才能成就精彩的写作。

Four examples:

四个例子：

At the inciting incident of The Leftovers , the longform series by Damon Lindelof and Tom Perrotta, 2 percent of the world’s population instantly disappears. With that, co-protagonists Kevin Garvey (Justin Theroux) and Nora Durst (Carrie Coon) suddenly find life meaningless.

在达蒙·林德洛夫和汤姆·佩罗塔创作的长篇剧集《守望尘世》的开篇事件中，全球2%的人口瞬间消失。随之而来的是，两位主人公凯文·加维（贾斯汀·塞洛克斯饰）和诺拉·德斯特（凯瑞·库恩饰）突然发现生命失去了意义。

At the inciting incident of Machinal , a play by Sophie Treadwell, Helen, submitting to parental and social pressure, marries a man who disgusts her, thinking that this will give her a secure life.

在索菲·特雷德韦尔的戏剧《机械》中，海伦迫于父母和社会的压力，嫁给了一个令她厌恶的男人，认为这样就能给她带来安稳的生活。

At the inciting incident of Fight Club , a novel by Chuck Palahniuk, the protagonist, known only in the first-person voice of the narrator, moves in with Tyler Durden, and together they build a fight club.

在查克·帕拉尼克的小说《搏击俱乐部》的开篇事件中，主人公（仅以叙述者的第一人称视角为人所知）搬进了泰勒·德顿的住处，两人一起建立了一个搏击俱乐部。

At the inciting incident of Mrs. Soffel , a film written by Ron Nyswaner, Kate Soffel (Diane Keaton), a prison warden’s wife, decides to save the soul of a condemned prisoner.

在罗恩·尼斯万纳编剧的电影《索菲尔夫人》的导火索中，监狱长的妻子凯特·索菲尔（黛安·基顿饰）决定拯救一名被判死刑的囚犯的灵魂。

#↩

2. Revelation

2.启示录

Principle: A story’s dynamic of events reveals true character in contrast with or contradiction to characterization.
原则：故事中事件的动态变化揭示了人物的真实性格，这与人物刻画形成对比或矛盾。

The vast majority of all genres reveal an inner truth of their characters but do not arc them. As Samuel Butler put it, “It is one against legion when a creature tries to differ from his own past selves.” Deep character change is difficult and exceptional. Six genres, however, do arc their protagonists over the course of a telling, and these will be laid out in Chapter Fourteen.

绝大多数文学类型都会揭示人物的内在真相，但不会塑造人物的弧光。正如塞缪尔·巴特勒所说：“当一个生物试图改变他过去的自己时，那将是一场孤军奋战。”深刻的人物转变既困难又罕见。然而，有六种文学类型会在叙事过程中塑造主人公的弧光，这些类型将在第十四章中详细阐述。

The genres of Action/Adventure, War, Horror, Fantasy, and Crime, as well as most dramas and comedies about physical, political, domestic, and romantic struggles, submerge a core self beneath layers of believable yet intriguing characterization. They then reveal this inner nature, exposing but never changing the character’s psychology and morality. What changes is the reader’s/audience’s insight.

动作/冒险、战争、恐怖、奇幻和犯罪等类型，以及大多数讲述身体、政治、家庭和爱情冲突的剧情片和喜剧，都将人物的核心自我隐藏在层层可信而引人入胜的角色刻画之下。然后，它们揭示这种内在本质，展现但从未改变角色的心理和道德观。改变的是读者/观众的洞察力。

The most powerful revelations occur when events put a character at maximum risk. The choice, for example, between life and death is easily made and any insight that follows relatively shallow. But a choice between two deaths—one by a long, painful disease, the other by quick suicide—strips away a character’s public and personal personae, revealing the core self. By the same token, if she stands to lose a thing of great value in order to gain another thing of equal value, her choice expresses who she is.

最震撼人心的启示往往发生在事件将角色置于最大风险之时。例如，生死抉择很容易做出，随之而来的领悟也相对肤浅。但如果要在两种死亡方式之间做出选择——一种是饱受疾病折磨而死，另一种是速死——则会剥离角色的公众形象和私人身份，揭示其本质。同样，如果她为了获得同等价值的东西而不得不失去一件极其珍贵的东西，她的选择也体现了她真正的自我。

In Martin McDonagh’s play The Beauty Queen of Leenane , Maureen Folan, a forty-year-old former inmate of an insane asylum, seems like a submissive, intimidated overgrown child until she murders her mother, puts on her mother’s clothes, and takes her mother’s place in the living room rocking chair. In Maureen’s schizophrenic mind, she has always been her mother; playing her daughter was just a temporary guise.

在马丁·麦克唐纳的戏剧《利纳恩的选美皇后》中，四十岁的莫琳·弗兰曾是精神病院的病人，起初她看起来像个顺从、胆怯的巨婴，直到她杀死了自己的母亲，穿上母亲的衣服，坐在客厅的摇椅上，取代了母亲的位置。在莫琳患有精神分裂症的意识里，她一直都是她的母亲；扮演女儿只不过是暂时的伪装。

In J. D. Salinger’s novel The Catcher in the Rye, the cynical, lonely Holden Caulfield suffers confusion about his sexuality and longing for an idealized romance. He feels alienated from people and alienates others in return. His attitudes vary, but his core self never fundamentally alters from first page to last.

在J·D·塞林格的小说《麦田里的守望者》中，愤世嫉俗、孤独寂寞的霍尔顿·考尔菲尔德对自己的性取向感到困惑，并渴望一段理想化的爱情。他感到与世隔绝，也因此疏远了他人。他的态度时而变化，但他的本质却始终未变，从第一页到最后一页都未曾改变。

In Woody Allen’s Annie Hall , Alvy Singer’s boyhood insecurities poisoned his adulthood. He so hates the truth, he chooses fantasy over reality. Happiness so sours him, he chooses misery over joy. His obsession with himself renders him incapable of love. Over time, his choices expose a twisted, unchanging neurotic lurking under his wit and charm.

在伍迪·艾伦的《安妮·霍尔》中，艾尔维·辛格童年的不安全感毒害了他的成年生活。他如此憎恨真相，以至于宁愿沉溺于幻想而非现实。快乐令他痛苦不堪，他宁愿选择痛苦而非喜悦。他对自我的执着使他无法去爱。随着时间的推移，他的选择逐渐暴露出他机智和魅力之下隐藏的扭曲而顽固的神经质。

To sum up: As the outer circumstances in a protagonist’s life undergo change, her choices and actions slowly uncover her core self. With each word and gesture, her characterization peels away, leaving her true self standing naked, as it were, at the climax. Although the true character, once revealed, did not evolve, the reader’s or audience’s perceptions did, growing deeper and deeper in understanding. Once again, this archetypal pattern of a revealed but unchanged character underlies the vast majority of major characters in the vast majority of all stories ever told.

总而言之：随着主人公生活外部环境的变化，她的选择和行动会逐渐揭示其内心深处的自我。她的一言一行，都如同剥开层层外衣，最终在故事高潮时，赤裸裸地展现出她真实的自我。虽然一旦揭示，真实的性格本身并没有改变，但读者或观众的感知却随之加深，理解也愈发深刻。这种揭示本质却不变的典型模式，贯穿了绝大多数故事中绝大多数主要人物的塑造。

Test this principle in your own work by asking two simple questions of primary characters: Who do we think she is at the beginning of the story? Who do we know she is by the story’s climax? Your answers should reveal a change of insight in the reader/audience.

在自己的作品中检验这一原则，可以向主要人物提出两个简单的问题：故事开始时我们认为她是谁？故事高潮时我们知道她是谁？你的答案应该揭示读者/观众认知上的变化。

#↩

3. Change

3. 变更

Principle: Character change puts dimension into action.
原则：性格变化赋予行动以维度。

An age-old puzzle known as the Ship of Theseus Paradox asks: “If a ship is repaired slowly over time so that eventually every part is replaced, is it still the same ship, deserving the same name? If, on the other hand, the ship were lost at sea but another were remade to its exact specifications, does it need a new name or is it essentially the same?”

一个被称为忒修斯之船悖论的古老谜题问道：“如果一艘船随着时间的推移慢慢修复，最终所有部件都被更换，它还是同一艘船，配得上原来的名字吗？另一方面，如果这艘船在海上沉没，但另一艘船按照它的精确规格重新建造，它需要一个新的名字，还是本质上是同一艘船？”

In both cases not a single board, cleat, or sail is left from the original. Nonetheless, the two ships prompt opposite conclusions: Most people feel that the slowly repaired craft stays the same and should keep its name, but the replacement vessel is new and needs a rechristening.

两艘船都已面目全非，原船的一块木板、一根系缆柱、一张帆都荡然无存。然而，这两艘船却引发了截然相反的结论：大多数人认为，经过缓慢修复的那艘船保持了原貌，应该保留原名；而新船则是一艘新船，需要重新命名。

This archaic puzzle, of course, is not about nautical nomenclature. It’s a metaphor for human change. Substitute identity for ship and it becomes a parable that raises the questions of “Who am I? Who was I? Who will I be? Will fate preserve me or remake me?” Like a ship navigating unknown waters, a complex character sails through random, unexpected, life-battering events that may or may not alter her nature.

当然，这个古老的谜题并非关乎航海术语，而是对人生变迁的一种隐喻。将“船”替换为“身份”，它便成了一则寓言，引人深思：“我是谁？我曾经是谁？我将成为谁？命运会保佑我，还是会重塑我？” 如同航行于未知海域的船只，一个复杂的人物经历着种种随机、意外、充满磨难的事件，这些事件或许会改变她的本性，也或许不会。

Some writers react to character change the same way the public treats the Theseus Paradox: Gradual revisions do not change their character’s core identity, while the shock and scar of an explosive event mutates it. Other writers do the opposite: Powerful events never dent their character, although time may slowly evolve her.

有些作家对待人物性格变化的态度，与公众对待忒修斯悖论的态度如出一辙：渐进式的修改不会改变人物的核心本质，而爆炸性事件带来的冲击和创伤却会使其发生改变。另一些作家则恰恰相反：强烈的事件不会对笔下的人物造成任何影响，尽管时间可能会缓慢地改变她。

As we saw in Chapter Three, every author needs a personal theory of human nature so she can answer the question: “Does damage to my character’s life change or not change her core identity?”

正如我们在第三章中所看到的，每个作者都需要一个关于人性的个人理论，以便回答以下问题：“对我的角色生活造成的伤害是否会改变她的核心身份？”

Which do you believe? Is a character, like the Ship of Theseus, becoming a more concentrated although essentially unchanged self over time, or is she transforming into a wholly different self that her past self wouldn’t recognize? In other words, does your character’s every thought evolve her into a minutely different self than she was the moment before? Does every hour she spends with others gradually make her more like them? Or do you believe that these shifts are trivial and that at heart your character always stays who she is?

你相信哪种说法？一个角色，就像忒修斯之船一样，随着时间的推移，会变得更加集中但本质上不变，还是会蜕变成一个完全不同的自我，以至于过去的自己都认不出来？换句话说，你笔下角色的每一个想法都会让她与前一刻略有不同吗？她与他人相处的每一小时都会让她逐渐变得更像他们吗？或者你认为这些变化微不足道，角色的本质始终不变？

The Theory of Perpetual Identity

永恒同一性理论

The theory of perpetual identity holds that a child at birth is a clean slate and could become almost anyone, but as life inscribes her with experience, she develops unique patterns of action/reaction that hold her mind together and create her persistent identity. Shifts in characterization take place around this stable center. Once the pattern is set, her choices and actions in the story’s future events make her more and more specific, more and more herself.

永恒身份理论认为，婴儿出生时就像一张白纸，可以成为任何人，但随着生活赋予她经验，她会发展出独特的行为/反应模式，这些模式维系着她的心智，并塑造出她持久的身份。人物性格的转变围绕着这个稳定的中心展开。一旦模式形成，她在故事后续事件中的选择和行动就会使她变得越来越具体，越来越像她自己。

In Middlemarch , George Eliot expressed her belief in perpetual identity with this often quoted image: “Even while we rave on the heights [we] behold the wide plain where our persistent self pauses and awaits us.”

在《米德尔马契》中，乔治·艾略特用这句经常被引用的意象表达了她对永恒身份的信念：“即使我们在高处狂喜，我们也能看到广阔的平原，在那里，我们执着的自我驻足等待着我们。”

In tellings about a protagonist’s search for identity, characters such as Jimmy Porter in John Osborne’s play Look Back in Anger and James McBride in his memoir The Color of Water recognize their outer changes, but at the same time feel that their past belongs to them and, in a sense, is them. In fact, the act of retrospection itself implies a constant identity. If a character’s core self didn’t persist through time, it couldn’t exist in the present to look back at its past.

在讲述主人公追寻自我认同的故事中，约翰·奥斯本的戏剧《愤怒的回顾》中的吉米·波特和詹姆斯·麦克布莱德的回忆录《水色》中的人物，都意识到自身外在的变化，但同时又感到过去属于自己，某种程度上，过去就是自己。事实上，回顾本身就蕴含着一种永恒的身份认同。如果一个人物的核心自我无法在时间长河中延续，那么它就无法存在于当下，也无法回顾过去。

Many writers believe that the core self secures itself against a steady succession of changes in its outer life—bodily changes, personal and social changes in relationships, career moves, housing moves, and the like. Constantly changing circumstances do not change its essence—least of all, its moral nature. 1 For example, Alex (Malcolm McDowell), the protagonist of Stanley Kubrick’s A Clockwork Orange (a film adaptation of Anthony Burgess’s novel), both inflicts and suffers hideous pain but stays steadfast, even happily, the same.

许多作家认为，核心自我能够抵御外在生活中持续不断的变化——身体的变化、人际关系和社交关系的变迁、职业变动、居住地搬迁等等。不断变化的环境并不会改变其本质，更不会改变其道德属性。例如，斯坦利·库布里克执导的电影《发条橙》（改编自安东尼·伯吉斯的小说）中的主人公亚历克斯（马尔科姆·麦克道尔饰）既承受着巨大的痛苦，也施加着巨大的痛苦，但他始终保持着自己的本性，甚至乐在其中。

The Theory of the Changing Identity

身份转变理论

Animals obey instincts; humans analyze theirs. Wolves never worry about what it means to be a wolf, they just wolf. But the self-aware human mind frets over its urges and intuitions, charts the push and pull of instinct and reason, all in an effort to become a better or at least a different version of itself. For this reason, many writers believe that change is not only possible but essential.

动物遵循本能；人类则分析本能。狼从不纠结于身为狼意味着什么，它们只是单纯地做狼。但具有自我意识的人类却为自身的欲望和直觉而焦虑，权衡本能与理性之间的拉锯，这一切都是为了让自己变得更好，或者至少成为一个不同的自己。正因如此，许多作家认为改变不仅是可能的，而且是必要的。

Change, when it occurs, arcs along a character’s defining dimension. In John Milton’s epic Paradise Lost , for example, the protagonist’s core contradiction is Good/Evil. The story traces a positive to negative arc as Lucifer, Angel of Light (Good), compelled by pride, gathers an army of like-minded angels and tries to overthrow God. After three days of war he’s hurled out of Heaven and down to Hell, where he takes the name Satan, Angel of Darkness (Evil).

改变一旦发生，便会沿着人物性格的核心维度展开。例如，在约翰·弥尔顿的史诗巨著《失乐园》中，主人公的核心矛盾便是善与恶。故事描绘了一条由善转恶的弧线：光明天使（善）路西法，因骄傲自满而聚集了一群志同道合的天使，试图推翻上帝。经过三天的战争，他被逐出天堂，坠入地狱，在那里他化身为黑暗天使（恶）撒旦。

Other examples: The dimension Kindness/Cruelty arcs from positive to negative in Chuck Tatum (Kirk Douglas) in Billy Wilder’s Ace in the Hole , but in the reverse direction in Amir in The Kite Runner by Khaled Hosseini. Generosity/Greed swings from negative to positive in Ebenezer Scrooge in Charles Dickens’s novella A Christmas Carol , but in the reverse for Bobby Axelrod (Damian Lewis) in the Showtime series Billions . Multiple dimensions could crisscross with irony: In Aravind Adiga’s novel The White Tiger , Balram Halwai goes from law-abiding citizen to criminal (positive to negative), while he also changes from impoverished laborer to a corporate executive (negative to positive).

其他例子：在比利·怀尔德执导的《倒扣的王牌》中，查克·塔图姆（柯克·道格拉斯饰）的善良/残忍维度由正面转为负面，而在卡勒德·胡赛尼执导的《追风筝的人》中，阿米尔的善良/残忍维度则相反。在查尔斯·狄更斯的小说《圣诞颂歌》中，埃比尼泽·斯克鲁奇的慷慨/贪婪维度由负面转为正面，而在Showtime电视台的剧集《亿万》中，鲍比·阿克塞尔罗德（达米安·刘易斯饰）的慷慨/贪婪维度则相反。多个维度交织在一起，形成讽刺：在阿拉文德·阿迪加的小说《白虎》中，巴尔拉姆·哈尔瓦伊从守法公民沦为罪犯（由正面转为负面），同时他也从贫困的劳动者摇身一变成了企业高管（由负面转为正面）。

The value-charge in a changing self can pivot in one of two directions: positive or negative.

不断变化的自我中的价值取向可以朝两个方向之一转变：正面或负面。

Positive Arcs

正弧

Definition: A positive arc, as the name implies, ends on a positive charge. It could open with a character in either a positive or a negative state, and then move in alternating positive/negative cycles that increase their impact to a climax that fulfills the character’s desire.

定义：正向弧线，顾名思义，以积极的能量结束。它可以以角色处于积极或消极状态开始，然后以正负交替的循环发展，不断增强其影响，最终达到高潮，满足角色的愿望。

A positive arc, therefore, often begins when a character senses a negative state within herself. At first, she resists change, but revelations of yet more bitter truths eventually overcome her reluctance until she finally reaches the top of a moral slope.

因此，积极的转变往往始于角色感知到自身消极状态之时。起初，她抗拒改变，但随着更多残酷真相的揭露，她的抵触情绪最终消散，直至她最终攀上道德的巅峰。

Examples:

例如：

In John Patrick Shanley’s play Doubt: A Parable , Sister Aloysius arcs from an autocrat blinded by self-righteousness (Arrogance) to a woman shamed by doubt (Humility).

在约翰·帕特里克·尚利的戏剧《怀疑：一个寓言》中，阿洛伊修斯修女从一个被自以为是蒙蔽的独裁者（傲慢）转变为一个因怀疑而感到羞愧的女人（谦卑）。

In Danny Rubin’s screenplay for Groundhog Day , Phil Connors (Bill Murray) evolves from an immature, self-absorbed egoist incapable of love (Selfishness) to a mature, compassionate, heartful lover (Selflessness).

在丹尼·鲁宾为《土拨鼠日》创作的剧本中，菲尔·康纳斯（比尔·默瑞饰）从一个不成熟、自私自利、无法去爱的人（自私）演变成一个成熟、富有同情心、充满爱心的人（无私）。

In J. M. Coetzee’s novel Disgrace , David Lurie, a manipulative seducer and pretentious intellectual (Self-deception) slowly deconstructs his life and finally accepts his place in a world beyond his control (Self-awareness).

在 J·M·库切的小说《耻辱》中，大卫·卢里是一个善于操纵的诱惑者和自命不凡的知识分子（自欺欺人），他慢慢地解构了自己的生活，最终接受了自己在一个无法控制的世界中的位置（自我意识）。

Here from the series and films Sex and the City are four positive arcs that take characters from incomplete to complete:

以下是《欲望都市》电视剧和电影中四个使角色从不完整走向完整的积极转变：

Carrie Bradshaw

凯莉·布雷萧

Carrie (Sarah Jessica Parker) is a pop journalist who writes about sexual and romantic relationships in New York City. Despite her intelligent study and careful observations of these issues, her emotions dominate her choices and behaviors. Carrie opens the series self-conscious and insecure. Over the course of six seasons and two films she arcs to self-possessed and secure.

凯莉（莎拉·杰西卡·帕克饰）是一位流行文化记者，专门报道纽约市的性与情感关系。尽管她对这些问题进行了深入的研究和细致的观察，但她的情绪仍然主导着她的选择和行为。剧集开始时，凯莉缺乏自信，不自信。经过六季剧集和两部电影的剧情发展，她逐渐变得沉稳自信。

At the beginning of the series she seeks acceptance and reassurance from her friends and the men in her life, particularly Mr. Big (Chris Noth). Her neuroses become obsessions such as having a key to her lover’s apartment and equal space in his bathroom cabinet. She’s aware of her behavior and blames it on her tendency to “get carried away.” “Just tell me I’m the one,” she begs Big at the end of Season 1. She’s flawed but empathetic, thanks to her self-deprecating humor.

在剧集开始时，她渴望从朋友和生命中的男人那里获得认可和肯定，尤其是“大先生”（克里斯·诺斯饰）。她的神经质逐渐演变成执念，比如想要一把爱人公寓的钥匙，以及在他浴室柜里拥有同等的空间。她清楚自己的行为，并将其归咎于自己“容易冲动”。“告诉我，我就是你的唯一，”她在第一季结尾恳求“大先生”。她虽然有缺点，但凭借着自嘲式的幽默，她也展现出了同理心。

She searches for true love and commitment but doubts that she’s the marriage and family type. Mr. Big, who she meets in the first episode of the series, is her first and only great love. Despite her many other affairs, she feels that Big is her soul mate. At the end of the sixth and last season, Big announces that he is coming back to New York City from California to be with Carrie. At the climax of the first film they marry. Question: Has she arced to self-possession on her own, or has marriage done it for her?

她渴望真爱和承诺，但又怀疑自己是否适合婚姻和家庭。她在剧集第一集中遇到的“大先生”（Mr. Big）是她初恋，也是她唯一的挚爱。尽管她有过许多恋情，但她仍然觉得“大先生”是她的灵魂伴侣。在第六季也是最后一季的结尾，“大先生”宣布他将从加州回到纽约与凯莉团聚。在第一部电影的高潮部分，他们结婚了。问题是：她是靠自己的努力成长为独立自主的人，还是婚姻造就了她？

Samantha Jones

萨曼莎·琼斯

The hypersexual Samantha (Kim Cattrall) is the oldest of the four friends and owns her own PR firm. As a self-proclaimed “Try-Sexual” (meaning she’ll try anything once), most of Samantha’s story lines revolve around her sexual escapades. Passion is her passion, with or without romantic ritual, but she never loves anyone other than herself. She seems incapable of love, and so the series arcs her through a Redemption Plot.

性欲旺盛的萨曼莎（金·凯特罗尔饰）是四位好友中最年长的，拥有一家自己的公关公司。她自称“尝试性爱者”（意指她什么都愿意尝试一次），萨曼莎的大部分剧情都围绕着她的性冒险展开。激情是她的激情所在，无论有没有浪漫的仪式，但她从未爱过除自己以外的任何人。她似乎无法去爱，因此这部剧集安排了一条救赎之路来塑造她的形象。

Although sexually narcissistic, among her friends Samantha is the most loyal and least judgmental. She engages in a few serious relationships, one of them lesbian, but rarely dates anyone more than once or twice. In Season 6, however, two things happen: She gets involved with Smith (Jason Lewis) and is diagnosed with breast cancer.

尽管萨曼莎在性方面有些自恋，但她的朋友中最忠诚、最不爱评判他人的。她谈过几段认真的恋爱，其中一段是女同性恋情，但很少和任何人交往超过一两次。然而，在第六季中，发生了两件事：她和史密斯（杰森·刘易斯饰）交往，并且被诊断出患有乳腺癌。

She faces her cancer with great courage and wit. No matter how ugly the therapy, Smith stands by her through the worst of times. She loves him for it; in the first film, set four years later, she lives with him in LA and does her best to stay in a committed relationship.

她以极大的勇气和智慧面对癌症。无论治疗多么痛苦，史密斯都始终陪伴在她身边，度过最艰难的时刻。她为此深深地爱着他；在第一部电影中，故事发生在四年后，她和他一起住在洛杉矶，并努力维持这段稳定的感情。

But despite her tender feelings for Smith, she finds herself madly attracted to her hypersexual neighbor. She finally questions her feeling and concludes that she loves herself more than Smith. They break up. In the second film, she’s back to her old self, having sex on the hood of a guy’s Mercedes.

尽管她对史密斯怀有温柔的感情，却发现自己疯狂地迷恋上了性欲旺盛的邻居。最终，她开始质疑自己的感情，并得出结论：她更爱自己。两人分手了。在第二部电影中，她又变回了以前的样子，在一个男人的奔驰车引擎盖上做爱。

Samantha undergoes a double arc: loveless sexual obsession (her true self) to committed sexless love (her false self) back to loveless sexual obsession (her truest self).

萨曼莎经历了双重弧线：从无爱的性痴迷（她真实的自我）到忠诚的无性爱情（她虚假的自我），再回到无爱的性痴迷（她最真实的自我）。

Charlotte York

夏洛特·约克

Charlotte (Kristin Davis) is a Connecticut blueblood, prom queen, cheerleader, track star, teen model, equestrienne, Smith College grad, art dealer—aka a WASP. She undergoes an Education Plot from naïve to worldly.

夏洛特（克里斯汀·戴维斯饰）是康涅狄格州的名门望族，曾是舞会皇后、啦啦队长、田径明星、青少年模特、马术运动员，毕业于史密斯学院，也是一名艺术品经销商——也就是典型的盎格鲁-撒克逊新教徒。她经历了从天真无邪到世故老练的成长历程。

She’s blindly romantic, always searching for her knight in shining armor. The least cynical of her friends, she believes love conquers all. She distains the libertine antics of her friends, convinced that dating has rules. Her friends are often envious and even in awe of Charlotte’s overall optimism about love. Yet she occasionally surprises them with dirty talk and her love of oral sex.

她是个盲目的浪漫主义者，总是在寻找她的白马王子。她是朋友中最不愤世嫉俗的一个，坚信爱情可以战胜一切。她鄙视朋友们放荡不羁的行为，坚信恋爱是有规则的。她的朋友们常常羡慕，甚至敬畏夏洛特对爱情的乐观态度。然而，她偶尔也会用一些露骨的言语和对口交的喜爱让他们大吃一惊。

Her belief in romance leads her to decide not to have sex with her fiancé until their honeymoon, only to discover that her “perfect” husband is impotent. She eventually divorces him due to his twisted relationship with his mother.

她对浪漫的迷信让她决定在蜜月前不与未婚夫发生性关系，却发现她“完美”的丈夫竟然阳痿。最终，由于他与母亲之间扭曲的关系，她与他离婚了。

Although Charlotte is initially put off by her divorce attorney’s constant sweating, messy eating, bald head, and hairy body, she sleeps with him when he confesses his intense attraction to her. Harry (Evan Handler) gives her the best sex of her life. She tries to keep their relationship strictly sexual, but because of Harry’s deep caring, she finds herself falling in love.

夏洛特起初对她的离婚律师哈里（埃文·汉德勒饰）的汗流浃背、邋遢的饮食习惯、光秃秃的脑袋和浓密的体毛感到反感，但当他坦白自己对她强烈的爱慕之情时，她还是和他发生了关系。哈里给了她此生最棒的性体验。她试图将这段关系维持在纯粹的性关系，但由于哈里深切的关怀，她发现自己渐渐爱上了他。

Initially, she tries to reform him to fit more closely with her image of the ideal man, but when she realizes how much pain she’s causing him, she accepts Harry the way he is. In fact, she converts to Judaism because of Harry’s avowal to only marry a Jewish woman.

起初，她试图改造他，使他更符合她理想男人的形象，但当她意识到自己给他带来了多大的痛苦时，她接受了哈里原本的样子。事实上，她皈依犹太教是因为哈里发誓只娶犹太女子。

Only when Charlotte realizes that she must put aside her romantic ideals and accept Harry on his own terms does she find a love that fulfills her romantic ideals. The man who is the antithesis of the perfect man becomes her ideal mate. She undergoes an arc from a real-life disaster with Mr. Right to ideal love with Mr. Wrong.

只有当夏洛特意识到她必须放下浪漫的理想，接受哈里本来的样子时，她才找到了真正符合她浪漫理想的爱情。这个与完美男人截然相反的男人，最终成为了她的理想伴侣。她的人生轨迹也随之发生了转变：从与“真命天子”的现实失败，到与“错先生”的理想爱情。

Miranda Hobbes

米兰达·霍布斯

Miranda (Cynthia Nixon), a Wall Street lawyer, overvalues work and undervalues men. She arcs through a double Education Plot, changing her attitudes toward both. In the early seasons, she treats men with distrust and resentment, finding them immature and unrealistically romantic.

米兰达（辛西娅·尼克松饰）是一位华尔街律师，她过分看重工作，轻视男性。她的人生经历贯穿两条教育线索，逐渐改变了她对工作和男性的态度。在剧集初期，她对男性抱有不信任和怨恨，认为他们不成熟，浪漫得不切实际。

Then Miranda meets Steve (David Eigenberg), a bartender. What starts as a one-night stand grows into sharing an apartment. Economic differences cause arguments, so they separate but keep a friendly sexual relationship. When Steve loses a testicle to cancer, Miranda sleeps with him to convince him that women will still find him attractive whether he has one ball or two.

米兰达遇到了酒吧招待史蒂夫（大卫·艾根伯格饰）。两人最初只是一夜情，后来发展成合租公寓。经济差异导致争吵，最终两人分手，但仍然保持着友好的性关系。史蒂夫因癌症切除了一侧睾丸后，米兰达为了让他相信无论剩下一颗睾丸还是两颗，女人依然会觉得他有魅力，便与他发生了关系。

As a result, she gets pregnant but decides against an abortion. Pregnancy softens her character and she tells Steve that she’ll take full responsibility, raise the child, and let him visit the boy if he likes. Motherhood stresses this workaholic, but she finds ways to balance career and a child. She and Steve try to raise their son as platonic partners.

结果，她怀孕了，但决定不堕胎。怀孕让她性格变得温和，她告诉史蒂夫，她会承担全部责任，抚养孩子，如果他愿意，也欢迎他来看望孩子。为人母给这位工作狂带来了压力，但她找到了平衡事业和家庭的方法。她和史蒂夫努力以柏拉图式的伴侣关系抚养他们的儿子。

At the boy’s first birthday party, Miranda blurts out her love for Steve and to her delight, Steve declares that she’s “the One.” They marry.

在男孩一周岁生日派对上，米兰达脱口而出自己对史蒂夫的爱意，令她欣喜的是，史蒂夫宣布她就是“命中注定的另一半”。他们结婚了。

In the second film, Miranda is so overworked that she misses her son’s school activities. What’s worse, her misogynistic boss disrespects her. Steve convinces her to quit and find a fulfilling job at a firm where she’s admired and appreciated. Miranda arcs from imbalance to balance in both work and love.

在第二部电影中，米兰达工作过度，甚至错过了儿子的学校活动。更糟糕的是，她那厌女的老板对她极不尊重。史蒂夫劝她辞职，去一家她能得到赏识和重视的公司找一份更有成就感的工作。米兰达最终在工作和爱情方面都实现了从失衡到平衡的转变。

Negative Arcs

负弧

A negative arc could begin with a character in either a positive or negative state, and then alternate positive/negative cycles that deepen in impact until ending in tragedy. This arc, of course, shapes the lives and deaths of Shakespeare’s greatest dramatic characters: Antony and Cleopatra, Macbeth and Lady Macbeth, Brutus and Cassius, Coriolanus, Richard III, Hamlet, Othello, King Lear—all of whom complete themselves in a tragic climax.

负面弧线可以从人物处于正面或负面状态开始，然后正反交替循环，影响不断加深，直至悲剧收场。当然，莎士比亚最伟大的戏剧人物的生与死正是由这种弧线塑造的：安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉、麦克白与麦克白夫人、布鲁图斯与卡西乌斯、科利奥兰纳斯、理查三世、哈姆雷特、奥赛罗、李尔王——所有这些人物最终都以悲剧收场。

Negative arcs often begin with a character living in youthful fantasies or naïveté. Reality punctuates her dreams, but she insists on her beliefs until she descends into a pain-filled, irreversible truth: Ibsen’s Hedda Gabler, Strindberg’s Miss Julie, along with the protagonists of almost every play by Tennessee Williams.

负面人物的命运往往始于一个沉浸在青春幻想或天真的角色。现实会打破她的梦想，但她坚持自己的信念，直到最终坠入充满痛苦且无法挽回的真相：易卜生的《海达·加布勒》、斯特林堡的《朱莉小姐》，以及田纳西·威廉姆斯几乎所有戏剧中的主人公都是如此。

A Good-to-Evil arc could start with a sweet little girl and end with a serial killer ( The Bad Seed , a play by Maxwell Anderson), or begin with a hard-working white collar engineer and end in a violent psychic breakdown ( Falling Down , a film by Joel Schumacher) or open with an idealist and arc him into a mass murderer ( Ostland , a novel by David Thomas).

从善到恶的转变可以始于一个可爱的小女孩，最终变成一个连环杀手（麦克斯韦·安德森的戏剧《坏种》），也可以始于一个勤奋的白领工程师，最终以一场暴力的精神崩溃告终（乔尔·舒马赫的电影《坠落》），或者始于一个理想主义者，最终变成一个连环杀人犯（大卫·托马斯的小说《奥斯特兰》）。

In Thomas Hardy’s novel Jude the Obscure , Jude Fawley, a manual laborer, homeschools himself in classical Greek and Latin in hopes of becoming a university scholar (Fantasy). But lower-class deprivations and upper-class bigotries quash his dream. He spends his entire working life cutting stone until he dies in bitter poverty (Reality).

在托马斯·哈代的小说《无名的裘德》中，体力劳动者裘德·福雷自学古典希腊语和拉丁语，梦想成为一名大学学者（幻想）。然而，底层阶级的匮乏和上层阶级的偏见粉碎了他的梦想。他终其一生都在切割石头，最终在极度贫困中死去（现实）。

The backstory of George Lucas’s Star Wars saga mirrors Lucifer’s fall. In it, a Jedi knight, Anakin Skywalker (Good), seeking power over life and death in hope of saving the woman he loves, moves from the realm of light to the infamous dark side. Burnt and dismembered in battle, he joins the empire and takes the name Darth Vader (Evil).

乔治·卢卡斯的《星球大战》系列故事背景与路西法的堕落有着异曲同工之妙。故事中，绝地武士安纳金·天行者（正义一方）为了拯救心爱的女人，寻求掌控生死的力量，最终从光明面堕入了臭名昭著的黑暗面。他在战斗中身负重伤、肢体残缺，之后加入帝国，化身为达斯·维达（邪恶一方）。

In Patrick Marber’s play Closer , Dan, Anna, Larry, and Alice search for loving, intimate relationships (Meaningful). All four cycle through years of meeting, making love, partnering up, and breaking up, finally ending in loneliness and discontent (Meaningless).

在帕特里克·马伯的戏剧《更近》中，丹、安娜、拉里和爱丽丝都在寻找充满爱意的亲密关系（有意义的）。这四个人经历了多年的相遇、恋爱、交往和分手，最终都以孤独和不满告终（无意义的）。

Character arcs, positive or negative, seldom trace a smooth line but more likely move in dynamic zigzags. If a story’s values never change their charge, the telling freezes into a portrait. Imagine if everything that happens runs positive, positive, positive, finally leaving the cast beaming in delight. Or if nothing but grim scenes surge further and further downhill until they crush the characters at the bottom. Repetition is the writer’s mortal enemy.

人物弧线，无论是正面的还是负面的，很少是笔直的，而更可能是动态的曲折变化。如果故事的价值观始终不变，叙述就会变成一幅僵硬的肖像。试想一下，如果所有事情都一帆风顺，最终让角色们喜笑颜开；或者如果只有阴暗的场景不断升级，直至将角色彻底击垮，那会是怎样一番景象？重复是作家的死敌。

Change from a Character’s POV

转换角色视角

When your character looks back on her life, who does she see? Herself or someone else? Is she still the same? Better? Worse? Unrecognizable? Does she hate, like, or ignore who she was, who she is, who she will be?

当你的角色回顾自己的一生时，她看到的是谁？是她自己还是别人？她还是原来的她吗？更好了？更糟了？还是面目全非？她憎恨、喜欢还是忽视过去的自己、现在的自己以及未来的自己？

Attitudes toward oneself span from narcissism to self-love to self-respect to self-indifference to self-criticism to self-hate to thoughts of suicide. Two contradictory visions bracket this spectrum: Life-as-Fate and Life-as-Destiny.

人们对自己的态度涵盖了从自恋到自爱，从自尊到自我漠视，从自我批评到自我憎恨，甚至到自杀念头。两种截然相反的观点构成了这一光谱的两端：人生即命运和人生即天命。

Life-as-Fate: If your character looks backward, rarely forward, she may feel trapped in a fate not her own. She may never satisfy her own desires, only the demands of others. She feels lost and out of contact with her true self, an identity hidden somewhere in her subconscious.

命运使然：如果你的角色总是回顾过去，很少展望未来，她可能会感到被困于并非自己选择的命运之中。她可能永远无法满足自己的愿望，只能满足他人的需求。她感到迷失，与真实的自我失去了联系，那个隐藏在她潜意识深处的自我。

As this child of fate surveys her past, does she feel that instead of evolving, she has turned into someone she doesn’t know? Do her old beliefs, values, and goals seem lost? Do past desires and behaviors baffle her? Does she wonder how she could have done the things she once did? Do her past deeds seem alien, if not incomprehensible? Does change seem so great that she can’t imagine how she could have ever been who she was? In other words, is she self-alienated?

当这位命运之子回顾过往时，她是否觉得自己非但没有进化，反而变成了一个完全陌生的人？她过去的信仰、价值观和目标是否都已消逝？过去的欲望和行为是否令她困惑不已？她是否疑惑自己当初怎么会做出那些事？她过去的所作所为是否显得陌生，甚至难以理解？变化是否如此巨大，以至于她无法想象自己曾经的模样？换句话说，她是否感到自我疏离？

Life-as-Destiny: If your character looks forward, rarely backward, she lives life on her own terms, freely choosing her own path. She never doubts that she is her core self. Destiny implies a destination, and hers awaits in the future, drawing her toward fulfillment.

人生即命运：如果你的角色总是向前看，很少回顾过去，她就会按照自己的意愿生活，自由地选择自己的道路。她从不怀疑自己的本质。命运意味着一个目的地，而她的目的地就在未来，引领她走向圆满。

As this child of destiny progresses to adulthood, does she identify with her changed self? As her teenage anger softens into midlife contentment, as her dedication to career gradually drains away, as arthritis slowly ages her, does she look back and feel that although she’s evolved physically and emotionally, at heart she’s essentially the same? Has her original psychological makeup evolved naturally? Do her past desires influence present actions? In other words, is she self-empathetic? How does your character see herself over time?

随着这位天命之女步入成年，她是否认同自己变化后的模样？当青春期的愤怒渐渐消退，中年人的满足感油然而生；当她对事业的热情逐渐消退；当关节炎慢慢侵蚀她的容颜，她是否会回首往事，觉得尽管身心都发生了变化，但内心深处却依然如故？她最初的心理构成是否自然而然地发生了改变？她过去的欲望是否影响着她现在的行为？换句话说，她是否能够理解自己？你的角色是如何看待自己随着时间推移而变化的？

For some characters, change brings clarity. In Frank Darabont’s screenplay for The Shawshank Redemption , Red (Morgan Freeman) sees his past without distortion or rationalization and wishes he could go back in time to his young self, who had committed a terrible crime, and shake sense into him.

对某些角色而言，改变带来清醒。在弗兰克·达拉邦特为《肖申克的救赎》创作的剧本中，瑞德（摩根·弗里曼饰）不再受任何扭曲或合理化的蒙蔽，而是以最真实的视角审视自己的过去，他多么希望能够回到过去，回到年轻时犯下滔天罪行的自己身边，狠狠地摇醒自己，让他幡然醒悟。

For some characters, change brings confusion. In D. H. Lawrence’s novel The Rainbow , Ursula Brangwen reviews her life in bewilderment. Every phase seems so different yet always herself: “But what did it mean, Ursula Brangwen? She did not know what she was. Only she was full of rejection, of refusal. Always, always she was spitting out of her mouth the ash and grit of disillusion, of falsity.”

对某些人来说，改变会带来困惑。在D·H·劳伦斯的小说《虹》中，厄休拉·布兰温困惑地回顾自己的一生。每个阶段似乎都截然不同，却又始终是她自己：“但这究竟意味着什么，厄休拉·布兰温？她不知道自己是什么。她只感到被拒绝，被否定。她总是，总是从口中吐出幻灭和虚假的灰烬和沙砾。”

For some characters change brings anger. In Samuel Beckett’s play Krapp’s Last Tape , Krapp at age sixty-nine listens to recordings he’s made over the decades. In his youth he believed in a lifelong identity. No more. When he listens to his past voices, he knows they were once him, but he sneers at them all and empathizes with none. Like a snake leaving his skin behind, year after year he sloughs off his earlier selves until he’s left with a bitter old man, the final Krapp.

对某些人来说，改变会带来愤怒。在塞缪尔·贝克特的戏剧《克拉普的最后录音带》中，69岁的克拉普聆听着他几十年来录制的音频。年轻时，他相信自己拥有终生不变的身份。如今，这种信念已然消逝。当他聆听过去的声音时，他知道它们曾经是他自己的声音，但他对它们嗤之以鼻，对任何一个人都无法产生共鸣。如同蛇蜕皮一般，他年复一年地蜕去过去的自己，最终只剩下一个愤世嫉俗的老人，最终的克拉普。

Whether change happens fast or slow, inward or outward, by chance or by will, all characters interpret change idiosyncratically—some accept, some deny, some take no notice. In general, however, change elicits four possible reactions:

无论变化发生得快还是慢，向内还是向外，出于偶然还是出于人为，每个人对变化的解读都各有不同——有些人接受，有些人拒绝，有些人则置之不理。但总的来说，变化会引发四种可能的反应：

1. A character may feel that change is merely cosmetic and she’ll be back to her old self soon.
1. 角色可能会觉得这种改变只是表面上的，她很快就会恢复原状。
2. She may feel transformed into a better self.
2. 她可能会觉得自己蜕变成了一个更好的自己。
3. She may view the past as the grave of the better woman she once was and left behind.
3. 她可能把过去看作是她曾经是的那个更优秀的女人的坟墓，而那个女人已经离开了她。
4. She may discover her true self, the self she repressed since childhood. Now, for better or worse, she can finally live who she really is.
4. 她或许会发现真正的自我，那个自童年起就被她压抑的自我。现在，无论好坏，她终于可以活出真正的自己了。

Change from an Author’s POV

从作者的角度转换视角

What is your personal take on character change? How do your characters react to it? Some writers believe in the permanence of identity, others in deep change. Some reveal true character, others keep it a mystery; some arc characters, others do not. In all cases, however, how an author connects a character to her past shapes the course of her identity.

你个人对角色转变有何看法？你笔下的角色对此有何反应？有些作家相信身份的永恒性，有些则相信深刻的转变。有些作家揭示角色的真实面貌，有些则将其隐藏起来；有些作家塑造角色弧光，有些则不然。然而，无论如何，作者如何将角色与其过去联系起来，都会影响角色身份的走向。

A healthy past, for example, strengthens the link between past and present and keeps identity whole; a traumatic past weakens and fragments it. Once damaged by abuse, the core self holds on to its sanity by clinging to its memories, struggling to keep them alive and true. In this case, the past may inflict itself on a character with various results. Here are four possibilities:

例如，健康的过去能够加强过去与现在之间的联系，并保持身份的完整性；而创伤性的过去则会削弱并分裂这种联系。一旦遭受虐待，核心自我就会紧紧抓住记忆，努力保持清醒，力求让记忆鲜活而真实。在这种情况下，过去可能会对一个人造成各种各样的影响。以下列举四种可能性：

1. Obsession: A trauma constantly reenters the mind with the sharp-edged impact of its original experience, unshaded and unblunted by time—PTSD, for example. Because a psychological scar never forms, each remembrance tears open the same wound.
1. 执念：创伤会不断地以最初经历的尖锐冲击力重新侵入大脑，时间无法冲淡或削弱这种冲击力——例如创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。由于心理创伤从未形成，每一次回忆都会撕开同一道伤口。
2. Repression: The conscious mind buries a painful memory in the subconscious where it festers, fueling neuroses, warping identity.
2. 压抑：意识将痛苦的记忆埋藏在潜意识中，使其不断恶化，加剧神经症，扭曲身份认同。
3. Fantasy: If a trauma refuses to fade, the mind copes with its pain by rewriting the past into alternative events it never lived but fantasizes it did.
3. 幻想：如果创伤无法消退，人的思维就会通过重写过去来应对痛苦，将其转化为从未经历过但幻想过经历过的替代事件。
4. Balance: The mind courageously faces the truth with neither excess nor distortion.
4. 平衡：心灵勇敢地面对真相，既不过度也不扭曲。

Does the cause and timing of change alter your character’s sense of self? If change comes suddenly (a kitchen accident scalds her face and hands), would physical disfigurement shred her identity? If change comes slowly by deliberate choice (each day she poisons her husband just enough to make him sick, as punishment for an insult, but over time she slowly decides he doesn’t deserve to live), is she exposed for who she always was, or does a changed self replace the old? Fine authors develop unique, idiosyncratic approaches to character arcs.

改变的原因和时机是否会改变角色的自我认知？如果改变来得突然（比如厨房意外烫伤了她的脸和手），身体上的毁容会彻底摧毁她的身份认同吗？如果改变是出于深思熟虑的选择而缓慢发生的（比如她每天都给丈夫下毒，让他生病，以此惩罚他的侮辱，但随着时间的推移，她逐渐认为他不配活在这个世上），她会彻底暴露她原本的模样，还是一个全新的自我会取代旧我？优秀的作家会发展出独特而别致的角色弧光塑造方式。

Change from the Reader’s/Audience’s POV

从读者/观众的角度转换视角

At a story’s beginning, as exposition piles up, readers and audiences absorb the surfaces, discovering who the characters seem to be. Twin curiosities about character revelation and change hold interest to the last moments: Who are these characters at heart? Who might they become?

故事伊始，随着背景信息的铺陈，读者和观众逐渐了解故事的表象，发现人物的本质。而关于人物性格的揭示和转变，则始终吸引着读者的注意力，直至故事的最后：这些人物的内心究竟是怎样的？他们最终会变成什么样？

Understanding the necessity to pace and build a reader’s or an audience’s interest, the writer must time a story’s events to first conceal, then reveal, the next change and ultimately complete a complex character.

作者深知把握节奏、培养读者或观众兴趣的必要性，必须精心安排故事事件的时机，先隐藏，再揭示，最终塑造出一个复杂的人物形象。

#↩

4. Completion

4. 完成

Principle: The finest works of story art fulfill their protagonist’s need and desire at the limits of human experience.
原则：最优秀的叙事艺术作品能够满足主人公在人类经验极限下的需求和欲望。

The terms need and desire may seem synonymous, but in my view, they name two very different aspects of character, seen from two very different points of view.

需求和欲望这两个词看似同义词，但在我看来，它们指的是性格中两个截然不同的方面，是从两个截然不同的角度来看待的。

Desire: a character’s persistent purpose, her unreached goal. Throughout a story’s telling, as the protagonist struggles to put her life back in balance, she pursues her object of desire as far as her emotional and mental powers can reach.

欲望：角色的执着追求，她尚未达成的目标。在故事的叙述过程中，主人公努力重回生活的平衡，她会竭尽全力地追求自己的欲望对象，直至达到她情感和精神所能企及的高度。

Need: an empty inner space, a potential that craves realization. At the inciting incident, the writer recognizes an incompleteness in her protagonist. She’s raw material for a superb character but lacking the unique experience that would fulfill her unique potential. She, therefore, needs to complete her humanity.

需求：内心一片空白，蕴藏着渴望实现的潜能。在故事的开端，作者意识到主人公身上存在着某种不完整之处。她拥有塑造一个杰出人物的潜质，却缺少能够充分发挥其独特潜能的经历。因此，她需要完善自身的人性。

At the climax, the events she creates do just that. The story’s final turning points put the protagonist’s emotional and mental capacities under enormous pressure. With her last actions, she experiences herself to the limit of her capacities as her author explores and expresses her core self at her greatest emotional and mental depths. She thus becomes a completed character—nothing left to reveal, nothing left to change.

在故事的高潮部分，她所创造的事件正是如此。故事的最后转折点将主人公的情感和精神承受了巨大的压力。通过她最后的行动，她体验到了自身能力的极限，而作者也借此探索并表达了她内心深处最真实的情感和精神状态。至此，她成为一个完整的人物——没有什么需要揭示，也没有什么需要改变。

Characters are never aware of their need. Only their author sees it; only their author knows what’s latent in her character; only the author can imagine her character in her most complete state.

人物本身并不会意识到自己的需求。只有作者才能看到；只有作者才知道人物内心深处潜藏着什么；只有作者才能想象出人物最完整的状态。

Characters who do not change—action heroes, cartoon figures, comic roles—have no need. They are unchanging yet fascinating. In Curb Your Enthusiasm , Larry David is the same obsessive at the beginning of each season as he is at the end. Episode after episode, he blindly pursues his slavish mania for propriety, acting out his rigid, hysterically funny self. This same pattern carries over, sequel after sequel, for the superheroes in Marvel’s cinematic universe.

那些一成不变的角色——动作英雄、卡通人物、喜剧角色——无需改变。他们固然不变，却魅力十足。在《抑制热情》中，拉里·大卫从每季开始到结束都保持着同样的执着。一集又一集，他盲目地追求着自己对礼仪的奴性狂热，演绎着他那僵硬却又滑稽可笑的自我。这种模式在漫威电影宇宙的超级英雄身上也一波又一波地延续着。

In character-driven genres (see Chapter Fourteen), however, stories open with their principals, especially protagonists, internally incomplete. Their lives to date have never called on them to use their capacities (intelligence, morality, talent, willpower, emotional forces such as love and hate, even courage and cunning) to their limit. But during the story’s clashes the characters’ actions and reactions do that work. At climax, their instinctive need to complete their humanity propels them to the end of the line, the limit of human experience.

然而，在以人物为中心的类型作品中（参见第十四章），故事的开篇往往是主人公，尤其是主角，内心并不完整。他们迄今为止的人生从未迫使他们将自身的能力（智力、道德、天赋、意志力、爱恨等情感力量，甚至勇气和谋略）发挥到极致。但在故事的冲突中，人物的行动和反应会完成这一过程。在故事的高潮，他们本能地渴望完善自身的人性，这种渴望驱使他们走向终点，走向人类经验的极限。

Examples of completed characters:

已完成角色的示例：

In Euripides’s play Medea , Princess Medea discovers that Jason, her lover and father of their two boys, has abandoned her for another woman. Medea not only poisons the other woman and the other woman’s father but, to punish Jason, murders their children as well. She escapes with her sons’ bodies and buries them in hiding so Jason can never say a prayer over their graves. With this revenge, Medea propels herself to a stunning extreme.

在欧里庇得斯的戏剧《美狄亚》中，美狄亚公主发现她的情人、两个儿子的父亲伊阿宋为了另一个女人抛弃了她。美狄亚不仅毒死了那个女人和她的父亲，为了惩罚伊阿宋，她还杀死了他们的孩子。她带着儿子的尸体逃走，并将他们藏匿起来，不让伊阿宋在他们的坟前祈祷。美狄亚的复仇将她推向了一个令人震惊的极端。

At the climax of Sophocles’s Oedipus Rex , Oedipus’s discovery that he has unwittingly murdered his father and married his mother so horrifies him that, raging with grief, he gouges out his eyes. This bolt of emotion numbs all thought, leaving Oedipus in shock and unfinished.

在索福克勒斯的《俄狄浦斯王》的高潮部分，俄狄浦斯发现自己无意中弑父娶母，悲痛欲绝，他挖出了自己的双眼。这突如其来的情感冲击使他丧失了所有理智，俄狄浦斯陷入了深深的震惊之中，他的人生也因此戛然而止。

Twenty-three years later, however, Socrates, at age ninety, completed his character. In Oedipus at Colonus , Oedipus thinks to the heart of his complicity and realizes that his pulsing pride and lack of self-awareness shaped his fate. In short, he should have known better. Once he accepts his guilt, he completes himself and dies in peace.

然而，二十三年后，九十岁高龄的苏格拉底完成了他的人生。在《俄狄浦斯在科罗诺斯》中，俄狄浦斯深入思考了自己的罪责，意识到自己狂妄自大、缺乏自知之明最终导致了他的命运。简而言之，他本应更加明智。一旦他接受了自己的罪责，他的人生便得以圆满，最终安详地离世。

In Kim Ki-duk’s Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter… and Spring , an apprentice Buddhist monk evolves from a cruel child to a lustful teenager to a wife-murdering felon to a repentant convict to a Buddhist master—an arc that ends in an inner gravity of genuine change, life-worn wisdom, and completion of self.

在金基德的《春夏秋冬……又春》中，一位佛教僧侣学徒从一个残酷的孩子成长为一个好色的少年，再到一个杀妻的罪犯，然后是一个忏悔的罪犯，最后成为一名佛教大师——这一弧线最终以内心深处的真正改变、饱经风霜的智慧和自我完善而告终。

In The Sea, The Sea , a novel by Iris Murdoch, Charles Arrowby, a playwright and director, pursues his lifelong obsession with romance, never understanding that his first, true, and only love is and always has been himself. He finally exhausts his limited humanity, trapped in a cul-de-sac of self-deception, completely blind to himself.

在艾瑞斯·默多克的小说《大海，大海》中，剧作家兼导演查尔斯·阿罗比终其一生都沉迷于浪漫爱情，却始终未能领悟，他最初、真正、也是唯一挚爱的，始终是他自己。最终，他耗尽了有限的人性，深陷自我欺骗的死胡同，对自己视而不见。

In Network by Paddy Chayefsky, adapted for stage by Lee Hall, TV anchorman Howard Beale (Peter Finch on-screen, Bryan Cranston onstage), makes headline news by declaring that modern life is bullshit. Beale’s prime-time rants bring higher and higher ratings as he spirals deeper and deeper into insanity. Eventually, his message about meaninglessness becomes meaningless. As his ratings fall, the network has him assassinated on camera. He dies, but not until all of his dimensions have been exposed and exhausted.

在帕迪·查耶夫斯基的小说《电视台风云》（Network，由李·霍尔改编为舞台剧）中，电视主播霍华德·比尔（电影版由彼得·芬奇饰演，舞台剧版由布莱恩·克兰斯顿饰演）因宣称现代生活都是狗屁而登上头条新闻。比尔在黄金时段的咆哮式言论为他带来了越来越高的收视率，而他本人也逐渐陷入疯狂。最终，他关于人生虚无的论调也变得毫无意义。随着收视率的下滑，电视台安排人在镜头前暗杀了他。他死了，但在此之前，他的所有面向都已被彻底揭露和耗尽。

When is Michael Corleone completed? At the end of The Godfather Part II ? Some think yes; I think not. Over the first two films, Michael makes others suffer, but he doesn’t burn in real hell until The Godfather Part III completes him.

迈克尔·柯里昂何时才算真正完结？是在《教父2》结尾吗？有人认为是，但我并不这么认为。在前两部电影中，迈克尔让其他人饱受折磨，但他直到《教父3》才真正下地狱。

In the finale of The Leftovers , the love story between Nora and Kevin climaxes quietly as they hold hands over a kitchen table. For three seasons, Nora’s cynicism keeps her from believing in Kevin, and Kevin’s intimacy aversion keeps him from believing he deserves Nora. In between their personal episodes, Nora travels sideways to a parallel universe in search of her lost family, while Kevin dies and rises from the dead, again and again. Once they realize that the only way to make sense of the senseless is to believe in their love, they reach completion.

在《守望尘世》的最终季中，诺拉和凯文的爱情故事在厨房餐桌旁悄然落幕，两人手牵着手。三季以来，诺拉的愤世嫉俗让她无法相信凯文，而凯文对亲密关系的抗拒也让他觉得自己配不上诺拉。在他们各自的内心挣扎之间，诺拉穿越到平行宇宙寻找失散的家人，而凯文则一次又一次地死去又复活。当他们意识到，唯有相信彼此的爱，才能理解这看似毫无意义的一切，他们的爱情也最终走向圆满。

#↩

COMPLETING A CHARACTER

完善角色

To sum up: For some characters, a fierce longing to make their mark on the world, an unquenchable thirst to find purpose, drives them to complete themselves. For others, an inner fear of fragmentation or a fervent curiosity about their natures propels them. In both cases, the uncompleted construct themselves inwardly by testing themselves outwardly. They take grave risks to pursue something they value supremely but cannot control fully… even when they reach it. 2

总而言之：对于某些人来说，强烈的渴望在世界上留下印记，对寻找人生意义的永不满足的渴求驱使他们不断完善自我。而对于另一些人来说，内心对破碎的恐惧或对自身本质的强烈好奇心则驱动着他们。无论哪种情况，这些不完整的人都会通过向外挑战来构建内在的自我。他们冒着巨大的风险去追求自己无比珍视却无法完全掌控的东西……即便最终达成目标。

The vast majority of characters, however, rarely question how deeply they’ve gone into life, how much wider they might go, if they’ll ever experience themselves to their fullest. Instead, the writer does that for them by taking key measurements and asking key questions.

然而，绝大多数角色很少会质疑自己对人生的投入程度，以及人生的广阔天地，更不会思考自己是否能够充分体验人生。相反，作者会通过关键的衡量标准和提出关键的问题来替他们完成这些思考。

Writing to fulfill a character’s need to complete begins with the recognition that we are all born with excess capacity, with far more thought and feeling than life will ever demand, with powers we will never use. So study your character in those days just before the story begins and ask: Given my character at this point in her life, given the small percentage of mental and emotional aptitude she’s used thus far and given the depths and breadths she might someday touch, what does her humanity lack?

写作的目的是为了满足角色的自我完善需求，而这首先要认识到我们生来就拥有过剩的潜能，拥有远超生活所需、丰富多彩的思想和情感，以及我们永远无法用尽的力量。因此，在故事开始前的那段时间里，仔细审视你的角色，并扪心自问：鉴于角色此时的人生阶段，鉴于她迄今为止所运用的少量心智和情感天赋，以及她未来可能触及的广博深邃，她的人性还缺少什么？

With that answer in hand, then ask: What does she need to complete herself? What specific event, should it happen to her, would propel her toward fulfillment of her promise? That turning point becomes your story’s inciting incident.

有了这个问题的答案，接下来就要问：她需要什么才能完善自我？如果发生什么具体的事情，会促使她实现自己的承诺？这个转折点就成了你故事的导火索。

After that ask: What events would carry her to the limits of her greatest thoughts, her deepest being? What pressures, conflicts, choices, actions, and reactions will take her humanity to its fullest? These answers become the story you tell.

接下来问问自己：什么样的事件会将她推向思想的极限，触及她内心最深处的自我？什么样的压力、冲突、选择、行动和反应会让她的人性得以充分展现？这些答案将成为你讲述的故事。

Once characters reach completion, they often reflect on the ironies that scarred and yet fulfilled their humanity. We’ll close with their thoughts:

人物塑造完成后，他们往往会反思那些既伤痕累累又成就了他们人性的讽刺事件。最后，让我们以他们的思考作为结尾：

To-morrow, and to-morrow, and to-morrow, creeps in this petty pace from day to day to the last syllable of recorded time…
明天，明天，再明天，就这样以这种缓慢的步伐，日复一日地悄然流逝，直到有记录的时间的最后一个音节……

— Macbeth in The Tragedy of Macbeth

——《麦克白》中的麦克白

Yes, she thought, laying down her brush in extreme fatigue, I have had my vision.
“是的，”她放下画笔，极度疲惫地想，“我已经看到了我的景象。”

— Lily in Virginia Woolf’s To the Lighthouse

——弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫《到灯塔去》中的莉莉

And soon now we shall go out of the house and go into the convulsion of the world, out of history into history and the awful responsibility of Time.
很快，我们将走出家门，进入动荡的世界，走出历史，进入历史以及时间的可怕责任。

– Jack Burden in Robert Penn Warren’s All the King’s Men

——罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦执导的电影《国王的人马》中的杰克·伯登

I’m thinking of aurochs and angels, the secret of durable pigments, prophetic sonnets, the refuge of art. And this is the only immortality you and I may share, my Lolita.
我想起了野牛和天使，持久颜料的秘密，预言般的十四行诗，艺术的避难所。而这，或许是你我唯一共享的永生，我的洛丽塔。

— Humbert Humbert in Vladimir Nabokov’s Lolita

——弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫《洛丽塔》中的亨伯特·亨伯特

Mediocracies everywhere—now and to come—I absolve you all. Amen.
凡是现在和将来所有平庸的政权，我都赦免你们。阿门。

— Salieri in Peter Shaffer’s play Amadeus

——彼得·谢弗戏剧《莫扎特传》中的萨列里

It’s old light, and there’s not much of it. But it’s enough to see by.
那是老式的灯光，而且亮度不高。但足够照明了。

— Elaine in Margaret Atwood’s Cat’s Eye

——玛格丽特·阿特伍德小说《猫眼》中的伊莱恩

It seems that destiny has taken a hand.
看来命运已经眷顾了他。

—Rick Blaine in Casablanca

——里克·布莱恩在《卡萨布兰卡》

#↩

12

THE SYMBOLIC CHARACTER

象征性角色

No matter how completed or limited, all characters mean more than themselves. Every figure you create is a metaphor for either a social identity (mother, child, boss, employee) or an inner identity (good, evil, wise, naïve) or a combination of the two. These roles form casts that can be divided into two grand affinities: Realism and Symbolism. Some storytellers create casts inspired by daily observation, and then set them to cope with everyday hell; other writers, such as the creators of the DC Comics and Marvel universes, work with an awareness of a symbolic dimension in their casts, costuming them in imaginary characterizations.

无论角色塑造多么完整或多么有限，它们都蕴含着超越自身意义的内涵。你创造的每一个人物都是某种社会身份（母亲、孩子、老板、员工）或内在身份（善良、邪恶、睿智、天真）的隐喻，或是二者的结合。这些角色构成了一系列人物，可以归纳为两大流派：现实主义和象征主义。一些故事讲述者从日常观察中汲取灵感，创作人物角色，并让他们面对日常生活的种种困境；而另一些作家，例如DC漫画和漫威宇宙的创作者，则在创作中意识到人物角色所蕴含的象征意义，并赋予他们虚构的形象。

For writers of Speculative Fiction—Fantasy, Sci-Fi, Horror, Superhero, Supernatural, Magical Realism, and the many subgenres of each—the symbol weighs more than its personification. For writers of conventional Realism—dramas and comedies that center in the down-to-earth problems of families, personal relationships, social institutions, legal systems, and moral psychology—the personification counts for more than the symbol.

对于思辨小说作家——包括奇幻、科幻、恐怖、超级英雄、超自然、魔幻现实主义及其众多子类型——而言，象征意义比拟人化更为重要。而对于传统现实主义作家——那些聚焦于家庭、人际关系、社会制度、法律体系和道德心理等现实问题的戏剧和喜剧——而言，拟人化则比象征意义更为重要。

Symbols evolve involuntarily during the writing. No author, no matter his talent, can deliberately create an all-new symbol from scratch. They are timeless. You can only borrow them. 1

符号在写作过程中会不由自主地演变。任何作者，无论才华如何，都无法凭空创造出一个全新的符号。它们是永恒的。你只能借用它们。

Symbols arise in this way: As the mind sees, hears, or touches an object, it instinctively asks, “What is this thing and why is it what it is?” Intellect and imagination then peer beneath the surface, as it were, looking for intrinsic structures and hidden causes; over time the insights they capture become idealized into meaning-rich, power-compressing icons.

符号的产生方式如下：当心灵看到、听到或触摸到某个物体时，它会本能地问：“这是什么？它为什么是现在的样子？” 随后，理智和想象力仿佛窥探到表面之下，寻找内在的结构和隐藏的原因；随着时间的推移，它们所捕捉到的洞见被理想化为意义丰富、力量强大的符号。

Examples: Inspired by curvatures found in nature, the mind pictured the perfect geometric circle, and then elevated this abstraction into a symbol for the Cycle of Life. Pregnant women exude the energy of replicating DNA that our ancestors deified as the Earth Mother. The ocean’s turbulence reminds sailors of an angry, punishing father who the Greeks then reimagined as Poseidon. Edible plants and animals became the ritual of meal taking that avant-garde chefs perfected into Haute Cuisine. This movement from particular to general to ideal generates the luminous, often fantastic images of symbolism. And where do writers find these visions? In their dreams.

例如：受自然界曲线的启发，人们构想出完美的几何圆，并将这种抽象概念提升为生命循环的象征。孕妇散发着复制DNA的能量，我们的祖先将其奉为大地之母。海洋的波涛汹涌令水手们想起一位愤怒而严厉的父亲，希腊人将其重新想象成海神波塞冬。可食用的动植物成为用餐仪式的一部分，而前卫的厨师们则将其发展成为高级料理。这种从特殊到普遍再到理想的演变过程，产生了象征主义中那些光彩夺目、往往充满奇幻色彩的意象。而作家们又从何处获得这些灵感呢？在他们的梦境中。

Dreaming in symbols is an evolutionary adaptation the pre–homo sapiens psyche acquired hundreds of thousands, perhaps millions, of years ago. Its adaptive purpose is to protect sleep.

以符号形式做梦是智人之前的人类心理在数十万年甚至数百万年前进化而来的一种适应性特征。它的适应性目的是为了保护睡眠。

When you toss and turn at night, what pours through your brain? Racing thoughts: those hopes and hungers, dreads and fears, passions and angers, longings and lovings—the unresolved conflicts a weary mind cannot control.

当你夜里辗转反侧时，你的脑海中会涌现出什么？是纷乱的思绪：那些希望和渴望，恐惧和害怕，激情和愤怒，思念和爱恋——疲惫的心灵无法控制的未解决的冲突。

Hindus symbolize the human mind as the chattering monkey—the yak, yak, yak, yak, yak, yak of thoughts running through the brain without pause every minute of every hour of every day and night. This prattle keeps you awake until the pineal gland secretes its melatonin and you drift into sleep. Dreaming then compresses your streaming thoughts inside symbols, giving intelligence a chance to rest and the body a chance to heal.

印度教徒将人的心智比作喋喋不休的猴子——思绪如同牦牛般在脑海中不停地奔涌，日夜不停。这种喋喋不休让你难以入眠，直到松果体分泌褪黑激素，你才渐渐进入梦乡。梦境则将你纷乱的思绪压缩成各种符号，让大脑得以休息，也让身体得以疗愈。

In the way a piston concentrates heat by reducing the volume inside a cylinder, a symbol creates power by compacting multiple meanings into a single image. A bearded figure, for example, dressed in robes, seated in a great chair, looking down from above symbolizes the Father . This image radiates complex ideas of judgment, wisdom, insight, and absolute authority, along with fear of punishment, guilt over broken rules, gratitude for protection, and adoration rooted in respect and dread. This grand mix of meanings and emotions condenses inside one image.

如同活塞通过缩小气缸内的容积来集中热量一样，符号通过将多种含义浓缩于单一图像之中来创造力量。例如，一位身着长袍、蓄着胡须的人物端坐于高椅之上，俯视着众生，象征着父亲。这幅图像散发出审判、智慧、洞察力和绝对权威等复杂意象，同时也蕴含着对惩罚的恐惧、对违背规则的愧疚、对庇护的感激以及根植于敬畏与恐惧的崇拜。所有这些意义和情感的交织浓缩于这幅图像之中。

#↩

SYMBOLIC CHARACTER SPECTRUM

符号特征谱

The spectrum of Symbolism in character creation spans from brightest to dimmest, beginning with the radiance of archetypes, followed by the glow of allegories, then the muted shades of types, and finally the gray outlines of stock characters.

角色创作中的象征主义光谱从最明亮到最暗淡，从原型的光辉开始，到寓言的光芒，再到类型的柔和色调，最后到典型角色的灰色轮廓。

#↩

Principle: Archetypes turn essences into characters

原则：原型将本质转化为角色

Humanity invented archetypes as instinctively as birds weave nests and spiders spin webs. The symbolic power of an archetypal image is so universal it can be endlessly varied in its details yet never lose its basic pattern. No matter how an archetype’s veneer shifts from culture to culture, from animation to live action, its presence commands fascination.

人类创造原型，如同鸟儿筑巢、蜘蛛织网一般，是出于本能。原型意象的象征力量如此普遍，以至于其细节可以千变万化，却始终保持着基本模式。无论原型在不同文化、动画或真人表演中呈现出何种面貌，它的存在都令人着迷。

Archetypes inhabit four major components of storytelling: events, settings, objects, roles:

原型存在于故事讲述的四个主要组成部分中：事件、场景、物品、角色：

1. Events such as the Sacred Birth, the Fall from Grace, the Battle between Good and Evil.
1. 诸如神圣的诞生、堕落、善恶之战之类的事件。
2. Settings such as the Desert as ground for meditation, the Garden as the miracle of fertility, the Castle as the seat of authority.
2. 沙漠作为冥想的场所，花园作为生育奇迹的象征，城堡作为权威的所在地。
3. Objects such as Light as the symbol of Hope, Red as the color of Passion, or the Heart as an icon for Love.
3. 诸如光作为希望的象征，红色作为激情的颜色，或者心形作为爱的标志之类的物体。
4. Roles such as Star-Crossed Lovers, the Outcast wandering in exile, the Wizard waving a magic wand.
4. 诸如命运多舛的恋人、流亡的流浪者、挥舞魔杖的巫师之类的角色。

An archetypal character, like a stone sculpture, is the same inside as out. The Earth Mother, for example, concentrates all aspects of motherhood—giver of life, nurturer of innocence, forgiver of failings—into one rock-solid identity. She has no subtext. She never pretends, never jokes, never thinks an ironic thought. No hidden wishes contradict her pronouncements; no secret feelings complicate her actions. She simply mothers.

原型人物如同石雕，内外一致。例如，大地之母将母性的所有面向——生命的赋予者、纯真的养育者、过错的宽恕者——凝聚成一个坚实无比的身份。她没有弦外之音。她从不伪装，从不开玩笑，也从不怀有讽刺意味。她的言辞中没有任何隐藏的愿望与之矛盾；她的行为中也没有任何隐秘的情感。她只是单纯地为人母。

Archetypes expand and contract. The Hag, the Crone, and the Wise Woman are all variations of the Earth Mother. They may or may not have magical or supernatural powers; they may or may not be disagreeable, malicious, or malevolent; they may or may not be helpful. Compare the Wicked Witch of the West with the Good Witch of the North in The Wizard of Oz .

原型既有扩展也有收缩。老巫婆、老妪和智者都是大地母亲的不同化身。她们可能拥有魔法或超自然力量，也可能没有；她们可能令人厌恶、心怀恶意，也可能并非如此；她们可能乐于助人，也可能毫无助益。不妨比较一下《绿野仙踪》中的西方女巫和北方女巫。

To a greater or lesser degree, a character, realistic or fantasized, stands in for his ancient original. Although rooted in its archetype, once on the stage, page, or screen, the character then diminishes the ideal because perfection can only be imagined, not performed. To freshen these repetitions, the writer must invent ingenious new traits of characterization.

在某种程度上，无论是现实主义的还是虚构的人物，都代表着其古老的原型。尽管人物根植于原型，但一旦登上舞台、书页或银幕，便会削弱理想化的形象，因为完美只能存在于想象中，而无法被演绎。为了使这些重复的形象焕发新生，作家必须创造出巧妙的新人物特征。

Character archetypes are limited in number, but from Plato to Carl Jung to today’s writers of Speculative Fiction no one agrees on what that number is. Many are drawn from religion: God, Devil, Angel, Demon; some are found in domestic life: Mother/Queen, Father/King, Child/Prince/Princess, Servant; and others are inspired by social conflicts: the Hero, the Rebel, Monsters (Villains), Tricksters (Clowns), and Helpers (Sage, Mentor, Magician).

人物原型数量有限，但从柏拉图到卡尔·荣格，再到当今的科幻小说作家，对于这个数字究竟是多少，至今无人达成共识。许多原型源于宗教：上帝、魔鬼、天使、恶魔；有些原型来自家庭生活：母亲/女王、父亲/国王、孩子/王子/公主、仆人；还有一些原型则受到社会冲突的启发：英雄、反叛者、怪物（恶棍）、骗子（小丑）和帮手（智者、导师、魔法师）。
