This last archetype, the Helper, has given us Gandalf in The Lord of the Rings , Obi-Wan Kenobi in Star Wars , Merlin in many versions of the King Arthur myth, and the Fairy Godmother in even more tellings. And, of course, one role can combine two or more archetypes. Prospero, protagonist of Shakespeare’s The Tempest , combines Wizard, Mentor, Ruler, Hero, and Villain.

最后一种原型是“帮助者”，它衍生出了《指环王》中的甘道夫、《星球大战》中的欧比旺·克诺比、许多亚瑟王传说版本中的梅林，以及更多版本中的仙女教母。当然，一个角色也可以融合两种或多种原型。莎士比亚戏剧《暴风雨》的主人公普洛斯彼罗就集巫师、导师、统治者、英雄和反派于一身。

Because an archetypal character in Speculative Fiction is dimensionless, he’s incapable of change: A superhero may resist the task, but in time he’ll put on his cape and fly to the rescue. Therefore, the purer the archetype, the less we care about his past or future, the less we imagine him outside his immediate scenes, the less we discern his inner life, the more predictable become his actions.

因为科幻小说中的原型人物缺乏维度，所以他们无法改变：超级英雄或许会抗拒任务，但最终还是会披上斗篷，飞向救援。因此，原型越纯粹，我们就越不关心他们的过去或未来，越少想象他们置身于特定场景之外的样子，越少了解他们的内心世界，他们的行为也就越容易预测。

Because the complex character of Realism is dimensional and changeable, the archetypal role and the myth he rode in on become less important. Nonetheless, whether grounded or imaginary, a character vibrates with greater intensity when he strikes an archetypal chord in the subconscious mind of the reader or audience. If, on the other hand, the reader/audience thinks the conscious thought, “Oh, he’s a symbol for…!,” if they recognize a character as symbolic, the role flattens and its impact drains away. Therefore, veil symbolism behind a never-seen-before characterization. Fascinate the reader/audience with whom the character seems to be, then quietly smuggle your archetype in below reader/audience awareness and let it slip into their subconscious, where they will feel its presence without knowing or caring why.

由于现实主义作品的复杂性在于其多面性和多变性，原型角色及其所承载的神话便显得不那么重要了。然而，无论角色是真实存在的还是虚构的，当它触动读者或观众潜意识中的原型共鸣时，其影响力都会显著增强。反之，如果读者/观众有意识地想到“哦，他是……的象征！”，一旦他们意识到某个角色具有象征意义，那么这个角色就会变得扁平化，其影响力也会随之消散。因此，要将象征意义隐藏在前所未见的角色塑造背后。先用角色吸引读者/观众，让他们产生共鸣，然后悄悄地将你的原型融入其中，使其在读者/观众的意识之外悄然潜入他们的潜意识，让他们在不知不觉中感受到它的存在。

#↩

Principle: Allegories turn values into characters

原则：寓言将价值观转化为人物形象

Like an archetype, an allegorical character is also made from a single substance but with less density. Whereas an archetype concentrates all facets of a universal role (Hero, Mother, Mentor) into a single persona, an allegorical character embodies only one facet, positive or negative. In the moral universe of an allegorical setting, the cast personifies a pattern of values. In the medieval morality play Everyman , for example, each character personifies an aspect of human existence such as Knowledge, Beauty, Strength, or Death.

与原型类似，寓言人物也由单一元素构成，但密度较低。原型将普遍角色（英雄、母亲、导师）的所有面向浓缩于单一人物之中，而寓言人物则仅体现其中一个面向，无论正面还是负面。在寓言故事的道德世界中，人物角色象征着一套价值体系。例如，在中世纪道德剧《人人》中，每个角色都象征着人类存在的某个方面，例如知识、美貌、力量或死亡。

In the alternative worlds of Jonathan Swift’s satire Gulliver’s Travels , populations represent values such as Pettiness, Bureaucracy, Absurd Science, and Obedience to Authority. William Golding set his novel Lord of the Flies on an island where schoolboys collectively represent humanity, while individually they symbolize values such as Democracy versus Tyranny, Civility versus Savagery, and the Rational versus Irrational Mind. Pixar’s Inside Out created an allegory inside its protagonist’s subconscious mind by selecting five emotional values and writing them into the characters Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear, and Disgust.

在乔纳森·斯威夫特的讽刺小说《格列佛游记》的平行世界中，不同群体分别代表着诸如斤斤计较、官僚主义、荒谬的科学和服从权威等价值观。威廉·戈尔丁的小说《蝇王》则将故事背景设定在一个岛屿上，岛上的学生们集体代表着人类，而个体则象征着民主与暴政、文明与野蛮以及理性与非理性等价值观。皮克斯动画电影《头脑特工队》则通过选取五种不同的情绪，分别赋予“快乐”、“悲伤”、“愤怒”、“恐惧”和“厌恶”五个角色，从而在主人公的潜意识中构建了一个寓言故事。

Other examples: a lion as Wisdom in The Chronicles of Narnia and as Cowardice in The Wizard of Oz ; Lord Business as Corporate Tyranny in The Lego Movie ; an enormous stuffed whale as the Apocalypse in Laszlo Krasznahorkai’s novel The Melancholy of Resistance ; Tweedledum and Tweedledee as Difference-Without-Difference in Alice Through the Looking Glass . The allegorical cast of Steven Universe (Cartoon Network) take their identities from gemstones.

其他例子：《纳尼亚传奇》中的狮子象征智慧，《绿野仙踪》中的狮子象征懦弱；《乐高大电影》中的商业大亨象征企业暴政；拉斯洛·克拉斯纳霍尔凯的小说《抵抗的忧郁》中，一头巨大的毛绒鲸鱼象征世界末日；《爱丽丝镜中奇遇记》中的双胞胎兄弟象征“没有区别的差异”。卡通频道动画《史蒂文宇宙》中的寓言角色也以宝石为原型塑造了各自的身份。

#↩

Principle: Types turn a behavior into a character

原则：类型将行为转化为性格

Stories, especially those told in the genres of Realism, need not include an archetypal or an allegorical character, but few can be cast without a type or two.

故事，尤其是现实主义题材的故事，不一定需要包含原型或寓言人物，但很少有故事可以完全不包含一两个典型人物。

A type is an animated adjective. Disney’s Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (adapting a Brothers Grimm fairy tale) turned seven adjectives into the characters Sleepy, Bashful, Grumpy, Happy, Sneezy, Dopey, and Doc (smart).

类型是一种动态形容词。迪士尼的《白雪公主和七个小矮人》（改编自格林兄弟的童话故事）将七个形容词变成了瞌睡虫、害羞鬼、爱生气鬼、开心果、喷嚏精、糊涂蛋和博士（聪明）。

These nondimensional supporting roles act out a single trait of behavior such as muddled, caring, blaming, fretting, artistic, shy, jealous, panicked, cruel, or a single trait of temperament such as the indifferent clerk, the talkative cabby, the unhappy little rich girl. All adjectives have an opposite charge of value—happy versus miserable, daydreamy versus vigilant, whining versus stoic—thus doubling the number of possible types. 2

这些非维度辅助角色展现单一的行为特征，例如迷茫、关心、责备、焦虑、艺术气质、害羞、嫉妒、惊慌、残酷，或者单一的气质特征，例如冷漠的职员、健谈的出租车司机、不快乐的小富家女。所有形容词都具有相反的价值倾向——快乐与痛苦、白日梦与警惕、抱怨与坚忍——从而使可能的类型数量翻倍。

The first storytellers typed characters according to their social role: king, queen, warrior, servant, herdsman, etc. But in the Nicomachean Ethics , Aristotle began studying people by personality. He used adjectives such as Excessively Vain, Great of Soul, Choleric, Good Tempered, Officious, Contentious, and the like.

早期的故事讲述者根据人物的社会角色对其进行分类：国王、王后、战士、仆人、牧人等等。但在《尼各马可伦理学》中，亚里士多德开始从性格的角度研究人。他使用了诸如过分虚荣、伟大灵魂、易怒、性情温和、爱管闲事、好争辩等等形容词。

Aristotle’s student, Theophrastus, expanded this idea in his The Study of the Character . He lists thirty brief, trenchant types, giving us an insightful portrait of his time and humanity at large. All thirty, however, are negatively toned: Superstitious, Lying, Nervous, Pretentious, Buffoonish, Flattering, Boring, Bragging, Cowardly, and so on. He could have listed correspondingly positive examples: Rational, Truthful, Calm, Modest, Wise, Sincere, Entertaining, Discrete, Heroic, but I suspect negative types were great fun for his readers. The comedy writer Menander cast many of Theophrastus’s types in farces with titles such as The Grouch , The Peevish Man , The Misogynist , and The Man Nobody Likes .

亚里士多德的学生泰奥弗拉斯托斯在他的《性格研究》中扩展了这一观点。他列举了三十种简明扼要、一针见血的性格类型，为我们展现了他所处时代乃至整个人类社会的深刻图景。然而，这三十种性格类型都带有负面色彩：迷信的、说谎的、紧张的、自负的、滑稽的、谄媚的、无趣的、吹牛的、懦弱的等等。他本可以列举一些相应的正面例子：理性的、诚实的、冷静的、谦逊的、智慧的、真诚的、风趣的、谨慎的、英勇的，但我怀疑这些负面类型对他的读者来说更有趣。喜剧作家米南德将泰奥弗拉斯托斯列举的许多性格类型运用到他的闹剧中，例如《爱发牢骚的人》、《易怒的人》、《厌女者》和《人见人厌的人》。

To elevate an extra into a type, simply give him a specific behavior. A nondescript teenager steps out of the crowd and takes on a role when, despite his best efforts to control himself, he constantly giggles with embarrassment.

要想让一个群众演员成为某种类型的角色，只需赋予他某种特定的行为即可。一个毫不起眼的青少年从人群中走出来，扮演某个角色，尽管他竭力克制自己，却还是会因为尴尬而不断傻笑。

For example, three familiar types:

例如，以下三种类型较为常见：

The Fanatic

狂热者

The Fanatic may be a bored misfit, an untalented artist, or a chronic discontent, but in all cases, he rejects his meaningless life and hates himself for who he is not. In search of a new identity, he joins a movement that gives him a new name, new uniform, and new vocabulary. So equipped, he becomes a fanatic for the thing he loves and a hater of anything opposed to it. At rock bottom, the angry fanatic projects his self-loathing onto something or someone foreign. 3

狂热者或许是百无聊赖的边缘人、才华平庸的艺术家，或是长期心怀不满的人，但无论如何，他都厌恶自己毫无意义的生活，并憎恨自己并非真实的模样。为了寻求新的身份认同，他加入了一个运动，获得了新的名字、新的制服和新的词汇。有了这些，他便成为自己所爱之物的狂热信徒，并憎恨一切与之相悖的事物。在人生的低谷，愤怒的狂热者会将自我厌恶投射到外在的事物或人身上。

For thought-provoking examples, study Daniel Balint (Ryan Gosling) in Henry Bean’s The Believer ; Freddie Quell (Joaquin Phoenix) in Paul Thomas Anderson’s film The Master ; Syndrome (Jason Lee) in Brad Bird’s film The Incredibles .

想要了解一些发人深省的例子，可以研究亨利·比恩执导的电影《信徒》中的丹尼尔·巴林特（瑞恩·高斯林饰）；保罗·托马斯·安德森执导的电影《大师》中的弗雷迪·奎尔（华金·菲尼克斯饰）；以及布拉德·伯德执导的电影《超人总动员》中的辛德罗姆（杰森·李饰）。

The Hipster

潮人

The Hipster is the opposite of the fanatic. He obsesses on the only thing he loves: himself. He wears forgotten fashions (Hawaiian shirts), collects antique things (portable record players), and takes up pointless hobbies (home brewing). The hipster wants to be one of a kind, not with fresh ideas of his own but from things no one else wants. To deflect mockery, he brags about his failure to do anything meaningful. To preempt criticism, he adopts an I’m-Only-Kidding smirk and lives ironically by hiding in public.

嬉皮士与狂热分子截然相反。他痴迷于自己唯一热爱的东西：他自己。他穿着过时的服饰（比如夏威夷衬衫），收藏古董（比如便携式唱片机），热衷于一些毫无意义的爱好（比如自酿啤酒）。嬉皮士想要独一无二，不是凭借自己独创的新颖想法，而是靠别人不感兴趣的东西来标榜自己。为了避免被嘲笑，他会吹嘘自己一事无成。为了先发制人地避免批评，他会摆出一副“我只是开玩笑”的姿态，讽刺地躲在人群中。

For hip examples, consider Jeff Bridges as The Big Lebowski , Jon Heder as Napoleon Dynamite , and Oscar Isaac as the title character in Inside Llewyn Davis .

举几个时髦的例子，可以看看杰夫·布里吉斯饰演的《谋杀绿脚趾》、乔恩·海德饰演的《大人物拿破仑》以及奥斯卡·伊萨克饰演的《醉乡民谣》中的主角。

The Cool

酷

Cool describes an emotionally controlled, never eager or needy, detached, and self-possessed type. He stands still, quiet and opaque, depriving the reader/audience of insight. We sense that he has a secret past, but we never know for sure. Gracefully skilled, he has found a unique way to make a living, but only he knows what it is. A morally ambiguous realist, he lives by his own code in an absurd world. He doesn’t need or want applause; he knows his worth. We sense his depth but can only guess what’s behind his eyes. 4

“酷”这个词用来形容情绪控制力强、从不急躁或依赖他人、超然物外、沉着冷静的人。他静静地伫立着，沉默寡言，难以捉摸，让读者/观众无法窥探他的内心。我们隐约感觉到他有着不为人知的过去，但始终无法确定。他技艺精湛，找到了一种独特的谋生之道，但只有他自己知道那是什么。作为一个道德模糊的现实主义者，他在这个荒诞的世界里遵循着自己的准则。他不需要也不想要掌声；他深知自己的价值。我们能感受到他的深邃，却只能猜测他眼神背后隐藏着什么。

Examples of cool: The enigmatic murderess Juliette Fontaine in I’ve Loved You So Long suffers decades of silence for her secret; Amy in Gone Girl impersonates many lethal selves, none of which are her; Clint Eastwood played cool in films such as Play Misty for Me and High Plains Drifter .

酷的例子：电影《我一直爱你》中神秘的女杀人犯朱丽叶·方丹为了自己的秘密默默忍受了数十年的沉默；电影《消失的爱人》中的艾米扮演了许多致命的角色，但没有一个是她自己；克林特·伊斯特伍德在《迷雾追魂》和《高平原漂泊者》等电影中扮演了酷的角色。

#↩

Principle: Stocks turn a job into a character

原则：股票将工作变成角色

Types act out a behavior; stocks take a job. Fictional societies require citizens playing social roles, defined primarily by their work.

类型代表某种行为；股票代表某种工作。虚构的社会需要公民扮演社会角色，而这些角色主要由他们的工作来定义。

People in the insecure gig economy—grad students waiting tables, elderly greeters at Walmart, artists doing something other than their art—cannot control their future. Because their jobs contradict what they want out of life, they may become too interesting and dimensional to play stock characters.

在不稳定的零工经济中，人们——比如在餐厅当服务员的研究生、在沃尔玛做迎宾员的老年人、以及从事与艺术创作无关工作的艺术家——无法掌控自己的未来。因为他们的工作与他们的人生追求背道而驰，他们或许会变得过于有趣和立体，以至于无法再扮演千篇一律的角色。

Instead, people in secure positions tend to work in a field small enough that they can control its machinery: lawyers, house painters, doctors, golf club pros, and the like. Job security may dull their inner creativity, as well as their empathy for clients, homeowners, patients, and club members, but professions such as these, placed around the principals, become stock roles.

相反，那些身居要职的人往往从事规模较小的行业，以便掌控行业运作：律师、油漆工、医生、高尔夫球俱乐部教练等等。工作保障或许会削弱他们的内在创造力，以及对客户、房主、病人、俱乐部会员的同理心，但围绕这些核心人物的职业，最终都会沦为千篇一律的模板角色。

The first stock characters were given props onstage so audiences could identify them: Shepherds held a crook, ambassadors carried the caduceus, kings a scepter, heroes a sword, old men a staff.

第一批固定角色在舞台上都配有道具，以便观众能够识别他们：牧羊人拿着牧羊杖，大使拿着双蛇杖，国王拿着权杖，英雄拿着剑，老人拿着拐杖。

The Roman satirist Plautus used and reused farcical stocks: Rich Miser, Clever Slave, Stupid Slave, Slave Dealer, Prostitute, Braggart Soldier, and the hanger-on parasite that today we would call a Groupie.

罗马讽刺作家普劳图斯反复使用滑稽的典型人物：吝啬鬼、聪明的奴隶、愚蠢的奴隶、奴隶贩子、妓女、吹牛的士兵，以及今天我们称之为追星族的寄生虫。

As they carry out their tasks, stocks make no choices: Doctors deliver bad news to families, lawyers explain provisions in a will, beggars beg. Whether clichéd or freshly drawn, the great advantage of stock characters is an instant recognition of purpose that lessens the need for exposition. The reader/audience knows why a stock has entered a story and his task in the telling. As they do their job, however, stocks needn’t be dull. A stock can be worth his moment in the light if you give him a one-of-a-kind characterization, the unique technique he uses to carry out his task.

在执行任务时，典型人物没有选择余地：医生向家属传达噩耗，律师解释遗嘱条款，乞丐乞讨。无论老套还是新颖，典型人物最大的优势在于其目的显而易见，无需过多解释。读者/观众一眼就能明白某个典型人物为何出现在故事中，以及他在故事中扮演的角色。然而，典型人物并非一定要枯燥乏味。如果赋予他们独一无二的性格特征，以及他们完成任务的独特技巧，他们也能在故事中大放异彩。

Stock roles go in and out of fashion. Prosperity preachers replace hippie gurus; Russian spies exit, Middle East terrorists enter; man-made monsters are out, people with genetic mutations are in; space aliens are passé, zombie hordes are hip.

老套的角色类型总是不断更迭。成功神学布道者取代了嬉皮士导师；俄罗斯间谍退出舞台，中东恐怖分子取而代之；人造怪物不再流行，基因突变者风靡一时；外星人过时了，僵尸大军又成了潮流。

Because stocks must act within their job and types within their type, they make very few, if any, choices. For that reason, they constantly risk becoming clichés. A cliché is a once-superb idea that’s been copied to death and is now done without originality.

因为股票必须在其职责范围内运作，类型必须在其类型范围内运作，所以它们很少做出选择，甚至根本不做选择。正因如此，它们时刻面临着沦为陈词滥调的风险。陈词滥调指的是曾经绝妙的想法，经过无数次的模仿，如今已毫无新意可言。

As Henry James pointed out, clichéd characters are used but never used up. Are the old miser, young spendthrift, penny pincher, gambler, drunk, and teetotaler never to appear again because they’ve been done before? Of course not. In the hands of an imaginative writer, a stock can be wonderfully idiosyncratic. Arnold Schwarzenegger’s assassin in The Terminator is a menacing villain, type and stock, but the melding of machine/human gave him a characterization like no other.

正如亨利·詹姆斯所指出的，陈词滥调的角色虽然被使用过，但却永远不会被用尽。难道老吝啬鬼、挥霍无度的年轻人、守财奴、赌徒、酒鬼和禁酒主义者就因为这些角色已经被用烂了，就永远不会再出现了吗？当然不是。在富有想象力的作家笔下，一个老套的角色也能变得独具特色。阿诺·施瓦辛格在《终结者》中饰演的杀手是一个令人胆寒的反派，虽然类型老套，但机器与人类的融合赋予了他独一无二的角色魅力。

In fact, over recent decades, the origin stories of superheroes make them seem more and more like super-stocks doing their job. Archetypal twentieth-century creations, such as Thor, a Norse god; Wonder Woman, a Greek goddess; and the godlike Superman are born super; while twenty-first-century heroes turn super by accident (a radioactive bug bites Silk, a random mutagen infects Ms. Marvel) or by scientists doing it themselves (Iron Man builds his own supersuit). Galaxy Quest satirizes this trend when stock actors become archetypes for stock aliens.

事实上，近几十年来，超级英雄的起源故事越来越像现成的超级演员在执行任务。二十世纪的典型超级英雄，例如北欧神祇雷神托尔、希腊女神神奇女侠以及神一般的超人，都是天生拥有超能力；而二十一世纪的英雄则要么是意外获得超能力（例如，丝绸被放射性昆虫叮咬，惊奇女士被随机突变体感染），要么是科学家自行改造（例如，钢铁侠打造了自己的超级战衣）。《银河追击令》讽刺了这种趋势，片中演员沦为千篇一律的外星人形象的原型。

#↩

Principle: Stereotypes turn prejudice into character

原则：刻板印象将偏见转化为性格

Stereotyping begins with a fallacy: “All Xs are Y.” The wealthy, for example, often stereotype the poor as lazy; the poor stereotype the too-rich as cruel. Prejudices, for that reason, are worse than clichés. A cliché is a very good idea someone had a very long time ago. Since then, writers have drummed this invention into a cliché, but still it holds a truth. Stereotypes, instead, distort the truth.

刻板印象始于一个谬误：“所有X都是Y”。例如，富人常常认为穷人懒惰；穷人则认为过于富有的人残忍。因此，偏见比陈词滥调更糟糕。陈词滥调是某人很久以前就有的一个非常好的想法。自那时起，作家们不断重复使用，最终将其变成陈词滥调，但它仍然包含着某种真理。而刻板印象则扭曲了真相。

A stereotype models itself after an archetype but reduces grandeur to bias: The Earth Mother becomes the Jewish mother, the Wise King becomes the mean boss, the Warrior Hero becomes the street hustler, the Goddess becomes the hooker, the Magician becomes the mad scientist.

刻板印象模仿原型，但将宏伟简化为偏见：大地母亲变成了犹太母亲，睿智的国王变成了刻薄的老板，英勇的战士变成了街头骗子，女神变成了妓女，魔法师变成了疯狂的科学家。

So why do stereotypes persist? Because they’re easy to write. Realistic characters demand work from the writer, reader, and audience.

那么，为什么刻板印象会一直存在呢？因为它们很容易塑造。而塑造真实的人物则需要作者、读者和观众付出努力。

#↩

REALISTIC VERSUS SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS

写实型人物与象征型人物

Realism and Symbolism create characters at opposite ends of the cast spectrum—one rooted in fact, the other in abstraction. In between these two extremes run the mixtures and mergers of qualities that make possible every character ever imagined. So, let’s separate these two poles to see what they are and how they influence character creation.

现实主义和象征主义塑造的角色处于人物塑造光谱的两端——一个根植于事实，另一个则抽象化。在这两个极端之间，各种特质相互融合，构成了所有人类想象中的角色。那么，让我们来区分这两个极端，看看它们究竟是什么，以及它们如何影响角色塑造。

The Symbolist tradition began in prehistoric myths. Mankind’s earliest storytelling symbolized the forces of nature (sun, moon, lightning, thunder, seas, mountains) into gods, demigods, and other supernatural beings. In these myths, gods create the cosmos and, with it, human beings. Paraphrased from epoch to epoch, culture to culture, myths travel mouth to ear with slight loss of meaning because they are not literature. In myths, words mean little, symbolic characters and actions everything.

象征主义传统起源于史前神话。人类最早的叙事方式将自然之力（太阳、月亮、闪电、雷霆、海洋、山脉）象征化为神祇、半神和其他超自然生物。在这些神话中，神祇创造了宇宙，并由此创造了人类。神话从一个时代、一种文化流传到另一个时代、另一种文化，口耳相传，意义虽略有损失，但它们并非文学作品。在神话中，文字意义不大，象征性的人物和行为才是一切。

The Realist tradition dates back to Homer’s vivid depictions of warrior psychology and blood-spattered battles in the Iliad . Realism seeks to portray life as lived, unclouded by false beliefs or sentimental beautifications. Its straightforward dramatizations avoid symbolic dream fiction to emphasize hard-edged thought fiction—characters living in the as-is rather than the as-wished-for.

现实主义传统可以追溯到荷马史诗《伊利亚特》中对战士心理和血腥战斗的生动描绘。现实主义力求展现真实的生活，不被虚假的信念或感伤的美化所蒙蔽。它直白的戏剧化手法避免了象征性的梦幻虚构，强调冷峻的思想虚构——人物生活在现实之中，而非理想之中。

The key differences between realistic and symbolic characters number at least ten:

现实主义人物和象征主义人物之间的主要区别至少有十点：

#↩

1. Truth: Factuality Versus Wish Fulfillment

1. 真相：事实与愿望的满足

Realism grapples with a factual world in which wishes almost never come true; whereas the symbolic genres of speculative fiction—myths and fantasies, both ancient and modern—put wish fulfillment into action. The heroes and superheroes of today, with or without magical powers, live in a strictly moral universe where Good always triumphs over Evil, love conquers all, and death does not end life.

现实主义探讨的是一个愿望几乎无法实现的现实世界；而思辨小说——无论是古代还是现代的神话和奇幻故事——则将愿望的实现付诸行动。当今的英雄和超级英雄，无论是否拥有魔法，都生活在一个道德至上的宇宙中，在这个世界里，善永远战胜恶，爱能征服一切，死亡并不能终结生命。

Other symbolic genres, such as fables and legends, treat wishes as dark and dangerous, so they tell cautionary tales that teach moral lessons. “The Fox and the Grapes” by Aesop, “Hansel and Gretel” by the Brothers Grimm, and the legend of the House of Atreus are three classic examples. Modern fables warn of a dystopian future: George Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four , Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale , Naomi Alderman’s The Power .

其他象征性体裁，例如寓言和传说，将愿望视为黑暗而危险的，因此它们讲述警世故事，以传达道德教训。伊索寓言的《狐狸与葡萄》、格林兄弟的《汉塞尔与格蕾特》以及阿特柔斯家族的传说都是三个经典的例子。现代寓言则警示着反乌托邦的未来：乔治·奥威尔的《一九八四》、玛格丽特·阿特伍德的《使女的故事》以及娜奥米·奥尔德曼的《权力》。

#↩

2. True Character: Complex Psychology Versus Imposing Personality

2. 真实性格：复杂的心理与强势的人格

Symbolic tellings incite conflicts between characters rather than contradictions within characters. As a result, symbolic characters have remarkable, imposing personalities, while realistic characters develop complex psychologies. Compare Batman (aka Bruce Wayne) to Saul Goodman (aka Jimmy McGill).

象征性叙事手法引发的是人物之间的冲突，而非人物内部的矛盾。因此，象征性人物往往拥有鲜明、令人敬畏的个性，而现实主义人物则发展出复杂的心理。例如，可以对比一下蝙蝠侠（又名布鲁斯·韦恩）和索尔·古德曼（又名吉米·麦吉尔）。

#↩

3. Level of Conflict: Outer Versus Inner

3. 冲突层次：外部冲突与内部冲突

Symbolic characters take action against external antagonistic social and physical forces, while realistic characters often battle self-doubt, self-deception, self-criticism, and other such inner confusions and invisible demons.

象征性人物会采取行动对抗外部的敌对社会和物理力量，而现实主义人物则经常与自我怀疑、自我欺骗、自我批评以及其他类似的内心困惑和看不见的恶魔作斗争。

#↩

4. Complexity: Solid Versus Dimensional

4. 复杂性：实体与立体

Like the archetypes that inspire them, modern mythical characters have traits but no dimensions, desires but no contradictions, a text but no subtext. They are one-piece symbols, inside and out.

如同启发他们的原型一样，现代神话人物拥有特征却缺乏维度，拥有欲望却不自相矛盾，拥有文本却不包含潜台词。他们是浑然一体的符号，由内而外。

Multidimensional realistic characters, on the other hand, string dynamic contradictions between their public, personal, private, and hidden selves.

另一方面，多维现实主义人物则在其公共自我、私人自我、隐秘自我和隐藏自我之间构成动态矛盾。

#↩

5. Detail: Scarcity Versus Density

5. 细节：稀缺性与密度

The Symbolist writer of fables, legends, and myths focuses on the essential. He simplifies the density of reality by avoiding meticulous traits of characterization.

象征主义作家创作寓言、传说和神话时，注重本质。他通过避免细致入微的人物刻画，简化了复杂繁复的现实。

The Realist author, on the other hand, gathers telling details that enrich and specify his characters. Compare, for example, the smooth outlines of the animated family in The Incredibles with the painstakingly particularized family in Six Feet Under .

另一方面，现实主义作家则注重收集能够丰富和刻画人物的细节。例如，比较一下动画电影《超人总动员》中人物轮廓的流畅线条和《六尺之下》中人物形象的细致刻画。

#↩

6. Comprehension: Hard Versus Easy

6. 理解力：难易程度

Realism calls for concentration and perception. A character seems real in proportion to how much we consider his total self. The more contradictory yet consistent, the more changeable yet unified, the more unpredictable yet credible, the more specific yet mysterious the role, the more real, fascinating, and intriguing he becomes. He makes us work to understand him but rewards us with insight once we do. Consider Vicomte de Valmont ( Dangerous Liaisons ), Thomas Sutpen ( Absalom, Absalom! ), and Jimmy McGill ( Better Call Saul ).

现实主义需要专注和敏锐的洞察力。一个角色的真实感取决于我们对他整体形象的理解程度。角色越是矛盾却又自洽，越是变化莫测却又浑然一体，越是难以预测却又合情合理，越是具体而又神秘莫测，他就越真实、越引人入胜、越令人着迷。他需要我们努力去理解，但一旦我们理解了他，他便会以深刻的洞察力回报我们。例如，《危险关系》中的瓦尔蒙子爵、《押沙龙，押沙龙！》中的托马斯·萨特彭，以及《风骚律师》中的吉米·麦吉尔。

The symbolic characters of myth, legend, and fable are instantly and easily understood. The more generalized, predictable, and text-bound the role, the less surprising, less intriguing, and less real he becomes. Consider Albus Dumbledore, Mad Max, and Superman.

神话、传说和寓言中的象征性人物形象往往易于理解。角色越是概括化、可预测化、受文本束缚，就越显得缺乏惊喜、缺乏吸引力，也越显得不真实。想想阿不思·邓布利多、疯狂的麦克斯和超人就知道了。

#↩

7. Worldview: Skeptical Versus Sentimental

7. 世界观：怀疑主义与感性主义

Realism encourages characters treated with tough-minded sentiment; Symbolism often sweetens its roles with sentimentality.

现实主义鼓励以冷峻的情感来刻画人物；象征主义则常常用感伤的情感来美化角色。

Sentiment is a feeling that flows when a creditable motivation compels a powerful action: a parent risking everything for a child, as in playwright Henrik Ibsen’s Ghosts and Alvin Sargent’s screenplay for Ordinary People .

情感是一种当正当的动机促使人们采取强有力的行动时所产生的感受：例如，父母为了孩子甘愿冒一切风险，就像剧作家亨利克·易卜生的《群鬼》和阿尔文·萨金特的电影剧本《普通人》中那样。

Sentimentality, however, manipulates emotion by using phony causes to trigger false effects. The forced happy ending, for example, is a device as antique as Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Little Mermaid” and as yesterday as Steven Spielberg’s War of the Worlds .

然而，感伤主义通过虚假的原因来操纵情感，从而引发虚假的结果。例如，强行安排一个皆大欢喜的结局，这种手法既可以追溯到安徒生的《小美人鱼》，也可以追溯到史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格的《世界大战》，可谓是老套过时了。

#↩

8. Endings: Irony Versus Simplicity

8. 结尾：反讽与简洁

The writers of Realism grapple with life’s constant duality: The steps you take to achieve something are exactly what’s necessary to make sure you never get it, while the steps you take to avoid something take you directly to it. Whether climaxing in grief or joy, Realism turns a double effect: Positive endings demand great sacrifice, while tragedies bring insight and wisdom. Reality is relentlessly ironic and characters suffer accordingly.

现实主义作家们探讨着人生永恒的二元性：你为达成目标所采取的步骤，恰恰是确保你永远无法达成目标的必要条件；而你为避免某些事物所采取的步骤，却反而会将你引向它。无论结局是悲欢离合，现实主义都呈现出双重效应：美好的结局需要巨大的牺牲，而悲剧则带来深刻的洞察和智慧。现实本身就充满无情的讽刺，而人物也因此饱受苦难。

With the exception of authors like Philip K. Dick, myth, fable, and legend resist irony; they cast characters who act out straight, pure, and positive stories.

除了像菲利普·K·迪克这样的作家之外，神话、寓言和传说都排斥讽刺；它们塑造的角色演绎的是直白、纯粹和积极的故事。

#↩

9. Character Dynamics: Flexible Versus Rigid

9. 角色动态：灵活与僵硬

Realism reveals the truths hidden in its characters and then often flexes their inner natures with change. Symbolic roles possess one rigid quality through and through, and therefore have nothing to reveal or change.

现实主义揭示人物内心深处的真相，并常常通过变化来展现他们内在的性格。象征性角色则从头到尾都具有一种僵化的特质，因此没有什么可以揭示或改变的。

Realism is skeptical; myths wishful. Test myths against reality, and their archetypes are exposed for the wish fulfillments they always were.

现实主义是怀疑的；神话是美好的愿望。用现实检验神话，就会发现它们的原型不过是愿望的满足。

In the early twentieth century, psychologist Carl Jung based theories about the collective unconscious on archetypes drawn from myths. Expanding on Jung, Joseph Campbell concocted a monomyth popularly known as “the hero’s journey,” hoping to replace Christianity with his personal brand of spiritualism. Hollywood actionsmiths hammered Campbell’s pseudomyth about the hero’s quest into a template to mass-produce summer hits. 5

二十世纪初，心理学家卡尔·荣格基于神话中的原型，提出了关于集体无意识的理论。约瑟夫·坎贝尔在荣格的基础上，炮制了一个被称为“英雄之旅”的单一神话，希望用他个人的灵性主义取代基督教。好莱坞动作片导演们将坎贝尔关于英雄之旅的伪神话打造成一个模板，用来批量生产暑期档大片。

#↩

10. Social Dynamics: Flexible Versus Rigid

10. 社会动态：灵活与僵化

The class structure in Symbolist genres tends to cast a ruler at the top, peasants at the bottom, the rest somewhere in between. Realism moves power through its cast with fluidity, even if the telling is set in a monarchy or dictatorship.

象征主义流派的阶级结构往往将统治者置于顶端，农民处于底层，其余人则介于两者之间。而现实主义则以一种流畅的方式在人物之间传递权力，即便故事背景设定在君主制或独裁政体中。

#↩

CASE STUDY: GAME OF THRONES

案例研究：《权力的游戏》

David Benioff and D. B. Weiss, adapting George R. R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire to the longform screen, brought harsh realism to high fantasy. Between the black-and-white outlines of Symbolism, they drew characters in every possible shade of gray. They merged the autocracy of myth with the freedom of fiction to create a vast cast of 160 roles, representing all degrees of Realism and Symbolism plus all possible points on the political compass.

大卫·贝尼奥夫和D·B·魏斯将乔治·R·R·马丁的《冰与火之歌》改编成电影长篇作品，为奇幻世界注入了冷峻的现实主义。在象征主义黑白分明的框架下，他们塑造了形形色色的人物，展现了人物复杂的人性。他们将神话的专制与虚构的自由融合，创造出160个角色，涵盖了现实主义和象征主义的各个层面，以及政治光谱上的所有可能立场。

On the extreme Right, the tyrannical Cersei of House Lannister, Protector of the Seven Kingdoms. On the progressive Left, the graceful Daenerys of House Targaryen, Mother of Dragons.

极右翼是兰尼斯特家族的暴君瑟曦，七大王国的守护者。进步左翼是坦格利安家族优雅的丹妮莉丝，龙之母。

Cersei embodies retrogressive, incestuous, matriarch, monarchical despotism. Temperamentally, she is pro-feudalism and anti-change. Daenerys embodies the future-leaning, humanistic spirit of justice and progress. Temperamentally, she’s anti-feudalism and pro-change. Daenerys denies myth; Cersei lives myth.

瑟曦体现了倒退、乱伦、母系氏族式的君主专制。从性格上看，她拥护封建制度，反对变革。丹妮莉丝则体现了面向未来、充满人道主义精神的正义与进步。从性格上看，她反对封建制度，支持变革。丹妮莉丝否定神话；瑟曦则活在神话之中。

Within this polarized world, the writers array the meritocracy of the Night’s Watch, the equalitarianism of the Unsullied, the fanaticism of the Sparrows, and the democracy of councils in which equals cast votes to make decisions. Death, however, has no politics, so when the Night King and his horde of White Walkers invade, the tension between Symbolism and Realism fades into the question of who lives and who dies.

在这个两极分化的世界里，作者们描绘了守夜人的精英统治、无垢者的平等主义、麻雀的狂热，以及由平等成员投票决策的议会民主制。然而，死亡不分政治，因此当夜王和他的异鬼大军入侵时，象征主义与现实主义之间的张力最终消融于生死存亡的抉择。

#↩

HOW TO MAKE THE OLD NEW

如何让旧物焕发新生

You hope to invent characters unlike any ever seen, but for thousands of years, storytellers have created, re-created, and recycled characters by the millions… literally. You write in this tradition, and therefore your character’s core identity will echo an archetype, an allegory, a type, or a stock. Your task is to create within the known (otherwise no one will know how to respond to your work) and yet make your characters unique, fresh, and unlike any ever met before. Try one of these four paths:

你渴望创造出前所未见的全新角色，但数千年来，说书人已经创作、重塑、再创作了数以百万计的角色……毫不夸张。你的写作也遵循着这一传统，因此，你笔下角色的核心特质必然会与某种原型、寓言、类型或既定模式有所关联。你的任务是在已知框架内进行创作（否则读者将不知如何欣赏你的作品），同时又要让你的角色独一无二、耳目一新，与以往任何角色都截然不同。不妨尝试以下四种方法：

1. Within the genres of Speculative Fiction, create plausible motivations for implausible actions.
1. 在科幻小说这一类型中，为不合情理的行为创造合理的动机。
2. Within the genres of Realism, create characters who live off-center lives and see people and actions in an off-center way.
2. 在现实主义的范畴内，创造过着非中心生活、以非中心视角看待人和事的角色。
3. In either subset, give characters radical experiences that shock old beliefs into the new.
3. 在任一子集中，让角色经历颠覆性的体验，使旧观念发生巨大变化，从而形成新的观念。
4. In either subset, add a sense of immediacy by writing in-character. In prose, write from the POV of a character who has lived these events in the past. On-screen or onstage, take the POV of a character living them in the now.
4. 无论采用哪种方式，都要通过角色视角来增强身临其境之感。散文写作时，要以过去经历过这些事件的角色的视角来叙述；影视作品或舞台剧则要以正在经历这些事件的角色的视角来叙述。
#↩

13

THE RADICAL CHARACTER

激进的性格

The Realism/Nonrealism/Radicalism Triangle

现实主义/非现实主义/激进主义三角

Fiction’s conflicting treatments of reality create a triangle of character possibilities: In one corner, Realism gives characters the powers they have in ordinary life; in a second corner, Nonrealism gives them powers far beyond the ordinary; at the third corner, Radicalism warps the powers found in the other two. All three extremes meet and overlap within this triangle, creating an infinite variety of characters.

小说对现实的不同处理方式，构成了一个人物可能性的三角：在三角的一端，现实主义赋予人物他们在日常生活中拥有的能力；在另一端，非现实主义赋予他们远超常人的能力；在另一端，激进主义扭曲了前两者所赋予的能力。这三个极端在这个三角中交汇重叠，创造出无穷无尽的人物类型。

#↩

REALISM: CONVENTIONAL CHARACTERS IN CONVENTIONAL WORLDS

现实主义：传统世界中的传统人物

The literary movement known as Realism began two centuries ago in reaction to the operatic excesses of Romanticism. Realism works from the ground up, but in truth, its style of offhanded underplay is as artificial as the high-style overplay it replaced.

现实主义文学运动兴起于两个世纪前，是对浪漫主义过度渲染的反动。现实主义自下而上地进行创作，但实际上，它那种漫不经心的含蓄风格，与它所取代的那种矫揉造作的华丽辞藻一样，都带有刻意雕琢的成分。

Realist writers gather close observations of people and behavior, stir these inside the imagination, filter this concoction through the latticework of the mind, and finally crystallize it into a character who lives in a world that echoes ours. She has a unified self, moral balance, rational perceptions of reality, interactions with other characters, willful pursuits of desire, capacity to choose and act with purpose, and flexibility to change. This protagonist, surrounded by a cast of similar roles, acts out a story that by cultural conventions readers and audiences accept as everyday reality. You have seen and read these works all your life.

现实主义作家细致观察人物和行为，将这些观察融入想象，经过思维的层层筛选，最终塑造出一个生活在与我们世界遥相呼应的世界中的角色。她拥有完整的自我、道德的平衡、对现实的理性认知、与其他角色的互动、对欲望的执着追求、选择和行动的能力以及适应变化的能力。这位主人公，在众多类似角色的环绕下，演绎着一个故事，而这个故事，按照文化惯例，被读者和观众视为日常现实。你一生中已经看过、读过无数这样的作品。

#↩

NONREALISM: CONVENTIONAL CHARACTERS IN UNCONVENTIONAL WORLDS

非现实主义：非常规世界中的常规人物

Nonrealism places the conventional characters of Realism inside extrarealities powered by forces such as the supernatural in Pirates of the Caribbean ; the magical in Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone ; the coincidental in 1Q84 ; the metaphorical in Babe ; the paranormal in The Dead Zone ; the transnormal in Six Characters in Search of an Author ; an opaque bureaucracy in The Trial ; dream power in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland ; futuristic science in Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? ; time travel in Somewhere in Time ; time warps in Looper .

非现实主义将现实主义的传统角色置于超现实之中，这些超现实由以下力量驱动：例如《加勒比海盗》中的超自然力量；《哈利·波特与魔法石》中的魔法力量；《1Q84》中的巧合；《小猪宝贝》中的隐喻；《死亡地带》中的超自然力量；《六个寻找作者的剧中人》中的超常力量；《审判》中的不透明官僚机构；《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的梦境力量；《仿生人会梦见电子羊吗？》中的未来科学；《似曾相识》中的时间旅行；《环形使者》中的时间扭曲。

Some of these extended realities are populated by characters who sing ( La Traviata ), dance ( The Sleeping Beauty ), or sing and dance ( The Book of Mormon ). Nonrealism often eliminates the “fourth wall” to let characters talk to theatre audiences ( Hair ), film audiences ( Wayne’s World ), or television audiences ( Fleabag ).

有些扩展现实作品中的角色会唱歌（《茶花女》）、跳舞（《睡美人》），或者边唱边跳（《摩门经》）。非现实主义作品常常打破“第四堵墙”，让角色直接与剧院观众（《毛发》）、电影观众（《韦恩的世界》）或电视观众（《伦敦生活》）对话。

Nonrealism grows out of either conscious fantasies during the day or subconscious dreams at night. Once these imaginary settings and casts inspire a story, they play as grand metaphors for idealized worlds, expressing humanity’s wish fulfillments.

非现实主义源于白天的意识幻想或夜晚的潜意识梦境。一旦这些虚构的场景和人物激发了故事的创作灵感，它们便成为理想世界的宏大隐喻，表达了人类的愿望和渴望。

The fictional worlds of Realism and Nonrealism vary extremely, but nonetheless, they share two things in common: (1) No matter how bizarre or real a setting may seem, once folded into a fiction, it develops rules of causality, of how and why things happen, patterns that operate like the laws of physics to shape what can and cannot occur. (2) Characters who live in both real and unreal worlds believe in them. From the cast’s point of view, everything they see and hear seems as real as pain.

现实主义和非现实主义的虚构世界千差万别，但它们却有两个共同点：(1) 无论一个场景看起来多么怪诞或真实，一旦融入虚构世界，它就会发展出一套因果法则，解释事物发生的方式和原因，这些模式如同物理定律一般，塑造着事物可发生和不可发生之事。(2) 生活在现实世界和非现实世界中的角色都相信它们。从角色的角度来看，他们所见所闻的一切都如同痛苦般真实。

They may at first, like Phil Connors in Groundhog Day , doubt their world and test its laws, but in time a fictional reality becomes their reality and they behave in a more or less normal way. This is the nature of storytelling. The world of Homer’s Odyssey contains gods and monsters, but Odysseus deals with them as any hero would.

他们起初或许会像电影《土拨鼠日》里的菲尔·康纳斯一样，对这个世界产生怀疑，并质疑它的法则，但随着时间的推移，虚构的现实会逐渐成为他们的现实，他们的行为也会变得或多或少地正常化。这就是故事的本质。荷马史诗《奥德赛》中的世界里有神祇和怪物，但奥德修斯像任何英雄一样与它们对抗。

Conventional characters exist in social, cultural, and physical settings that are either Realism’s imitations of reality or Nonrealism’s imagined reinventions of reality. The behaviors and motivations of conventional characters demand credibility; the meanings of their stories are ultimately clear and expressed with emotional impact; their dialogue strives to be instantly understood; their tellings bring freshly observed details and insights into human nature.

传统人物存在于特定的社会、文化和物质环境中，这些环境要么是现实主义对现实的模仿，要么是非现实主义对现实的想象性重构。传统人物的行为和动机力求可信；他们故事的意义最终清晰明了，并带有强烈的情感冲击力；他们的对话力求瞬间易懂；他们的叙述展现了对人性的全新观察和深刻洞察。

The note to take here is that the fully expressed character built around a unified dimensionality is standard in both Realism and Nonrealism. These characters inhabit the hits and best sellers of page, stage, and screen.

这里需要注意的是，围绕统一维度构建的、形象饱满的角色是现实主义和非现实主义的共同特征。这些角色活跃于小说、舞台剧和电影等畅销作品中。

Therefore, think carefully about the tastes of your readers and audiences and which reality they want: Realism or Nonrealism. Because in all probability, they do not want Radicalism.

因此，请仔细考虑读者和受众的喜好，以及他们想要哪种现实：现实主义还是非现实主义。因为他们很可能并不想要激进主义。

#↩

RADICALISM: UNCONVENTIONAL CHARACTERS IN UNCONVENTIONAL WORLDS

激进主义：非常规世界中的非传统人物

The more a writer loses faith in meaning, the more she feels a pull toward Radicalism.

作家越是对意义失去信心，就越会感到被激进主义所吸引。

From the very first, philosophers assumed that life had meaning and that finding that meaning is mankind’s chief goal. This pursuit wound its way through the centuries, but then by the nineteenth century, Nietzsche, Kierkegaard, and other voices warned of a rising tide of meaninglessness. This trend deepened as psychoanalysis, led by Freud, Jung, and Adler, discovered disunities within the self and the near impossibility of knowing your true identity, let alone finding a meaning to guide it. Two world wars and a dozen genocides later, nihilism found its voice in postmodern works of theatre, cinema, and prose of the absurd that revolutionized storytelling and character.

从一开始，哲学家们就假定生命具有意义，而寻找意义是人类的首要目标。这种追求贯穿了数个世纪，但到了十九世纪，尼采、克尔凯郭尔等人开始警告人们，无意义的浪潮正在兴起。随着以弗洛伊德、荣格和阿德勒为代表的精神分析学的出现，这种趋势愈演愈烈。精神分析学发现了自我内部的矛盾，以及几乎不可能了解自身真实身份，更遑论找到指引人生的意义。两次世界大战和十余起种族灭绝之后，虚无主义在后现代戏剧、电影和荒诞散文作品中找到了表达的途径，这些作品彻底革新了叙事和人物塑造的方式。

Radicalism finds both the outer and inner life meaningless, so it reverses everything: instead of continuity, fragmentation; instead of clarity, distortion; instead of emotional immersion, intellectual exertion; instead of involvement, distance; instead of progression, repetition.

激进主义认为外在生活和内在生活都毫无意义，所以它颠倒一切：用分裂代替连续性；用扭曲代替清晰；用理性努力代替情感投入；用疏离代替参与；用重复代替进步。

Unconventionality is Radicalism’s convention. Whatever’s orthodox, the Radicalist does the opposite, but, ironically, that doesn’t set her free. As Martin Heidegger pointed out: “Opposition is invariably comprised of a decisive, and often even perilous, dependence.” 1

非传统性是激进主义的惯例。无论正统观念如何，激进主义者都反其道而行之，但讽刺的是，这并不能使她获得自由。正如马丁·海德格尔所指出的：“反对总是包含着一种决定性的、甚至是危险的依赖。”

Radicalism is to character what Cubism is to portraiture. The writer, as if painting a Picasso-esque portrait, exaggerates, shatters, shrinks, distorts, and rearranges selves, yet somehow the reader/audience still sees a character.

激进主义之于人物塑造，正如立体主义之于肖像画。作家仿佛在绘制毕加索式的肖像，夸张、破碎、缩小、扭曲、重组自我，然而读者/观众仍然能从中看到人物的轮廓。

Radical settings are highly symbolic, but their rules for causality are radically inconsistent. In Jean-Luc Godard’s film Weekend , anything can happen for no reason; in Samuel Beckett’s play Waiting for Godot , nothing happens, again, for no reason. These reimaginings, needless to say, demanded new and very radical characters.

激进的设定极具象征意义，但其因果关系规则却极度矛盾。在让-吕克·戈达尔的电影《周末》中，任何事情都可能毫无缘由地发生；而在塞缪尔·贝克特的戏剧《等待戈多》中，同样毫无缘由地什么也没发生。毋庸置疑，这些重构需要塑造全新且极具颠覆性的角色。

Radical characters have little relationship to anything beyond themselves—not god or society, not family or lovers. They are either isolated and static (Tom Stoppard’s play Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead ) or mobbed and frantic (Marlon James’s novel A Brief History of Seven Killings ). Their dialogue often degenerates into babble (David Lynch’s film Inland Empire ).

激进人物与自身之外的任何事物都鲜有联系——既不与上帝或社会联系，也不与家人或爱人联系。他们要么孤立而静止（如汤姆·斯托帕德的戏剧《罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿之死》），要么被人群包围而疯狂（如马龙·詹姆斯的小说《七杀简史》）。他们的对话常常沦为胡言乱语（如大卫·林奇的电影《内陆帝国》）。

The medium for expressing radical characters with relative ease is prose. The novelist, in first or third person, can reach into the mind of a character and emulate her splintered, skipping-stone thoughts, sketching out her wildly subjective, often paranoid anxieties and impressions, her instant impulses, fragmented desires, and fractured personality. This technique was foundational to everything Samuel Beckett wrote for page and stage.

散文是相对容易地展现激进人物形象的媒介。小说家可以采用第一人称或第三人称，深入人物的内心世界，模仿她支离破碎、如同跳石般跳跃的思绪，勾勒出她极度主观、时常带有偏执色彩的焦虑和印象，以及她瞬间的冲动、支离破碎的欲望和扭曲的个性。这种技巧是塞缪尔·贝克特所有文学和戏剧作品的基石。

In White Noise , novelist Don DeLillo created characters whose identities are not just in doubt, but absolutely uncertain. Thomas Pynchon’s Gravity’s Rainbow swirls four hundred characters around Tyrone Slothrop, who may or may not be anything that he, other characters, or even the author say he is.

在小说家唐·德里罗的《白噪音》中，他塑造的人物身份不仅令人怀疑，而且完全无法确定。托马斯·品钦的《万有引力之虹》则围绕着泰隆·斯洛思罗普展开了四百多个人物的故事，而泰隆的真实身份究竟如何，无论是他自己、其他人物，甚至是作者所说的，都无法确定。

For the playwright and screenwriter, expressing radical characters becomes a bit more difficult because the physical presence of an actor gives a role a sense of solidity.

对于剧作家和编剧来说，表达激进的角色变得更加困难，因为演员的肢体存在赋予了角色一种实体感。

In Happy Days , Samuel Beckett worked against the actor effect by burying his only two characters, Winnie and Willie, up to their necks in dirt and debris.

在《快乐的日子》中，塞缪尔·贝克特通过将他仅有的两个角色温妮和威利埋在泥土和瓦砾中，只露出脖子，来对抗演员效应。

In Holy Motors , Cinema of the Absurd filmmaker Leos Carax has his protagonist, Oscar, perform nine different impersonations, ranging from an old female beggar to a Chinese gangster to the husband and father of chimpanzees.

在荒诞派电影导演莱奥·卡拉克斯的《神圣车行》中，主人公奥斯卡扮演了九个不同的角色，从年老的女乞丐到中国黑帮分子，再到黑猩猩的丈夫和父亲。

#↩

CREATING A RADICAL CHARACTER

塑造一个激进的角色

To radicalize a character, simply empty out her conventional aspects. Below are nine possible deletions that lead characters toward the extreme:

要使一个角色走向极端，只需剥离她传统的性格特征即可。以下列举了九种可能导致角色走向极端的做法：

#↩

1. Subtract Self-Awareness

1. 减去自我意识

The self-aware dramatic character can step back from the struggle and think the thought, “You know, this could get me into real trouble,” and then, despite the threat, go on. But when you subtract self-awareness, dramatic characters turn into comic obsessives.

具有自知之明的戏剧性角色能够从困境中抽身而出，思考“你知道吗，这可能会给我带来真正的麻烦”，然后，尽管面临威胁，仍然继续前进。但一旦失去了这种自知之明，戏剧性角色就会变成滑稽的执迷者。

The comic mind is ruled by a blind obsession—single-minded as a stone, persistent as the sea, repetitious as rain. To create a farce, the comedy writer locks the character into her fixation, then exploits it at every opportunity:

喜剧演员的思维受一种盲目的执念支配——像石头一样执着，像大海一样持久，像雨一样反复无常。为了创作闹剧，喜剧作家将角色牢牢锁定在这种执念之中，然后抓住一切机会加以利用：

In A Fish Called Wanda , Archie Leach obsessively fears embarrassment, yet stumbles into one red-faced humiliation after another.

在《一条名叫旺达的鱼》中，阿奇·利奇极度害怕尴尬，却一次又一次地陷入尴尬的境地。

In the Pink Panther films, Inspector Clouseau obsesses on perfection as a detective, yet blunders through his investigations, one pratfall after another.

在《粉红豹》系列电影中，克鲁索探长痴迷于完美侦探工作，但他的调查却总是磕磕绊绊，屡屡出糗。

In Curb Your Enthusiasm , Larry David obsesses on proper social behavior, and yet finds himself surrounded with people who constantly break his petty rules.

在《抑制热情》中，拉里·大卫痴迷于恰当的社交行为，却发现自己身边的人总是违反他那些琐碎的规则。

In Bridesmaids , Annie Walker obsesses on her one and only friendship, and yet ruins the relationship at every turn.

在电影《伴娘》中，安妮·沃克对她唯一的友谊无比执着，却又处处破坏这段关系。

Conventional comic obsessives, like the above, have a commonsense interest or two that rounds out their natures. But not the radical character. Radicals push beyond obsession into the absurd limits of monomania. To radicalize a comic character, take away everything except her obsession, then trap her inside it and never let her out:

像上面提到的那些传统漫画狂热者，通常也会有一两个符合常理的兴趣爱好来完善他们的性格。但激进型人物则不然。激进型人物会超越痴迷，达到偏执狂的荒谬极限。要让一个漫画人物变得激进，就剥夺她除痴迷之外的一切，然后把她困在痴迷之中，永远不让她出来：

In The Maids , Jean Genet traps the maids in their sadomasochistic games.

在《女佣》中，让·热内让女佣们陷入了她们的虐恋游戏中。

In Exit the King , Eugene Ionesco traps Berenger in his fear of death.

在《国王之死》中，尤金·尤内斯库让贝朗热陷入了对死亡的恐惧之中。

In Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead , Tom Stoppard traps Rosencrantz and Guildenstern in Hamlet’s story.

在《罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿之死》中，汤姆·斯托帕德将罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿困在了哈姆雷特的故事中。

In A Behanding in Spokane , Martin McDonagh traps Carmichael in an endless search for his missing hand.

在《斯波坎的断手》中，马丁·麦克唐纳让卡迈克尔陷入了无休止地寻找他丢失的手的困境。

#↩

2. Subtract Depth

2. 减去深度

The opposite of a full, complex, and revealed character is a role that’s emptied out—a character whose humanity shrinks into an inner void, putting her just a step or two away from the radical.

与一个完整、复杂、鲜活的角色相反的是一个被掏空的角色——一个角色的人性萎缩成内心的空洞，使她离激进主义只有一两步之遥。

In Falling Down , Ebbe Roe Smith peels away William Foster’s (Michael Douglas) sanity.

在《坠落》中，埃贝·罗·史密斯逐渐瓦解了威廉·福斯特（迈克尔·道格拉斯饰）的理智。

In Capote , Dan Futterman extracts Truman Capote’s (Philip Seymour Hoffman) morality.

在《卡波特》中，丹·富特曼挖掘出了杜鲁门·卡波特（菲利普·西摩·霍夫曼饰）的道德观。

In The Imitation Game , Graham Moore amputates Alan Turing’s (Benedict Cumberbatch) core self.

在《模仿游戏》中，格雷厄姆·摩尔砍掉了艾伦·图灵（本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇饰）的核心自我。

Despair swallows the humanity of all three of these men, leading their lives to the brink of absurdity.

绝望吞噬了这三个人的人性，将他们的生活推向了荒诞的边缘。

#↩

3. Subtract Change

3. 减去找零

Complex, multidimensional protagonists undergo arcs of change; flat characters do not. Flat characters contract into themselves, eliminating their ties to other characters.

复杂、多维的主角会经历成长弧线；扁平的角色则不会。扁平的角色会封闭自我，切断与其他角色的联系。

In genres of Realism, flat characters are revealed but incapable of change—for example, Jude and Tess in Thomas Hardy’s novels Jude the Obscure and Tess of the d’Urbervilles . Their only change is a downward slide from hopeful to hopeless. 2

在现实主义文学中，扁平的人物形象被刻画出来，但却无法改变——例如托马斯·哈代的小说《无名的裘德》和《德伯家的苔丝》中的裘德和苔丝。他们唯一的改变就是从充满希望滑向绝望。

In genres of non-Realism, heroes and villains, with or without superpowers, are also flat. Characters in action-filled, speculative fictions change the world but never themselves. They personify Good or Evil and obey ancient storytelling traditions by staying either good or evil until they die.

在非现实主义题材中，无论是否拥有超能力，英雄和反派都显得扁平化。在充满动作场面的科幻小说中，人物能够改变世界，却无法改变自身。他们代表着善与恶，遵循着古老的叙事传统，直至死亡都保持着善恶的本质。

In both non-Realism and Realism, unchanged characters suggest that the possibility of change, no matter how remote, exists. If Hardy had allowed Jude to become the classical scholar of his dreams, Jude’s arc to fulfillment would be profound and moving. If Bruce Wayne got fed up with the public’s lack of respect for Batman and decided to use his skills to build an evil empire, the change would be shocking and yet fascinating. I would watch that sequel.

在非现实主义和现实主义作品中，人物性格的不变暗示着改变的可能性，无论多么渺茫。如果哈迪让裘德成为他梦寐以求的古典学者，那么裘德的成长历程将会深刻动人。如果布鲁斯·韦恩厌倦了公众对蝙蝠侠的漠视，决定利用自己的能力建立一个邪恶帝国，那么这种转变将会令人震惊，却又引人入胜。我会去看这样的续集。

So if flat characters in conventional genres change, their change surprises, yet seems credible and meaningful. On the other hand, if a radical character living in a radical world were to change from flat to complex, the switch would seem false.

因此，如果传统类型作品中的扁平人物发生变化，这种变化会令人惊讶，但又显得合情合理且意义深远。另一方面，如果一个生活在激进世界中的激进人物从扁平变得复杂，这种转变就会显得不自然。

In Waiting for Godot , two aimless characters, Vladimir and Estragon, sum up the flatness of their natures with the refrain: “Nothing to be done.” But if one were to turn to the other and say, “Enough waiting. I don’t think Godot will ever show up. Let’s go find jobs and make something of our lives,” and off they went, excited by the chance to change, Samuel Beckett’s existential masterpiece would collapse into silliness. 3

在《等待戈多》中，两个漫无目的的人物弗拉基米尔和爱斯特拉贡用一句反复出现的“无所事事”概括了他们性格的平淡。但如果其中一个转向另一个说：“别再等了。我觉得戈多永远不会出现。我们去找份工作，好好过日子吧。”然后他们就兴高采烈地出发了，渴望改变，那么塞缪尔·贝克特的这部存在主义杰作就会沦为荒诞之作。

In novelist Will Self’s trilogy of Umbrella , Shark, and Phone , flat characters fragment into five different points of view. Shards of thought express variations of dissociative identity disorder, drug-induced hallucination, and autism-spectrum discord. If the author unified these pieces into whole characters, they would corrupt his wild creation.

在小说家威尔·塞尔夫的《雨伞》、《鲨鱼》和《电话》三部曲中，扁平的人物形象分裂成五个不同的视角。这些碎片化的思维表达了分离性身份障碍、药物引起的幻觉以及自闭症谱系障碍的不同表现形式。如果作者将这些碎片整合为完整的人物，就会破坏他原本狂野的创作。

#↩

4. Subtract Identity

4. 减去单位元

Prior to the twentieth century, authors wove their characters’ identities from the cultural threads that encircled them: gender, class, family, age, religion, nationality, education, profession, language, race, taste in art, and the like. When a character said, “I am a—,” what followed were nouns drawn from her immediate world. This ancient practice continues today, reenforced by identity politics.

在二十世纪之前，作家们通过人物所处的文化环境来塑造他们的身份：性别、阶级、家庭、年龄、宗教、国籍、教育程度、职业、语言、种族、艺术品味等等。当一个人物说“我是一个——”时，后面跟着的往往是她所处环境中的名词。这种古老的做法延续至今，并被身份政治所强化。

The Modernist movement, however, reversed that pattern. It turned away from conflicts between characters to tell tales located in the inner life and the search for an ever-lasting private truth. Modernist characters turn their back on the world, hoping to find a core self waiting quietly within, surrounded by infinite freedom of thought and the beauty of creativity.

然而，现代主义运动却颠覆了这一模式。它摒弃了人物间的冲突，转而讲述内心世界的故事，以及对永恒私人真理的追寻。现代主义人物背离尘世，渴望在内心深处找到一个静静等待的自我，那里充满无限的思想自由和创造之美。

By the end of the century, however, postmodernists found that the inner life offers no such refuge. The outer and inner worlds are just two versions of hell. In Samuel Beckett’s novel The Unnamable , the protagonist declares that he’s “shut the door, at home to no one,” including himself. A character homeless within himself suffers derealization or depersonalization or both. Derealization is the sudden perception of the world as unreal; depersonalization is the sudden perception of yourself as unreal.

然而，到了世纪末，后现代主义者发现，内心世界并不能提供这样的避难所。外部世界和内心世界不过是两种不同的地狱。在塞缪尔·贝克特的《无名氏》中，主人公宣称他“关上了门，谁也进不去”，包括他自己。内心无家可归的人物会经历现实解体或人格解体，或两者兼有。现实解体是指突然感知到世界是不真实的；人格解体是指突然感知到自身是不真实的。

Derealization is the side effect of despair, often magnified by drugs and alcohol. Depersonalization is the side effect of physical and psychological trauma or extreme loneliness. A prisoner condemned to solitary confinement over time inevitably loses his identity. When finally taken out in a straitjacket, his first question (if he can still speak) is “Who am I?”

现实感丧失是绝望的副作用，毒品和酒精往往会加剧这种症状。人格解体是身心创伤或极度孤独的副作用。长期被单独监禁的囚犯不可避免地会丧失自我认同。当他最终被束缚衣带出来时，他的第一个问题（如果他还能说话的话）是“我是谁？”

Derealization strips a character of the power to empathize, to see the humanity in others; depersonalization severs self-empathy, a character’s power to feel her own humanity.

现实感丧失会剥夺角色的同理心，使其无法看到他人的人性；人格解体会切断角色的自我同理心，使其无法感受自己的人性。

How many different ways can a character lose self-empathy and with it, her identity? Here’s a brief list:

一个角色会以多少种不同的方式失去自我同理心，进而失去自我认同？以下列举几种：

(A) Loss of an Identity Source

（A）身份来源的丧失

A character draws both characterization and true character from her surrounding culture. If an outside power destroys the sources of her identity, she vanishes with them.

人物的性格特征和真实性格都源于其所处的文化环境。如果外力摧毁了她身份认同的根基，她也会随之消失。

In Wide Sargasso Sea by Jean Rhys, Antoinette Cosway, a Creole/Jamaican heiress, marries an Englishman. He takes her from her island home to his, then insults her race and poisons their marriage with adultery. Locked in an attic and stripped of all sense of self, she goes mad.

在让·里斯的小说《藻海无边》中，克里奥尔/牙买加混血女继承人安托瓦内特·科斯韦嫁给了一位英国人。他把她从家乡岛屿带到自己的岛屿，然后侮辱她的种族，并用婚外情毒害了他们的婚姻。她被锁在阁楼里，失去了所有自我意识，最终精神失常。

In Things Fall Apart by Chinua Achebe, a Nigerian tribal champion fights against English colonists and missionaries, but his tribe converts to Christianity and turns against him. Stripped of his ancestral identity, he commits suicide.

在钦努阿·阿切贝的《瓦解》中，一位尼日利亚部落勇士与英国殖民者和传教士作战，但他的部落皈依基督教后，转而与他为敌。失去祖先身份后，他选择了自杀。

(B) Rejection of an Identity Source

（B）拒绝身份来源

If a character hates her ancestry and so turns against her religion, ethnicity, gender, or any other personality-shaping influence, she alters, if not utterly erases, her identity.

如果一个角色憎恨自己的血统，从而反对自己的宗教、种族、性别或任何其他塑造其性格的因素，那么她就会改变自己的身份，甚至彻底抹杀自己的身份。

In Look Back in Anger by John Osborne, Jimmy Porter feels heroic energies pulsing through him, but now that the British Empire has collapsed, he realizes that his chance for an epic life is lost. He’s an ordinary working man who will never be part of a great enterprise, never live the courageous identity he craves.

在约翰·奥斯本的《愤怒的回顾》中，吉米·波特感到体内涌动着英雄气概，但随着大英帝国的瓦解，他意识到自己成就传奇人生的机会已经逝去。他只是一个普通的劳动者，永远无法参与伟大的事业，也永远无法活出他渴望的那种英勇无畏的人生。

In More Happy Than Not by Adam Silvera, teenager Aaron Soto hires a psycho-technology company to erase his gay identity. The company removes a few memories, but gayness isn’t a memory, it’s genetic.

在亚当·西尔维拉的《比快乐更快乐》中，少年亚伦·索托雇佣了一家心理科技公司来抹去他的同性恋身份。该公司确实删除了他的一些记忆，但同性恋并非记忆，而是基因决定的。

(C) Trauma

（C）创伤

Damage caused by ordeals or genetic abnormalities such as schizophrenia can shatter a character’s identity.

磨难或精神分裂症等遗传异常造成的伤害会摧毁一个人的身份认同。

In The Bourne Identity , Jason Bourne suffers traumatic amnesia and goes in search of his identity.

在《谍影重重》中，杰森·伯恩遭遇创伤性失忆症，踏上了寻找自己身份的旅程。

In The Three Faces of Eve and Alias Grace , doppelgängers and multiple personalities give the protagonist different identities, none of them hers.

在《夏娃的三张面孔》和《别名格蕾丝》中，分身和多重人格赋予了主人公不同的身份，但没有一个是她自己的。

In Blue Jasmine , Jasmine Francis revenges her husband’s adultery by betraying him to the FBI for embezzlement. Soon penniless, her identity crumples as she suffers a pathological, delusional breakdown.

在《蓝色茉莉》中，茉莉·弗朗西斯为了报复丈夫的婚外情，向联邦调查局举报他挪用公款。很快，她便一贫如洗，身份也随之崩溃，陷入病态的妄想之中。

(D) Identity Theft

（D）身份盗窃

An impostor slowly steals a character’s identity until no one believes that she is who she says she is.

一个冒名顶替者慢慢窃取一个角色的身份，直到没有人相信她就是她所声称的那个人。

In Single White Female , Hedy Carlson suffers a soulless, deep-seated emptiness. To find a fulfilling self, she imitates her roommate and then steals her identity.

在《单身白领女性》中，海蒂·卡尔森内心深处感到空虚寂寞。为了找到自我价值，她模仿室友，最终窃取了她的身份。

(E) Obsession

（E）痴迷

When fanatics obsess, they take actions that seem out of character. Shocked, they step back from what they’ve done and excuse it with “I wasn’t myself.” In fact, their choice under pressure revealed exactly who they are.

当狂热分子陷入某种狂热状态时，他们会做出看似反常的行为。事后，他们会感到震惊，并为自己的行为辩解说“我当时神志不清”。事实上，他们在压力下做出的选择恰恰暴露了他们的真面目。

In Lust, Caution , the Japanese army occupies Shanghai in 1942. As part of an assassination plot, a beautiful young rebel seduces the head of the secret police, but their passion becomes her sexual obsession. When given a chance to kill, she suddenly shocks herself by choosing not to end his life but to save it.

在《色，戒》中，1942年日军占领上海。一位年轻貌美的叛逆少女参与了一项刺杀计划，她勾引了秘密警察头目，但两人之间的激情却演变成了她难以自拔的性欲。当她有机会杀人时，她却出人意料地选择不结束他的生命，而是救了他。

#↩

5. Subtract Purpose

5. 减去目的

Many radical characters turn their backs on the world. They flee the turmoil of relationships by withdrawing into the mental life, thinking that there they will enjoy freedom, creativity, and quiet self-awareness. Instead, their mediations meander pointlessly; they find creativity pretentious and self-knowledge painful. When involuntary memories pop up from the past, they either deny their truth or draw a blank. Stuck between the inner and outer life, they try to flee both and live in neither. When radical characters crave company, it’s to escape their acute anxieties about modern afflictions, existential minutiae, and meaningless inner boredom. They are purposeless.

许多激进分子背弃世界。他们逃避人际关系的纷扰，遁入精神世界，以为在那里就能享受自由、创造力和宁静的自我觉察。然而，他们的冥想却漫无目的；他们觉得创造力矫揉造作，自我认知痛苦不堪。当过往的记忆不由自主地涌现时，他们要么否认其真实性，要么茫然不知所措。他们困于内心世界与外部世界之间，试图逃离两者，最终却两边都无法真正融入。当激进分子渴望陪伴时，那只是为了逃避他们对现代社会种种弊病、存在主义琐事以及内心空虚无聊的强烈焦虑。他们漫无目的。

In Beckett’s Krapp’s Last Tape , Krapp’s doctor has warned him that bananas are bad for his health. So Krapp peels a banana, sticks it in his mouth, then stands for minutes on end, staring into space, unable or willing to bite down, a banana protruding from his face. 4

在贝克特的《克拉普的最后录音带》中，克拉普的医生警告他香蕉对健康有害。于是克拉普剥开一根香蕉，塞进嘴里，然后站着一连几分钟，目光呆滞地望着前方，既不肯也不打算咬下去，一根香蕉就那样从他的脸上伸出来。

Radical characters are purposeless and thus trapped: trapped in an incomplete play ( Six Characters in Search of an Author ), in mindless repetition ( The Chairs ), in maniacal politics ( The Arsonists ), by an unknown menace ( The Birthday Party ), in conformity ( Rhinoceros ), by death ( Exit the King ), in Shakespeare’s play ( Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead ), in bureaucracy ( The Trial ), in a police state ( Pillowman ), in mundanity ( The Flick ), in the Amazon jungle ( The Encounter ), in a neighbor’s backyard ( Escaped Alone ). Like an improv actor on Whose Line Is It Anyway? , these characters are stuck onstage and cannot escape their playwright’s premise.

激进的角色漫无目的，因此也身陷囹圄：困于未完成的剧本（《六个寻找作者的剧中人》），困于无意义的重复（《椅子》），困于疯狂的政治（《纵火犯》），困于未知的威胁（《生日派对》），困于墨守成规（《犀牛》），困于死亡（《国王之死》），困于莎士比亚的戏剧（《罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿之死》），困于官僚主义（《审判》），困于警察国家（《枕头人》），困于平庸（《电影》），困于亚马逊丛林（《邂逅》），困于邻居的后院（《独自逃脱》）。如同《即兴喜剧秀》中的演员，这些角色被困在舞台上，无法逃脱剧作家设定的前提。

For many twenty-first-century writers, political absurdity has blurred their sense of purpose. Gridlock inside an artist often paralyzes the creatures she creates—static characters who feel that nothing redeems life—not love, not art, not knowledge, not God, and certainly not sex. Thus, the perfect metaphor for today’s loss of purpose is the zombie. Like zombies, radical characters long to live no life at all. Were it possible, they would inhabit a zombie zone of nothing.

对许多二十一世纪的作家而言，政治的荒谬模糊了他们的人生意义。艺术家内心的僵局常常使她笔下的人物陷入停滞——这些静止的人物感到生命毫无救赎——爱情、艺术、知识、上帝，当然还有性，都无济于事。因此，僵尸是当今人们失去人生意义的最佳隐喻。如同僵尸一般，激进的人物渴望彻底放弃生命。如果可能，他们会栖身于一片虚无的僵尸地带。

#↩

6. Subtract Unity

6. 减去单位元

A complex character is one person who acts in two directions: She loves and hates, tells truth and lies. These cohesive contradictions unify her, whereas the unstable shards of a radical role fragment the character.

复杂型人物是指一个人同时展现出两种截然不同的性格：她既爱又恨，既说真话又说谎。这些内在的矛盾使她浑然一体，而极端角色的不稳定碎片则会使人物支离破碎。

In today’s participatory theatre, for example, when a cast interacts with its audience, their roles splinter into character and performer: Brute Force , Sleep No More , 66 Minutes in Damascus .

例如，在当今的参与式戏剧中，当演员与观众互动时，他们的角色会分裂成角色和表演者：例如《蛮力》、《不眠之夜》、《大马士革66分钟》。

In Isabel Waidner’s novel Gaudy Bauble , objects become characters and then compound themselves: A face printed on a sweatshirt multiplies into an army of transsexuals.

在伊莎贝尔·韦德纳的小说《华丽的小玩意》中，物品变成了角色，然后又自我复合：印在运动衫上的脸变成了变性人的大军。

#↩

7. Subtract Maturity

7. 减去到期日

The daily task of the mature mind is to mediate between the world around her and the instincts inside her, balancing these two hostile powers and negotiating an inner peace. 5

成熟心灵的日常任务是调和周遭世界与内心本能之间的冲突，平衡这两种相互对立的力量，并最终达成内心的平静。

The radical character is an eternal child who surrenders to the world (obedience) or to her impulses (violence) or to both at once (the violent savage who obeys orders).

激进的性格是一个永远的孩子，他要么屈服于世界（服从），要么屈服于自己的冲动（暴力），或者两者兼而有之（服从命令的暴力野蛮人）。

In Haruki Murakami’s The Wind-up Bird Chronicle , when Toru, the novel’s childlike protagonist, isn’t searching for his cat, or his wife, he’s ruminating at the bottom of a well.

在村上春树的《发条鸟年代记》中，小说中孩子气的主人公透，除了寻找他的猫或妻子之外，就是在井底沉思。

The risqué send-ups staged by Madison, Wisconsin’s Broom Street Theater, such as Oklahomo! and The Ballerina and the Economist , show little interest in maturity.

威斯康星州麦迪逊市的布鲁姆街剧院上演的那些带有挑逗意味的讽刺剧，如《俄克拉荷马！》和《芭蕾舞女与经济学家》，对成熟主题几乎没有兴趣。

The same is true of screenplays by Broom Street alumnus Charlie Kaufman. Human Nature , for example, features a psychologist who teaches table manners to mice.

布鲁姆街编剧团校友查理·考夫曼的剧本也是如此。例如，《人性》讲述了一位心理学家教老鼠餐桌礼仪的故事。

#↩

8. Subtract Conscience

8. 减去良心

An evil character commits unregretted acts of brutality because she has no conscience to restrain her. Characters of conscienceless evil motivate power struggles in a wide variety of genres such as Crime, War, and Action/Adventure, as well as Political and Family Dramas. When stakes are high, people know how to vacate their conscience. It’s commonplace.

邪恶角色之所以能犯下毫无悔意的暴行，是因为她没有良知约束自己。这种丧尽天良的邪恶角色在犯罪、战争、动作/冒险、政治剧和家庭剧等多种类型作品中都扮演着推动权力斗争的角色。当利害攸关时，人们往往懂得如何抛弃良知。这已是司空见惯。

Radical evil takes brutality to another level: As the Marquis de Sade explains in Philosophy in the Bedroom : “Through cruelty one rises to heights of superhuman awareness and sensitivity to new modes of being that cannot be reached any other way.”

极端邪恶将残暴提升到了另一个层次：正如萨德侯爵在《卧室哲学》中所解释的那样：“通过残暴，人们可以达到超人的意识和对新的存在方式的敏感度的高度，而这是其他任何方式都无法达到的。”

The core psychology of radical evil is Sadism: the belief that the common objectives of torture (information and confession) distract from the unutterable pleasure and transcendent purity of the torturer’s experience. Radical evil seeks grotesque pleasure.

极端邪恶的核心心理是虐待狂：他们认为酷刑的常见目的（获取信息和供词）会分散施虐者对难以言喻的快感和超凡脱俗的纯粹体验的注意力。极端邪恶追求的是怪诞的快感。

Acts of radical evil nauseate into disgust. Disgust is a gut reaction to rot, to foul-tasting, foul-smelling feces, gore, pulp, puke. Physical disgust reacts against these rank animal spillages to protect the body from poisons; social disgust reacts against moral rot to protect the soul from evil. Profoundly evil characters turn your stomach… literally.

极端邪恶的行为令人作呕，甚至厌恶。厌恶是对腐烂、对恶臭难闻的粪便、血腥、残渣、呕吐物的本能反应。生理上的厌恶是为了保护身体免受毒素侵害而对这些令人作呕的动物污秽物做出的反应；社会上的厌恶是为了保护灵魂免受邪恶侵害而对道德败坏做出的反应。那些极其邪恶的角色会让你感到恶心……真的。

In Lord of the Rings , Lord Sauron is not radically evil. He is, in fact, rather elegant. He fights to maintain power, but he’s not sadistic, so he provokes no disgust.

在《指环王》中，索伦并非彻头彻尾的邪恶之王。事实上，他相当优雅。他为维护权力而战，但他并不残暴，因此不会引起人们的厌恶。

In contrast, O’Brien, the Party enforcer in George Orwell’s dystopian Nineteen Eighty-Four , locks a wire enclosure around Winston Smith’s head, then fills the surrounding cage with ravenous rats scrabbling to eat the man’s face. O’Brien, content in his pleasures, watches as this horrific psychic torture rips through his victim. O’Brien is radical evil.

与之形成鲜明对比的是，在乔治·奥威尔的反乌托邦小说《一九八四》中，党的执法者奥布莱恩用铁丝网将温斯顿·史密斯的头罩起来，然后在周围的笼子里塞满饥饿的老鼠，让它们争先恐后地啃噬史密斯的脸。奥布莱恩沉浸在自己的快感中，看着这种可怕的精神折磨撕裂着他的受害者。奥布莱恩是彻头彻尾的邪恶化身。

#↩

9. Subtract Belief

9. 减去信念

Here’s a useful question to ask of any role you create, conventional or radical: How crazy is my character? Sane in a sane world? Insane in a sane world? Sane in an insane world? Or insane in an insane world? The first three possibilities encompass characters found in Realism and non-Realism; radical characters inhabit the fourth.

无论你创作的角色是传统的还是激进的，都可以问问自己这样一个有用的问题：我的角色有多疯狂？在一个理智的世界里，他/她还算理智吗？在一个理智的世界里，他/她还算疯狂吗？在一个疯狂的世界里，他/她还算理智吗？还是在一个疯狂的世界里，他/她还算疯狂？前三种情况涵盖了现实主义和非现实主义作品中的角色；激进的角色则属于第四种情况。

Patricia Highsmith’s Tom Ripley falls into the second category. The world around him is sane, but he is not. He’s a psycho-sociopath who kills when necessary. To Ripley, necessary means getting what he wants by paying for it with someone else’s life.

帕特里夏·海史密斯的《汤姆·里普利》属于第二类。他周围的世界看似正常，但他自己却并非如此。他是一个反社会人格者，会在必要时杀人。对里普利来说，“必要时”意味着用他人的生命来换取自己想要的东西。

Lewis Carroll’s Alice fits the third case. She’s sane, but the world around her is not. This well-bred, snobby little girl needs to make sense out of an insane world, or she’ll never find her way home.

刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下的爱丽丝符合第三种情况。她神智清醒，但她周围的世界却并非如此。这个出身良好、略带傲慢的小女孩需要在这个疯狂的世界中找到意义，否则她将永远找不到回家的路。

What makes Ripley and Alice conventional characters is their trust that the world makes sense. A radical character lacks any such belief. Radical characters cannot find meaning in either their outer or their inner lives, and they certainly do not believe in anything spiritual.

瑞普利和爱丽丝之所以是传统角色，是因为她们相信世界自有其逻辑。而激进角色则缺乏这种信念。激进角色既无法在外部生活中找到意义，也无法在内心世界中找到意义，他们当然也不会相信任何精神信仰。

Belief is a personal interpretation of reality. Religious belief trusts that a god created reality and gave it moral imperatives. Patriotic belief trusts in the righteous and tradition-bound reality of a nation-state. Scientific belief trusts that mathematical laws of causality hold reality together. Romantic belief trusts that love is the ultimate value. With beliefs such as these, conventional characters find purpose in their lives.

信仰是对现实的个人诠释。宗教信仰相信上帝创造了现实并赋予其道德准则。爱国主义信仰相信民族国家拥有正义且恪守传统的现实。科学信仰相信数学因果律维系着现实。浪漫主义信仰相信爱情是终极价值。拥有这些信仰的人，往往能找到人生的意义。

Radical characters, having no belief to buoy them, despair in the face of absurdity.

激进分子没有信仰支撑，面对荒谬之事感到绝望。

In Perfume , a novel by Patrick Suskind, Jean-Baptiste finds people, himself included, disgusting and meaningless. Void of belief, he makes the ultimate escape from absurdity by enticing a starving mob into ripping him apart and cannibalizing him in the street.

在帕特里克·聚斯金德的小说《香水》中，让-巴蒂斯特觉得人，包括他自己，都令人作呕且毫无意义。他丧失了信仰，最终通过引诱一群饥饿的暴民在街头将他撕成碎片并吃掉，以此逃离了荒诞。

#↩

THE FUTURE: UNCONVENTIONAL CHARACTERS IN CONVENTIONAL WORLDS

未来：非传统角色在传统世界中

The postmodern avant-garde died decades ago and was replaced by a retro-garde. Postpostmodernist theatre, films, and novels of today simply recycle the twentieth century, exhausting its every minimal or maximal device ad nauseam. As a Beckett character might say, “Nothing that hasn’t been done.” So, instead of copying the past, the leading edge of twenty-first-century storytelling satirizes the present.

后现代先锋派早在几十年前就已消亡，取而代之的是复古先锋派。如今的后后现代主义戏剧、电影和小说，不过是对二十世纪的简单重复，将其所有极简或极繁的技巧都用尽，令人作呕。正如贝克特笔下的人物可能会说的那样，“没有什么是以前没做过的。” 因此，二十一世纪叙事的前沿不再是复制过去，而是讽刺当下。

In classical satire, clear-minded narrators ridiculed lunatic societies. Jonathan Swift perfected this technique in Gulliver’s Travels . Seventy years ago, Samuel Beckett ridiculed reality itself with radical characters in absurd settings. Today’s writers reverse both Swift and Beckett. They place radical characters in a conventional setting, and then draw us into empathy despite our better natures.

在古典讽刺作品中，头脑清醒的叙述者会嘲讽荒诞的社会。乔纳森·斯威夫特在《格列佛游记》中将这种技巧发挥到了极致。七十年前，塞缪尔·贝克特用极端人物和荒诞的背景来讽刺现实本身。而今天的作家则反其道而行之，他们把极端人物置于循规蹈矩的环境中，然后让我们不由自主地产生同情，即便我们本性善良。

The Black Comedy protagonists of The White Tiger by Aravind Adiga, A Behanding in Spokane by Martin McDonagh, Birdman by Alejandro Inarritu, The Sellout by Paul Beatty, and All Grown Up by Jami Attenberg are criminal or lunatic or criminally lunatic.

《白虎》（阿拉文德·阿迪加著）、《斯波坎的断头台》（马丁·麦克唐纳著）、《鸟人》（亚历杭德罗·伊纳里图著）、《出卖》（保罗·比蒂著）和《长大成人》（杰米·阿滕伯格著）等黑色喜剧的主角都是罪犯、疯子或既是罪犯又是疯子。

In fact, the utmost radical characters now star in their own longform series: the anxiety disordered and clinically depressed protagonist of Mr. Robot ; the charming cannibal of Santa Clarita Diet ; the psychotic, drug experimenters in Maniac ; the darkly obsessed comedians in I’m Dying Up Here ; Villanelle, the lovable serial killer in Killing Eve ; Barry, the actor/assassin in Barry ; and Jimmy McGill, the criminal criminal lawyer in Better Call Saul .

事实上，最激进的角色现在都有了自己的长篇剧集：《黑客军团》中患有焦虑症和临床抑郁症的主角；《圣克拉丽塔饮食》中魅力十足的食人族；《疯子》中精神错乱的毒品实验者；《我快要死了》中痴迷于黑暗的喜剧演员；《杀死伊芙》中可爱的连环杀手维拉内尔；《巴里》中演员/杀手巴里；以及《风骚律师》中罪犯律师吉米·麦吉尔。

As writers push the limits of empathy, they ask their readers and audiences to identify with more and more crazed and dangerous characters. The answer to the question “How dark is too dark for the contemporary reader/audience?” seems further and further away.

随着作家们不断挑战读者同理心的极限，他们要求读者和观众去认同越来越疯狂、越来越危险的角色。对于“当代读者/观众而言，怎样的黑暗才算过头？”这个问题，答案似乎越来越遥不可及。

PART 3

第三部分

#↩

THE CHARACTER UNIVERSE

角色宇宙

The next three chapters look at character from three different angles: the casts in various types of stories, the actions characters take within a story, and character from the point of view of readers and audiences.

接下来的三章将从三个不同的角度探讨人物：各种类型故事中的人物、人物在故事中采取的行动，以及从读者和观众的角度看待人物。

#↩

14

CHARACTER IN GENRE

类型中的角色

Nothing in the art of storytelling compels a writer to do anything in a rule-driven way. The genres impose no dictates; they simply follow traditional, conventional patterns. Like trends in music or painting, readers and audiences come to know their favorite genres, expecting and enjoying these designs. They naturally want to reexperience them but each time with a satisfying difference.

讲故事的艺术中，没有任何规则能强迫作家按部就班地创作。各种类型小说并不强加任何限制，它们只是遵循传统的、约定俗成的模式。就像音乐或绘画的潮流一样，读者和观众会逐渐熟悉自己喜欢的类型，期待并享受这些既定的模式。他们自然而然地想要再次体验这些类型，但每一次都希望有所创新，获得令人满意的感受。

Here, for example, are three sets of event expectations:

例如，以下是三组事件预期：

1. The Crime Story: (a) A crime will be committed. (b) The injustice will be discovered. (c) The protagonist will seek to identify, apprehend, and punish the criminal. (d) The criminal will fight against his discovery and punishment. (e) The protagonist may or may not restore justice.
1. 犯罪故事：（a）犯罪行为将会发生。（b）不公正的事件将被揭露。（c）主人公将努力识别、逮捕并惩罚罪犯。（d）罪犯将反抗罪行的揭露和惩罚。（e）主人公可能伸张正义，也可能不伸张正义。
2. The Love Story: (a) The lovers will meet. (b) They will fall in love. (c) Powerful forces will oppose their love. (d) The lovers will combat these forces. (e) Their love will triumph or fail.
2. 爱情故事：（a）恋人相遇。（b）他们坠入爱河。（c）强大的势力将阻挠他们的爱情。（d）恋人将与这些势力抗争。（e）他们的爱情将胜利或失败。
3. The Education Plot: (a) The protagonist will lead an unfulfilling life. (b) His sense of emptiness and meaninglessness will weigh on him, but he will not know what to do. (c) He will meet a “teacher character.” (d) The teacher will guide or inspire him. (e) The protagonist will develop a new understanding that gives his life meaning and purpose.
3. 教育情节：（a）主人公将过着不充实的生活。（b）他会感到空虚和无意义，却不知所措。（c）他会遇到一位“老师”。（d）这位老师会引导或启发他。（e）主人公会形成新的认知，从而获得生活的意义和目标。

The ways courts define crime, the ways families encourage or oppose romance, the ways intellectuals define meaning evolve over time. When a society’s beliefs undergo change, genre conventions develop innovative ways to express these evolving ideas. The writer, sensitive to the changing world around him, keeps, cuts, or reinvents these conventions. But any innovation must anticipate the public’s expectations. Because readers and audiences love their genres, bending or breaking conventions must add newer, clearer meaning and emotion to the telling.

法院对犯罪的定义、家庭对恋爱关系的鼓励或反对、知识分子对意义的阐释，都会随着时间推移而演变。当社会信仰发生改变时，文学体裁的惯例也会发展出创新的方式来表达这些不断演变的思想。作家敏锐地感知着周遭世界的变化，并会保留、删减或重塑这些惯例。但任何创新都必须预见到公众的期待。因为读者和观众喜爱他们所熟悉的文学体裁，所以对惯例的突破或创新必须为故事增添更新、更清晰的意义和情感。

Genre conventions, properly understood, do not limit expression but make it possible. Love Stories can’t be told if lovers never meet. Crime Stories can’t be told if crimes go undiscovered. An Education Plot can’t be told if a protagonist leads a happy, satisfying life. Without conventions, the story arts would not exist.

正确理解类型惯例，它们并非限制表达，而是使表达成为可能。如果恋人从未相遇，爱情故事就无从谈起；如果罪行未被发现，犯罪故事就无从讲述；如果主人公过着幸福美满的生活，教育题材的故事就无从展开。没有惯例，故事艺术便不复存在。

The genres divide into two basic classes:

这些类型可以分为两大类：

1. Primary genres that create content: characters, events, values, and emotions.
1. 构成内容的主要类型：人物、事件、价值观和情感。
2. Presentational genres that express content: comic or dramatic, gritty or poetic, factual or fantasied, and the like.
2. 表达内容的呈现类型：喜剧或戏剧、写实或诗意、纪实或虚构等等。
#↩

THE ORIGIN OF PRIMARY GENRES

初级体裁的起源

The primary genres evolved in reaction to life’s major levels of conflict: Physical, Social, Personal, Private.

主要类型片的出现是为了应对生活中的主要冲突层面：身体冲突、社会冲突、个人冲突、私人冲突。

In reaction to physical conflicts, storytellers first told origin myths of how gods created the skies, the earth, the seas, and humanity. Once belief in the supernatural gave reality a sense of order, storytellers moved from gods to heroes and invented the Action/Adventure Genre. These fictions acted out life-and-death battles against storms, floods, lightning, and voracious beasts.

为了应对自然灾害带来的冲突，说书人最初讲述了神明创造天空、大地、海洋和人类的起源神话。随着对超自然力量的信仰赋予现实秩序感，说书人开始从神明转向英雄，并创造了动作/冒险题材。这些虚构作品描绘了与风暴、洪水、闪电和凶猛野兽进行的生死搏斗。

But the most lethal threat to anyone’s life comes from other human beings, so storytellers developed additional genres based on social, domestic, and intimate levels of conflict. These conflicts generated arcs of outer change. Last, struggles within the mind gave rise to arcs of character change.

但对任何人生命而言，最致命的威胁往往来自其他人，因此，故事讲述者们根据社会、家庭和个人层面的冲突发展出了其他类型的故事。这些冲突引发了外在的变化弧线。最后，内心的挣扎则催生了人物性格的转变弧线。

Few stories are so pure that they engage their characters on only one level of conflict. In most tellings, levels mix, merge, and multiply, but let’s separate the levels of conflict to see how they generate primary genres.

很少有故事纯粹到只围绕一个层面的冲突展开。在大多数故事中，冲突层面会相互交织、融合甚至叠加，但让我们把冲突层面分开来看，看看它们是如何衍生出主要类型的。

#↩

Self Versus Nature

自我与自然

The Action/Adventure Genre: The first action tales pit heroes against the powers of nature personified as gods: Odysseus battles a hurricane driven by the breath of Poseidon; Lot flees Yahweh’s volcanic fire and brimstone; Gilgamesh slaughters the Bull of Heaven, and thousands more.

动作/冒险类型：最早的动作故事讲述英雄与被拟人化的神灵所代表的自然力量对抗：奥德修斯与波塞冬的呼吸所引发的飓风搏斗；罗得逃离耶和华的火山之火和硫磺；吉尔伽美什屠杀了天牛，等等。

The Horror Genre: The Greeks exaggerated nature into monsters such as the Hydra, Chimera, Minotaur, Cyclops, the vampire Mormo, the werewolf Lycaon, and the gorgon Medusa—each a nightmare of imagination.

恐怖类型：希腊人将自然界夸大成各种怪物，如九头蛇、奇美拉、弥诺陶洛斯、独眼巨人、吸血鬼莫尔莫、狼人吕卡翁和美杜莎——每一个都是想象中的噩梦。

#↩

Self Versus Society

自我与社会

The War Genre: Warfare has raged ever since the first man picked up the first club, but Homer launched this genre with the Iliad ’s telling of the Trojan War and Achilles in battle.

战争题材：自从第一个人拿起第一根棍棒以来，战争就一直肆虐，但荷马通过《伊利亚特》中对特洛伊战争和阿喀琉斯战斗的描述，开创了这一题材。

The Political Genre: When Athenians instituted democracy around 500 BC, political power struggles immediately became subject matter for tragedies such as Antigone as well as farces such as The Wasps .

政治题材：公元前 500 年左右，雅典人建立了民主制度，政治权力斗争立即成为《安提戈涅》等悲剧以及《黄蜂》等闹剧的主题。

The Crime Genre: Crime detection as a genre took root with Edgar Allan Poe’s master investigator C. Auguste Dupin in “The Murders in the Rue Morgue.” The genre captured the reading world when Arthur Conan Doyle gave it Sherlock Holmes.

犯罪小说类型：侦探小说这一类型起源于埃德加·爱伦·坡的《莫格街谋杀案》，书中塑造了侦探大师C·奥古斯特·杜宾这一角色。而当阿瑟·柯南·道尔笔下的夏洛克·福尔摩斯出现时，这一类型便风靡全球。

The Modern Epic: Spurred by the rise and fall of twentieth-century dictators, writers revamped the ancient quest epic into a fight for freedom that pits a lone hero against an all-powerful tyrant. This wide-ranging underdog/overdog genre spans both realism and nonrealism: Lord of the Rings , Nineteen Eighty-Four , Spartacus , Star Wars , The Handmaid’s Tale , Braveheart , Game of Thrones .

现代史诗：受二十世纪独裁者兴衰的启发，作家们将古老的冒险史诗改编成争取自由的斗争，讲述孤胆英雄对抗权势滔天的暴君的故事。这种弱者逆袭的题材包罗万象，涵盖了现实主义和非现实主义两种风格，例如《指环王》、《1984》、《斯巴达克斯》、《星球大战》、《使女的故事》、《勇敢的心》和《权力的游戏》。

Social Drama: Political upheavals in the nineteenth century exposed social problems such as poverty, corruption, and gender inequality. This genre identifies these conflicts and dramatizes their possible cures. Novelists like Charles Dickens and playwrights like Henrik Ibsen spent their literary lives exposing social injustices. Today, Social Drama is a magnet for Oscars.

社会剧：十九世纪的政治动荡暴露了贫困、腐败和性别不平等之类的社会问题。这一剧种旨在揭示这些冲突，并以戏剧化的方式探讨可能的解决之道。像查尔斯·狄更斯这样的小说家和像亨利克·易卜生这样的剧作家毕生致力于揭露社会不公。如今，社会剧已成为奥斯卡奖的热门题材。

#↩

Self Versus Intimates

自我与亲密关系

At the level of intimate relationships two genres act out conflicts between families and lovers:

在亲密关系层面，有两种类型片展现了家庭和恋人之间的冲突：

Domestic Drama: From Medea to King Lear to Wally Lamb’s novel I Know This Much Is True to Christopher Lloyd’s sitcom Modern Family , family stories, dramatic and comic, are an ancient and unending genre. They dramatize the loyalties and betrayals that bind or shred families.

家庭剧：从《美狄亚》到《李尔王》，从沃利·兰姆的小说《我知道这是真的》到克里斯托弗·劳埃德的情景喜剧《摩登家庭》，家庭故事，无论是戏剧性的还是喜剧性的，都是一个古老而经久不衰的题材。它们生动地展现了维系或撕裂家庭的忠诚与背叛。

The Love Story: The idealization of romantic love began as an effort to civilize male rage. In the late Middle Ages, an epidemic of rape swept through Europe, and so in reaction, troubadours, the pop culture of their day, told stories and sang songs praising the virtues of chaste, chivalric love. Since then, waves of Romanticism followed by tides of anti-Romanticism have buoyed and swamped Western culture and the love stories it tells.

爱情故事：浪漫爱情的理想化起源于对男性暴怒的一种文明化尝试。中世纪晚期，强奸案席卷欧洲，为了应对这一局面，当时的流行文化代表——游吟诗人——创作了许多歌谣，歌颂纯洁骑士精神的爱情美德。自此以后，浪漫主义的浪潮与反浪漫主义的浪潮交替出现，不断影响着西方文化及其所讲述的爱情故事。

A subgenre of the Love Story, known as the Buddy Story, dramatizes the intimacies of friendship rather than romantic love. Examples: My Brilliant Friend by Elena Ferrante, A Coupla White Chicks Sitting Around Talking by playwright John Ford Noonan, Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid , Thelma and Louise .

爱情故事的一个子类型，被称为“友情故事”，它着重描写友谊的亲密关系，而非浪漫爱情。例如：埃莱娜·费兰特的《我的天才女友》、约翰·福特·努南的剧作家《几个白人女孩围坐在一起聊天》、电影《虎豹小霸王》和《末路狂花》。

#↩

Self Versus Self

自我对抗自我

Stories of deep psychological complexity arc a character’s inner nature from who he is at the inciting incident to who he becomes by the climax. But what exactly can a writer change within a character? One of three qualities: morality, mentality, humanity.

深刻的心理复杂性故事，通过人物内心世界的演变，展现其从事件起因到高潮时的转变。但作家究竟能改变人物的哪些方面呢？无非是三种特质之一：道德、心智和人性。

Morality: How does a protagonist treat other people?

道德：主人公如何对待他人？

Responses to life’s temptations either strengthen or corrupt a character’s moral nature, changing him for better or worse, making him more honest or lying, more kind or cruel, more giving or selfish.

对生活诱惑的反应要么会增强要么会腐蚀一个人的道德本性，使他变得更好或更坏，使他更诚实或更说谎，更善良或更残忍，更慷慨或更自私。

Mentality: How does a protagonist think and feel about reality and his life in it?

心态：主人公如何看待和感受现实以及他在现实中的生活？

The genetic imperative against suicide makes us wait for death, but beyond that pause, existence has no intrinsic meaning. Faced with the relentlessness of time and randomness of luck, each complex character must answer a deeply private question: Does my existence have a purpose beyond survival? Is my life meaningful or absurd? In stories told at the level of an existential conflict, a protagonist either discovers a positive reason for living or surrenders to meaninglessness.

基因中抑制自杀的本能驱使我们等待死亡，但超越这短暂的停顿，存在本身并无意义。面对无情的时间流逝和命运的无常，每个复杂的人物都必须回答一个深刻的私人问题：除了生存之外，我的存在是否还有其他目的？我的人生是有意义还是荒谬？在以存在主义冲突为主题的故事中，主人公要么找到活着的积极意义，要么屈服于虚无。

Humanity: How does a character’s human potential change? To a fuller or lesser self?

人性：一个角色的人性潜能会发生怎样的变化？是变得更完整，还是更不完整？

The most subtly complex stories engage and change a character’s humanity. They raise the most difficult questions a writer ever asks: Does my character evolve or devolve over time? If so, what need or lacking in the character’s humanity does the telling fulfill or fail to fulfill? Does he grow or hollow out? Answers to these questions will come as you carry out two major tasks:

最精妙复杂的故事能够触动并改变人物的人性。它们会提出作家最难回答的问题：我的角色会随着时间推移而成长还是退化？如果会，故事满足了角色人性的哪些需求或缺失？他是在成长还是在消亡？当你完成以下两项主要任务时，这些问题的答案就会浮现：

(1) At the beginning of a story, a character’s overall humanity could be profound or shallow depending on an intricate weave of qualities such as wisdom versus ignorance, compassion versus indifference, generosity versus selfishness, emotional calm versus impulsiveness, and the like. In the planning stages of a story, imagine the relative maturity and fullness of your character’s inner world, and then measure its propensity for positive or negative change.

（1）故事伊始，人物的整体人性可能深刻也可能肤浅，这取决于诸多复杂特质的交织，例如智慧与无知、同情与冷漠、慷慨与自私、情绪沉稳与冲动等等。在故事构思阶段，设想一下人物内心世界的成熟度和完整性，然后评估其发生积极或消极变化的可能性。

(2) Once you have a grip on the depth and breadth of your character, reveal his nature at the inciting incident and the events that follow, arcing it over an expanse of story.

（2）一旦你掌握了角色的深度和广度，就在引发事件和随后的事件中揭示他的本性，并将其展开成一个广阔的故事。

You can execute these two tasks in only one way: Put your character under pressure, then, as he pursues his desire, give him choices of action that reveal who he is now and set up who he will become. At the story’s climax, the character will either heighten or diminish his humanity, becoming either a fuller or lesser human being.

你只能通过一种方法来完成这两个任务：先让你的角色承受压力，然后在他追求欲望的过程中，让他做出选择，这些选择既能揭示他现在的为人，也能塑造他未来的走向。在故事的高潮，角色的人性要么会得到提升，要么会逐渐消磨殆尽，最终成为一个更完整的人，或者成为一个更渺小的人。

#↩

THE SIXTEEN PRIMARY GENRES

十六种主要类型

Primary genres cause critical change in a character’s life on either the outer levels or in the inner life. As a result, primary genres are divided into two basic sets: Plots of Fortune and Plots of Character.

主要类型会对人物的外部生活或内心世界产生重大影响。因此，主要类型可分为两大类：命运情节和人物情节。

To cause and express change, primary genres contain four core conventions: core value, core event, core emotion, core cast. The next two sections examine the sixteen primary genres—ten of fortune, six of character—with their quartets of key conventions:

为了引发和表达变化，主要体裁包含四个核心要素：核心价值、核心事件、核心情感和核心人物。接下来的两节将探讨十六种主要体裁——十种命运体裁和六种人物体裁——及其各自的四个关键要素：

#↩

The Ten Plots of Fortune

命运的十大格局

Plots of Fortune change the outer conditions of a character’s life for better or worse. His fortunes could swing up or down between winning and losing, poverty and riches, loneliness and togetherness, and the like.

命运的安排会改变角色生活的外部环境，使其变得更好或更糟。他的命运可能会在成功与失败、贫穷与富有、孤独与团聚等等之间摇摆不定。

Genres under Plots of Fortune have numerous subgenres, some a dozen or more: Action, for example, has sixteen; Crime, fourteen; Love, six. This list outlines only the mother form without her children.

故事类型分为众多子类型，有些甚至多达十几个：例如，动作片有十六个子类型；犯罪片有十四个子类型；爱情片有六个子类型。此列表仅列出母类型，不包括其子类型。

1. The Action Genre

1. 动作类型

Core Value: Life Versus Death
核心价值观：生命与死亡
Core Event: Hero at the Mercy of the Villain
核心事件：英雄落入反派之手
Core Emotion: Excitement
核心情绪：兴奋
Core Cast: Hero, Villain, Victim
核心角色：英雄、反派、受害者

These three characters form a triangle of moral archetypes. The essential trait of the hero is altruism; of the villain, narcissism; of the victim, vulnerability.

这三个人物构成了一个道德原型三角。英雄的本质特征是利他主义；反派的本质特征是自恋；受害者的本质特征是脆弱。

Heroes change the world but not themselves. Their shades of power run from superhero (Superman) to action hero (Jason Bourne) to everyman hero (Captain Phillips). Superheroes employ extrahuman powers to battle extrahuman villains and monsters; action heroes test their strengths against conventional villains; everyday heroes have no special skills, except the willpower to suffer pain and risk out of necessity.

英雄改变世界，却不改变自身。他们的力量各不相同，从超级英雄（超人）到动作英雄（杰森·伯恩），再到平民英雄（菲利普船长）。超级英雄运用超人的力量对抗超人般的恶棍和怪物；动作英雄与普通恶棍搏斗，检验自身实力；而平民英雄并无特殊技能，唯有出于必要而承受痛苦和风险的意志力。

Villains range from supervillains to master criminals to street gangs. They use violence without hesitation because they’re indifferent to the humanity of their victims; the hero has to be provoked to violence because he cannot be indifferent to anyone’s humanity, including the villain’s.
