Sentimentality is an imbalanced, undermotivated, overexpressed indulgence that’s out of proportion to the events that caused it: for example, a brave smile through trembling tears shed over a child’s better-than-average report card.

如前所述，情感是一种与引发事件相称的平衡的情绪反应。而感伤则是一种失衡的、缺乏动机的、过度表达的情感，与引发事件不成比例：例如，孩子成绩优异却强颜欢笑，泪流满面。

In the climax of Game of Thrones , Season 8, Episode 5, “The Bells,” Jaime Lannister fights his way to the trapped and terrified Cersei. Just as the Red Keep collapses around them, he takes her in his arms and says, “Look at me. Just look at me. Nothing else matters. Only us.” He sacrifices his life so that she won’t die alone. This act, in proportion to his love, moves an honest sentiment.

在《权力的游戏》第八季第五集“钟声”的高潮部分，詹姆·兰尼斯特奋力杀出一条血路，来到被困的瑟曦身边。就在红堡即将崩塌之际，他将她拥入怀中，轻声说道：“看着我。看着我。其他的一切都不重要了。只有我们。”他牺牲了自己的生命，只为不让她孤单地死去。这一举动，与他的爱相得益彰，真挚动人。

In Schindler’s List , a black-and-white film set during the Holocaust, a little girl wearing a bright red coat walks through the horrific liquidation of Krakow. Later, Oskar Schindler sees the child’s dead body wrapped in her red coat and the sight moves him to change from selfish, callous materialist to noble, self-sacrificing hero. This is wish fulfillment and as phony as a villain stroking a kitten to show that, evil as he is, he can feel something for a pet. As Carl Jung pointed out, cruelty seduces its victims with the syrup of sentimentality.

在以纳粹大屠杀为背景的黑白电影《辛德勒的名单》中，一个身穿鲜红外套的小女孩走过克拉科夫惨绝人寰的清算现场。后来，奥斯卡·辛德勒看到了裹在她红外套里的小女孩的遗体，这一幕触动了他，使他从一个自私冷酷的唯物主义者转变为一个高尚的、自我牺牲的英雄。这是一种愿望的实现，就像一个恶棍抚摸小猫，试图表明他虽然邪恶，但也会爱护宠物一样虚伪。正如卡尔·荣格所指出的，残忍会用感伤的糖浆来诱惑受害者。

#↩

Reader/Audience Interpretation

读者/观众解读

A story asks its reader/audience to interpret not only the events in front of them, but offscreen, offstage, or off-page happenings as well. They must add up what has occurred since the previous scene that led to the present, and they must infer the future this present event may bring. Without their ability to interpret, involvement is impossible.

故事要求读者/观众不仅要解读眼前发生的事件，还要解读屏幕之外、舞台之外或书页之外发生的事情。他们必须将前一幕之后发生的事情串联起来，推断出当前事件可能带来的未来走向。如果缺乏解读能力，就无法真正投入其中。

The same is true for subtext. To discover the truth of a character’s motivations, readers and audiences must look past his words and deeds, his choices and actions, and seek hidden causes and meanings.

潜台词也是如此。为了发现人物动机的真相，读者和观众必须透过他的言行、选择和行动，去寻找隐藏的原因和意义。

Interpretation, however, depends on an understanding of desires and values. To react fully and grasp a clear meaning, the reader/audience must sense a character’s immediate desire in each scene, and how these scene-by-scene desires feed into his end goal at the climax. To understand what a character wants, however, the reader/audience must also understand the values at play in each scene and the core value that drives the story.

然而，解读取决于对欲望和价值观的理解。为了充分理解剧情并把握其清晰的含义，读者/观众必须感知角色在每个场景中的即时欲望，以及这些逐一展现的欲望如何最终促成其在故事高潮中的目标。而要理解角色的真正需求，读者/观众还必须理解每个场景中体现的价值观以及推动故事发展的核心价值观。

A misunderstanding of a story’s values causes a misunderstanding of character desires, which leads to misinterpretation. If readers or audiences cannot sort out what’s at stake in your character’s life, what’s positive from what’s negative, then they may misunderstand what the character wants or why he wants it. Their bewilderment leads to mistaken readings that distort the meaning you want to express.

对故事价值观的误解会导致对人物欲望的误解，进而造成误读。如果读者或观众无法分辨人物生活中的利害关系，无法区分积极与消极，他们就可能误解人物的愿望或愿望背后的原因。这种困惑会导致错误的解读，从而扭曲你想要表达的含义。

Case Study: Heart of Darkness

案例研究：《黑暗之心》

Set in Africa in the 1890s, Joseph Conrad’s novella Heart of Darkness follows riverboat captain Charles Marlow up the Congo on a mission for a Belgian trading company to bring back a cargo of ivory and the company’s agent, Kurtz, who they fear has gone rogue.

约瑟夫·康拉德的中篇小说《黑暗之心》以 19 世纪 90 年代的非洲为背景，讲述了河船船长查尔斯·马洛受一家比利时贸易公司之托，沿刚果河逆流而上，带回一批象牙货物以及该公司的代理人库尔茨的故事。他们担心库尔茨已经叛变。

During the voyage, Marlow questions people who know Kurtz, and everything he hears seems contradictory. Some fear and distrust him, hinting at a sinister nature. Others claim he’s a civilized and charismatic artist and musician. One thing is certain: Kurtz knows how to inspire the slaughter of elephants and pile up their tusks by the ton.

在航行途中，马洛询问了所有认识库尔茨的人，但他听到的却莫衷一是。有些人害怕他、不信任他，暗示他本性险恶。另一些人则声称他是一位文明而富有魅力的艺术家和音乐家。但有一点可以肯定：库尔茨深谙如何煽动屠杀大象，并成吨地收集象牙。

In one possible interpretation, Marlow is a psychological detective, fascinated by the enigmatic Kurtz. This makes the story’s core value Insight/Ignorance and the discovery of the real Kurtz Captain Marlow’s object of desire.

一种可能的解读是，马洛是一位心理侦探，对神秘的库尔茨着迷。这使得故事的核心价值在于洞察/无知，以及发现库尔茨的真实面目——马洛上尉所渴望的对象。

In a different reading, Marlow is a lost soul, adrift in moral confusion. His fellow Europeans think that colonialism brings civilization to the “dark continent,” but Marlow suspects that this is a convenient self-deception to rationalize their greed. He hopes that Kurtz understands this, too, and has rebelled against his employers by choosing the virtues of primitive nobility over perverse civilization. In this case, the story’s core value becomes Purity/Corruption, and Marlow’s object of desire is to prove that human nature, in its primal state, is innately good.

另一种解读是，马洛是一个迷失的灵魂，在道德迷茫中漂泊。他的欧洲同胞认为殖民主义将文明带到了“黑暗大陆”，但马洛怀疑这不过是他们为贪婪开脱的自欺欺人。他希望库尔茨也明白这一点，并选择了原始高贵的德行而非堕落的文明，从而反抗了他的雇主。在这种情况下，故事的核心价值在于纯洁与堕落的对立，而马洛的渴望则在于证明，人性在其原始状态下，本质上是善良的。

When Marlow reaches Kurtz, however, he discovers that the once-civilized gentleman has turned into a vicious tyrant worshipped like a god by brutalized, terrified tribesmen. Kurtz’s embrace of the primitive has not unleashed his nobility but his barbarity.

然而，当马洛找到库尔茨时，他发现这位曾经彬彬有礼的绅士已经变成了一个残暴的暴君，被那些饱受摧残、惊恐万分的部落成员奉为神明。库尔茨对原始的拥抱并没有释放出他的高贵品质，反而激发了他的野蛮本性。

Different values create different meanings: In the first interpretation, when Marlow discovers the radically changed Kurtz, he realizes that because the core self evolves, it’s impossible to know another person’s true identity. In the second interpretation, Marlow gains a deeper, more universal insight into the innate savagery of human nature.

不同的价值观造就不同的意义：在第一种解读中，当马洛发现库尔茨发生了翻天覆地的变化时，他意识到，由于人的核心自我会不断演变，因此不可能了解另一个人的真实身份。在第二种解读中，马洛对人性中固有的野蛮本质有了更深刻、更普遍的洞察。

Key point: Once the reader/audience grasps the story’s essential subject matter, its core value, that perception grounds their interpretation of character.

关键点：一旦读者/观众掌握了故事的基本主题和核心价值，这种认知就会成为他们对角色进行解读的基础。

#↩

Reader/Audience Perception

读者/观众感知

In addition to the emotions they feel and the meanings they interpret, readers and audiences also perceive characters on different levels (text versus subtext), at different points in the chain of events (free will versus fate), and from different angles of awareness (mystery versus suspense versus dramatic irony). During the creative process, an author needs to work with his characters from each of these three points of view:

除了感受情感和解读意义之外，读者和观众还会从不同的层面（文本层面与潜台词层面）、不同的事件节点（自由意志与命运）以及不同的视角（神秘、悬疑、戏剧性讽刺）来感知人物。在创作过程中，作者需要从这三个方面来塑造人物：

#↩

Text Versus Subtext

文本与潜台词

Feeling empathy is not the same as perceiving subtext. Readers and audiences read the minds of characters they hate as well as love. Rather than simply following a story with interest, they become simultaneously aware of what’s going on at two levels: outward sayings and doings versus inward thinking and feeling—text versus subtext.

产生共情并不等同于理解言外之意。读者和观众会揣摩他们所爱之人以及所恨之人的内心世界。他们不再只是饶有兴趣地追随故事，而是同时意识到两个层面上发生的事情：外在的言行与内在的思考和感受——文本与潜台词。

As Dostoevsky noted, the implied inner life of a complex role is symphonic. When one character tells another what’s on his mind, readers and audiences hear just two or three notes, but then perceive an orchestra of thoughts and feeling playing within. The two modes of character performance activate this perception in two very different ways:

正如陀思妥耶夫斯基所指出的，复杂角色的内在世界如同交响乐一般。当一个角色向另一个角色倾诉心声时，读者和观众或许只听到两三个音符，但却能感受到其中交响乐般的思想和情感。两种不同的角色表演方式以截然不同的方式激活了这种感知：

On page, the creativity of the writer and the imagination of the reader combine to generate characters. Onstage and on-screen, the actor, supported by directors, lighting and set designers, cinematographers, editors, makeup artists, and composers, work in concert to bring the writer’s creation to the audience.

在书页上，作者的创造力与读者的想象力相结合，塑造出鲜活的人物形象。在舞台和银幕上，演员在导演、灯光师、布景师、摄影师、剪辑师、化妆师和作曲家的共同协作下，将作者的创作呈现给观众。

In terms of characterization, audiences watching the screen or stage see characters from head to foot as they move through their social and physical settings. They absorb an enormous amount of detail, leaving little work for the imagination. The reader, on the other hand, notes details, some concrete, some metaphorical, then adds his own personal experiences scattered through a lifetime, and finally pours these ingredients into his imagination, stirring the bits and pieces together to concoct a characterization.

就人物塑造而言，观众在银幕或舞台上观看人物时，会从头到脚地观察他们在社会和物理环境中的活动。他们会吸收大量细节，几乎没有想象的余地。而读者则不同，他们会注意到一些细节——有些是具体的，有些是隐喻的——然后融入自己一生中零散的个人经历，最终将这些素材倾注到想象中，将各种碎片混合在一起，从而构建出一个人物形象。

In terms of true character, when watching performances onstage or on-screen, the imagination peers past the actors’ eyes, past words and gestures, past intentions and self-deceptions, searching for the truth rising up from the subconscious. It sees the character form ideas in his conscious mind, but then hold them unspoken beneath the surface of his persona.

就人物的真实性格而言，当我们观看舞台或银幕上的表演时，想象力会超越演员的眼神、言语和姿态，超越他们的意图和自欺欺人，去探寻潜意识中涌现的真相。它看到人物在意识层面形成各种想法，却又将它们隐藏在人格表象之下，不轻易说出口。

First-person prose often puts the character’s conscious thoughts, although unspoken to other characters, on the page. Now the reader must penetrate the written text to scan the protagonist’s subconscious. The inner life of the rest of the cast comes filtered through the narrator’s perceptions. How much that warps the true thoughts and desires of these characters alters from author to author.

第一人称叙述通常会将人物的意识层面想法——即使这些想法并未对其他人物说出口——直接呈现在读者面前。读者必须深入文本，才能窥探主人公的潜意识。其他角色的内心世界则通过叙述者的视角得以展现。这种视角在多大程度上扭曲了人物的真实想法和欲望，则因作者而异。

Third-person prose varies perceptions. Some writers show and imply, others tell and explain. Writers who show dramatize surface behaviors and imply a character’s inner life; those who tell portray a character’s thoughts and feelings directly on the page. Hemingway’s The Old Man and the Sea is an example of the first; Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway is an example of the second. Today, most third-person prose mixes showing with telling, implying with explaining.

第三人称散文的表达方式多种多样。有些作家采用展示和暗示的手法，有些作家则采用叙述和解释的手法。采用展示手法的作家着重刻画人物的表面行为，暗示其内心世界；而采用叙述手法的作家则直接在纸面上展现人物的思想和情感。海明威的《老人与海》是前者的典范；弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《达洛维夫人》则是后者的代表。如今，大多数第三人称散文都融合了展示与叙述、暗示与解释的手法。

#↩

Free Will Versus Fate

自由意志与命运

As noted previously, when we begin a story and look forward to its ending, the protagonist’s course to the future seems open to all possibilities. But when the story ends and we look back to the beginning, events seem predetermined. Now that we know him in depth, we feel that his psychology could not let him act any way other than he did. Given the innate powers of the physical and social world that surrounded him, what happened had to happen. He was at the mercy of an invisible but inevitable fate.

如前所述，当我们开始阅读一个故事并期待它的结局时，主人公的未来似乎充满无限可能。但当故事结束，我们回望开头时，一切似乎都已注定。如今我们对他有了更深入的了解，我们感到他的心理状态不允许他做出其他选择。鉴于他所处的物质和社会环境的固有力量，一切的发生都是必然的。他只能任由一种无形却又无法避免的命运摆布。

In storytelling, the perception of determinism versus free will depends on the reader’s/audience’s location in time: before, during, or after events. Before things happen, we’re ignorant of what lies ahead, so the characters seem free to choose and act. But after things happen, we look back and discover that a multitude of interconnected forces flowed into everything. The outcome now seems destined. The writer, therefore, needs to pace character arcs, scene by scene, sequence by sequence, act by act, so that our curiosity at the beginning is satisfied at the ending by a retrospective insight into their fate.

在故事叙述中，对决定论与自由意志的感知取决于读者/观众所处的时间位置：事件发生之前、之中或之后。在事件发生之前，我们对未来一无所知，因此角色似乎可以自由选择和行动。但事件发生之后，我们回过头来看，发现无数相互关联的力量共同作用于一切。此时，结果似乎早已注定。因此，作者需要精心安排角色弧线，逐场、逐段、逐幕地推进，才能让我们在故事开始时的好奇心在结尾得到满足，从而对角色的命运有更深刻的理解。

#↩

Mystery / Suspense / Dramatic Irony

悬疑/惊悚/戏剧性讽刺

Characters struggle through invented events in invented worlds unaware that they live in a fiction; to them the telling is their life. Readers and audiences, meanwhile, sit outside story-time, knowing events before, during, or after the characters experience them. This split in awareness creates three storytelling strategies: Mystery, Suspense, Dramatic Irony.

故事中的人物在虚构的世界中经历着虚构的事件，却浑然不知自己身处虚构之中；对他们而言，讲述故事就是他们的人生。而读者和观众则置身于故事之外，他们了解事件的发生时间，无论是在人物经历之前、之中还是之后。这种认知上的差异催生了三种叙事策略：悬疑、惊悚和戏剧性讽刺。

Mystery puts characters ahead of the reader or audience. In the classic Murder Mystery, for example, someone goes to a closet for a shirt, opens the door, and a dead body falls out. This twist puts the victim’s killer ahead of the storygoer. The murderer knows who did it, but he’s not talking. Therefore, the ever-curious reader/audience, knowing less than the characters, runs from behind, looking ahead, following events wherever they lead, trying to find out what the characters already know.

悬疑小说让角色先于读者或观众掌握信息。例如，在经典的谋杀悬疑小说中，有人去衣橱拿衬衫，打开衣橱门，一具尸体掉了出来。这种情节转折让凶手掌握了更多信息。凶手知道是谁干的，但他却守口如瓶。因此，永远充满好奇心的读者/观众，由于掌握的信息比角色少，只能紧随其后，不断向前探寻，跟随剧情发展，试图弄清角色早已知晓的真相。

Stories ruled by mystery, especially those propelled by master detectives, draw sympathy but no empathy. Sherlock Holmes is likable but not like us. We can’t identify with him because his brilliance touches perfection.

以悬疑为主线的故事，尤其是那些由神探侦探主导的故事，往往能博得读者的同情，却难以引起共鸣。夏洛克·福尔摩斯讨人喜欢，但他与我们截然不同。我们无法与他产生共鸣，因为他的才智近乎完美。

Suspense puts the reader/audience in the same moment as the cast. The instant events happen, they impact both characters and storygoers. The reader/audience may anticipate certain turning points and characters may hide certain secrets, but overall, each knows the past and present, while neither knows the future. Thus, the major dramatic question (MDQ) becomes “How will this turn out?” Ninety percent of all storytelling employs this strategy.

悬念让读者/观众与剧中人物感同身受。事件发生的瞬间，既影响着角色，也影响着读者/观众。读者/观众或许能预料到某些转折点，角色或许会隐藏某些秘密，但总的来说，每个人都了解过去和现在，却对未来一无所知。因此，主要的戏剧性问题（MDQ）就变成了“故事将如何发展？”。90%的叙事手法都运用了这种策略。

Dramatic Irony puts the reader/audience ahead of the characters, knowing future events before they happen to the cast. This strategy shifts the MDQ from “How will this turn out?” to “How and why did these characters do what I already know they did?”

戏剧性讽刺让读者/观众先于角色，在事件发生之前就知晓未来。这种策略将故事主线问题从“事情会如何发展？”转变为“这些角色为什么会做出我早已知道的事情？”

Two films by Billy Wilder, Double Indemnity and Sunset Blvd. , open with their protagonists riddled with bullets, then flash back to the choices and actions that cost them their lives. Because the filmgoer knows the ending from the very beginning, he watches from a godlike perspective, knowing that the schemes the protagonist thinks will enrich him will ultimately kill him.

比利·怀尔德的两部电影，《双重赔偿》和《日落大道》，都以主人公身中数弹开场，然后闪回展现导致他们丧命的选择和行动。由于观众从一开始就知道结局，因此他们以上帝视角观看，明白主人公自以为能让他致富的计划最终会害死他。

Stories set during renowned historical events or told about famous people automatically position the reader/audience in dramatic irony. But then to some degree, no matter the telling’s strategy, the reader/audience often knows things characters don’t. For example, anything said, done, or planned in any scene that does not contain the protagonist instantly gives us greater knowledge than him because we were there and he wasn’t.

以著名历史事件为背景或讲述名人故事的叙事，自然而然地会给读者/观众带来戏剧性的反讽。但即便如此，无论叙事手法如何，读者/观众往往也知道一些角色所不知道的事情。例如，任何发生在主角不在场的场景中，任何所说、所做或所计划的事情，都会让我们比他更了解情况，因为我们身临其境，而他却不在。

However, other than biographies and murder mysteries, the exclusive use of either dramatic irony or closed mystery is relatively rare. Instead, most writers merge all three: Suspense shapes their overall strategy, but within its arc, characters that hide secrets know more than the storygoer, while readers and audiences reacting to flashbacks know more than the characters in them.

然而，除了传记和推理小说之外，单独使用戏剧性反讽或封闭式悬疑手法的情况相对较少。大多数作家会将这三种手法融合在一起：悬念构成了他们的整体策略，但在故事结构中，隐藏秘密的角色比读者知道得更多，而读者和观众对闪回片段的反应也比片段中的角色更了解情况。

The political and romantic plotlines in Casablanca fill the film with suspense, but within that tension, a flashback to the young lovers’ meeting in Paris adds a layer of dramatic irony. As the audience watches Rick and Ilsa’s romance, they know the dark future that awaits the lovers. Later, the telling shifts to mystery when Rick chooses his final action but keeps it secret from everyone, including the audience.

《卡萨布兰卡》中交织的政治与爱情故事线营造出紧张悬疑的气氛，而穿插其中的一段对年轻恋人在巴黎相遇的回忆，则增添了一层戏剧性的讽刺意味。当观众目睹里克和伊尔莎的爱情时，他们早已预知这对恋人即将面临的悲惨结局。随后，叙事手法转向了悬疑，里克做出了最终选择，却对所有人，包括观众，都守口如瓶。

More recently, in The Sympathizer , a first-person novel by Viet Thanh Nguyen, an espionage chief holds a double agent captive and forces him to write out his life story and, above all, tell the truth. The prose we read is that “confession.” Suspense hangs on the MDQ: Will the spy tell the truth or lie? And will his choice save him or kill him?

最近，在阮越清的第一人称小说《同情者》中，一位间谍头目囚禁了一名双面间谍，强迫他写下自己的生平，更重要的是，要他说出真相。我们读到的正是那份“自白”。悬念就在于这个关键问题：间谍会说真话还是说谎？他的选择会救他还是害他？

As the narrator’s confession weaves back and forth over three decades, mysteries surrounding hidden assassination plots entice the reader, while, at the same time, dramatic irony haunts every page. We realize that even though the protagonist faced death, he must have survived or we couldn’t be reading his book.

随着叙述者在三十年间来回穿梭的自白，围绕着隐秘刺杀阴谋的谜团吸引着读者，与此同时，戏剧性的讽刺贯穿始终。我们意识到，即便主人公曾面临死亡，他必定活了下来，否则我们不可能读到他的故事。

#↩

The Power of First Impressions

第一印象的力量

Let’s end this chapter with a look at beginnings:

让我们以回顾起源来结束本章：

While creating starting points—images that establish locations, chapters that open novels, actions that trigger scenes—be alert to the power of first impressions. When the reader/audience encounters something new, his thoughts rush ahead, driven by curiosity, anticipating the worst or best or both, wondering where this new thing will lead. This is particularly true the moment a character enters the telling, and absolutely true when it’s your protagonist.

在构思故事的起点——描绘场景的画面、开启小说的章节、触发场景的动作——时，务必重视第一印象的力量。当读者/观众遇到新鲜事物时，他们的思绪会迅速展开，好奇心驱使他们预想最坏的结果或最好的结果，或者两者兼而有之，并思考这件新事物将把他们引向何方。当一个角色出现在故事中时，这种现象尤为明显，而当这个角色是你的主角时，则更是如此。

Resist the urge to plant your protagonist on page one. Instead, intrigue the reader or audience by withholding the protagonist until the most effective scene, and then give him an entrance.

不要急于在第一页就让主角出场。相反，要等到最精彩的场景才让主角登场，以此来激发读者或观众的兴趣。

In the opening scenes of Casablanca , characters raise questions about the protagonist, finding him charismatic yet aloof, renowned yet mysterious. When the camera finally settles on Rick Blaine, he’s dressed in a white tuxedo, playing chess against himself. After all those setups, the audience naturally wonders, “Who is this guy?”

在《卡萨布兰卡》的开场，人物们对主人公提出了诸多疑问，他们发现他既魅力四射又冷漠疏离，既声名显赫又神秘莫测。当镜头最终定格在里克·布莱恩身上时，他身着白色燕尾服，独自下着棋。经过这些铺垫，观众自然会好奇：“这个人究竟是谁？”

No matter where you bring in your major characters, fame them with an entrance that introduces them with impact:

无论你让主要角色在哪里出场，都要让他们以震撼人心的方式亮相：

In David Lean’s Lawrence of Arabia , Sherif Ali first appears as a distant speck on the horizon, then rides slowly toward us, growing larger and larger against a blazing desert sky.

在大卫·里恩的《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》中，谢里夫·阿里最初只是地平线上一个遥远的小点，然后慢慢地骑马向我们靠近，在炽热的沙漠天空下越来越大。

In Eugene O’Neill’s Long Day’s Journey into Night , Mary Tyrone wanders into her living room, mumbling in a morphine haze.

在尤金·奥尼尔的《长夜漫漫路迢迢》中，玛丽·泰隆迷迷糊糊地走进客厅，喃喃自语。

In Ralph Ellison’s Invisible Man , a man sits in a basement lit by a hundred blindingly bright bare bulbs strung from the ceiling. He calmly tells the reader that he’s stealing electricity from the city.

在拉尔夫·埃里森的小说《看不见的人》中，一个男人坐在地下室里，天花板上挂着一百盏刺眼的裸露灯泡。他平静地告诉读者，他正在从城市里偷电。

In Season 1, Episode 1 of Phoebe Waller-Bridge’s Killing Eve , a sweet-faced child sits in an ice cream parlor eating a sundae. From across the room, Villanelle smiles at her and the kid gleams back. Then as Villanelle heads for the door, she smacks the girl’s ice cream into her startled face.

在菲比·沃勒-布里奇的《杀死伊芙》第一季第一集中，一个面容甜美的小女孩坐在冰淇淋店里吃圣代。维拉内尔从房间另一头朝她微笑，小女孩也露出灿烂的笑容。然后，维拉内尔走向门口，突然把冰淇淋狠狠地砸在了小女孩惊愕的脸上。

In William Golding’s Darkness Visible , the Luftwaffe pulverizes World War II London. Then out of the raging bomb-blasted inferno, a child emerges naked, horribly burnt and disfigured.

在威廉·戈尔丁的小说《可见的黑暗》中，二战期间，德国空军将伦敦夷为平地。随后，在熊熊燃烧的炸弹废墟中，一个赤身裸体、浑身烧伤、面目全非的孩子走了出来。

In the Jerry Herman–Jerome Lawrence–Robert E. Lee musical Mame , Mame blows a bugle atop a curved staircase, then slides down the banister.

在杰瑞·赫尔曼、杰罗姆·劳伦斯和罗伯特·E·李创作的音乐剧《梅姆》中，梅姆站在弧形楼梯的顶端吹响号角，然后顺着栏杆滑了下来。

Ideally, the entrance of a complex character intrigues us about his future and invites insight into his core self.

理想情况下，一个复杂角色的登场会让我们对他的未来感到好奇，并促使我们深入了解他的内心世界。

#↩

PART 4

第四部分

#↩

CHARACTER RELATIONSHIPS

人物关系

No one reveals her complete self to anyone. Each of us exposes only certain facets to others, holding back the rest, keeping big secrets at home. The same is true for self-knowledge. No one shows all of herself to herself. Blind to who we really are, certain truths are perceived only by other people. 1

没有人会向任何人完全袒露自己。我们每个人都只会向他人展现某些方面，而将其他方面隐藏起来，把重大的秘密藏在家里。自我认知也是如此。没有人会向自己完全敞开心扉。当我们对真实的自己视而不见时，某些真相只有他人才能感知。

As in life, so in fiction. One character may link to another through a shared academic interest or religious feelings or romantic love, but never all aspects equally at once with any one person. However, if you surround this character with a cast, each member geared to draw out a specific aspect, her traits and dimensions will reveal themselves as she encounters the various cast members. The writer’s problem, therefore, is how to design a cast so that by the climax, the reader/audience knows the characters better than the characters know themselves.

现实生活如此，虚构作品亦然。一个角色可能因为共同的学术兴趣、宗教信仰或浪漫爱情而与另一个角色产生联系，但绝不可能与任何一个角色同时具备所有这些特质。然而，如果围绕这个角色构建一个群像，每个角色都旨在展现她性格中的某个特定方面，那么随着她与这些角色的互动，她的性格特征和多面性就会逐渐显露出来。因此，作家面临的难题是如何设计一个群像，使得在故事高潮时，读者/观众对角色的了解甚至超过了角色自身。

Principle of Character Relationships: Every cast member draws traits and truths out of every other cast member.
角色关系原则：每个演员都能从其他演员身上汲取性格特征和真理。

Part Four puts this principle to work as it guides the mapping and designing of a cast.

第四部分运用这一原则来指导演员阵容的规划和设计。

#↩

17

CAST DESIGN

铸造设计

No one travels to her destiny down a razor-straight road. Each of us winds through a maze of social and personal intersections, navigating crossroads and cloverleafs, the entrances, exits, and U-turns of relationships. A character’s core self, therefore, is never the sole determiner of her fate. Her instincts push her toward one set of desires, while the tides of physical, social, and personal oceans pull her toward others. Because people impact one another, we design casts around links and oppositions that define each other’s qualities. Within these conjoined yet contrasted dealings, a cast forms.

没有人能沿着笔直的道路走向自己的命运。我们每个人都穿梭于错综复杂的社会和人际关系迷宫，在十字路口和立交桥间徘徊，经历着人际关系的入口、出口和转弯。因此，一个角色的核心自我绝非其命运的唯一决定者。她的本能驱使她走向某种欲望，而物质、社会和个人层面的种种变迁又将她拉向其他方向。因为人与人之间相互影响，我们围绕着彼此的联系和对立来构建角色，这些联系和对立定义了彼此的特质。在这些既相互关联又相互对比的互动中，角色逐渐形成。

Inside a well-formed cast, traits and dimensions create counterpoints that distinguish each character from every other character. While interacting within scenes, or talking or thinking about each other in separate scenes, roles reveal and clarify one another by contrast and contradiction. What’s more, as characters interact face-to-face, they provoke actions and reactions in each other that reveal the positive/negative charges of their dimensionalities.

在一个精心构建的角色阵容中，人物的性格特征和维度相互映衬，形成鲜明的对比，使每个角色都独具特色。无论是在同一场景中互动，还是在不同场景中交谈或思考，角色之间都通过对比和矛盾相互揭示和阐明。此外，当角色面对面交流时，他们会激发彼此的行为和反应，从而展现出各自性格维度的正负能量。

As focus shifts from character to character, this system shapes how they help and hinder each other, what they want or refuse, what they will or will not do, who they are, and how each character exposes the traits and dynamics of the others. When incompatible desires fester into conflict, the links between characters break, transforming relationships.

随着故事焦点在不同角色间转移，这套体系塑造了他们彼此间的帮助与阻碍、他们的欲望与拒绝、他们的行动意愿与否、他们的本质，以及每个角色如何展现其他角色的特质和互动模式。当不相容的欲望滋生冲突时，角色间的联系便会断裂，关系也会随之改变。

So as a writer develops her story, she constantly compares and contrasts characters, arranging similarities and differences, creating patterns only she can see. Hamlet desperately searches for meaning, but Shakespeare always knew where his prince would finally find it.

因此，作家在构思故事时，会不断地比较和对比人物，梳理他们的异同，从而形成只有她自己才能看到的模式。哈姆雷特苦苦追寻意义，但莎士比亚始终知道他的王子最终会在哪里找到答案。

Therefore, just because a character appears in your imagination doesn’t mean she’s earned a place in your cast. Each role must play a part in a creative strategy that enhances the storytelling. The reader’s/audience’s full psychological involvement comes not from the protagonist alone, but from the tensions between resemblances and differences among all cast members. If characters are opposed on just one axle—good versus evil, or courageous versus cowardly—they trivialize each other, and interest in them wanes. But if they are opposed in complex ways, they arouse curiosities and empathies that draw energy and concentration from the storygoer. This calls for thoughtful cast design. The next five sections explore five examples from the major storytelling media.

因此，仅仅因为某个角色出现在你的想象中，并不意味着她就理应成为你故事中的一员。每个角色都必须在增强故事叙述效果的创作策略中发挥作用。读者/观众的心理投入并非仅仅来自主角，而是来自所有角色之间相似与差异的张力。如果角色之间仅仅存在单一的对立——善与恶，或勇敢与懦弱——那么他们就会彼此贬低，观众对他们的兴趣也会逐渐减弱。但如果他们之间存在复杂的对立，就能激发观众的好奇心和同理心，从而吸引他们的注意力和精力。这就需要精心设计角色。接下来的五个部分将探讨来自主流叙事媒介的五个例子。

#↩

CASE STUDY: PRIDE AND PREJUDICE

案例研究：《傲慢与偏见》

Jane Austen’s basic cast design embraces the five Bennet sisters. Austen places Elizabeth, her complex protagonist, at the center and gives her four visible traits: cool rationality, social charm, self-esteem, and independence. To span Elizabeth’s dimensions, Austen then opposes these outer features with four inner qualities of impulse, private convictions, humility, and romantic longing.

简·奥斯汀的基本人物设定围绕着班纳特家的五姐妹展开。她将性格复杂的女主角伊丽莎白置于中心位置，并赋予她四个外在特征：冷静理性、社交魅力、自信和独立。为了更全面地展现伊丽莎白的性格，奥斯汀又用四个内在品质与这些外在特征形成对比：冲动、内心信念、谦逊和浪漫情怀。

These four contradictions—Rational/Impulsive, Social Charm / Private Conviction, Self-Esteem/Humility, Independence / Romantic Longing—set her dimensions and come into play as Austen links Elizabeth to a quartet of sisters: Jane, Mary, Kitty, and Lydia.

这四个矛盾——理性/冲动、社交魅力/私人信念、自尊/谦逊、独立/浪漫渴望——构成了她的维度，并在奥斯汀将伊丽莎白与四姐妹（简、玛丽、凯蒂和莉迪亚）联系起来的过程中发挥作用。

The personalities of her four siblings depend on their outer traits only. None of the four are dimensional; instead, each is flat and exactly who she seems to be. In a design of mutual oppositions, each sister’s traits define and highlight one of Elizabeth’s dimensions, while Elizabeth’s dimensions counterpoint their traits. These distinctions clarify and individualize all five characters.

她的四个兄弟姐妹的性格仅取决于外在特征。她们四人都缺乏立体感；相反，她们都十分扁平，表里如一。在一种相互对立的设计中，每个姐妹的特征都定义并突出了伊丽莎白性格的某个维度，而伊丽莎白的维度又与她们的特征形成对比。这些区别使五个人物形象更加清晰鲜明，个性鲜明。

#↩

1. Elizabeth and Jane

1. 伊丽莎白和简

Elizabeth’s core dimension pits intellect against impulse. At the novel’s inciting incident, she’s a woman with patient, mature insights into people. But when she meets Mr. Darcy, an impulsive, prejudicial judgment about the prideful gentleman (thus the title Pride and Prejudice ) suddenly contradicts her normally balanced acumen, turning her against Darcy and setting their story on its rocky road to love when she at last realizes that her private convictions are in fact prejudices, that her self-esteem is a synonym for pride, and that she and Darcy mirror each other.

伊丽莎白的核心特质在于理智与冲动的冲突。在小说开篇，她是一位耐心而成熟的女性，对人性有着深刻的洞察。然而，当她遇见达西先生后，她对这位骄傲的绅士产生了冲动而带有偏见的判断（这也是小说标题《傲慢与偏见》的由来），这种判断突然与她平日里冷静的判断力相悖，使她对达西心生敌意，并最终意识到自己内心的信念其实是偏见，自尊是骄傲的代名词，而她和达西彼此映照，他们的爱情之路也因此变得坎坷曲折。

Elizabeth’s Four Dimensions
伊丽莎白的四个维度

In clear contrast to Elizabeth’s sophisticated skepticism, Jane, her older sister, innocently trusts in the goodness of people. Jane’s fawn-like naïveté sharply diverges from her clear-eyed sister and leads to unfortunate choices.

与伊丽莎白老练的怀疑主义形成鲜明对比的是，她的姐姐简天真地相信人性的善良。简如同小鹿般懵懂无知的性格与她目光清澈的姐姐截然不同，并最终导致了不幸的选择。

#↩

2. Elizabeth and Mary

2. 伊丽莎白和玛丽

Elizabeth’s second dimension counterpoints her charming wit with moral conviction. Deep within, Elizabeth holds unambiguous ethical beliefs, but rather than bore or antagonize friends and family, she keeps them unseen and unspoken behind her smiling charisma.

伊丽莎白的另一面，除了她迷人的机智之外，还蕴藏着坚定的道德信念。在她内心深处，伊丽莎白拥有明确的道德准则，但她不会因此让亲朋好友感到厌烦或反感，而是将这些信念隐藏在她迷人的微笑背后，不为人知，也从不轻易表露。

Mary, on the other hand, irks people with her moralizing pedantry and pretentiousness. As a result, she has, unlike Elizabeth, no social life.

玛丽则恰恰相反，她那说教式的迂腐和自命不凡令人厌烦。因此，与伊丽莎白不同，她没有任何社交生活。

#↩

3. Elizabeth and Lydia

3. 伊丽莎白和莉迪亚

Elizabeth’s third dimension contradicts her spirited sense of self-worth with restrained, unaffected modesty.

伊丽莎白的第三维度与她充满活力的自我价值感形成鲜明对比，她表现得克制而朴实无华。

Lydia, conversely, puts her animal spirits on constant display, making her frivolous vanities and flirtations all the more immodest.

相反，莉迪亚总是毫不掩饰自己的天性，这使得她轻浮的虚荣心和轻佻的行为更加不得体。

#↩

4. Elizabeth and Kitty

4. 伊丽莎白和凯蒂

Elizabeth’s fourth dimension pits her willful independence against her equally strong romantic attraction to Mr. Darcy.

伊丽莎白的第四个维度体现了她任性的独立性与她对达西先生同样强烈的浪漫情愫之间的矛盾。

Kitty is her opposite: dependent, needy, weak willed, and easily reduced to tears.

Kitty 与她截然相反：依赖性强，需要人照顾，意志薄弱，动不动就哭。

Elizabeth’s intelligent, self-possessed calm contradicts the weak, frantic insecurities of her four sisters. In the scenes between the sisters, each evokes the contrasting traits of the others, so that the five become distinctive and memorable, all the while keeping Elizabeth solidly at the novel’s center.

伊丽莎白的聪慧沉稳与她四个姐妹的软弱和焦虑不安形成鲜明对比。在姐妹间的互动场景中，每个人都展现出其他姐妹截然不同的特质，使得这五个人个性鲜明、令人难忘，同时又始终将伊丽莎白牢牢地置于小说的中心位置。

Like Elizabeth, dimensions in highly complex characters crisscross between all four levels of self: social, personal, private, hidden. The more dimensions in a character, the more relationships she needs to delineate her complexities. Therefore, to activate your imagination as you develop each character and explore the interplay of your cast’s traits and dimensions, I suggest that you lay out a map of your cast’s traits and dimensions.

就像伊丽莎白一样，高度复杂的人物性格维度交织于自我的四个层面：社交层面、个人层面、私密层面和隐秘层面。人物的维度越多，她就需要越多的关系来展现其复杂性。因此，为了激发你的想象力，帮助你塑造每个角色，并探索角色特质和维度之间的相互作用，我建议你绘制一张角色特质和维度的地图。

#↩

Cast Map

施法地图

To map your cast’s interconnections, create three concentric circles. At the center of it place your protagonist. Because contradictions need performance time to reveal themselves to the reader/audience, give this character a majority of dimensions. The four-dimensional Elizabeth Bennet, for example, centers the cast map of Pride and Prejudice .

为了绘制出角色之间的相互关系，可以画出三个同心圆。将主角放在圆心。由于矛盾需要通过表演才能逐渐展现给读者/观众，因此要赋予主角较多的维度。例如，四维的伊丽莎白·班纳特就位于《傲慢与偏见》角色关系图的中心。

Around the first circle, distribute major supporting and servicing players, noting their traits and dimensions. Then counterpoint them with the protagonist. For example, the three-dimensional Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth’s four sisters:

围绕第一层，列出主要配角和服务角色，并注明他们的特征和侧重点。然后将他们与主角进行对比。例如，立体丰满的达西先生和伊丽莎白的四个姐妹：

Darcy (Prideful/Chastened, Arrogant/Kindhearted, Self-deceived/Self-aware), Jane (Innocent), Mary (Pedantic), Kitty (Immodest), Lydia (Dependent). Elizabeth brings out the three positive sides of Darcy.

达西（骄傲/受挫，傲慢/善良，自欺/自知），简（天真），玛丽（迂腐），凯蒂（放荡），莉迪亚（依赖）。伊丽莎白展现了达西身上三种积极的特质。

Because dimensions draw interest to a character and consume storytelling time to express, limit second circle roles to their distinctive traits only. For example: Mr. and Mrs. Bennet (anxious parents), Charles Bingley (amiable friend), Caroline Bingley (snobbish), Charlotte Lucas (sensible), William Collins (pompous), George Wickham (deceitful), Louisa Hurst (snobbish), Lady Catherine de Bourgh (imperious), Mr. and Mrs. Edward Gardiner (genteel).

因为人物的性格维度会吸引观众的注意力，并且会占用叙事时间来展现，所以第二层级的角色应该仅限于他们各自的独特特征。例如：班纳特夫妇（焦虑的父母）、查尔斯·宾利（和蔼可亲的朋友）、卡罗琳·宾利（势利眼）、夏洛特·卢卡斯（明智）、威廉·柯林斯（傲慢自大）、乔治·威克姆（狡诈）、路易莎·赫斯特（势利眼）、凯瑟琳·德·伯格夫人（专横跋扈）、爱德华·加德纳夫妇（温文尔雅）。

Third circle parts fill out the periphery: servants, villagers, tradesmen, and distant relatives.

第三圈的组成部分填充了外围：仆人、村民、商人、远房亲戚。

#↩

CASE STUDY: A FISH CALLED WANDA

案例研究：一条名叫旺达的鱼

A Fish Called Wanda was written by John Cleese and Charles Crichton. The Motion Picture Academy nominated them for Best Original Screenplay and Best Director, giving an Oscar to Kevin Kline for Best Supporting Actor. John Cleese and Michael Palin won BAFTAs for Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor. The British Film Institute ranks it among the greatest British films of the twentieth century. Its inspiration happened over lunch.

《一条名叫旺达的鱼》由约翰·克里斯和查尔斯·克莱顿编剧。美国电影艺术与科学学院提名他们角逐最佳原创剧本和最佳导演奖，凯文·克莱恩凭借此片荣获奥斯卡最佳男配角奖。约翰·克里斯和迈克尔·帕林分别凭借此片荣获英国电影学院奖最佳男主角和最佳男配角奖。英国电影协会将其列为二十世纪最伟大的英国电影之一。这部电影的创作灵感源于一次午餐。

One day, as the two worked together on a corporate video, Cleese, who graduated in law from Cambridge University, remarked that he’d always dreamed of playing a barrister. Crichton responded that he’d always dreamed of directing a scene with a steamroller in it. They decided to coauthor a screenplay containing both a barrister and a steamroller.

一天，两人一起制作企业宣传片时，毕业于剑桥大学法学院的克里斯·克莱斯说，他一直梦想扮演一名律师。克莱顿回应说，他一直梦想执导一场有压路机出现的戏。于是，他们决定合作创作一个剧本，剧本里既有律师也有压路机。

Cleese then mused this bit of whimsy: A man who loves dogs can’t stop killing them. Crichton naturally asked the logical question, Why? Answer: He’s actually trying to kill the dogs’ owner and keeps missing. Why is he trying to kill the owner? Because she’s a witness. A witness to what? A robbery. And on they went to satirize film noir plots into a delightful “crimedy.”

克里斯接着抛出了一个奇思妙想：一个爱狗的男人总是忍不住杀狗。克莱顿自然而然地问了一个合乎逻辑的问题：为什么？答案是：他其实是想杀狗的主人，但总是失手。他为什么要杀主人？因为她是目击证人。目睹了什么？抢劫案。于是，他们继续用黑色电影的桥段，创作了一部妙趣横生的“犯罪喜剧”。

#↩

Story

故事

Wanda, an American con artist, and Otto, her boyfriend, plan to double-cross George, a London gangster, and his partner, Ken. After the four of them pull a multi-million-dollar diamond heist, Wanda and Otto immediately rat George out to the police, but then discover that he has triple-crossed them by secretly hiding the diamonds.

美国女骗子旺达和她的男友奥托计划背叛伦敦黑帮老大乔治和他的同伙肯。四人成功劫走价值数百万美元的钻石后，旺达和奥托立即向警方告发了乔治，却发现乔治已经三重背叛了他们，他竟然秘密藏匿了钻石。

Wanda gets a lead on George’s stash when she discovers a safe deposit box key in Ken’s fish tank and hides it in her pendant. Next, the film adds a Love Story subplot when Wanda seduces George’s barrister, Archie, hoping to learn the diamonds’ whereabouts from him. But then she accidently loses her pendant in Archie’s house and Archie’s wife, Wendy, mistakes it for a gift from Archie.

旺达在肯的鱼缸里发现了一把保险箱钥匙，并将其藏在自己的吊坠里，由此获得了乔治藏匿钻石的线索。接下来，影片加入了一条爱情副线：旺达勾引了乔治的律师阿奇，希望从他口中套取钻石的下落。然而，她却意外地在阿奇家遗失了吊坠，阿奇的妻子温迪误以为这是阿奇送给她的礼物。

George tells Ken to kill the only eyewitness to the robbery, Mrs. Coady, a mean old lady who owns three pocket dogs. Ken tries to knock her off three times over, but each time he accidentally kills one of her dogs instead. He finally succeeds when he crushes the third dog under a massive construction block and the horrifying sight gives Coady a fatal heart attack.

乔治命令肯杀掉抢劫案的唯一目击证人科迪太太，她是个刻薄的老太太，养了三条宠物狗。肯三次试图干掉她，但每次都误杀了她的一条狗。最后，他用一块巨大的建筑砖块压死了第三条狗，科迪太太被这可怕的景象吓得心脏病发作，当场死亡。

With no witness, George is ready for release from jail, so he tells Ken where he hid the diamonds as they plan their getaway. But in a courtroom hearing, Wanda double-crosses George. Stunned, Archie inadvertently calls her “darling.” Wendy, watching from the gallery, realizes that Archie had an affair with Wanda and ends their marriage.

由于没有目击证人，乔治即将出狱，于是他告诉肯他藏钻石的地方，两人开始计划逃跑。但在法庭听证会上，旺达背叛了乔治。震惊之余，阿奇无意中叫了她“亲爱的”。旁听席上的温迪意识到阿奇和旺达有染，于是结束了他们的婚姻。

Meanwhile, Otto tortures Ken and learns that the jewels are hidden in a hotel safe deposit box. Otto knows the hiding place and Wanda has the key to the box, so they join forces.

与此同时，奥托拷问肯，得知珠宝藏在一家酒店的保险箱里。奥托知道保险箱的藏匿地点，而旺达有钥匙，于是他们联手行动。

Archie resolves to cut his losses, steal the loot, and flee to South America with Wanda. He pulls her into his Jag and they race to Ken’s flat. But when Archie runs into Ken’s building, Otto steals Archie’s car, taking Wanda with him.

阿奇决定及时止损，偷走赃款，带着旺达逃往南美。他把旺达拉进自己的捷豹车，两人飞驰到肯的公寓。但当阿奇冲进肯的公寓楼时，奥托偷走了阿奇的车，并带走了旺达。

Ken and Archie give chase. Otto and Wanda recover the diamonds, but Wanda double-crosses Otto, knocking him unconscious in a broom closet. Otto recovers and sprints for Wanda’s plane, but Archie confronts him on the airport tarmac. Otto is just about to shoot Archie when Ken runs him over with a steamroller. Archie and Wanda reunite aboard the plane.

肯和阿奇追了上去。奥托和旺达找回了钻石，但旺达背叛了奥托，把他打晕在杂物间里。奥托醒来后冲向旺达的飞机，但在机场停机坪上被阿奇拦住。奥托正要开枪打死阿奇时，肯开着压路机把他碾了过去。阿奇和旺达在飞机上重逢。

Here is the A Fish Called Wanda cast map, setting out their obsessions and dimensions:

以下是《一条名叫旺达的鱼》的角色关系图，列出了他们的执念和性格特点：

As we saw in Chapter Thirteen, comic characters are marked by a blind obsession, a rigid behavior they do not see in themselves and from which they cannot deviate.

正如我们在第十三章中所看到的，喜剧人物的特点是盲目的痴迷，一种他们自己看不到的、也无法摆脱的僵化行为。

Archie Leach (John Cleese) obsesses on his fear of embarrassment. Once he realizes this, however, he takes on the “Cary Grant” role and becomes the film’s romantic lead. (Archie Leach was Cary Grant’s real name.)

阿奇·利奇（约翰·克里斯饰）极度害怕尴尬。然而，当他意识到这一点后，他便扮演了“加里·格兰特”的角色，成为了影片的男主角。（阿奇·利奇正是加里·格兰特的真名。）

Archie’s three dimensions:
阿奇的三个维度：
He’s fearful and courageous. At first, he’s frightened of the mad Otto but eventually finds the courage to face him.
他既胆怯又勇敢。起初，他害怕疯子奥托，但最终鼓起勇气面对他。
He’s a lawyer and a criminal. Many people would not see that as a contradiction, but in Archie’s case it is. He’s devoted to the law but commits crimes for love.
他既是律师又是罪犯。很多人可能不觉得这有什么矛盾，但对阿奇来说，这的确是个矛盾。他忠于法律，却为了爱情而犯罪。
He’s devoted to others but then to himself. He works for his wife, daughter, and clients, denying himself, but once he falls for Wanda, he finally fights for what he wants out of life.
他一心为他人，却又偏袒自己。他为了妻子、女儿和客户拼命工作，牺牲自己，但自从爱上旺达后，他终于开始为自己想要的生活而奋斗。

Wanda Gershwitz (Jamie Lee Curtis) obsesses on men who speak foreign languages.

旺达·格什维茨（杰米·李·柯蒂斯饰）对会说外语的男人着迷。

Wanda’s two dimensions:
旺达的两个维度：
She’s sexually calculating and sexually impulsive. Smarter by far than any of the male characters, she uses her charms to manipulate them, occasionally falling prey to her blind obsession.
她性情狡诈，性冲动。她比任何男性角色都聪明得多，利用自己的魅力操纵他们，有时也会陷入盲目的迷恋之中。
She’s devoted to herself but then to Archie. Money is her only object of desire, but then she falls for Archie and gives him her heart.
她一心只想着自己，但后来又爱上了阿奇。金钱是她唯一的追求，但她最终还是爱上了阿奇，并将自己的心交给了他。

Otto West (Kevin Kline) obsesses on Nietzsche.

奥托·韦斯特（凯文·克莱恩饰）痴迷于尼采。

Otto’s two dimensions:
奥托的两个维度：
He’s intelligent but ignorant. Otto is an ex-CIA operative who quotes Nietzschean philosophy but thinks that the London Underground is a political movement.
他聪明却无知。奥托曾是中央情报局特工，他引用尼采的哲学思想，却认为伦敦地铁是一场政治运动。
He’s clever but confused. Otto thinks quickly under pressure and lies with easy skill but loses focus during conversations and can’t remember the “middle thing.”
他很聪明，但思维混乱。奥托在压力下思维敏捷，撒谎也游刃有余，但在谈话中却容易走神，记不住“中间发生的事情”。

Ken Pile (Michael Palin) obsesses on animal welfare.

肯·派尔（迈克尔·帕林饰）痴迷于动物福利。

Ken’s one dimension:
肯的单一维度：
He loves animals to the point of obsession but disdains people. He feels a tragic loss when an animal dies, sending him to the pet cemetery in tears and grief, but he happily kills a human being on the street.
他热爱动物到了痴迷的程度，却鄙视人类。当动物死去时，他会感到无比悲痛，泪流满面地前往宠物墓地；然而，他却会毫不犹豫地在大街上杀死一个人。

George Thomason (Tom Georgeson) obsesses on crime as a white-collar profession.

乔治·托马森（汤姆·乔治森饰）痴迷于将犯罪视为一种白领职业。

George’s one dimension:
乔治的单一维度：
He’s icy and volcanic. George is cool, calculating, ruthless, dapper, and devoted to his criminal trade, but when Wanda double-crosses him in a courtroom, his rage exposes him to the world.
他冷若冰霜，却又怒火中烧。乔治冷静、精于算计、冷酷无情、衣着考究，并且一心扑在犯罪事业上，但当旺达在法庭上背叛他时，他的愤怒让他暴露在世人面前。

Wendy Leach (Maria Aitken) obsesses on her superiority. She’s aristocratic, arrogant, and unloving toward others, even her daughter.

温蒂·利奇（玛丽亚·艾特肯饰）极度自负。她傲慢自大，目空一切，甚至对自己的女儿也冷酷无情。

Portia Leach (Cynthia Cleese) obsesses on her nose. Her key trait is self-centeredness.

波西亚·利奇（辛西娅·克里斯饰）对自己的鼻子非常在意。她的主要特点是自我中心。

Eileen Coady (Patricia Hayes) obsesses on her dogs. Her dominant trait is irritability.

艾琳·科迪（帕特里夏·海耶斯饰）对她的狗非常痴迷。她最主要的性格特点是易怒。

The rest of the cast contains prosecutors, a judge, jewelers, locksmith, clerks, clients, jailors, and passersby.

其余角色包括检察官、法官、珠宝商、锁匠、职员、委托人、狱警和路人。

#↩

Conclusion

结论

Although critics rarely take comedy seriously, all well-told stories make meaning. The controlling idea of A Fish Called Wanda is that you, too, could end up in Rio de Janeiro with $20 million in diamonds and the lover of your dreams if you’re willing to throw away your career and your family.

尽管评论家很少认真对待喜剧，但所有精彩的故事都蕴含意义。《一条名叫旺达的鱼》的核心思想是：如果你愿意放弃事业和家庭，你也有可能带着价值2000万美元的钻石和梦寐以求的爱人，在里约热内卢过上奢华的生活。

#↩

CASE STUDY: SLAVE PLAY

案例研究：奴隶游戏

A play by Jeremy O. Harris
杰里米·O·哈里斯的剧作

Slave Play is a modern allegory. The title suggests a drama about slavery but also hints at whips and bondage, welts and orgasms. Individually, its characters seem realistic as they grapple with intimate, personal problems, but at the same time they symbolize a range of types caught up in the eternal conflict between the powerful and the powerless.

《奴隶游戏》是一部现代寓言。片名暗示这是一部关于奴隶制的戏剧，同时也影射了鞭笞、束缚、鞭痕和性高潮。片中人物各自真实可信，他们努力应对着私密的个人问题；但与此同时，他们也象征着形形色色的人群，这些人身陷于强权与弱者之间永恒的冲突之中。

Jeremy Harris began writing Slave Play while a student at Yale University. It opened off-Broadway in 2018 and sparked immediate controversy. The following year it moved to Broadway, where it played to sold-out houses until COVID-19 closed all theatres.

杰里米·哈里斯在耶鲁大学就读期间开始创作《奴隶游戏》。该剧于2018年在外百老汇首演，立即引发争议。次年，该剧移师百老汇，场场爆满，直到新冠疫情导致所有剧院关闭。

Slave Play raises these questions: What drives racism? Why is America’s racial ménage so dysfunctional? Is it nature or nurture? Power-hungry impulses in the human psyche? Or the tyrannical social institutions of segregation and mass incarceration? To seek answers, the play casts four troubled interracial couples.

《奴隶游戏》提出了这些问题：种族主义的根源是什么？为什么美国的种族关系如此失衡？是先天因素还是后天因素？是人类心理中对权力的渴望？还是种族隔离和大规模监禁等专制的社会制度？为了探寻答案，该剧选取了四对陷入困境的跨种族伴侣作为主角。

The play’s black characters burn with the history of racial trauma, but their white lovers don’t, can’t, or won’t see it or feel it. Although they genuinely care for their black partners, they either ignore their blackness or find it charmingly erotic. And if the black partners felt safe to express what they suffer, would their white lovers ever see it and get it? Or are black lovers condemned to live forever in their partners’ blind spots? The effect of this impasse on the black characters is anhedonia, the inability to feel sexual pleasure.

剧中的黑人角色饱受种族创伤的历史折磨，但他们的白人伴侣却对此视而不见、无法理解，或者根本不愿面对。尽管他们真心关爱自己的黑人伴侣，却要么忽视他们的肤色，要么觉得这充满魅力，甚至带有情色意味。如果黑人伴侣能够安心地表达自己的痛苦，他们的白人伴侣是否终有一天能够理解？难道黑人伴侣注定要永远活在伴侣的盲点之中吗？这种僵局对黑人角色造成的后果是快感缺失，即无法感受到性愉悦。

The play takes place on a former Virginia plantation. Its multiplot design crosscuts three story lines of conflicted interracial couples: Phillip and Alana, Gary and Dustin, Kaneisha and Jim. Two supporting characters in a lesbian interracial coupleship, Teá and Patricia, help build the play’s tensions, but their relationship never develops into a plot.

该剧的故事发生在弗吉尼亚州的一处昔日种植园。它采用多线叙事结构，交织讲述了三对跨种族情侣的冲突故事：菲利普和阿拉娜、加里和达斯汀、凯妮莎和吉姆。剧中还有一对跨种族女同性恋伴侣——蒂娅和帕特里夏，她们的出现也为剧情增添了张力，但她们的关系并未发展成一条主线。

The three acts go like this:

这三幕的结构如下：

#↩

Act One—“Work”

第一幕——“工作”

Act One plays out three vignettes of sadomasochistic seduction and copulation. The three couples, dressed in antebellum garb, act out brutal, sexually raw conflicts that seem genuinely nineteenth century, although occasional touches of modern music, modern names, and anachronistic dialogue seep in:

第一幕展现了三段虐恋式的诱惑和性交场景。三对身着南北战争前服饰的男女，演绎着残酷而原始的性冲突，这些冲突看似真实地展现了十九世纪的风貌，尽管偶尔穿插着现代音乐、现代人名和时代错置的对话：

Scene 1: A slave named Kaneisha calls her overseer “Massa Jim” and asks if he is going to beat her. Jim wonders why she’d think such a thing, and Kaneisha replies, “You got that whip, ain’tcha?” Jim has had no training with a whip, so when he tries to crack it, he hits himself in the face. To seduce him, Kaneisha eats off the floor and twerks.

场景一：一个名叫凯妮莎的奴隶称呼她的监工“吉姆老爷”，问他是不是要打她。吉姆不明白她为什么会这么想，凯妮莎回答说：“你有鞭子吧？”吉姆没受过鞭子的训练，所以当他试图挥动鞭子时，却打到了自己的脸。为了引诱他，凯妮莎趴在地上吃东西，还跳起了扭臀舞。

Scene 2: Alana, a sexually frustrated Southern belle, flounces seductively on her canopied bed, flourishing a formidable black dildo. Phillip, her handsome, light-skinned slave, services her lust as she forcibly penetrates his anus with her dildo.

场景二：性欲得不到满足的南方佳丽阿兰娜，在她那张带顶篷的床上搔首弄姿，手中挥舞着一根硕大的黑色假阳具。她英俊的白皙奴隶菲利普，在她用假阳具强行插入他肛门时，满足了她的欲望。

Scene 3: In the plantation’s barn, Dustin, a white indentured servant, bales hay in the shadow of Gary, a threatening black overseer. As Dustin rebels, the violence morphs into virtual rape. When Dustin licks Gary’s boots, Gary comes, then breaks into tears.

第三幕：在种植园的谷仓里，白人契约劳工达斯汀在黑人监工加里的阴影下捆扎干草。加里面目狰狞，令人胆寒。达斯汀反抗后，暴力演变成近乎强奸。当达斯汀舔舐加里的靴子时，加里射精了，然后嚎啕大哭。

Suddenly, a powerful turning point sends Teá and Patricia, two clipboard-carrying psychotherapists, bursting into the room, revealing that the three vignettes were actually exercises in sex therapy for interracial couples.

突然，剧情急转直下，两位手持写字板的心理治疗师蒂亚和帕特里夏冲进房间，揭露这三个小故事实际上是针对跨种族夫妇的性治疗练习。

#↩

Act Two—“Process”

第二幕——“过程”

The psychologists believe that their radical remedy, known as Antebellum Sexual Performance Therapy, cures anhedonia as it “helps black partners reengage intimately with the white partners from whom they no longer receive sexual pleasure.” But as Teá and Patricia “process” the three couples through their slave-master experiences, the real selves behind Act One’s sadomasochistic fantasy roles look each other in the eye and inflict pains far worse than whips, boots, and dildoes. One by one, the six deliver cutting insights into the clashes between their real-life selves and their hidden selves, between what terrifies them and what tantalizes them.

心理学家们认为，他们提出的激进疗法——“战前性爱表现疗法”——能够治愈快感缺失症，因为它“帮助黑人伴侣重新与不再从中获得性快感的白人伴侣建立亲密关系”。然而，当蒂亚和帕特里夏引导这三对伴侣回顾他们作为奴隶主的经历时，第一幕中那些虐恋幻想角色背后真实的自我开始彼此对视，并造成远比鞭子、靴子和假阳具更可怕的痛苦。六个人逐一深刻地剖析了他们现实生活中的自我与隐藏的自我之间的冲突，以及恐惧与诱惑之间的矛盾。

This, for example, from the usually reticent Phillip: “So, like, are you saying that my… um… the reason I can’t get it up… the reason I don’t come is because of… just, like, racism?” Throughout the play, lines like this inflict the pleasures of pain, causing delight and damage.

例如，一向沉默寡言的菲利普就曾说过这样的话：“所以，你是说我……嗯……我勃起不了……我射不出来是因为……种族歧视吗？”在整部剧中，诸如此类的台词都体现了痛苦与快感并存的矛盾，既带来愉悦，也造成伤害。

As Act Two builds, psychotherapy becomes psychotorture. Rather than curing racist wounds, the therapeutic experiment inflames them. Partner turns on partner; the “process” crashes and burns; masks fall; core selves strip naked. The Phillip-Alana and Gary-Dustin plots climax to bring down the Act Two curtain. This leaves Kaneisha-Jim, the play’s dominant story line, to carry Act Three.

随着第二幕的展开，心理治疗逐渐演变成精神折磨。这场治疗实验非但没有治愈种族创伤，反而火上浇油。伴侣反目成仇；“治疗过程”彻底崩溃；伪装被揭穿；真实的自我赤裸裸地暴露出来。菲利普-阿兰娜和加里-达斯汀的阴谋最终走向高潮，为第二幕画上句号。这使得卡尼莎-吉姆这条贯穿全剧的主线，得以在第三幕中继续展开。

#↩

Act Three—“Exorcise”

第三幕——“驱魔”

The last act paints a fierce portrait of a racial dilemma. Alone in a bedroom with Jim, Kaneisha struggles to understand her visceral distaste for her husband. He worries that the therapy traumatized her, and he’s right but for reasons he doesn’t understand.

最后一幕生动地描绘了一个种族困境。卡尼莎独自一人和吉姆待在卧室里，她难以理解自己对丈夫发自内心的厌恶。吉姆担心治疗给她造成了创伤，他的担心不无道理，但他自己却不明白个中缘由。

Initially Kaneisha was attracted to Jim’s whiteness because he’s British and so unmarred by American prejudices. In time, she came to realize that because he’s white, he carries an invisible whip, and because she’s black, her hands are empty. The power is his, just as simple as that. This hard truth he denies. She wants him to see it; he won’t listen.

起初，凯妮莎被吉姆的白人身份所吸引，因为他是英国人，不受美国偏见的影响。但随着时间的推移，她逐渐意识到，正因为他是白人，他才拥有无形的权力；而因为她是黑人，她却一无所有。权力在他手中，就这么简单。他却否认这个残酷的真相。她想让他明白，但他却充耳不闻。

At the play’s climax, they suddenly replay their sadomasochistic master and slave selves from Act One. When their rape improv becomes too violent, Kaneisha shouts the safe word. As they slowly return to normal, she thanks him for listening. Curtain.

在剧的高潮部分，他们突然重现了第一幕中施虐受虐的主奴角色。当他们即兴的强奸戏变得过于暴力时，凯妮莎喊出了安全词。随着他们慢慢恢复正常，她感谢他倾听。幕落。

The play reveals the characters’ dual identities, dividing them into Act One’s symbolic selves, contradicted by Act Two’s core selves, merged in Act Three as their core selves fuse with their symbolic selves—two completed characters.

该剧揭示了人物的双重身份，将他们分为第一幕的象征性自我，与第二幕的核心自我相矛盾，并在第三幕中融合，核心自我与象征性自我融合——两个完整的人物。

#↩

Cast

投掷

To shape his cast, Jeremy Harris created a spectrum of character awareness ranging from sharp insight to dull blindness. At one end stands Kaneisha, who’s painfully self-aware and black; at the far end is Jim, who’s happily self-deceived and white. The other six roles symbolize various mental types along a continuum of attitudes toward blackness: Gary hates being black; Patricia ignores her blackness; Teá intellectualizes her blackness; Phillip transcends blackness; Dustin loves blackness; Alana finds blackness erotic.

为了塑造他的演员阵容，杰里米·哈里斯创造了一个角色意识光谱，从敏锐的洞察力到迟钝的盲目。一端是痛苦地自我认知、身为黑人的凯妮莎；另一端是乐于自欺欺人的白人吉姆。其他六个角色象征着对黑人身份态度上的各种心理类型：加里憎恨自己的黑人身份；帕特里夏忽视自己的黑人身份；蒂娅理性地看待自己的黑人身份；菲利普超越了黑人身份；达斯汀热爱黑人身份；阿拉娜则觉得黑人身份充满情欲。

Before we map the cast, let’s review the eight roles from least complex to the most.

在介绍演员阵容之前，让我们先回顾一下这八个角色，从最简单到最复杂。

Patricia and Teá

帕特里夏和蒂亚

Patricia and Teá, a duet of therapists, speak in mind-numbing psychobabble. When they refer to feelings, they talk about “processing materials in psychic spaces and communication spheres.” They indulge in jargon such as “materiality” and “positionality.” Black people become “minoritarians”; white society is “heteropatriarchal.”

治疗师二人组帕特里夏和蒂娅满口晦涩难懂的心理学术语。她们谈到感受时，会说“在心理空间和沟通领域处理素材”。她们沉迷于“物质性”、“立场性”之类的行话。黑人变成了“少数族裔”；白人社会是“异性恋父权制”。

The team researches the abrasive effects of racism, then re-inflicts them on their subjects with blindly dangerous experiments. Although they seem empathetic and caring, the real reason they take notes on psychological pain is to gather data for monographs. To them, science outweighs solace. This inner/outer contradiction between seemingly sensitive beliefs and insensitive science strikes the first dimension in both women.

这个团队研究种族主义的毒害作用，然后通过盲目而危险的实验，将这些毒害作用重新施加在受试者身上。尽管他们表面上富有同情心和关怀，但他们记录心理痛苦的真正目的是为了收集数据撰写专著。对他们而言，科学比慰藉更重要。这种看似敏感的信念与冷酷无情的科学之间的内在矛盾，触动了这两位女性的第一层心理。

A second contradiction between true character and characterization, between reality and appearance adds a layer of complexity to each. The light-brown-skinned Patricia secretly feels she’s white, mirroring Dustin who’s white but claims he’s black. The coolly professional but inwardly troubled Teá wishes she were, like Phillip, detached. These unfulfilled wishes give both women their second dimension: a secure professional self versus an insecure personal self.

真实性格与人物塑造、现实与表象之间的第二个矛盾，为两人都增添了一层复杂性。肤色浅棕的帕特里夏内心深处觉得自己是白人，这与达斯汀如出一辙——达斯汀是白人，却自称是黑人。冷静专业的蒂娅内心却饱受煎熬，她渴望像菲利普一样超脱尘世。这些未实现的愿望赋予了两位女性双重性格：她们拥有自信的职业形象，却又缺乏安全感。

Phillip

菲利普

Phillip is powerfully built, mixed-race, model handsome, educated but none too bright. Alana, his white girlfriend, talks for him, keeping him in the background. He believes race doesn’t matter and sees himself as a “superhuman dude beyond black and white.” Stuck between his dominating partner and his a-racial identity, he suffers anhedonia. His core dimension makes him sexy to behold but at heart unsexed.

菲利普身材魁梧，混血儿，长相俊美，受过高等教育，但头脑并不聪明。他的白人女友阿兰娜替他说话，让他始终处于幕后。他认为种族无关紧要，并自诩为“超越黑白的超人”。夹在强势的女友和无种族身份之间，他饱受快感缺失的折磨。他外表性感，内心却缺乏性欲。

Alana

阿兰娜

In Act One, Alana plays a nervous, horny, wild plantation dominatrix who yearns to sodomize her house slave and does, confessing, “It was hot for me, really hot.” During the next act, however, she reverts to a hand-raising, note-taking student. When this A-type perfectionist finally glimpses the truth of her relationship, that her deliberate blindness to Phillip’s race has ruined their love, she suddenly retreats into denial, repeating “It wasn’t racial” like a mantra.

在第一幕中，阿兰娜扮演一位紧张、好色、狂野的种植园女主人，她渴望鸡奸自己的男奴，并最终得逞，坦白道：“我当时很兴奋，真的非常兴奋。”然而，在第二幕中，她却变回了举手认真记笔记的学生。当这位A型完美主义者最终看清了她与菲利普关系的真相——她刻意对菲利普的种族视而不见毁了他们的爱情——她突然又陷入了否认，像念咒语一样反复念叨着“这不是种族歧视”。

Her dimensions pit curiosity against self-deception, and a hypercontrolled manner against an out-of-control sex drive.

她的性格矛盾之处在于：好奇心与自欺欺人、高度自律与失控的性欲。

Gary

加里

Gary hates being black. His stifled, lifelong, slow-burning rage hides behind a mask of quiet resentment. In Act One’s fantasy play, he forces Dustin, his lover of nearly a decade, to lick his boots, and then comes in a shuddering climax. His core dimension pits inner rage against outer cool.

加里憎恨自己的黑人身份。他压抑已久、日积月累的愤怒，隐藏在平静的怨恨面具之下。在第一幕的幻想游戏中，他强迫与他相恋近十年的爱人达斯汀舔他的靴子，然后在颤抖的高潮中达到高潮。他内心深处的愤怒与外在的冷静形成了鲜明的对比。

Dustin

达斯汀

Dustin hates being white. He could be Hispanic or Sicilian but swears he’s black. His partner, Gary, can’t see him as anything but white; still, the narcissistic Dustin argues that the evidence is obvious. When finally forced to confront his truth, Dustin throws a diva tantrum, shouting, “There are shades between!” He wears his dimension on his sleeve: a white man insisting he’s black.

达斯汀讨厌自己是白人。他可能是西班牙裔或西西里裔，但他坚称自己是黑人。他的伴侣加里只能把他看作白人；然而，自恋的达斯汀却坚持认为证据显而易见。当最终被迫面对真相时，达斯汀像个耍大牌的明星一样大发脾气，喊道：“肤色之间还有深浅不一的色调呢！”他把自己的真实身份毫不掩饰：一个白人却坚持说自己是黑人。

Jim

吉姆

In Act One, Jim plays Kaneisha’s reluctant master, but when he orders her to eat off the floor, he shivers with lust. He calls her his “queen” and that, by implication, makes him a king, and kings rule queens.

在第一幕中，吉姆扮演凯妮莎不情愿的主人，但当他命令她吃掉地上的食物时，他却因欲望而颤抖。他称她为他的“女王”，这暗示着他自己就是国王，而国王统治女王。

In the play’s last minutes, the truth he’s been suppressing arcs into awareness: A white man always has greater power. Finally, he hears Kaneisha plead and gives her the rough sex she wants. As he assured her, “We’re on the same ground. Only difference is, I am, you know, your manager.” An inner dimension cuts through Jim: Consciously he loves his wife; subconsciously he loves punishing her.

在剧终的最后几分钟，他一直压抑的真相终于浮出水面：白人男性总是拥有更大的权力。最终，他听到了凯妮莎的恳求，满足了她想要的粗暴性爱。他向她保证：“我们地位平等。唯一的区别是，你知道，我是你的经理。”吉姆内心深处涌现出一个念头：他理智上爱着妻子；潜意识里，他却喜欢惩罚她。

Kaneisha

兼井社

White demons haunt Kaneisha. Nonetheless, in Act One’s fantasy play, she begs Jim to call her “negress.” Then mingling fear with lust, she slips into the role of “bed wench.” In Act Three, she takes their role-playing even further, forcing Jim to admit that, although genuinely loving, he is a sadistic white devil. As she lures him into playing that part, she arcs from fantasy to reality, revealing that the masochist she portrayed in Act One is in fact her true self. As the contradiction between her improv self and her true self dissolves, she ends the play a completed character.

白人恶魔萦绕着凯妮莎。然而，在第一幕的幻想剧中，她恳求吉姆称她为“黑妞”。随后，恐惧与欲望交织，她扮演起了“床伴”的角色。在第三幕中，她将角色扮演推向极致，迫使吉姆承认，尽管他真心爱她，却是一个虐待狂般的白人恶魔。随着她引诱他扮演这个角色，她的内心也从幻想走向现实，揭示出她在第一幕中扮演的受虐狂其实是她真实的自我。当她即兴表演的自我与真实的自我之间的矛盾消解时，她以一个完整的人物形象结束了整部剧。

Given these relationships, the play’s cast map looks like this:

基于这些关系，该剧的演员表如下所示：

Racist society forms the third circle.

种族主义社会构成了第三个圈子。

Teá and Patricia (sensitive/insensitive, secure/insecure) are on opposite sides of the second circle.

Teá 和 Patricia（敏感/不敏感，有安全感/无安全感）位于第二个圆圈的两侧。

This surrounds three separate inner circles: one containing Gary/Dustin (inner rage / outer cool, hates white / hates black); another with Phillip/Alana (sexed/unsexed, sighted/blind, overcontrolled/out-of-control); and a third holding Kaneisha/Jim (self-aware/self-deceived, loving/punishing, sadist/masochist) that’s slightly larger than the other two to signify that theirs is the central plot.

这围绕着三个独立的内圈：一个包含 Gary/Dustin（内心愤怒/外表冷静，憎恨白色/憎恨黑色）；另一个包含 Phillip/Alana（性欲旺盛/性冷淡，视力正常/视力障碍，过度控制/失控）；第三个包含 Kaneisha/Jim（自我意识清醒/自我欺骗，充满爱意/惩罚他人，施虐者/受虐者），这个内圈比其他两个略大，以表明他们的故事是中心情节。

#↩

Conclusion

结论

Slave Play ’s title nails its meaning: Slavery puts sadomasochism into action. The massive wealth that slavery created was simply the side effect of mankind’s darkest desire. Money is a means, not an end. The deep-seated cause of slavery—or, for that matter, the oppression of any underclass—is the lust for power and the pleasure of pain, aka sadomasochism.

《奴隶游戏》这个标题一针见血地指出了它的含义：奴隶制将虐恋付诸实践。奴隶制创造的巨额财富仅仅是人类最黑暗欲望的副产品。金钱只是手段，而非目的。奴隶制——或者说，任何对底层阶级的压迫——的根源在于对权力的渴望和对痛苦的快感，也就是虐恋。

Flash back to the issue of motivation raised in Chapter Eight: “Why do people do the things they do?” Over the centuries, philosophers and psychologists have sought a single grand answer to that grand question. Sigmund Freud said it was all about sex; Alfred Adler said it was all about power; Ernest Becker said it was all about death. When you think about it, sex and power are actually about death—just two ways to either defeat it by reproducing yourself or control it by defeating your enemies. So I go with Becker.

回到第八章提出的动机问题：“人们为什么会做他们所做的事情？”几个世纪以来，哲学家和心理学家一直在寻求对这个宏大问题的终极答案。西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说一切都与性有关；阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒说一切都与权力有关；欧内斯特·贝克尔说一切都与死亡有关。仔细想想，性和权力实际上都与死亡有关——只不过是两种战胜死亡的方式：一种是通过繁衍后代，另一种是通过击败敌人来控制死亡。所以我赞同贝克尔的观点。

Sadomasochism follows this path: Fear is a trembling emotion that grips us when we don’t know what’s going to happen. Dread is a terrible awareness that floods the mind when we know what’s going to happen, but there’s nothing we can do to stop it. At an early age, we discover that death is a fact of life. Sooner or later, we’re going to die and there’s nothing we can do to change that fact. Some handle death-dread better than others, but all feel it.

虐恋遵循这样的路径：恐惧是一种颤抖的情绪，当我们不知道将会发生什么时，它会攫住我们。而惊恐则是一种可怕的认知，当我们知道将会发生什么，却无力阻止时，它会充斥我们的脑海。我们很小的时候就发现，死亡是生命的一部分。迟早有一天，我们会死去，而我们无法改变这个事实。有些人比其他人更能承受对死亡的恐惧，但所有人都会感受到它。

At some point, a child may discover that power makes her feel better… at least for the moment. Perhaps she crushes the life out of an insect and suddenly feels a rush of pleasure. For an instant, a godlike power over life and death ignites her body. She wants to repeat that pleasure, more and more often, to a greater and greater degree. As she seeks power, her personality—at times, at least—leans toward the sadistic, toward someone who bends the dread of death to her will by usurping power over death. Slave owners felt that rush every day; the ultrarich still do.

在某个时刻，一个孩子可能会发现权力能让她感觉更好……至少在那一刻是这样。也许她会捏死一只昆虫，然后突然感到一阵快感。那一瞬间，一种掌控生死的神力在她体内燃烧。她想要重复这种快感，越来越频繁，越来越强烈。随着她对权力的追求，她的性格——至少在某些时候——会倾向于虐待狂，倾向于通过篡夺死亡的权力来驾驭对死亡的恐惧。奴隶主每天都能感受到这种快感；超级富豪们至今仍然如此。

Or, perhaps the child discovers that she is powerless and always will be but can still enjoy an escape from the anxiety of death if she shelters in the shadow of someone powerful. So long as that person exhibits their power by making her suffer, she feels the masochistic comfort of a temporary release from dread, aka the pleasure of pain. Slaves felt that thrill when they bowed to their masters; employees still feel it when they applaud their boss. 1

或者，也许孩子发现自己无能为力，而且永远如此，但如果她躲在某个强者的阴影下，仍然可以暂时逃避死亡的焦虑。只要那个人通过让她受苦来展现自己的力量，她就能感受到一种受虐式的快感，暂时摆脱恐惧，也就是痛苦的愉悦。奴隶在向主人鞠躬时感受到了这种快感；员工在为老板鼓掌时仍然能感受到这种快感。

Harris’s drama speaks wisely and wittily about personal politics. As will your writing, if you give power room to play. For no matter how you set up your story—a cast of thousands to a pair of lovers—power will ebb and flow. Weigh, therefore, the balance of power in your cast members as you open the telling, then follow the dynamic of change (Who’s up? Who’s down?) to the final scene. Playing with power as you shape a cast often inspires the unexpected.

哈里斯的戏剧以睿智而诙谐的方式探讨了个人政治。如果你给予权力足够的发挥空间，你的写作也能做到这一点。无论你如何构建故事——从成千上万的角色到一对恋人——权力都会此消彼长。因此，在故事开篇，就要权衡角色之间的权力平衡，然后跟随权力变化的动态（谁强势？谁弱势？）直至最后一幕。在塑造角色时巧妙运用权力，往往会激发意想不到的惊喜。

#↩

CASE STUDY: “BLOODCHILD”

案例研究：“血亲”

A short story by Octavia E. Butler
奥克塔维娅·E·巴特勒的短篇小说

“Bloodchild” tells a love story between species.

《血亲》讲述的是不同物种之间的爱情故事。

Isaac Asimov’s Science Fiction Magazine published it in 1984. In the years since, it has won both Hugo and Nebula awards; Locus and Science Fiction Chronicle have also named it Best Novelette. 2

《艾萨克·阿西莫夫科幻杂志》于1984年发表了这篇小说。此后，它荣获了雨果奖和星云奖；《轨迹》杂志和《科幻纪事》杂志也将其评为最佳中篇小说。

#↩

Backstory

背景故事

Generations ago, the vestiges of humanity migrated to a planet inhabited by the Tlic, gigantic insects that reproduce by injecting their eggs into animals. When the earthlings landed, the Tlic realized that the human body is the perfect incubation host. The Tlic government then built an encapsulated preserve to protect humans from the planet’s egg-laying hordes, but as quid pro quo for survival, each family must select one of its own to bear a Tlic’s larvae. The chance of dying when these worms hatch and eat their way out of the host’s body is great. Humanity agreed to the deal.

很久以前，残存的人类迁徙到了一个居住着巨型昆虫——特里克人的星球。特里克人通过将卵注入动物体内进行繁殖。地球人登陆后，特里克人发现人体是完美的孵化宿主。为了保护人类免受星球上大量产卵昆虫的侵袭，特里克政府建造了一个封闭的保护区。但作为生存的交换条件，每个家庭必须选择一名成员来孕育特里克人的幼虫。这些幼虫孵化后会吞噬宿主的身体，死亡的几率极高。人类接受了这项交易。

Lien, a widow with four children, chose Gan, her youngest son, to bear the eggs of T’Gatoi, a high government official. T’Gatoi is a loving creature who befriended the family years ago, visiting daily, providing them with the comforts of mildly narcotic drugs. She feels a special maternal caring for Gan.

寡妇莲带着四个孩子，她选择让小儿子甘孕育高官特加托伊的卵。特加托伊心地善良，多年前就与莲一家结为好友，每天都来探望，并为他们提供一些轻度麻醉药物。她对甘有着特殊的母爱。

#↩

Story

故事

Inciting incident: The day arrives when the body of someone in Lien’s family must accept T’Gatoi’s eggs. Gan is intensely aware that when his mother was pregnant, she selected him for this duty. His feelings wait in limbo and confusion. Gan’s two sisters, however, feel that hosting Tlic eggs would be an honor, while their older brother, Qui, hates the idea. He once witnessed a man die in agony as larvae ate their way out of him.

导火索：利恩家族中某位成员的遗体必须接受特加托伊的卵。甘清楚地记得，母亲怀孕时就选定他来承担这项使命。他的内心充满矛盾和困惑。甘的两个妹妹认为能够孕育特里克卵是一种荣耀，而他们的哥哥奎却对此深恶痛绝。他曾亲眼目睹一个男人在幼虫的啃噬下痛苦死去。

Ideally, when the eggs hatch and their worms emerge, the Tlic performs a kind of cesarean section on the human, passing the hungry worms into some animal flesh, saving the host’s life. Indeed, that afternoon Bram, a pregnant man who’s been abandoned by his Tlic, bangs on their door and T’Gatoi performs the emergency operation. Gan helps save the man by shooting an animal kept on the preserve and providing nonhuman food for the emerging larvae.

理想情况下，当虫卵孵化，幼虫破壳而出时，特里克会为人类进行类似剖腹产的手术，将这些饥饿的幼虫转移到某种动物肉中，从而挽救宿主的生命。那天下午，被特里克抛弃的孕妇布拉姆敲响了他们的房门，特加托伊立即为他实施了紧急手术。甘射杀了一只饲养在保护区的动物，为幼虫提供了非人类的食物，从而帮助布拉姆脱险。

As T’Gatoi pulls worm after worm from the man’s body, Gan witnesses the blood-soaked surgery and the victim’s hideous suffering. He is so repulsed, he contemplates suicide rather than impregnation. Afterward, T’Gatoi, who must lay her eggs that night, gives him a way out and asks if he would rather have her impregnate one of his sisters.

当T’Gatoi从那人体内一条条地取出虫子时，Gan目睹了血淋淋的手术和受害者惨不忍睹的痛苦。他感到无比厌恶，宁愿自杀也不愿怀孕。事后，当晚必须产卵的T’Gatoi给了他一个选择，问他是否更愿意让她让他的一个姐妹怀孕。

Now in crisis, Gan must choose: risk a sister’s life to save himself or risk his own life as an act of honor and manhood. He chooses to accept his fate and offers his body out of love for his family, humanity, and T’Gatoi. As T’Gatoi impregnates Gan, she lovingly promises she will never abandon him.

如今，甘面临生死抉择：是冒着妹妹性命的风险自救，还是为了荣誉和男子气概而牺牲自己的生命？他最终选择接受命运，出于对家人、对人类以及对特加托伊的爱，献出自己的身体。特加托伊使甘怀孕，并深情地承诺永远不会抛弃他。

#↩

Cast

投掷

Short stories don’t offer the pages necessary to develop a complex cast of great size. In this telling, only Gan and T’Gatoi are complex; the rest have nicely drawn characterizations but no dimensions.

短篇小说篇幅有限，不足以塑造庞大而复杂的人物群像。在这个故事里，只有甘和特加托伊这两个角色比较复杂；其他角色虽然刻画得不错，但缺乏立体感。

Gan

两个都

Gan narrates the story in the first person, giving us access to his inner conflicts and the three dimensions that span within him.

甘以第一人称叙述故事，让我们得以了解他内心的冲突以及他内心的三个维度。

1. He’s fearful yet brave. Terror grips him, but his untapped courage waits in reserve.
1. 他既恐惧又勇敢。恐惧攫住了他，但他尚未开发的勇气却蓄势待发。
2. He’s self-preserving yet self-sacrificing. He fights against his fate for selfish reasons but finally surrenders to it for moral reasons.
2. 他既自保又自我牺牲。他出于自私的原因与命运抗争，但最终出于道德原因屈服于命运。
3. He’s a child on the cusp of maturity. His opening words set the story with “My last night of childhood…”
3. 他正值青春期，即将步入成年。他开篇便以“我童年的最后一夜……”这句话奠定了故事的基调。

T’Gatoi

T’Gatoi

This nine-foot-tall segmented insect has multiple limbs on each segment and a stinger in her tail that puts people to sleep. Her long friendship with Lien and her wise, patient devotion to Gan gives her a grandmotherly aura. At the same time, however, her genes are driving her to reproduce. She, too, has three dimensions:

这只九英尺高的分节昆虫，每个节上都有多条肢体，尾巴上还有一根能让人昏睡的毒刺。她与莲的深厚友谊，以及她对甘的睿智而耐心的奉献，让她散发出一种慈祥祖母的气息。然而与此同时，她的基因也在驱使她繁衍后代。她也拥有三维空间：

1. She’s kind but autocratic. Like a zookeeper, T’Gatoi is a generous, caring protector, but also the master of her human charges.
1. 她心地善良但又专断独行。就像动物园管理员一样，T'Gatoi 既是一位慷慨、体贴的保护者，也是她所照管的人类的主人。
2. She soothes pain yet causes pain. T’Gatoi knows the dread, even death, her species causes human beings. So her guilty conscience moves her to pacify the fear and anxiety in Lien’s family with gifts of narcotic pills and injections.
2. 她抚慰痛苦，却也带来痛苦。T’Gatoi深知她的种族会给人类带来恐惧，甚至是死亡。因此，出于愧疚，她用麻醉药丸和注射剂来安抚Lien一家人的恐惧和焦虑。
3. She cares but kills. She loves Lien’s family, especially Gan, but will end their lives, if necessary, to secure the survival of her species.
3. 她既关心他人，又会杀戮。她深爱着莲的家人，尤其是甘，但为了确保种族的延续，必要时她会结束他们的生命。

The other cast members have no dimensions, just one distinctive trait each.

其他演员没有多面性，每个人都只有一个鲜明的特点。

Lien

留置权

Trait: Sadness. The widow Lien knows that her son or one of her daughters will be impregnated with T’Gatoi’s larvae that evening, and there’s nothing she can do to stop it. A mood of pained resignation seems to age her.

特质：悲伤。寡妇莉恩知道，当晚她的儿子或女儿中必有一人会被T'Gatoi的幼虫所侵染，而她却无力阻止。一种痛苦的无奈感似乎让她显得更加苍老。

Qui

WHO

Trait: Anger. Qui rebels, furious that human beings must submit to Tlic rule.

特质：愤怒。奎族反叛者，对人类必须臣服于特里克族的统治感到愤怒。

Gan’s sisters

甘的姐妹们

Trait: Submission. Gan’s sisters take the opposite view. They believe that being chosen for a Tlic impregnation is a privilege.

特质：顺从。甘的姐妹们则持相反观点。她们认为被选中进行特里克族的受孕仪式是一种荣幸。

Bram

布拉姆

Trait: Terror. Bram screams in a panic as the worms inside him burst out of their shells.

特征：恐惧。布拉姆惊恐地尖叫起来，他体内的蠕虫破壳而出。

T’Khotgif

T’Khotgif

Trait: Personal concern. The Tlic who impregnated Bram hurries to him.

特征：个人关切。使布拉姆怀孕的特里克急忙赶到他身边。

Doctor

医生

Trait: Professional concern. He helps T’Gatoi save Bram.

特点：职业操守。他帮助T’Gatoi救了Bram。

#↩

Conclusion

结论

Science Fiction is a presentational genre, home to any of the sixteen primary genres. In the case of “Bloodchild,” Gan arcs along an Evolution Plot from immaturity to maturity.

科幻小说是一种表现形式多样的类型，涵盖了十六种主要类型中的任何一种。以《血亲》为例，主人公甘的成长历程遵循着从不成熟到成熟的进化叙事模式。

Sci-Fi’s distinguishing convention is its setting. Its temporal location may or may not be futuristic, but its society is somehow warped (even dystopian). 3 This disturbance in the natural social order began in the backstory when human folly misused science.

科幻小说的显著特征在于其设定。故事发生的时代背景可能设定在未来，也可能并非如此，但其社会在某种程度上是扭曲的（甚至是反乌托邦式的）。这种对自然社会秩序的扰乱始于人类滥用科学的愚昧历史。

In “Bloodchild,” the author never tells us what global catastrophe caused the cast’s ancestors to abandon Earth, but their migration reversed nature’s balance. On planet Earth, humanity was the dominant species that used various subspecies as food, clothing, and pets. On planet Tlic, human beings are reduced to a subspecies, useful as a nesting place for eggs.

在《血亲》中，作者从未明确指出是什么全球性灾难导致主人公们的祖先离开地球，但他们的迁徙颠覆了自然界的平衡。在地球上，人类是主宰物种，利用各种亚种作为食物、衣物和宠物。而在特里克星球上，人类沦为亚种，仅仅作为其他生物产卵的巢穴。

If Science Fiction is your genre, then like Octavia Butler, use its power to invert reality to create an empathetic cast in an unpredictable story that warns of things to come.

如果你喜欢科幻题材，那么就像奥克塔维亚·巴特勒一样，利用科幻的力量颠覆现实，在不可预测的故事中塑造出富有同情心的角色，并警示未来可能发生的事情。

#↩

CASE STUDY: BREAKING BAD

案例研究：《绝命毒师》

The longform series is a unique medium, as different from prose as cinema is from theatre. Longform tellings, with their open episodes and open seasons, put mammoth casts through years of screen performance. To the writer, longform offers the opportunity to create characters of dimensionality and complexity beyond the reach of any other storytelling form. So before we unravel Breaking Bad , let’s take a brief look at the medium that made it possible.

长篇剧集是一种独特的媒介，它与散文的差异，正如电影与戏剧的差异一样显著。长篇剧集采用开放式的剧情模式，每集和每一季都允许庞大的演员阵容进行长达数年的荧幕表演。对于编剧而言，长篇剧集提供了塑造其他任何叙事形式都无法企及的立体而复杂的人物的机会。因此，在深入剖析《绝命毒师》之前，让我们先简要了解一下成就这部作品的媒介。

#↩

The Effects of Length and Cast Size

长度和抛投尺寸的影响

The smaller the cast, the fewer the relationships between characters, and therefore, the less numerous and various their tactics, behaviors, and desires. The fewer the scenes and less the diverse their turning points, the fewer the choices and actions its characters must make and take. For these reasons, the casts of one-act plays, short stories, short films, and comic books are limited in number and dimensionality.

角色越少，人物之间的关系就越少，因此，他们的策略、行为和欲望也就越单一、越缺乏多样性。场景越少，转折点越单一，角色需要做出的选择和采取的行动也就越少。正因如此，独幕剧、短篇小说、短片和漫画的角色数量和维度都比较有限。

Conversely, the larger the cast, the greater the ramifications of character relationships and dimensions. In addition, the more numerous and diverse the scenes and the longer the performance time, the greater the variety of desires, choices, and actions characters must take and make. As a result, the casts that fill novels, as well as full-length dramas, comedies, and musicals onstage and on-screen tend to be rich in variety and psychological complexity.

反之，演员阵容越大，人物关系和性格维度就越复杂深远。此外，场景越多、越多样化，演出时间越长，人物必须面对的欲望、选择和行动就越多。因此，无论是小说，还是舞台剧、喜剧、音乐剧，其演员阵容往往都丰富多元，心理刻画也更为复杂。

Longform screen works, by reason of cast size and years of performance, take the art of story into complexities of character beyond the scope of any other medium. A thousand-page novel or epic saga, for example, contains about the same event and character development as a single season of longform. Multiseason storytelling tests an author’s limits of insight, memory, and human feeling. Therefore, the herculean task for the longform writer is holding viewers’ interest in a vast cast of characters through fifty to one hundred episodes told over five to ten years.

由于演员阵容庞大且演出周期长达数年，长篇影视作品将故事的艺术推向了其他任何媒介都无法企及的复杂人物刻画层面。例如，一部千页小说或史诗巨著所包含的事件和人物发展，与一季长篇剧集的内容大致相当。多季叙事考验着作者的洞察力、记忆力和对人性的理解力。因此，对于长篇剧集的编剧而言，一项艰巨的任务是如何让观众在长达五到十年的时间里，通过五十到一百集的剧集，持续关注众多人物的精彩故事。

#↩

The Two Modes of Interest

两种兴趣模式

A story compels interest by drawing on the reader’s or audience’s conscious curiosity and subconscious concern.

故事之所以能引起兴趣，是因为它能唤起读者或观众的意识好奇心和潜意识关注。

Curiosity: the intellectual need to answer questions, solve puzzles and problems, close open patterns, and learn the hows and whys of a character’s life.

好奇心：一种求知欲，想要回答问题、解决谜题和难题、填补空白、了解人物生活来龙去脉的需要。

Concern: the emotional need to experience the positive charge of values—life, not death; love, not hate; justice, not injustice; peace, not war; good, not evil; and the like.

关注：一种情感需求，即体验价值观带来的积极影响——生命而非死亡；爱而非仇恨；正义而非不义；和平而非战争；善而非恶；等等。

Neither curiosity nor concern, however, will hold interest if an audience cannot identify with at least one major character in the cast. In fact, the ideal longform work draws empathy to many centers of good, not only in the central plot’s protagonist but in the protagonists of subplots as well.

然而，如果观众无法与剧中至少一个主要角色产生共鸣，那么好奇心和关注感都将荡然无存。事实上，理想的长篇作品能够唤起观众对诸多善意之处的共鸣，不仅体现在主线剧情的主角身上，也体现在支线剧情的主角身上。

A story’s major dramatic question is a specific variation on the universal question “How will this turn out?” MDQs such as “Will Ragnar Lothbrok conquer England?” in Vikings or “Will Kendall Roy take over his father’s business empire?” in Succession hook and hold its audience’s curiosity over years.

故事的主要戏剧性问题是普遍问题“事情会如何发展？”的特定变体。例如，《维京传奇》中的“拉格纳·洛德布罗克会征服英格兰吗？”或《继承之战》中的“肯德尔·罗伊会接管他父亲的商业帝国吗？”这类主要戏剧性问题能够抓住并保持观众多年的好奇心。

However, the greatest magnetic force, the one that grips the deepest interest over the longest stretches of time, arises from the psychological depths of major characters in longform tellings. Like the allure of the ocean, the inner lives of complex characters fascinate the audience, inducing multihour binges as they discover unforeseen traits, marvel at contradictions between public selves and core selves, and most important, follow the protagonist’s arc until she completes herself with moral, mental, or humanistic change.

然而，最强大的吸引力，能够长时间牢牢抓住观众心的，源自长篇故事中主要人物的内心世界。如同海洋的魅力，复杂人物的内心世界令观众着迷，促使他们连续数小时沉浸其中，探索人物不为人知的特质，惊叹于其公众形象与内在自我之间的矛盾，而最重要的是，跟随主人公的成长历程，直至其在道德、心理或人性层面完成蜕变。

The point to remember: Revelation and evolution hold longform audiences to the screen over years of time. What kills that long-term interest? Repetitiousness and rigidity. Once a protagonist has nothing left to reveal, once she is no longer capable of change, once she is emptied out and her psychology exhausted, her behavior becomes predictable and monotonous. With that, the audience dwindles.

关键在于：揭示和发展是吸引观众多年观看长篇电影的根本。那么，什么会扼杀这种长期兴趣呢？重复和僵化。一旦主角没有什么可揭示的了，一旦她不再能够改变，一旦她被掏空，心理也耗尽，她的行为就会变得可预测且单调。随之而来的是观众的流失。

Consider Dexter : This eight-season series ran on Showtime from 2006 to 2013. Season 1 sets up Dexter (Michael C. Hall) as a psychopathic vigilante hiding behind a likable characterization. Devoid of emotion, compassion, or conscience, he comes to life only in the midst of murder. The next three seasons, however, give Dexter compassion for children, feelings of romantic love, and guilt over unintended consequences. That completes him; everything knowable about Dexter was known by the end of Season 4. Seasons 5 to 8 neither revealed previously unseen traits nor changed his psychology. Plot twists proliferated, but Dexter stagnated until his diehard audience gave up. I hope its proposed renewal as a 10-episode miniseries in Fall 2021 manages the character arc its audience has long desired.

以《嗜血法医》（Dexter）为例：这部共八季的剧集于2006年至2013年在Showtime电视台播出。第一季将德克斯特（迈克尔·C·霍尔饰）塑造成一个外表讨喜却内心冷酷无情的冷血义警。他缺乏情感、同情心和良知，只有在杀戮中才会展现出真正的自我。然而，接下来的三季赋予了德克斯特对孩子的怜悯、浪漫的爱情以及对无意后果的愧疚。至此，他的人物形象已臻于完整；到第四季结束时，关于德克斯特的一切已知信息都已呈现。第五季到第八季既没有展现出之前未曾揭示的特质，也没有改变他的心理。剧情反转层出不穷，但德克斯特的形象却停滞不前，最终令他的铁杆粉丝们放弃了追剧。我希望这部剧集计划于2021年秋季以十集迷你剧的形式续订，能够满足观众们长久以来对德克斯特角色弧光的期待。

Fifty to one hundred hours of longform performance calls for a protagonist whose complexity goes far beyond three dimensions.

50 到 100 小时的长篇表演需要一个复杂程度远远超出三维的主角。

#↩

Breaking Bad

绝命毒师

by Vince Gilligan
作者：文斯·吉利根

Breaking Bad ran for sixty-two episodes over five seasons. Its creator titled the series after a Southernism that means taking your life down an immoral, violent road. Gilligan sold the series with the now-famous four-word pitch describing the story’s arc: “Mr. Chips goes Scarface.”

《绝命毒师》共播出五季，六十二集。它的创作者以一句南方俚语为剧名，意指走上一条不道德、充满暴力的道路。吉利根用一句如今广为人知的四字推介来推销这部剧，概括了故事的走向：“《绝命毒师》变成了《疤面煞星》。”

It has a central plot, twenty-five subplots, and a cast of more than eighty speaking roles. In 2013, the Guinness Book of World Records declared Breaking Bad the highest-rated screen series ever. The three lead actors won nine Emmys among them, while the show itself won another seven Emmys and two Golden Globes as well as two Peabodys, two Critics’ Choice Awards, four Television Critics Association awards, and three Satellite awards.

它有一条主线剧情、二十五条支线剧情，以及超过八十个有台词的角色。2013年，《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》宣布《绝命毒师》为史上收视率最高的电视剧。三位主演共获得九项艾美奖，而该剧本身则斩获七项艾美奖、两项金球奖、两项皮博迪奖、两项评论家选择奖、四项电视评论家协会奖和三项卫星奖。

A series prequel, Better Call Saul , debuted in 2015, and a movie sequel, El Camino , premiered in 2019.

剧集前传《风骚律师》于 2015 年首播，电影续集《绝命毒师：续命之徒》于 2019 年上映。

#↩

Backstory

背景故事

Walter White (Bryan Cranston), a polymath scientist, and Gretchen (Jessica Hecht), his girlfriend, teamed with Elliot Schwartz (Adam Godley) to found Gray Matter Technologies. After a falling-out, Walt sold his share and quit. Elliott and Gretchen persevered, and exploiting Walt’s corporate-owned inventions, built a highly successful company. In time, Elliott and Gretchen married.

博学多才的科学家沃尔特·怀特（布莱恩·克兰斯顿饰）和他的女友格雷琴（杰西卡·赫克特饰）与埃利奥特·施瓦茨（亚当·戈德利饰）共同创立了格雷玛特科技公司。后来，由于意见不合，沃尔特卖掉了自己的股份并退出了公司。埃利奥特和格雷琴则坚持不懈，利用沃尔特在公司拥有的发明，打造了一家非常成功的企业。最终，埃利奥特和格雷琴结为夫妻。

Walt, embittered by his failures, became an Albuquerque high school teacher, married Skyler (Anna Gunn), and fathered two children.

沃尔特因失败而心怀怨恨，成为阿尔伯克基的一名高中教师，与斯凯勒（安娜·冈恩饰）结婚，并育有两个孩子。

#↩

Season 1

第一季

Although never a smoker, Walt discovers he has inoperable stage-3 lung cancer. To secure his family’s future before he dies, Walt turns to a life of crime. He coerces a former student, Jesse Pinkman (Aaron Paul), to work with him cooking methamphetamine. Jesse buys an old RV to serve as their kitchen. In it, Walt uses commonplace chemicals to create a powerful blue-tinted meth.

尽管从未吸烟，沃尔特却发现自己患上了无法手术的第三期肺癌。为了在临终前保障家人的未来，沃尔特走上了犯罪的道路。他胁迫以前的学生杰西·平克曼（亚伦·保尔饰）与他一起制造冰毒。杰西买了一辆旧房车作为他们的制毒窝点。在房车里，沃尔特利用常见的化学品制造出了一种强效的蓝色冰毒。

When Jesse tries to sell their drug on the street, Emilio (John Koyama) and Krazy-8 (Maximino Arciniega), two low-level drug dealers, horn in. Walt lures them to the RV where he poisons one and later garrotes the other. Walt and Jesse then go into business with Tuco Salamanca (Raymond Cruz), a ruthless, virtually insane gangster.

杰西试图在街头贩卖毒品时，两个小毒贩埃米利奥（约翰·科亚马饰）和克雷兹-8（马克西米诺·阿西涅加饰）插手了。沃尔特把他们引到房车里，毒死了其中一人，之后又勒死了另一人。之后，沃尔特和杰西与冷酷无情、近乎疯狂的黑帮老大图科·萨拉曼卡（雷蒙德·克鲁兹饰）合作。

#↩

Season 2

第二季

A deadly shoot-out with Tuco leaves Walt and Jesse without a distributor, so they find their way to a criminal lawyer, Saul Goodman (Bob Odenkirk) who hooks them up with a major drug dealer, Gus Fring (Giancarlo Esposito). Gus pays them a huge sum, and Walt adopts the street name “Heisenberg.” The DEA, led by Walt’s brother-in-law Hank Schrader (Dean Norris), begins to investigate this mysterious crime boss.

与图科的致命枪战让沃尔特和杰西失去了分销商，于是他们找到了刑事律师索尔·古德曼（鲍勃·奥登科克饰），古德曼帮他们联系上了一位大毒枭古斯·弗林（吉安卡洛·埃斯波西托饰）。古斯付给他们一大笔钱，沃尔特也因此改名为“海森堡”。由沃尔特的妹夫汉克·施拉德（迪恩·诺里斯饰）领导的缉毒局开始调查这位神秘的犯罪头目。

Jesse falls in love with Jane Margolis (Krysten Ritter), a heroin addict, and becomes addicted himself. Walt refuses to give Jesse half of Gus’s money until he gets off drugs. Jane tries to blackmail Walt into paying up, but she passes out on heroin, and then chokes to death on her own vomit while Walt watches silently from across the room. Walt gets Jesse into rehab. A few days later, he witnesses the midair collision of two passenger jets over the city—a tragedy caused by Jane’s distraught, air-traffic controller father, Donald (John de Lancie). The blame is Walt’s.

杰西爱上了海洛因成瘾者简·玛格丽丝（克里斯汀·里特饰），自己也染上了毒瘾。沃尔特拒绝给杰西一半古斯的钱，除非他戒掉毒瘾。简试图勒索沃尔特，逼他付钱，但她却因吸食海洛因而昏迷，随后被自己的呕吐物呛死，沃尔特在房间另一头默默地看着这一切发生。沃尔特把杰西送进了戒毒所。几天后，他目睹了两架客机在城市上空相撞——这场悲剧是由简悲痛欲绝的空中交通管制员父亲唐纳德（约翰·德·兰西饰）造成的。沃尔特因此背负了罪责。

#↩

Season 3

第三季

At home, Walt’s marriage falls apart. When Skyler seeks a divorce, Walt reveals his secret criminal life, pleading that he did it for his family. Skyler, in revenge, seduces her boss, then taunts Walt with her affair.

在家中，沃尔特的婚姻走向破裂。当斯凯勒提出离婚时，沃尔特坦白了自己的犯罪生涯，并辩解说他这么做都是为了家人。斯凯勒为了报复，勾引了自己的老板，然后用这段婚外情来嘲讽沃尔特。

Walt and Jesse go to work for Gus, cooking meth in a hidden high-tech lab. Soon after, two cartel assassins, seeking revenge for Tuco, attack Hank. He dispatches them and survives, although temporarily paralyzed.

沃尔特和杰西开始为古斯工作，在一个隐蔽的高科技实验室里制毒。不久之后，两名卡特尔杀手为了替图科报仇，袭击了汉克。汉克击退了他们，虽然暂时瘫痪，但最终活了下来。

Jesse rebels against Gus because he uses children to sell drugs on the street. Gus replaces Jesse with Gale Boetticher (David Costabile). Walt fears that once Gale learns to cook on his own, Gus will kill both him and Jesse. He tells Jesse to kill Gale, and Jesse does.

杰西反抗古斯，因为古斯利用儿童在街头贩毒。古斯用盖尔·博蒂彻（大卫·科斯塔比尔饰）取代了杰西。沃尔特担心盖尔一旦学会独立制毒，古斯就会杀了他和杰西。他让杰西杀了盖尔，杰西照做了。

#↩

Season 4

第四季
